name: a0poster
caption: Support for designing posters on large paper

descriptions.text: Provides fonts in sizes of 12pt up to 107pt and also makes sure that in math formulas the symbols appear in the right size. Can also create a PostScript header file for dvips which ensures that the poster will be printed in the right size. Supported sizes are DIN A0, DIN A1, DIN A2 and DIN A3.

name: a2ac
caption: AFM to AFM plus Composites

descriptions.text:
Enables the use of PostScript fonts while typesetting texts in languages where inflected letters are used. The font will typically not contain the complete alphabet of a given language; the program will derive composite glyph structures using accent glyphs, and output their details in the derived AFM file.

The configuration files of the program are independent of the PostScript font encoding and of the typesetting system encoding. The program may be used to prepare a font for any typesetting system, especially TeX.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: a2ping
caption: Advanced PS, PDF, EPS converter

descriptions.text: a2ping is a Perl script command line utility written for Unix that converts many raster image and vector graphics formats to EPS or PDF and other page description formats. Accepted input file formats are: PS (PostScript), EPS, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PNM, BMP, GIF, LBM, XPM, PCX, TGA. Accepted output formats are: EPS, PCL5, PDF, PDF1, PBM, PGM, PPM, PS, markedEPS, markedPS, PNG, XWD, BMP, TIFF, JPEG, GIF, XPM. a2ping delegates the low-level work to Ghostscript (GS), pdftops and sam2p. a2ping fixes many glitches during the EPS to EPS conversion, so its output is often more compatible and better embeddable than its input.

name: a4
caption: Support for A4 paper sizes

descriptions.text:
Provides support for A4 paper sizes, superseding a LaTeX 2.09 package of the same name (the package was developed from a now-extinct package called a4dutch).

The package is mostly superseded by the a4paper option of LaTeX itself and by the geometry package. Its margins are slightly narrower than those of the a4paper option (there are those that claim this is a typographically poor choice), but it also has a widemargins option.

The package is now distributed as part of the ntgclass bundle.

name: a4wide
caption: <q>Wide</q> a4 layout

descriptions.text:
This package increases the width of the typeset area of an a4 page. This sort of operation is capable of producing typographically poor results; the operation itself is better provided by the geometry package.

The package uses the a4 package.

name: a5comb
caption: Support for a5 paper sizes

descriptions.text: Superseded by geometry.

name: aaai
caption: AAAI style

descriptions.text: LaTeX 2.09 conference style for AAAI-88. (The package does not work with current LaTeX, and the style it implements is not that which the AAAI seems now to favour.)

name: aaai-named
caption: BibTeX style for AAAI

descriptions.text: A BibTeX style derived from the standard master, presumably for use with the aaai package.

name: Aalok
caption: LaTeX class file for the Marathi journal <q>Aalok</q>

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: This package provides the class file for typesetting Aalok, a Marathi journal with LaTeX.
आलोक मराठी नियतकालिकाची अक्षरजुळणी करण्याकरिता लाटेक्-वर्ग.

name: aastex
caption: Macros for manuscript preparation for AAS Journals

descriptions.text: The package provides a document class for preparing papers for American Astronomical Society publications. Authors who wish to submit papers to AAS journals are strongly urged to use this class in preference to any of the alternatives available.

name: abbr
caption: Simple macros supporting abbreviations for Plain and LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides some simple macros to support abbreviations in Plain TeX or LaTeX. It allows writing (e.g.) \<TEX> instead of \TeX, hence frees users from having to escape space after parameterless macros.

topics.details: macros for defining abbreviations in documents

name: abbrevs
caption: Text abbreviations in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package defining abbreviation macros, which expand to defined text and insert following space intelligently, based on context. They can also expand to one thing the first time they are used and another thing on subsequent invocations. Thus they can be abbreviations in two senses, in the source and in the document. Also includes a facility for suffixes like 1900\BC and 6:00\PM which correctly handles following periods.

The package is part of the frankenstein bundle.

topics.details: macros for defining abbreviations in documents

name: abc
caption: Support ABC music notation in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The abc package lets you include lines of music written in the ABC Plus language. The package will then employ the \write18 facility to convert your notation to PostScript (using the established utility abcm2ps) and hence to the format needed for inclusion in your document.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: abc2mtex
caption: Notate tunes stored in ABC notation

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: A package to notate tunes stored in an ascii format (abc notation, commonly used to notate traditional music). One of the most important aims of ABC notation, and perhaps one that distinguishes it from most, if not all, computer-readable musical languages is that it can be easily read by humans. The package produces files that can be processed with MusicTeX.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: abnt
caption: Typesetting academic works according to ABNT rules

descriptions.text: The ABNT package provides a clean and practical implementation of the ABNT rules for academic texts. Its purpose is to be as simple and user-friendly as possible.

name: abntex2
caption: Typeset technical and scientific Brazilian documents based on ABNT rules

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides support for typesetting technical and scientific Brazilian documents (like academic thesis, articles, reports, research project and others) based on the ABNT rules (Associação Brasileira de Normas Técnicas).

It replaces the old abntex.

name: abntexto
caption: LaTeX class for formatting academic papers in ABNT standards

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX class created for Brazilian students to facilitate the use of standards from the Associação Brasileira de Normas Técnicas (ABNT) in academic works like TCCs, dissertations, theses.

name: abntexto-uece
caption: LaTeX class for formatting academic papers in UECE standards

descriptions.text: This is a unofficial LaTeX class created for Brazilian students to facilitate the use of standards from the Universidade Estadual do Ceará (UECE) in academic works like TCCs, dissertations, and theses.

name: Aboensis
caption: A late medieval OpenType cursive font

descriptions.text:
The package contains the free OpenType medieval cursive font Aboensis and a style file to use it in XeLaTeX documents.

The font is based on Codex Aboensis, that is a law book written in Sweden in the 1430s. Since medieval cursive is very difficult to read for modern people, the font is not suitable for use as an ordinary book font, but is intended for emulating late medieval manuscripts.

The font contains two sets of initials: Lombardic and cursive to go with the basic alphabet, and there is support for writing two-colored initials and capitals. There are also a large number of abbreviation sigla that can be accessed as ligature substitutions.

The style file contains macros that help to use the extended features of the font such as initials and two-colored capitals. There are also macros to help achieve even pages with consistent line spacing.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: abraces
caption: Asymmetric over-/underbraces in maths

descriptions.text: The package provides a character key-driven interface to supplement new constructions of the traditional \overbrace and \underbrace pairs in an asymmetric or arbitrary way.

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: abspos
caption: Absolute placement with coffins

descriptions.text:
This package lets you place contents at an absolute position, anchored at some specified part of the contents, similar to how TikZ nodes work, though without using the two-pass strategy of TikZ. It also avoids messing with the order of beamer overlays, which is what happens when one uses the textpos package with the overlay option.

The solution used is quite straightforward, combining coffins (using l3coffins) with the placement mechanisms of atbegshi.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: abstbook
caption: Books of abstracts

descriptions.text: A LaTeX class file for making books of abstracts, commonly used for conferences. It is based on report class, however \chapter has been redefined and shouldn't be used.

name: abstr-collect
caption: Print a collection of abstracts

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 document style (based on article.sty) which provides facilities for printing abstracts from bibliographies.

name: abstract
caption: Control the typesetting of the abstract environment

descriptions.text: The abstract package gives you control over the typesetting of the abstract environment, and in particular provides for a one column abstract in a two column paper.

name: abstyles-babel
caption: Adaptable styles for use with Babel

descriptions.text: This set of BibTeX styles is a version of the adaptable BibTeX styles, modified so that the styles react to Babel operations.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: abstyles-orig
caption: Adaptable BibTeX styles

descriptions.text:
A family of modifications of the standard BibTeX styles whose behaviour may be changed by changing the user document, without change to the styles themselves.

The package is largely used nowadays in its adaptation for working with Babel.

name: academicons
caption: Font containing high quality icons of online academic profiles

descriptions.text:
The academicons package provides access in (La)TeX to 146 high quality icons of online academic profiles included in the free Academicons font. This package works with both Xe(La)TeX or Lua(La)TeX by using fontspec to load the included font, as well as with pdf(La)TeX by loading a Type 1 converted format of the original font.

The Academicons font was designed by James Walsh and released (see http://jpswalsh.github.io/academicons/) under the open SIL Open Font License. This package is a redistribution of the free Academicons font with specific bindings for (La)TeX. It is inspired and based on the fontawesome package.

The generic \aiicon macro takes as mandatory argument the ⟨name⟩ of the desired icon. Icons can also be accessed directly by their respective macro. For example, \aiicon{googlescholar} yields the same result as \aiGoogleScholar. The full list of icons with their respective names and direct commands can be found in the manual.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts

name: accanthis
caption: Accanthis fonts, with LaTeX support

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text:
Accanthis No. 3 is designed by Hirwin Harendal and is suitable as an alternative to fonts such as Garamond, Galliard, Horley old style, Sabon, and Bembo.

The support files are suitable for use with all LaTeX engines.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: accenti
caption: Extra accented character macros, designed for Italian

descriptions.text:
The package defines several simple commands for accented letters commonly used in Italian writing. Some of these commands redefine existing standard LaTeX versions. (The author reports that he no longer uses the package, preferring more standard techniques to express the inflected characters.)

The package is part of the bosisio collection.

name: accents
caption: Multiple mathematical accents

descriptions.text: A package for multiple accents in mathematics, with nice features concerning the creation of accents and placement of scripts.

name: accents-cs
caption: Create a VF for the accents used in Czech/Slovak

descriptions.text: This a program, distributed as WEB source, that takes the TFM for a (OT1) font, and generates a virtual font (and associated TFM file) for a font implementing the KOI8-CS character coding for Czech/Slovak.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: accessibility
caption: Create tagged and structured PDF files

descriptions.text:
The accessibility package is intended to create tagged, structured PDF documents from LaTeX source code. It allows to produce tagged PDF output following Adobe’s PDF-1.5 and 1.6 specifications.

This package is predominantly targeted at documents produced using the KOMA-Script document classes.

However, the author told us towards the end of June 2020:

Based on feedback to the accessibility package and discussions with a few folks, I’d like to discourage people from using the package any more. It’s evident that it’s not going to work in it’s current form, and I don’t have the skills or time to update it.

I know the general concept is very important, and so I’m looking at getting support from various funding agencies to employ someone to completely refactor the code in a more future-proof fashion. I’ll coordinate this with the core LaTeX Team once I have more solid ideas.

name: accfonts
caption: Utilities to derive new fonts from existing ones

descriptions.text: The accfonts package contains three utilities to permit easy manipulation of fonts, in particular the creation of unusual accented characters. Mkt1font works on Adobe Type 1 fonts, vpl2vpl works on TeX virtual fonts and vpl2ovp transforms a TeX font to an Omega one. All three programs read in a font (either the font itself or a property list), together with a simple definition file containing lines such as 128 z acute ; they then write out a new version of the font with the requested new characters in the numerical slots specified. Great care is taken over the positioning of accents, and over the provision of kerning information for new characters; mkt1font also generates suitable hints to enhance quality at small sizes or poor resolutions. The programs are written in Perl.

topics.details: Omega and packages that use it
process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: accsupp
caption: Better accessibility support for PDF files

descriptions.text:
Since PDF 1.5 portions of a page can be marked for better accessibility support. For example, replacement texts or expansions of abbreviations can be provided. This package starts with providing a minimal low-level interface for programmers; its status is experimental.

Support necessary for the package was added to the distill capabilities of Ghostscript with version 9.15 of Ghostscript; the dvips is only available with that version (or later).

name: achemso
caption: Support for American Chemical Society journal submissions

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a BibTeX style file following the requirements of the American Chemical Society (ACS), and a package to pass settings to the BibTeX style. It also includes a class which was used for submission support in the past.

All of this material is largely of historical interest and is retained for stability. For new material, the chem-acs style is available for bibliographies, and a short template for the ACS website is better suited to submission.

name: achicago
caption: Chicago Manual citations in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
Produces author-date citations based on The Chicago Manual of Style, using a BibTeX style such as achicago-bst.

The package is part of the frankenstein bundle of packages.

name: achicago-bst
caption: Chicago Manual BibTeX style

descriptions.text:
Produces bibliographies based on The Chicago Manual of Style. Requires the achicago LaTeX package.

The package is part of the frankenstein bundle of packages.

name: acm
caption: ACM document style

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX 2.09 document style, built by modifying Lamport's article.doc (source of the article style).

A BibTeX style is also provided.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: acmart
caption: Class for typesetting publications of ACM

descriptions.text: This package provides a class for typesetting publications of the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM).

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: acmconf
caption: Class for ACM conference proceedings

descriptions.text: This class may be used to typeset articles to be published in the proceedings of ACM (Association for Computing Machinery) conferences and workshops. The layout produced by the acmconf class is based on the ACM’s own specification.

name: acmproc
caption: Style option for ACM proceedings

descriptions.text: Designed to produce camera-ready conference proceedings.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: acmtrans
caption: Class and BibTeX style for ACM Transactions

descriptions.text:
The acmtrans2e class formats articles in the style of ACM transactions. Users who have prepared their document with LaTeX can, with very little effort, produce camera-ready copy for these journals.

The accompanying BibTeX style is based on the chicago style.

documentation.details: Documentation in the form of an ACM paper

name: acro
caption: Typeset acronyms

descriptions.text:
The package enables the author to create acronyms in a simple way, and provides means to add them to different classes of acronyms. Lists can be created of separate acronym classes.

The package option single instructs the package to ignore acronyms that are used only once in the whole document.

As an experimental feature the package also offers the option sort which automatically sorts the list created by \printacronyms.

name: acroflex
caption: Create a graphing widget in a PDF file

descriptions.text:
The acroflex package is part of the AeB Pro family of packages. It is a package that creates a graphing screen using the rmannot package. The user can type in functions and graph them. A graphing screen can be populated with pre-packaged functions for the user to scrutinize and interact with. The package can graph functions of a single variable x, a pair of parametric equations that are functions of t, and a polar function of t.

The graphing screen is a rich media annotation what uses a specially developed SWF file, called the AcroFLeX Graphing widget. This package takes advantage of rich media annotations, which is a version 9 feature of Acrobat. This package requires Acrobat Pro and Distiller version 9. The user needs to use Adobe Reader 9.0 in order to obtain the graphing functionality.

This package has become obsolete as of December 2020. Since December 2020, Adobe no longer supports Flash player (SWF, FLV). This package uses a custom SWF file (acroflex.swf); as a result this package will no longer function in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC. The package will continue to produce PDFs as designed, but only if built using Acrobat XI (or a version Acrobat prior to December 2020) and viewed in Adobe Acrobat Reader XI (or a version of Reader prior to December 2020).

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller
create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

name: acromake
caption: Make commands for acronyms

descriptions.text: The command \acromake defines a command that will expand to an acronym and its definition (on first use) and just the acronym thereafter.

name: AcroMemory
caption: Memory games in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package implements two variations of a memory game:

  • a single game board consisting of a number of tiles, each tile has a matching twin, the object is to find all the matching twins; and
  • two game boards, both identical except one has been randomly rearranged, the object is the find the matching pieces in each of the two game boards.

All LaTeX workflows are now supported: pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and dvips → distiller.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: acronym
caption: Expand acronyms at least once

descriptions.text:
This package ensures that all acronyms used in the text are spelled out in full at least once. It also provides an environment to build a list of acronyms used. The package is compatible with pdf bookmarks.

The package requires the suffix package, which in turn requires that it runs under e-TeX.

name: acronym209
caption: An algorithm package developed for LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
The package defines a rather flexible command \newacronym that may be used to define a macro for each acronym. Documentation is fairly comprehensive, in comments within the package itself.

Note that the package has little (if any) relationship to the LaTeX2e acronym package.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: acroreloadpdf
caption: Reload-the-current-PDF utility for Adobe Reader on Unix systems

descriptions.text: AcroReloadPDF.js is a small JavaScript that adds a ``Reload'' entry to the ``File'' menu of Adobe Reader on Linux and other Unix-like systems. It allows to reload the PDF document currently viewed in the Reader to reflect the latest changes. The last view of the document (page number and zoom state) will be restored.

name: AcroSort
caption: Sort sliced image into order

descriptions.text:
The AcroSort is a novelty LaTeX package for importing a series of tiled images of a picture. The tiled images are randomly arranged, then resorted before the user’s eyes using a bubble sort. The package now supports all common PDF creators: pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, dvips->distiller. Multiple bubble sort tiles images are now supported.

Images can be tiled using the tile-graphic package, also available through CTAN.

name: acroterm
caption: Manage and index acronyms and terms

descriptions.text: Yet another package for acronyms: the package offers simple markup of acronyms and technical terms in the text, giving an index each of terms and acronyms with their expanded form.

name: acrotex
caption: The AcroTeX education bundle

descriptions.text:
The bundle contains:

  • the web package to redefine page layout to web-friendly dimensions;
  • the exerquiz package for defining on-line exercises and quizzes of various sorts;
  • the eForms package for support of PDF forms;
  • the insdljs package for inserting document-level JavaScript in LaTeX documents;
  • the dljslib library of JavaScript functions for use with exerquiz; and
  • the eq2db package for converting an exerquiz quiz for processing by a ASP server-side script.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

name: acrotex-js
caption: JavaScript files used by acrotex and other packages

descriptions.text: In the distribution of this package are two critical JavaScript files (aeb.js and aeb_pro.js) used by the packages insdljs, aeb-pro, thorshammer, and docassembly. Previously these JS files where distributed with the individual packages, now they are distributed by this package and must be installed according to the instructions in the docs folder.

topics.details: relies on availability of Adobe Acrobat, etc.

name: acrotex-web
caption: Establish a page layout for an on-screen (PDF) document

descriptions.text:
The AcroTeX web package (for LaTeX – nothing to do with literate programming) is a set of macros that establishes a page layout for a (PDF) document that is designed to be read on-screen and not meant to be printed. The package also redefines the table of contents to a web style and defines optional navigational aids. The package has options for use with pdfTeX, dvips, dvipdfm, dvipsone and dviwindo.

The package is part of the AcroTeX bundle.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: acroweb
caption: Scripts to create interactive tests from a database

descriptions.text: The AcroWeb script collection offers a tool for creation of interactive PDF tests on the fly on the Internet, using the AcroTeX eDucation bundle and pdfLaTeX; it does not require too much knowledge of LaTeX. The questions are stored in a plain text database.

name: acs
caption: LaTeX 2.09 support for Advances in Control Systems

descriptions.text: A document style (apparently based on article) and a BibTeX style (based on one of the standard styles) are provided.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: active-conf
caption: Class for typesetting ACTIVE conference papers

descriptions.text: Active-conf is a class for typesetting papers for the Active conference on noise and vibration control. It is initially intended for the 2006 conference in Adelaide, Australia. The class is based on article with more flexible front-matter, and can be customised for conferences in future years with a header file.

name: actuarialangle
caption: Angle symbol denoting a duration in actuarial and financial notation

descriptions.text: This package provides commands to typeset the angle symbol denoting a duration in actuarial notation, such as in symbols for the present value of certain or life annuities, and an over angle square bracket used to emphasize joint status in symbols of life contingencies.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: actuarialsymbol
caption: Actuarial symbols of life contingencies and financial mathematics

descriptions.text:
This package provides commands to compose actuarial symbols of life contingencies and financial mathematics characterized by subscripts and superscripts on both sides of a principal symbol. The package also features commands to easily and consistently position precedence numbers above or below statuses in symbols for multiple lives contracts.

Since the actuarial notation can get quite involved, the package defines a number of shortcut macros to ease entry of the most common elements.

Appendix A of the package documentation lists the commands to typeset a large selection of symbols of life contingencies.

This package requires actuarialangle.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: adami
caption: A DOS system for working with Tamil

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: add-wes
caption: A <q>book</q> style for Addison-Wesley house style

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX 2.09 document style written for the production of a book to be published by Addison-Wesley.

The package uses a package times.sty that would nowadays be replaced by something from the psnfss bndle.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: addfont
caption: Easier use of fonts without LaTeX support

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This package is intended for use by users who know about fonts. It is a quick-fix for fonts which do not have genuine LaTeX support. It is not meant as a replacement of the LaTeX font definition files.

It is meant as something more useable for LaTeX users than the \newfont command. With addfont the loaded font scales along with the usual LaTeX size selection.

Using this package still requires some knowledge on how to use fonts with LaTeX.

name: addindex
caption: Add index entries to LaTeX document

descriptions.text: Addindex is C/Lex program to add index entries to a LaTeX document. You start with a names database, which looks like the strings section of a BibTeX database; addindex scans your LaTeX file for strings in the database, and adds \index commands for each match.

documentation.details: README, in Q and A form

name: addliga
caption: Access basic ligatures in legacy TrueType fonts

descriptions.text: This small and simple package allows LuaLaTeX users to access basic ligatures (ff, fi, ffi, fl, ffl) in legacy TrueType fonts (those lacking a liga table) accessed via fontspec.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: addlines
caption: A user-friendly wrapper around \enlargethispage

descriptions.text:
This small package provides the command \addlines for adding or removing space in the textblock of the page it’s used on. E.g., adding an extra line of text to the page so that a section fits better on the next page.

It will also add space to the facing page in a two-sided document.

name: address
caption: Generate form letters and address labels

descriptions.text: Model files and file preambles for producing form letters, envelopes and envelope labels (in 3-across layout), using LaTeX 2.09.

name: AddTeX2Eps
caption: Use LaTeX syntax on EPS figures, within Mathematica

descriptions.text: This Mathematica script permits the user to write psfrag commands at the same place as the fragments for replacement are defined.

name: addtoluatexpath
caption: Add paths to Lua packages and input TeX files

descriptions.text: This package provides a convenient way to add input and Lua package paths in your document. You may want this package, for example, if a .cls or .sty file is located on a network or cloud storage drive.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: adfathesis
caption: Australian Defence Force Academy thesis format

descriptions.text: The bundle includes a BibTeX style file.

name: adforn
caption: OrnementsADF font with TeX/LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides the Ornements ADF font in PostScript type 1 format with TeX/LaTeX support files.

The font is licensed under GPL v2 or later with font exception. (See NOTICE, COPYING, README.)

The TeX/LaTeX support is licensed under LPPL. (See README, manifest.txt.)

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: adfsymbols
caption: SymbolsADF with TeX/LaTeX support

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text: The package provides Arkandis foundry’s ArrowsADF and BulletsADF fonts in Adobe Type 1 format, together with TeX/LaTeX support files.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: adhocfilelist
caption: <q>\listfiles</q> entries from the command line

descriptions.text:
The package provides a Unix shell script to display a list of LaTeX \Provides...-command contexts on screen. Provision is made for controlling the searches that the package does.

The package was developed on a Unix-like system, using (among other things) the gnu variant of the find command.

name: adigraph
caption: Augmenting directed graphs

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides the means to easily draw augmenting oriented graphs, as well as cuts on them, to demonstrate steps of algorithms for solving max-flow min-cut problems.

This package requires the other LaTeX packages fp, xparse, xstring, and TikZ (in particular the TikZ calc library).

name: adjmulticol
caption: Adjusting margins for multicolumn and single column output

descriptions.text: The package adds, to the multicol package, the option to change the margins for multicolumn and unicolumn layout. The package understands the difference between the even and odd margins for two side printing.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page
more than one column on the page

name: adjustbox
caption: Graphics package-alike macros for <q>general</q> boxes

descriptions.text:
The package provides several macros to adjust boxed content. One purpose is to supplement the standard graphics package, which defines the macros \resizebox, \scalebox and \rotatebox , with the macros\trimbox and \clipbox. The main feature is the general \adjustbox macro which extends the key=value interface of \includegraphics from the graphics package and applies it to general text content. Additional provided box macros are \lapbox, \marginbox, \minsizebox, \maxsizebox and \phantombox.

All macros use the collectbox package to read the content as a box and not as a macro argument. This allows for all forms of content including special material like verbatim content. A special feature of collectbox is used to provide matching environments with the identical names as the macros.

topics.details: breaking boxes over a page boundary, etc
support for variations of typographic style

name: adobe-euro
caption: Metric and map files for the Adobe Euro fonts

descriptions.text:
Provides maps and metrics for using Adobe’s Euro fonts. The fonts themselves are only available from Adobe (though the fonts are free of charge, the licence conditions prevent CTAN from distributing them).

Note that most text fonts now provide an appropriate glyph for the euro, so that this font is somewhat of a specialist interest.

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: adobecaslon
caption: Adobe Caslon font in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides support files for the Adobe Caslon font family. The font’s name, in the naming scheme specified in fontname, is pac.

The package does not provide the (commercial) fonts themselves.

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: adobemapping
caption: Adobe cmap and pdfmapping files

descriptions.text: The package comprises the collection of CMap and PDF mapping files made available for distribution by Adobe.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: adobeornaments
caption: Using ornaments in Adobe Fonts with LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides an easy way to use Adobe fonts’ ornaments in LaTeX. It requires LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX.

NOTE: The Adobe fonts are not included with the package and must be purchased separately.

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other support for miscellaneous fonts (not on CTAN)
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: adrconv
caption: BibTeX styles to implement an address database

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a collection of BibTeX style files to turn an address database stored in the .bib format into files suitable for printing as address books or included into letter classes like akletter or scrletter2. The data may be sorted either by name or birthday and output provides files in various formats for address books or time planners.

name: adrlist
caption: Using address lists in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides a read-file command (\ForEachAdress) and a set of commands for unpicking the address data in the file.

name: adtrees
caption: Macros for drawing adpositional trees

descriptions.text:
This package provides a means to write adpositional trees, a formalism devoted to representing natural language expressions.

The package relies on epic and cancel.

name: advdate
caption: Print a date relative to <q>today</q>

descriptions.text: Provides macros which can add a specified number of days to the current date (as specified in \today), to save, set and restore the current date and to print it. Intended use is, for example, in invoices payable within 14 days from today, etc. The package has only been tested with Czech dates.

name: Advice
caption: Extend commands and environments

descriptions.text:
Like its namesake from the Emacs world, this cross-format package implements a generic framework for extending the functionality of selected commands and environments.

It was developed as an auxiliary package of Memoize. This is why it is, somewhat unconventionally, documented alongside that package. This applies to both the manual and the documented code listing.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: ae
caption: Virtual fonts for T1 encoded CMR-fonts

descriptions.text:
A set of virtual fonts which emulates T1 coded fonts using the standard CM fonts. The package name, AE fonts, supposedly stands for Almost European. The main use of the package was to produce PDF files using Adobe Type 1 versions of the CM fonts instead of bitmapped EC fonts.

Note that direct substitutes for the bitmapped EC fonts are now available, via the CM-super, Latin Modern and (in a restricted way) CM-LGC font sets.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: aeb-minitoc
caption: Create mini-tocs

descriptions.text:
This package creates mini-TOCs through the use of the \insertminitoc command. The system is powerful and flexible and allows for some amount of logic.

The package works for the usual workflows.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: aeb-mlink
caption: Multi-line links with hyperref

descriptions.text:
This package defines new link commands to create multi-line links. The new commands are \mlhypertext, \mlhyperlink, \mlhyperref, \mlnameref, \mlNameref, \mlhref, and \mlurl. There is a mechanism for breaking links across pages as well.

PDF Creators: Adobe Distiller or ps2pdf.

This package requires the latest version of AeB; in particular, the eforms package required is dated 2018/03/22 or later, see acrotex.

topics.details: relies on availability of Adobe Acrobat, etc.
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: aeb-mobile
caption: Format PDF files for use on a smartphone

descriptions.text:
The package is a simple application of the web and eforms packages from the acrotex collection to format a PDF for a smartphone.

The design aim was to maximise the viewing and printing experience when the PDF is viewed on the desktop/laptop and in a smartphone.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: AeB Pro
caption: Items from the AeB Pro Family of Software

descriptions.text:
The AeB Pro bundle provides further functionality for the user of the AcroTeX eDucation Bundle. Except as noted in the documentation, the bundle is aimed at users of Acrobat Pro 7.0 or later and deals with using distiller to create PDF.

AeB Pro itself implements a number of features:

  • AeB Central (this can be used by non-distiller users);
  • Complete support for set up the initial view of the document;
  • Extensive support for document actions: document level JS, set document actions (willSave, didSave, etc.) and open document actions;
  • Complete support for page actions;
  • Complete support for full screen mode, and all the
  • current transition effects through version 8;
  • Methods to easily attach documents;
  • document assembly methods, methods used immediately following distillation;
  • Methods for linking to attachments and launching attachments;
  • Support for creating PDF Packages;
  • Initializing fields using unicode; and
  • Basic support for layers, rollovers and animations.

The bundle also contains Robot Man , a less than totally serious demo application.

topics.details: relies on availability of Adobe Acrobat, etc.
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: aeb-tilebg
caption: AeB Tiling Backgrounds

descriptions.text:
The package takes a rectangular graphic and uses it to tile the background of pages.

The package is distributed as part of the AeB Pro bundle.

topics.details: decorate/confuse text by adding a background

name: aeb_dad
caption: A drag-and-drop matching game with PDF files

descriptions.text: The package is used to create a DAD (Drag and Drop) Matching Game that uses stamps and push buttons. DAD Matching works in any version of Acrobat, and in Adobe Reader XI; it can use the stamps created by the mkstmp_pro.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: aebenvelope
caption: The AeB Pro eEnvelope System

descriptions.text: The package uses the concept of an eEnvelope to direct the user’s attention to attached files. The system may use any one of four provided eEnvelope templates, or can use a custom designed template. The AeB Pro package is required to attach documents to the eEnvelope. AeB Pro, and hence also eEnvelope, requires Acrobat Pro, version 7.0 or later, and requires the document author to create PDF using distiller.

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: AeB slicing
caption: An image slicer

descriptions.text:
The package provides a batch sequence for Acrobat, used by other packages in the aeb_pro bundle.

The sequence takes the current open image and slices it into a specified number of rows and columns, saving the results.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

name: aebXMP
caption: Add advanced metadata to PDF files

descriptions.text:
The package fills in advanced metadata (more than is possible with hyperref), using the E4X xml parser in Acrobat Professional 8.

The package is part of the AeB Pro bundle of packages.

topics.details: relies on availability of Adobe Acrobat, etc.

name: aecc
caption: Almost European Concrete Roman virtual fonts

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of virtual fonts (built from the standard Concrete fonts) providing a set of fonts that almost cover the T1 encoding.

The main characters missing, of those specified in the T1 specification are eth, thorn, and the Sami letter eng. Sometimes the £ (pound sterling) character is also missing. For the typewriter fonts, the situation is worse.

According to the author, the purpose of this package is nowadays better served by a combination of the MLTeX and ccfonts packages.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: aeguill
caption: Add several kinds of guillemets to the ae fonts

descriptions.text: The package enables the user to add guillemets from several source (Polish cmr, Cyrillic cmr, lasy and ec) to the ae fonts. This was useful when the ae fonts were used to produce PDF files, since the additional guillemets exist in fonts available in Adobe Type 1 format.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: aeskwadraat
caption: A–Eskwadraat package catalogue

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This is the official package catalogue of the A–Eskwadraat association.

A–Eskwadraat is the study association for mathematics and physics at Utrecht University.

The catalogue includes packages for meeting notes, a beamer theme, invoices and letters.

The beamer theme can also be used for Utrecht University-styled presentations. Do refer to the UU website for information on logo use.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: aesupp
caption: Special support for the æ character

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This package provides special support for the italic æ character in some fonts, due to design flaws (in the author’s opinion) regarding this character.

At the moment only the fonts TeX Gyre Bonum, TeX Gyre Schola, TeX Gyre Pagella, and the Latin Modern fonts are supported. The other fonts in the TeX Gyre bundle do not need this support.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts with specific small application areas

name: affilauthor
caption: Tag author and affiliation information in a key-value style

descriptions.text: This package provides key-value style author and affiliation information tagging in a structured format. Each field has a specific name similar to the bib format. We can customize the styles as per preferences for article.cls class layout. Instead of giving all the information (author and affiliation) in a single tag, we can split the information in a format of key-value style.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: AFMtoPL (Clark)
caption: Convert AFM files to PLs for use with dvitops

descriptions.text: A converter that does not (as a modern application would) provide for use of virtual fonts. The conversion is tailored to work with the author's dvitops.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: AFMtoPL (Elwell)
caption: An early converter from AFM to PL

descriptions.text: Probably only of historical interest; it predates Knuth's introduction of virtual fonts.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: AFMtopl (Wolczko)
caption: Unix utilities for translating AFM files to PL

descriptions.text: The conversion is done using an awk script, and a few Bourne shell scripts are provided for running the scripts for various synthetic outputs (such as faked small-caps). The mechanism cannot generate virtual fonts.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: afparticle
caption: Typesetting articles for Archives of Forensic Psychology

descriptions.text: This package provides a class for typesetting articles for the open access journal Archives of Forensic Psychology.

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: afperpack
caption: A parametric questions’ repositories framework

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This is a personal pre-configuration package which (selectively) loads package sets with package options pre-defined by the author.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: afterpackage
caption: Add commands to package after it’s loaded

descriptions.text:
The package allows you to specify (using the command \AfterPackage{<package name>}{<commands>}) commands that are to be executed immediately after a package is loaded. Such commands would set up defaults, define which options to use, etc.

The package is part of the ncctools bundle.

name: afterpage
caption: Execute command after the next page break

descriptions.text:
Implements a command that causes the commands specified in its argument to be expanded after the current page is output. For example, LaTeX's float positioning mechanism sometimes gets overloaded and all floating figures and table drift to the end of the document. One may flush out all the unprocessed floats by issuing a \clearpage command, but this has the effect of making the current page end prematurely. Now you can issue \afterpage{\clearpage} and the current page will be filled up with text as usual, but then the \clearpage command will flush out all the floats before the next text page begins.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: afthesis
caption: Air Force Institute of Technology thesis class

descriptions.text: LaTeX thesis/dissertation class for US Air Force Institute Of Technology.

name: aguplus
caption: Styles for American Geophysical Union

descriptions.text: This bundle started as an extension to the AGU’s own published styles, providing extra facilities and improved usability. The AGU now publishes satisfactory LaTeX materials of its own; the author of aguplus recommends that users switch to using the official distribution.

name: aiaa
caption: Typeset AIAA conference papers

descriptions.text: A bundle of LaTeX/BibTeX files and sample documents to aid those producing papers and journal articles according to the guidelines of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA).

name: aichej
caption: Bibliography style file for the AIChE Journal

descriptions.text: The style was generated using custom-bib, and implements the style of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers Journal (or AIChE Journal or AIChE J or AIChEJ).

name: aidisclose
caption: Generate disclosure statements and checklists for the use of generative AI

descriptions.text:
This package provides a standardized, transparent way to declare the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in academic, technical, and professional documents. It implements an extension of the GAIDeT (Generative AI Delegation Taxonomy), letting authors mark which tasks were delegated to AI, list the tools used (or state that none were), add optional numbered or unnumbered comments, and automatically typeset a formatted disclosure section or chapter with a task-based checklist.

Configuration uses a key-value interface, and citations for the taxonomy and the package can be managed automatically. The package detects the document language through babel or polyglossia and ships translations for fourteen languages, falling back to English. A companion web generator/configurator is available at https://aidisclose.org.

name: aifont
caption: Remap Computer Modern fonts

descriptions.text:
Virtual fonts and other related files for remapping the BSR/Y&Y/AMS Type 1 Computer Modern fonts; the remapping creates fonts which have no characters in the numeric range 0–31 (mod 128), and the virtual fonts map Knuth’s original encodings to the remapped fonts.

These mechanisms aid the production of robust PDF output from TeX-related systems, when they use CM fonts.

The original impetus for developing this bundle came from problems with Adobe Illustrator (hence the first two letters of the bundle name). Current versions of Adobe Illustrator can apparently use the CM fonts without remapping, so the bundle is not needed for such use.

name: aiplans
caption: A TikZ-based library for drawing POCL plans

descriptions.text: This TikZ library is designed for generating diagrams related to Automated Planning, a subdiscipline of Artificial Intelligence. It allows users to define a domain model for actions, similar to PDDL and HDDL used in hierarchical planning. The package is useful for researchers and students to create diagrams that represent sequential action sequences or partially ordered plans, including causal links and ordering constraints (e.g., POCL plans). It is particularly suited for presentations and scientific publications.

topics.details: finite-state machines, automata, labelled graphs, etc.

name: ajl
caption: BibTeX style for AJL

descriptions.text: Bibliographic style references in style of Australian Journal of Linguistics.

name: AkkTeX
caption: A collection of packages and classes

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides:

  • new document classes for technical documents, thesis works, manuscripts and lecture notes;
  • many mathematical packages providing a large number of macros for mathematical texts;
  • layout providing a non-empty parskip with extended length corrections and new section definition commands;
  • easy label creation for counters; and
  • german language tools and predefined abbreviations.

name: akletter
caption: Comprehensive letter support

descriptions.text:
An advanced letter document class which extends LaTeX's usual letter class, providing support for building your own letterhead and marking fold points for window envelopes. Options supported by the package include: letterpaper for US letter; a4offset for a modified A4 layout suitable for platic binders that cover a part of the left margin.

The class’s handling of dates has inspired an extended version of date-handling in the isodate package.

The class supersedes an earlier class called myletter.

name: akshar
caption: Support for syllables in the Devanagari script

descriptions.text: This LaTeX3 package provides macros and interfaces to work with Devanagari characters and syllables in a more correct way.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: alatex
caption: Abstract LaTeX

descriptions.text: ALaTeX provides the user with all the functionality of LaTeX but with one small change: a general, legal way to override standard LaTeX behavior without altering source files. ALaTeX can interpret official LaTeX markup in an abstract way.

name: albatross
caption: Find fonts that contain a given glyph

descriptions.text: This is a command line tool for finding fonts that contain a given (Unicode) glyph. It relies on Fontconfig.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: alchemist
caption: Typeset alchemist and astrological symbols

descriptions.text: This style file makes the alchemical and astrological symbols accessible in Unicode.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: alegreya
caption: Alegreya fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: The Alegreya fonts are designed by Juan Pablo del Peral for Huerta Tipográfica. Alegreya is a typeface originally intended for literature. It conveys a dynamic and varied rhythm which facilitates the reading of long texts. The italic has just as much care and attention to detail in the design as the roman. Bold, black, small caps and five number styles are available.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: aleph
caption: Extended TeX

descriptions.text: An development of omega, using most of the extensions of TeX itself developed for e-TeX.

topics.details: Omega and packages that use it

name: alertmessage
caption: Alert messages for LaTeX

descriptions.text: Some macros to display alert messages (informational, error, warning and success messages).

name: AlfaSlabOne
caption: The Alfa Slab One font face with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX

copyright.owner: The Alfa Slab One Project Authors

descriptions.text:
The alfaslabone package supports the Alfa Slab One font face for LaTeX.

There is only a Regular font face. It’s useful for book-chapter headlines.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: alg
caption: LaTeX environments for typesetting algorithms

descriptions.text: Defines two environments for typesetting algorithms in LaTeX2e. The algtab environment is used to typeset an algorithm with automatically numbered lines. The algorithm environment can be used to encapsulate the algtab environment algorithm in a floating body together with a header, a caption, etc. \listofalgorithms is defined.

name: algobox
caption: Typeset Algobox programs

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package can typeset Algobox programs almost exactly as displayed when editing with Algobox itself, using an input syntax very similar to the actual Algobox program text.

It gives better results than Algobox’s own LaTeX export which does not look like the editor rendition, produces standalone documents cumbersome to customize, and has arbitrary and inconsistent differences between the input syntax and the program text.

This package depends upon the following other LaTeX packages: expl3, TikZ, environ, xparse, and xcolor.

name: algolrevived
caption: A revival of Frutiger’s Algol alphabet

descriptions.text:
The package revives Frutiger's Algol alphabet, designed in 1963 for the code segments in an ALGOL manual. OpenType and type1, regular and medium weights, upright and slanted.

Not monospaced, but good for listings if you don't need code to be aligned with specific columns. It also makes a passable but limited text font.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: algorithm2e
caption: Floating algorithm environment with algorithmic keywords

descriptions.text: Algorithm2e is an environment for writing algorithms. An algorithm becomes a floating object (like figure, table, etc.). The package provides macros that allow you to create different keywords, and a set of predefined key words is provided; you can change the typography of the keywords. The package allows vertical lines delimiting a block of instructions in an algorithm, and defines different sorts of algorithms such as Procedure or Function; the name of these functions may be reused in the text or in other algorithms.

name: algorithmicx
caption: The algorithmic style you always wanted

descriptions.text: Algorithmicx provides a flexible, yet easy to use, way for inserting good looking pseudocode or source code in your papers. It has built in support for Pseudocode, Pascal and C, and offers powerful means to create definitions for any programming language. The user can adapt a Pseudocode style to his native language.

name: algorithms
caption: A suite of tools for typesetting algorithms in pseudo-code

descriptions.text: Consists of two environments: algorithm and algorithmic. The algorithm package defines a floating algorithm environment designed to work with the algorithmic style. Within an algorithmic environment a number of commands for typesetting popular algorithmic constructs are available.

name: algpseudocodex
caption: Package for typesetting pseudocode

descriptions.text:
This package allows typesetting pseudocode in LaTeX. It is based on algpseudocode from the algorithmicx package and uses the same syntax, but adds several new features and improvements.

Notable features include customizable indent guide lines and the ability to draw boxes around parts of the code for highlighting differences.

This package also has better support for long code lines spanning several lines and improved comments.

name: algxpar
caption: Support multiple lines of pseudocode

descriptions.text: This package extends the package algorithmicx to support long text which spans over multiple lines.

name: aliascnt
caption: Alias counters

descriptions.text: This package introduces aliases for counters that share the same counter register and clear list.

name: aligned-overset
caption: Fix alignment at \overset or \underset

descriptions.text: This package allows the base character of \underset or \overset to be used as the alignment position for the amsmath aligned math environments.

name: alkalami
caption: A font for Arabic-based writing systems in Nigeria and Niger

descriptions.text: This font is designed for Arabic-based writing systems in the Kano region of Nigeria and Niger.

name: alleqno
caption: Automatic numbering of all equations

descriptions.text: Redefines \[ ... \] to behave as a equation environment, and defines \[[ ... \]] to behave as an eqnarray environment.

name: allrunes
caption: Fonts and LaTeX package for almost all runes

descriptions.text: This large collection of fonts (in Adobe Type 1 format), with the LaTeX package gives access to almost all runes ever used in Europe. The bundle covers not only the main forms but also a lot of varieties.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: alltt
caption: Everything in tt font, but obey commands and line endings

descriptions.text:
The alltt package defines the alltt environment which is like the verbatim environment except that \ and braces have their usual meanings. Thus, other commands and environments can appear within an alltt environment.

The package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: alltt2
caption: Indented version of alltt

descriptions.text:
A version of alltt (an old version from LaTeX 2.09, now obsolete), patched to apply a left margin (of the user’s choice) to the verbatim text.

A similar patch could be created for current alltt, but it seems that no-one has felt the need.

name: almendra
caption: Almendra fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and LuaLaTeX support for the Almendra family of fonts, designed by Ana Sanfelippo. Almendra is a typeface design based on calligraphy. Its style is related to the chancery and gothic hands. There are regular and bold weights with matching italics. There is also a regular-weight small-caps.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: almfixed
caption: Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed extends TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular to full Arabic Unicode support

descriptions.text:
Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed is an extension of TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular. Every glyph and OpenType feature of the Latin Modern Mono has been retained, with minor improvements. On the other hand, we have changed the vertical metrics of the font. Although the Arabic script is designed to use the same x-size as Latin Modern Mono, the former script needs greater ascender and descender space.

Every Arabic glyph in each Unicode-code block is supported (up to Unicode 7.0): Arabic, Arabic Supplement, Arabic Extended, Arabic Presentation-Forms A, and Arabic Presentation-Forms B.

There are two versions of the font: otf and ttf. The ?penType version is for print applications (and usually the default for TeX). The TrueType version is for on-screen applications such as text editors. Hinting in the ttf version is much better for on-screen, at least on Microsoft Windows.

The unique feature of Arabic-Latin Modern is its treatment of vowels and diacritics. Each vowel and diacritic (ALM Fixed contains a total of 68 such glyphs) may now be edited horizontally within any text editor or processor. The author believes this is the very first OpenType Arabic font ever to have this capability. Editing complex Arabic texts will now be much easier to input and to proofread.

name: alnumsec
caption: Alphanumeric section numbering

descriptions.text: This package allows you to use alphanumeric section numbering, for instance A. Introduction … III. International Law. Its output is similar to alphanum, but you can use the standard LaTeX sectioning commands, so that it is possible to switch numbering schemes easily. Greek letters, double letters (bb) and different delimiters around them are supported.

name: alpha
caption: Editor for the Macintosh with good TeX support

descriptions.text: Alpha is a powerful, scriptable and extensible editor, which is well configured to interact with other Mac applications, including most TeX implementations.

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

name: alpha-persian
caption: Persian version of alpha.bst

descriptions.text: The package provides a Persian version of the alpha BibTeX style and offers several enhancements. It is compatible with the hyperref, url, natbib, and cite packages.

name: alphabib
caption: Add alphabetical headers into citations

descriptions.text: AlphaBib is a bash script that adds alphabetical headers into BibTeX bibliographies; such headers can assist searching in a large list of citations. AlphaBib takes a bibliography produced by BibTeX (the .bbl file), and creates a new file with the alphabetic headers inserted.

name: alphalph
caption: Convert numbers to letters

descriptions.text: Provides commands \alphalph and \AlphAlph. They are like \number but the expansion consists of lowercase and uppercase letters respectively (1 to a, 26 to z, 27 to aa, 52 to zz, 53 to ba, 702 to zz, 703 to aaa, etc.). Can be used as a replacement for LaTeX's \@alph and \@Alph macros.

name: alphanum
caption: Sectioning commands for jura

descriptions.text:
The package defines the sectioning commands for jura.cls, but can also be used independently. It defines 12 levels of section numbering; the default numbering is shown on page 4 of the documentation. The package uses the same command for all levels of sectioning: \toc{Title}, and you switch between levels with the commands \sub and \levelup.

The package is part of the jura distribution.

name: alphanum-bst
caption: Modified alpha BibTeX style

descriptions.text:
Modified from alpha.bst in the BibTeX distribution; differences are:

  • Labels do not contain the year;
  • Otherwise identical labels are distinguished by a number, rather than a letter, and
  • Entries are sorted by month as well as year.

name: alphanumb
caption: A modification of alpha.bst

descriptions.text:
This style is characterised by:

  • Labels do not contain the year;
  • Labels which would otherwise be identical have a number appended, not a letter; and
  • Entries are sorted by month as well as by year.

name: alterqcm
caption: Multiple choice questionnaires in two column tables

copyright.owner: Alain Matthes, Apostolos Syropoulos, and Anastasios Dimou

descriptions.text: The alterqcm package is a LaTeX2e package, for making multiple choices questionnaires in a table with two columns. The aim is to provide some useful macros to build QCM in tables. These macros may be used by only LaTeX TeX users. The package works with utf8, pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX (with some languages). The documentation is in English.

name: altfont
caption: Alternative font handling in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides a replacement for that part of psnfss and mfnfss that changes the default font.

The package is distributed together with the psfont package, by the same author.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: altnline
caption: Line numbering in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text: Line numbering in LaTeX. Note that the code here works with the LaTeX 2.09 output routine, and cannot therefore be used with current LaTeX – its replacement was numline, but that has itself been declared obsolete, in favour of lineno.

documentation.details: Article about techniques, which inspired the package

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: altsubsup
caption: Subscripts and superscripts with square brackets

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package to write alternative and customisable subscripts and superscripts, with square brackets in the source code.

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

name: altverse
caption: Typesetting verse

descriptions.text:
Straightforward typesetting, using the xtab package to aid layout.

The package is part of the shipunov bundle.

name: ama
caption: AMA manual of style citations

descriptions.text: The style covers JAMA, Cancer, and many others. It provides up to 6 authors, or 3 et.al.; titles are in italics, labels are numeric, and sorting is by order of reference.

name: ametsoc
caption: Official American Meteorological Society LaTeX template

descriptions.text: This bundle contains all the files necessary to write an article using LaTeX for the American Meteorological Society journals. The article and bibliography style files are provided (with documentation) and a blank template for authors to use when writing their article. Also available is a separate style package used to format a two-column, journal page layout draft for the author’s personal use.

name: amiri
caption: A classical Arabic typeface, Naskh style

descriptions.text:
Amiri is a classical Arabic typeface in Naskh style for typesetting books and other running text.

It is a revival of the beautiful typeface pioneered in the early 20th century by Bulaq Press in Cairo, also known as Amiria Press, after which the font is named.

The project aims at the revival of the aesthetics and traditions of Arabic typesetting, and adapting it to the era of digital typesetting, in a publicly available form.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Arabic

name: amiweb2c
caption: An Amiga port of web2C

descriptions.text:
A port of the web2C system that forms the basis of most Unix-TeX implementations, together with the rest of a usable system.

The system is based on web2C v7.2, including e-TeX v2.0 and PDFTeX v0.12.

documentation.details: Outline of patches for TeX Live edition 3

name: amiweb2c-guide
caption: How to install AmiWeb2c

descriptions.text:
This is a guide for the installation of (La)TeX with the Amiga port of Web2C named AmiWeb2C in the version 2.1 on an emulated Amiga 4000 computer running Workbench 3.1.

Furthermore the installation of an ARexx server for calling LaTeX from an editor is described and some tips for the installation of new fonts are given.

name: amnestyreport
caption: A LaTeX class for Amnesty International

descriptions.text: This package provides a class for Amnesty International reports according to guidelines at https://brandhub.amnesty.org/.

name: ams-cd
caption: AMSTeX Commutative Diagrams for LaTeX

descriptions.text: A version of the CD macros for AMSTeX, for use with LaTeX.

name: ams2bib
caption: Convert AMS-TeX style bibliography entries to BibTeX

descriptions.text: Ams2bib is a simple Perl script that takes an AMS-TeX file as input and creates a BibTeX database as output.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: amsaddr
caption: Alter the position of affiliations in amsart

descriptions.text: The package is to be used with the amsart documentclass. It lets you move the authors’ affiliations either just below the authors’ names on the front page or as footnotes on the first page. The email addresses are always listed as a footnote on the front page.

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: amsart
caption: LaTeX document class for AMS math journal articles

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX document class for articles that is tailored to the design of American Mathematical Society journals. If you have a standard installation of LaTeX, you should find that amsart is already present, since it is part of the (required) AMS-LaTeX distribution.

For publication-specific AMS document classes (jams-l.cls, bull-l.cls, tran-l.cls, proc-l.cls, mcom-l.cls, etc.), see the AMS author information.

documentation.details: Code documentation of all three classes

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: amsbook
caption: LaTeX document class for AMS books

descriptions.text: A LaTeX document class for books that is tailored to the design of American Mathematical Society publications. If you have a standard installation of LaTeX, you should find that amsbook is already present, since it is part of the (required) AMS-LaTeX distribution. For publication-specific AMS document classes (surv-l.cls, memo-l.cls, mmono-l.cls, gsm-l.cls, stml-l.cls, etc.), see the AMS author information.

documentation.details: Code of the classes, with documentation

name: amsbsy
caption: Produce bold math symbols (AMS-LaTeX)

copyright.owner: LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command for producing bold mathematics symbols where appropriate fonts exist, and a poor mans bold’ command that can be applied when no appropriate bold font is available. The facility is available through the macro \boldsymbol.

The package is part of the AMS-LaTeX distribution.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: amscd
caption: AMS-LaTeX commutative diagrams

copyright.owner: LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text: Part of the AMS-LaTeX distribution, this package adapts the commutative diagram macros of AMS-TeX for use in LaTeX.

name: amscdx
caption: Enhanced commutative diagrams

copyright.owner: LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text:
The original amscd package provides a CD environment that emulates the commutative diagram capabilities of AMS-TeX version 2.x. This means that only simple rectangular diagrams are supported, with no diagonal arrows or more exotic features.

This enhancement package implements double (fat), dashed, and bidirectional arrows (left-right and up-down), and color attributes for arrows and their annotations. The restriction to rectangular geometry remains. This nevertheless allows the drawing of a much broader class of commutative-diagram-like diagrams.

This update, 2.2x of 2019-07-02, fixes the dashed-arrows parts placement bug, and adds the package option lyx, for use with lyx to prevent conflict with the already loaded amscd. The packages xcolor and graphicx are made required.

name: amscls
caption: AMS document classes for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains three AMS classes, amsart (for writing articles for the AMS), amsbook (for books) and amsproc (for proceedings), together with some supporting material.

This material forms one branch of what was originally the AMS-LaTeX distribution. The other branch, amsmath, is now maintained and distributed separately.

The user documentation can be found in the package amscls-doc.

name: amscls-doc
caption: User documentation for AMS document classes

descriptions.text:
This collection comprises a set of four manuals, or Author Handbooks, each documenting the use of a class of publications based on one of the AMS document classes amsart, amsbook, amsproc and one hybrid, as well as a guide to the generation of the four manuals from a coordinated set of LaTeX source files. The Handbooks comprise the user documentation for the pertinent document classes.

As the source for the Handbooks consists of a large number of files, and the intended output is multiple different documents, the principles underlying this collection can be used as a model for similar projects. The manual Compiling the AMS Author Handbooks provides information about the structure of and interaction between the various components.

documentation.details: AMS Author Handbook for the Memoirs Class
AMS Author Handbook for Monograph Classes
AMS Author Handbook for Proceedings and Collections Classes
AMS Author Handbook for Journal Classes

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

name: amsfonts
caption: TeX fonts from the American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text:
An extended set of fonts for use in mathematics, including: extra mathematical symbols; blackboard bold letters (uppercase only); fraktur letters; subscript sizes of bold math italic and bold Greek letters; subscript sizes of large symbols such as sum and product; added sizes of the Computer Modern small caps font; cyrillic fonts (from the University of Washington); Euler mathematical fonts. All fonts are provided as Adobe Type 1 files, and all except the Euler fonts are provided as Metafont source.

The distribution also includes the canonical Type 1 versions of the Computer Modern family of fonts.

Basic LaTeX support for the symbol fonts is provided by amsfonts.sty, with names of individual symbols defined in amssymb.sty. The Euler fonts are supported by separate packages; details can be found in the documentation.

documentation.details: Details of the fonts msam and msbm
Users’ guide to the fonts (for version 2.2d)

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: amslatex
caption: Mathematical enhancements for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A collection of loosely related files originally commissioned by the American Mathematical Society; the bundle consists of two groups,

  • latex-amsmath, which provides miscellaneous enhancements to LaTeX to improve the appearance and information structure of mathematical documents, and
  • amscls, which offers document classes designed for preparing articles and books for publication by the American Mathematical Society (though they are often used in other contexts).

name: amslatex-primer
caption: Getting up and running with AMS-LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The document aims to get you up and running with AMS-LaTeX as quickly as possible. These instructions (along with a template file template.tex) are not a substitute for the full documentation, but they may get you started quickly enough so that you will only need to refer to the main documentation occasionally.

In addition to AMS-LaTeX out of the box, the document contains:

  • a section describing how to draw commutative diagrams using Xy-pic; and
  • a section describing how to use amsrefs to create a bibliography.

name: amslatexdoc-vietnamese
caption: Vietnamese translation of AMSLaTeX documentation

descriptions.text: This is a Vietnamese translation of amsldoc, the users’ guide to amsmath.

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language

name: amsltx11
caption: AMS-LaTeX, original version (obsolete)

descriptions.text:
Obsolete original version of AMS-LaTeX for version 2.09 of LaTeX.

The package is retained as a ZIP archive, only.

name: amsmath
caption: AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX

copyright.owner: LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text:
The principal package in the AMS-LaTeX distribution. It adapts for use in LaTeX most of the mathematical features found in AMS-TeX; it is highly recommended as an adjunct to serious mathematical typesetting in LaTeX.

When amsmath is loaded, AMS-LaTeX packages amsbsy (for bold symbols), amsopn (for operator names) and amstext (for text embedded in mathematics) are also loaded.

amsmath is part of the LaTeX required distribution; however, several contributed packages add still further to its appeal; examples are empheq, which provides functions for decorating and highlighting mathematics, and ntheorem, for specifying theorem (and similar) definitions.

name: amsmath-it
caption: Italian translations of some old amsmath documents

descriptions.text: The documents are: diffs-m.txt of December 1999, and amsmath.faq of March 2000.

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language

name: amsmidx
caption: Support for multiple indexes in AMS Classes

descriptions.text:
The package supports the creation and typesetting of multiple of multiple indexes with AMS Classes; it supersedes the single-index mechanisms provided within those classes. The package also provides a means of inserting a paragraph of text between the title and the index proper.

The package is based on multind package; it is distributed as part of the AMS Classes bundle.

name: amsopn
caption: Typeset mathematical operator names

copyright.owner: LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society

descriptions.text: Part of the AMS-LaTeX distribution, this package defines a command \DeclareMathOperator that may be used to define commands like the LaTeX built-in commands \log and \lim; the command \operatorname allows ad-hoc operator names in the body of a document.

name: amspell
caption: ASCII and LaTeX spell checker

descriptions.text: Amspell is a spell checker for plain ASCII files, with some special features for dealing with TeX files. The program is written in Turbo Pascal and runs on any MS-DOS computer.

name: amsppt
caption: AMS-TeX article preprint document style

name: amsppt1
caption: AMS-TeX v.2 compatibility for amsppt.sty v.1

descriptions.text: AMS-TeX conversion file to provide compatibility between amsppt.sty version 1 and amsppt.sty version 2.

name: amsproc
caption: LaTeX document class for AMS conference proceedings

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX document class for conference proceedings that is tailored to the design of American Mathematical Society publications. If you have a standard installation of LaTeX, you should find that amsproc is already present, since it is part of the (required) AMS-LaTeX distribution.

For publication-specific AMS document classes (coll-l.cls, conm-p-l.cls, lam-l.cls, llsci-l.cls, psam-l.cls, pspum-l.cls, etc.), see AMS author information.

documentation.details: Code and documentation of all three classes

name: amsrefs
caption: A LaTeX-based replacement for BibTeX
