descriptions.text: Using the \AtBeginPage hook, you can add material in the background of a page. \PageLayout can be used to give page makeup commands to be executed on every page (e.g., depending on the page style).

name: borceux
caption: Diagram macros by François Borceux

descriptions.text: The macros support the construction of diagrams, such as those that appear in category theory texts. The user gives the list of vertices and arrows to be included, just as when composing a matrix, and the program takes care of computing the dimensions of the arrows and realizing the pagesetting. All the user has to do about the arrows is to specify their type (monomorphism, pair of adjoint arrows, etc.) and their direction (north, south-east, etc.); 12 types and 32 directions are available.

name: border
caption: Draw a black border around a Plain TeX page

descriptions.text: The border is drawn (as it were) on top of the page; since the border doesn't honour the \hoffset/\voffset positioning of the text, this is less of a problem than it might be.

name: bosisio
caption: A collection of packages by Francesco Bosisio

descriptions.text: A collection of packages containing: accenti dblfont; envmath; evenpage; graphfig; mathcmd; quotes; and sobolev.

name: boustrophedon
caption: A LaTeX package for boustrophedon typography

descriptions.text:
This package typesets text in boustrophedon style, alternating the writing direction on each line.

Have you ever wondered why most Western languages are written left-to-right, while many Middle Eastern languages are written right-to-left? Both conventions may seem arbitrary today – but this was not always the case. In one of the earliest fully developed alphabets, the Archaic Greek alphabet (from alpha and beta, hence alphabet ), writing was often performed boustrophedon, meaning as the ox turns in ploughing. Text was written left-to-right on one line, then right-to-left on the next, with both the direction of the text and the letterforms themselves mirrored accordingly.

This method creates a continuous flow of reading, as the reader does not need to jump back to the start of each new line, but instead follows the text in a natural back-and-forth motion. Reading takes some getting used to, but after a while it becomes surprisingly natural.

name: boxedart4mac
caption: Import graphics into Macintosh TeX

descriptions.text: The package is an (accelerated) alternative to the author’s boxedeps package, for the ozTeX and Textures distributions only.

name: boxedeps
caption: Incorporate EPS files into TeX documents

descriptions.text: A package to enable the user to treat Encapsulate PostScript figures as TeX boxes. The package is configurable to a variety of DVI drivers.

name: boxedminipage
caption: Framed minipages of a specified total width (text and frame combined)

descriptions.text:
The package essentially just wraps a minipage within an \fbox. However, while \fbox{\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}...\end{minipage}} juts out into the margin, \begin{boxedminipage}...\end{boxedminipage} does not. Instead, it subtracts the frame’s dimensions from the specified dimensions of the minipage before typesetting the minipage.

Note: The package was formerly known as boxedminipage2e and now replaces Mario Wolczko’s earlier boxedminipage package.

name: boxhandler
caption: Flexible Captioning and Deferred Box/List Printing

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to optimise presentation of LaTeX tables and figures. Boxhandler will lay out table and figure captions with a variety of stylistic appearances, and will also allow figures and tables to be wrapped in a manner consistent with many business and government documents.

For a document that might appear in different venues with different formatting, boxhandler permits the creation of a LaTeX source document that can, with a single-line change in the source code, produce an output that has very different layout from the baseline configuration, not only in terms of caption style, but more importantly in terms of the locations where figures, tables and lists appear (or not) in the document.

Deferral routines also allow one to keep all figure and table data in a separate source file, while nonetheless producing a document with figures and tables appearing in the desired location.

name: boxit
caption: Draw a box around a text

descriptions.text: This is pretty much the same macro that appears in the TeXbook.

name: boxit-ltx
caption: An environment for boxing things

descriptions.text: The package defines a boxit environment that draws lines around its contents. The environment can box things like verbatim text, unlike the \boxit macro that originally appeared in the TeXbook.

name: bpchem
caption: Typeset chemical names, formulae, etc

descriptions.text: The package provides support for typesetting simple chemical formulae, those long IUPAC compound names, and some chemical idioms. It also supports the labelling of compounds and reference to labelled compounds.

name: bpolynomial
caption: Drawing polynomial functions of up to order 3

descriptions.text: This MetaPost package helps plotting polynomial and root functions up to order three. The package provides macros to calculate Bézier curves exactly matching a given constant, linear, quadratic or cubic polynomial, or square or cubic root function. In addition, tangents on all functions and derivatives of polynomials can be calculated.

topics.details: plot a representation of a function

name: br-lex
caption: A Class for Typesetting Brazilian legal texts

descriptions.text: This class implements rules to typeset Brazilian legal texts. Its purpose is to be an easy-to-use implementation for the end-user.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: bracealign
caption: Align braces under and over math expressions

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package to align braces under and over math expressions. A new environment called bracealign is provided, inside which braces and brackets drawn with the commands \underbrace, \overbrace, \underbracket, \overbracket, \underparen or \overparenare vertically aligned. The package also allows adding support for new commands.

name: bracketkey
caption: Produce bracketed identification keys

descriptions.text: The package provides an environment bracketkey for use when producing lists of species.

name: braids
caption: Draw braid diagrams with PGF/TikZ

descriptions.text: The package enables drawing of braid diagrams with PGF/TikZ using a simple syntax. The braid itself is specified by giving a word in the braid group, and there are many options for styling the strands and for drawing floors.

name: braille
caption: Support for braille

descriptions.text: This package allows the user to produce Braille documents on paper for the blind without knowing Braille (which can take years to learn). Python scripts grade1.py and grade2.py convert ordinary text to grade 1 and 2 Braille tags; then, the LaTeX package takes the tags and prints out corresponding Braille symbols.

name: braket
caption: Dirac bra-ket and set notations

descriptions.text:
Provides macros to typeset bra-ket notation, as well as set specifiers, with a single ( | ) or a double ( || or ( \| ) vertical bar specifier in between two bracketed parts. Each macro comes in a fixed-size version and an expanding version.

If the package finds itself operating under e-tex, it uses the extended primitive \middle for more reliable results

name: brandeis-dissertation
caption: Class for Brandeis University dissertations

descriptions.text: The class will enable the user to typeset a dissertation which adheres to the formatting guidelines of Brandeis University Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GSAS).

name: brandeis-problemset
caption: Document class for COSI Problem sets at Brandeis University (Waltham, MA)

descriptions.text:
Brandeis University’s computer science (COSI) courses often assign problem sets which require fairly rigorous formatting. This document class, which extends article, provides a simple way to typeset these problem sets in LaTeX.

Although the class is compatible with all LaTeX flavors, XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX are recommended for fontspec support.

name: brandeis-thesis
caption: A class for Brandeis University M.A. theses

descriptions.text: brandeis-thesis.cls provides the structures and formatting information for an M.A. thesis for the Brandeis University Graduate School of Arts and Sciences.

name: brandstyler
caption: Automatic brand style implementation

descriptions.text: brandstyler automatically adapts the style of a LaTeX document to that of a specific organisation. It is also compatible with beamer, able to change the style of many beamerthemes. It currently supports the adaption of fonts and colours.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: brclc
caption: Support 16-bit (double) calculations in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides a preprocessor brclc (written in C; a DOS executable is available), and a package, which processes a LaTeX file that's been run through the preprocessor (the output of the preprocessor tells LaTeX how to process the \clc commands in the in the LaTeX file. The script testclc (available as a shell script or a DOS batch file) shows a typical processing run.

name: breakcites
caption: Ensure that multiple citations may break at line end

descriptions.text: Makes a very minor change to the operation of the \cite command. Note that the change is not necessary in unmodified LaTeX; however, there remain packages that restore the undesirable behaviour of the command as provided in LaTeX 2.09. (Note that neither cite nor natbib make this mistake.)

name: breakurl
caption: Line-breakable \url-like links in hyperref when compiling via dvips/ps2pdf

descriptions.text: This package provides a command much like hyperref’s \url that typesets a URL using a typewriter-like font. However, if the dvips driver is being used, the original \url doesn’t allow line breaks in the middle of the created link: the link comes in one atomic piece. This package allows such line breaks in the generated links.

name: bredzenie
caption: A Polish version of <q>lorem ipsum…</q> in the form of a LaTeX package

descriptions.text:
This is a polish version of the classic pseudo-Latin lorem ipsum dolor sit amet….

It provides access to several paragraphs of pseudo-Polish generated with Hidden Markov Models and Recurrent Neural Networks trained on a corpus of Polish.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: breqn
caption: Automatic line breaking of displayed equations

descriptions.text:
The package provides solutions to a number of common difficulties in writing displayed equations and getting high-quality output. For example, it is a well-known inconvenience that if an equation must be broken into more than one line, left...right constructs cannot span lines. The breqn package makes them work as one would expect whether or not there is an intervening line break.

The single most ambitious goal of the package, however, is to support automatic linebreaking of displayed equations. Such linebreaking cannot be done without substantial changes under the hood in the way formulae are processed; the code must be watched carefully, keeping an eye on possible glitches.

The bundle also contains the flexisym and mathstyle packages, which are both designated as support for breqn.

name: bridge
caption: Typesetting bridge diagrams

descriptions.text: The file contains an article that sets out macros for typesetting bridge in LaTeX (2.09).

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: bridge-pln
caption: Plain TeX macros for writing about bridge

descriptions.text: The macros come in three parts, declarations, macros supporting bidding and layout, and macros supporting commentary.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: brief-t
caption: LaTeX support for the brief editor

descriptions.text: The package comprises a set of brief macros to create key assignments for common (La)TeX functions.

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

name: bropd
caption: Simplified brackets and differentials in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package simplifies the process of writing differential operators and brackets in LaTeX. The commands facilitate the easy manipulation of equations involving brackets and allow partial differentials to be expressed in an alternate form.

name: broydensolve
caption: Solve a system of equations with Broyden’s good method

descriptions.text: This package implements Broyden’s good method to solve a system of equations. It is also possible to use coordinates defined by TikZ as known and unknown variables.

name: brushscr
caption: A handwriting script font

descriptions.text: The BrushScript font simulates hand-written characters; it is distributed in Adobe Type 1 format (but is available in italic shape only). The package includes the files needed by LaTeX in order to use that font. The file AAA_readme.tex fully describes the package and sample.tex illustrates its use.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: bsf
caption: Access bold computer modern sans in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
Provides LaTeX 2.09 (dynamic-loading) font tables for a font selection command \bsf, giving access to Computer Modern Sans Serif Bold fonts.

Note that these macros do not work with current LaTeX, but since the NFSS supports the fonts anyway, this is not a problem.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: bsheaders
caption: Double-ruled chapter heading style

descriptions.text: The style, inspired by those in a book by Bjarne Stroustrup, implements chapter headers in sans-serif and bounded by lines \textwidth wide, both above and below the header itself.

name: bsl
caption: Access bold computer modern slanted in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
Provides LaTeX 2.09 (dynamic-loading) font tables for a font selection command \bsl, giving access to Computer Modern Sans Serif Bold fonts.

Note that these macros do not work with current LaTeX, but since the NFSS supports the fonts anyway, this is not a problem.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: BSR2dvi
caption: Convert a TeXtures working file to DVI

descriptions.text:
Produces a portable DVI file (modulo \special commands) which may be used with any standard DVI processor.

The program apparently runs on MacOS 9 (or possibly earlier).

name: btable
caption: Bordered tables

descriptions.text: Provides a mechanism for tables with borders, in plain TeX.

documentation.details: EuroTeX 92 paper about tables in general

name: btOOL
caption: Perl library for parsing and processing BibTeX files

descriptions.text: Includes a C library called btparse and a perl library Text::BibTeX. Features include: robust, efficient lexical scanning and parsing of BibTeX files; excellent error detection, reporting, and recovery in the parser; full processing of BibTeX strings (macros expanded, whitespace collapsed, strings concatenated); handles all common entry types (@comment, @preamble, @string, and everything else) with ease, and gives you full access to the contents of all entry types; support for processing author names identically to BibTeX; preliminary support for imposing/enforcing a particular database structure.

name: bubblesort
caption: Bubble sorts a list

descriptions.text: This package sorts a list of TeX items {item 1}...{item k} in increasing order where increasing is determined by a comparator macro. By default it sorts real numbers with the usual meaning of increasing but some other examples are discussed in the documentation. A second macro is included which sorts one list and applies the same permutation to a second list.

name: BUCTthesis
caption: Beijing University of Chemical Technology thesis template

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class and template for Beijing University of Chemical Technology, supporting bachelor, master, and doctor theses.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: bullcntr
caption: Display list item counter as regular pattern of bullets

descriptions.text: The bullcntr package defines the command bullcntr, which may be thought of as an analogue of the \fnsymbol command: like the latter, it displays the value of a counter lying between 1 and 9, but uses, for the purpose, a regular pattern of bullets.

name: bundledoc
caption: Bundle together all the files needed to build a LaTeX document

descriptions.text:
The bundledoc package is a post-processor for the snapshot package that bundles together all the classes, packages and files needed to build a given LaTeX document. It reads the .dep file that snapshot produces, finds each of the files mentioned therein, and archives them into a single .tar.gz (or .zip, or whatever) file, suitable for moving across systems, transmitting to a colleague, etc.

A script, arlatex, provides an alternative archiving mechanism, creating a single LaTeX file that contains all of the ancillary files of a LaTeX document, together with the document itself, using the filecontents* environment.

topics.details: creating archival copies, or copies for distribution
pack files up for distribution or archiving

name: burmese
caption: Basic Support for Writing Burmese

descriptions.text: This package provides basic support for writing Burmese. The package provides a preprocessor (written in Perl), an Adobe Type 1 font, and LaTeX macros.

name: buscard
caption: A document style for business cards

descriptions.text: This style uses the LaTeX 2.09 version of the NFSS, which is no longer available; some adaptation would seem essential for its use.

topics.details: typeset cards for business, filing, etc.

name: business-research
caption: Markup for the journal Business Research

descriptions.text: The package is supplied for authors of the journal Business Research, the journal of the German Academic Association of Business Research.

name: businesscard-qrcode
caption: Business cards with QR-Code

descriptions.text:
What happens when you give your visiting card to someone? Either they manually type the text into their computer or mobile phone, or it will end up in a box and be forgotten. Nowadays data is required electronically, not on paper. Here is the solution: A visiting card with QR-Code that contains a full vcard so that it can be scanned with an app on the mobile phone and thereby automatically imported into the electronic contacts. This also works well when you are offline and bluetooth transfer fails. So here is the highly configurable business card or visiting card with full vcard as QR-Code, ready to send to online printers. You can specify the exact size of the paper and the content within the paper, including generation of crop marks.

The package depends on the following other LaTeX packages: calc, crop, DejaVuSans, etoolbox, fontawesome, fontenc, geometry, kvoptions, marvosym, qrcode, varwidth, and wrapfig.

The package needs XeLaTeX for working properly.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
typeset cards for business, filing, etc.

name: bussproofs
caption: Proof trees in the style of the sequent calculus

descriptions.text:
The package allows the construction of proof trees in the style of the sequent calculus and many other proof systems. One novel feature of the macros is they support the horizontal alignment according to some centre point specified with the command \fCenter. This is the style often used in sequent calculus proofs.

The package works in a Plain TeX document, as well as in LaTeX; an exposition of the commands available is given in the package file itself.

name: bussproofs-colorful
caption: Color extension for the bussproofs package

descriptions.text: This is a small extension to the bussproofs package that adds color control for proof trees. It allows users to customize the colors of nodes (formulas), inference lines, and labels via package options and runtime commands, while preserving the original layout and spacing of bussproofs.

name: bussproofs-extra
caption: Extra commands for bussproofs.sty

descriptions.text: This package provides additional functionality for bussproofs.sty; specifically, it allows for typesetting of entire (sub)deductions.

name: BXbase
caption: BX bundle base components

descriptions.text:
The main purpose of this bundle is to serve as an underlying library for other packages created by the same author (their names start with BX or PX).

However bxbase package contains a few user-level commands and is of some use by itself.

name: bxcalc
caption: Extend the functionality of the calc package

descriptions.text:
This package bundle consists of the following packages:

  • bxcalcize: To make calc expressions available in more places.
  • bxcalcux: To add user-defined units to the calc syntax.

In addition, this bundle provides the bxcalc package, which simply loads the above-mentioned packages internally.

name: bxcjkjatype
caption: Typeset Japanese with pdfLaTeX and CJK

descriptions.text: The package provides a working configuration of the CJK package, suitable for Japanese typesetting of moderate quality. Moreover, it facilitates use of the CJK package for pLaTeX users, by providing commands that are similar to those used by the pLaTeX kernel and some other packages used with it.

documentation.details: Small example of use (Japanese and English)
Sample: Introductory beamer slides (English and Japanese)

name: bxcoloremoji
caption: Use color emojis more conveniently

descriptions.text:
This package lets users output color emojis in LaTeX documents. Compared to other packages with similar functionality, this package has the following merits:

  • It supports all major LaTeX engines.
  • Emojis can be entered as the characters themselves, as their Unicode code values, or as their short names.
  • It works reasonably well in PDF strings when using hyperref.
  • Emojis can be handled properly even in Japanese typesetting environments.

This package has been widely used among the Japanese LaTeX community, but there are already many emoji packages on CTAN and in TeX Live. To avoid uploading a large amount of emoji image data that are essentially identical, the package was revised in version 1.0 so that the image output was delegated to the twmojis package. Therefore, this package now contains no image data.

name: bxdpx-beamer
caption: Dvipdfmx extras for use with beamer

descriptions.text:
The package is a driver to support beamer Navigation symbols and \framezoomed regions when using dvipdfmx as PDF generator (e.g., as part of e-pTeX).

The package does not define any user commands.

name: bxdvidriver
caption: Enables specifying a driver option effective only in DVI output

descriptions.text: This single-function package enables authors to specify a global driver option (dvips, dvipdfmx, etc) which is applied only when the engine outputs a DVI file. It is useful to create special document- templates that can be compiled in both PDF-mode and DVI-mode.

name: bxeepic
caption: Eepic facilities using pict2e

descriptions.text: The package provides an eepic driver to use pict2e facilities.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: bxenclose
caption: Enclose the document body with some pieces of code

descriptions.text: The package enables authors to designate in the preamble to make the document body enclosed with the given pieces of code. As is known, there are already various mechanisms provided by LaTeX kernel or packages that attach hooks at the beginning and end of documents.

name: BXghost
caption: Ghost insertion for proper xkanjiskip

descriptions.text: The package provides two commands to help authors for documents in Japanese to insert proper xkanjiskips. It supports LuaTeX, XeTeX, pTeX, upTeX, and ApTeX (pTeX-ng).

name: BXjaholiday
caption: Support for Japanese holidays

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides a command to convert dates to names of Japanese holidays. Another command, converting dates to the day of the week in Japanese, is available as a free gift. Further (lower-level) APIs are provided for expl3.

The package supports pdfTeX, XeTeX, LuaTeX, pTeX, and upTeX.

name: BXjalipsum
caption: Dummy text in Japanese

descriptions.text:
This package enables users to print some Japanese text that can be used as dummy text. It is a Japanese counterpart of the lipsum package.

Since there is no well-known nonsense text like Lipsum in the Japanese language, the package uses some real text in public domain.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: BXjaprnind
caption: Adjust the position of parentheses at paragraph head

descriptions.text: In Japanese typesetting, opening parentheses placed at the beginning of paragraphs or lines are treated specially; for example, while the paragraph indent before normal kanji characters is 1em, the indent before parentheses can be 0.5em, 1em or 1.5em deoending on the local rule in effect.

name: bxjatoucs
caption: Convert Japanese character code to Unicode

descriptions.text: This package is meant for macro/package developers: It provides function-like (fully-expandable) macros that convert a character code value in one of several Japanese encodings to a Unicode value. Supported source encodings are: ISO-2022-JP (jis), EUC-JP (euc), Shift_JIS (sjis), and the Adobe-Japan1 glyph set.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: BXjscls
caption: Japanese document class collection for all major engines

descriptions.text: This package provides an extended version of the Japanese document class collection provided by jsclasses. While the original version supports only pLaTeX and upLaTeX, the extended version also supports pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX, with the aid of suitable packages that provide capability of Japanese typesetting.

name: bxnewfont
caption: Enhanced \newfont command

descriptions.text: This package provides a new command \newfontx. It is similar to the old (and deprecated) command \newfont in function, but is more compatible with NFSS. In particular, one can safely change font size after invoking a font command defined by \newfontx. The new command will be useful to users who know much of the old \newfont command, but are unfamiliar with the details of NFSS.

name: bxorigcapt
caption: To retain the original caption names when using Babel

descriptions.text: This package forces the caption names (\chaptername, \today, etc) declared by the document class in use to be used as the caption names for a specific language introduced by the Babel package.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: bxpapersize
caption: Synchronize output paper size with layout paper size

descriptions.text: As is well known, in LaTeX processing layout paper size specified by document class options is not automatically applied to output paper size. This package enables LaTeX authors to synchronize both kinds of paper sizes.

topics.details: select pages to be output, etc.

name: bxpdfver
caption: Specify version and compression level of output PDF files

descriptions.text:
This package enables users to specify in their sources the following settings on the PDF document to output:

  • PDF version (1.4, 1.5 etc.);
  • whether or not to compress streams;
  • whether or not to use object streams.

This package supports all major PDF-output engines and dvipdfmx.

name: bxtexlogo
caption: Additional TeX-family logos

descriptions.text:
The hologo package provides many useful logos of popular (and not so popular) TeX-family software. However, its interface is a bit cumbersome because you must type \hologo{BibTeX} instead of \BibTeX.

This package makes it possible to import some of the logos provided by hologo as single commands, such as \BibTeX.

Additionally, the package provides logos of some TeX-family software that is popular mainly in Japan. These logos can be imported in the same way as those provided by the \hologo command.

bxtexlogo depends on hologo and cjhebrew (if \logoAleph and \logoLamed are used).

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: bxwareki
caption: Convert dates from Gregorian to Japanese calender

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides commands to convert from the Gregorian calendar (e. g. 2018/8/28) to the Japanese rendering of the Japanese calendar (e. g. Heisei 30 nen 8 gatsu 28 nichi; actually with kanji characters). You can choose whether the numbers are written in Western numerals or kanji numerals.

Note that the package only deals with dates in the year 1873 or later, where the Japanese calendar is really a Gregorian calendar with a different notation of years.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: byo-twemojis
caption: <q>Build your own twemojis</q> with TikZ

descriptions.text: This package provides the means to create your own emojis (the simple, round, and mostly yellow ones) from elements of existing emojis. The provided command creates a TikZ picture from the stated elements with multiple possibilities to modify the result in color and position.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: byrne
caption: Typeset geometric proofs in the style of Oliver Byrne’s 1847 edition of Euclid’s Elements

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This package is a LaTeX adaptation of a set of tools developed for ConTeXt reproduction of Oliver Byrne’s 1847 edition of the first six books of Euclid’s Elements . It consists of a MetaPost library, responsible for all the drawing, and a set of LaTeX macros to conveniently use them.

This package works with LuaLaTeX and relies on luamplib v2.23.0 or higher.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: bytefield
caption: Create illustrations for network protocol specifications

descriptions.text: The bytefield package helps the user create illustrations for network protocol specifications and anything else that utilizes fields of data. These illustrations show how the bits and bytes are laid out in a packet or in memory.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: byzantinemusic
caption: Facilitates writing byzantinemusic

descriptions.text: The package facilitates writing byzantinemusic offering fonts and useful utilities.

name: byzfonts
caption: Byzantine Music Font

descriptions.text: A font (as Metafont source) and macros that allows those familiar with the music of the Greek Orthodox Church (aka, Byzantine Music) to typeset music phrases using LaTeX.

name: c-pascal
caption: Typeset Python, C and Pascal programs

descriptions.text: A TeX macro package for easy typesetting programs in Python, C and Pascal. Program source files may also be input.

name: c2cweb
caption: C language prettyprinter

descriptions.text: A utility to prettyprint C and C++ source files using cweb.

name: c2latex
caption: Simple conversion of C programs to LaTeX

descriptions.text:
c2latex provides simple support for documentation of C programming. Given a C source file in which the comments have been written in LaTeX, c2latex converts the C source file into a LaTeX source file. It can be used to produce typeset listings of C programs and/or documentation associated with the program.

The C source given to c2latex usually has the following form: It starts with a large comment containing LaTeX commands that start a document along with any initial text. Then there is a sequence of comment and code pairs, with the comment explaining the code to follow. The source file is ended by a comment containing LaTeX commands that finish the document. The source of c2latex is distributed in this form.

name: cabin
caption: A humanist Sans Serif font, with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
Cabin is a humanist sans with four weights and true italics and small capitals. According to the designer, Pablo Impallari, Cabin was inspired by Edward Johnston's and Eric Gill's typefaces, with a touch of modernism. Cabin incorporates modern proportions, optical adjustments, and some elements of the geometric sans.

cabin.sty supports use of the font under LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX; it uses the mweights, to manage the user’s view of all those font weights.

An sfdefault option is provided to enable Cabin as the default text font. The fontaxes package is required for use with [pdf]LaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: cachepic
caption: Convert document fragments into graphics

descriptions.text: The bundle simplifies and automates conversion of document fragments into external EPS or PDF files. The bundle consists of two parts: a LaTeX package that implements a document level interface, and a command line tool (written in Lua) that generates the external graphics.

name: caesarcm
caption: Hyphenation of inflected languages, using CM fonts

descriptions.text:
In the period between the definition (in 1990) of the Cork font encoding (now known to LaTeX users as the T1 encoding), and availability of extended versions of the Computer Modern fonts, various partially-extended versions were briefly available. These macros provided a means of using the extensions, pending the availability of the real thing.

The package should be regarded as obsolete.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cahierprof
caption: Schedule and grade books for French teachers

descriptions.text: This package provide tools to help teachers in France to produce weekly schedules and grade books.

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: cahyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for the Catalan language

descriptions.text:
The macros used were created for ghyph31.tex by Bernd Raichle (see the German hyphenation pattern files for further details); the patterns were created using standard, conservative hyphenation rules for Catalan. The results were then refined by running them through patgen, which increased the number of hits.

The results were checked against Diccionari Ortogràfic i de Pronúncia, Enciclopèdia Catalana; no incorrect results were detected, and misses amounted to less than 1%.

For Catalan, both \lefthyphenmn and \righthyphenmin should be set to 2.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Catalan

name: caladea
caption: Support for the Caladea family of fonts

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Caladea family of fonts, designed by Carolina Giovagnoli and Andres Torresi of the Huerta Tipografica foundry and adopted by Google for ChromeOS as a font-metric compatible replacement for Cambria.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: calc
caption: Simple arithmetic in LaTeX commands

copyright.owner: Kresten Krab Thorup and Frank Jensen
Kresten Krab Thorup, Frank Jensen, and the LaTeX3 Project

descriptions.text:
Adds infix expressions to perform arithmetic on the arguments of the LaTeX commands \setcounter, \addtocounter, \setlength, and \addtolength. Since many packages start their arithmetic by storing an argument in a register, the package has wide applicability.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: calcage
caption: Calculate the age of something, in years

descriptions.text: The package calculates the age of someone or something in years. Internally it uses the datenumber package to calculate the age in days; conversion from days to years is then performed, taking care of leap years and such odd things.

name: calcfrac
caption: Calculates the value of an expression containing fractions

descriptions.text:
This package is an engine for calculating numerical expressions containing fractions. The numerical value of the expression is calculated with a non-expandable method and displayed in the form of an irreducible fraction or, where appropriate, an integer.

This package is intended for educational purposes. The videos showing its writing from scratch are available on youtube from episode 24: https://youtu.be/6lF4P6B3msw. This is why it is delivered with only a minimalist documentation.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: calctab
caption: Language for numeric tables

descriptions.text: The calctab package helps the user to typeset a kind of economic table such as invoices, expense notes and liquidation, or other tabular material with a values column. The code computes sum and percentage with floating point numeric methods (using the fltpoint package) and builds the render table task.

name: calculation
caption: Typesetting reasoned calculations, also called calculational proofs

descriptions.text:
The calculation environment formats reasoned calculations, also called calculational proofs.

The notion of reasoned calculations or calculational proofs was originally advocated by Wim Feijen and Edsger Dijkstra. The package accepts options fleqn and leqno (with the same effect as the LaTeX options fleqn and leqno, or may inherit the options from the document class). It allows steps and expressions to be numbered (by LaTeX equation numbers, obeying the LaTeX \label command to refer to these numbers), and a step doesn't take vertical space if its hint is empty. An expression in a calculation can be given a comment; it is placed at the side opposite to the equation numbers. Calculations are allowed inside hints although numbering and commenting is then disabled.

name: calculator
caption: Use LaTeX as a scientific calculator

descriptions.text:
The calculator and calculus packages define several instructions which allow us to realise algebraic operations and to evaluate elementary functions and derivatives in our documents.

The package’s main goal is to define the arithmetic and functional calculations needed in the author’s package xpicture, but the numeric abilities of calculator and calculus may be useful in other contexts.

name: calculatoritems
caption: Insert menus/items for classic calculators

descriptions.text: Insert inline (based on tcolorbox, graphicx and calc packages) items/menus for classic calculators (numworks, casio, texas instruments, hp).

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: calendar
caption: A package for calendars and timetables

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Includes, for example, a package which organizes date items in a format suitable for conference schedules, itineraries, academic teaching timetables and the like. Developments of the bundle appear as evautofl and evweek.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: calendar-Barr
caption: A calendar document

descriptions.text: Generates a Gregorian calendar for any year up to 3999 (the year 4000 probably needs another calendar adjustment...).

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: calendarweek
caption: Calculate the week number of a date

descriptions.text:
Calculates the week number of a given date; usage is \calendarweek{30}{12}{2006}. The package uses the e-TeX extensions (available in any current distribution); it is suitable for inclusion into larger calendar-based packages.

Watch out: Dec 29 can be evaluated to week 1 of the next year; and Jan 3 can be week 53 of the previous year.

name: calligra
caption: Calligraphic font

descriptions.text:
A calligraphic font in the handwriting style of the author, Peter Vanroose. The font is supplied as Metafont source.

LaTeX support of the font is provided in the calligra package in the fundus bundle.

name: calligra-type1
caption: Type 1 version of Calligra

descriptions.text: This is a conversion (using mf2pt1) of Peter Vanroose’s handwriting font.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: callout-itembox
caption: A LaTeX package for colored callout item/numbered text boxes with a tinted

descriptions.text: A small LaTeX package for colored callout item/numbered boxes with a tinted background, a colored side bar with circular/numbered marker. Each box can show a bold colored heading plus body text, or body text only.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: callouts
caption: Put simple annotations and notes inside a picture

descriptions.text: The package defines the annotation environment in which callouts, notes, arrows, and the like can be placed to describe certain parts of a picture.

name: callouts-box
caption: Provides visually appealing callout boxes

descriptions.text: This package provides a collection of visually appealing, structured callout boxes for LaTeX documents. These boxes are useful for highlighting important information such as warnings, errors, notes, and success messages. The package is built on top of tcolorbox for highly customizable, breakable callout boxes and xcolor for predefined color schemes.

name: calorie
caption: Calorie checking for dieters

descriptions.text:
The package (designed for use with LaTeX 2.09) allows the user to specify calorific values of items of diet (in a data file), and then to typeset a document that lists the user’s consumption and sums the calories.

An example calorie table and a sample document are included in the file.

name: calrsfs
caption: Copperplate calligraphic letters in LaTeX

descriptions.text: Provides a maths interface to the rsfs fonts.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cals
caption: Multipage tables with wide range of features

descriptions.text: The package is a set of macros to typeset multipage tables with repeatable headers and footers, with cells spanned over rows and columns. Decorations are supported: padding, background color, width of separation rules. The code is compatible with multicol and bidi.

topics.details: typeset tables that may be too big for a page

name: calxxxx
caption: Prints a card-size calendar for any year

descriptions.text: Prints a card-size calendar for any year, AD or BC, with Gregorian or Julian leap rules (useful for years before adoption of Gregorian rules). Cal2000.tex prints a calendar for years 1990--2020.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: calxxxx-yyyy
caption: Print a calendar for a group of years

descriptions.text:
The package prints a calendar for two or more years, according to a language selection. The package is also culture dependent in the sense that it will start weeks according to local rules: e.g., weeks conventionally start on Monday in the English-speaking world.

The package requires array, babel, and geometry.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: camel
caption: Prototype work on future citation engine

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Comprehensive bibliography manager (developed as a demonstration engine for the work on citations for LaTeX3).

name: cancel
caption: Place lines through maths formulae

descriptions.text: A package to draw diagonal lines (cancelling a term) and arrows with limits (cancelling a term to a value) through parts of maths formulae.

name: canoniclayout
caption: Create canonical page layouts with memoir

descriptions.text:
A canonic text layout has specified relations to a circle inscribed within the enclosing page.

The package allows the user to use a canonic layout with the memoir class.

name: cantarell
caption: LaTeX support for the Cantarell font family

descriptions.text:
Cantarell is a contemporary Humanist sans serif designed by Dave Crossland and Jakub Steiner. This font, delivered under the OFL version 1.1, is available on the GNOME download server.

The present package provides support for this font in LaTeX. It includes Type 1 versions of the fonts, converted for this package using FontForge from its sources, for full support with Dvips.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: capbas
caption: Capital baseball <q>matrix printer</q> font collection

descriptions.text: The collection contains a Metafont toolkit and a set of small fonts that emulate various matrix printers, including Flyspec 3 (a 5x5 grid font), Neckerspoel (a 5x7 grid font), and Capital baseball itself. Documentation on the web is in Dutch.

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

name: capparmode
caption: Dropped capitals for Plain TeX

descriptions.text: Macros to typeset paragraphs with the first letter of the paragraph in a large font with the first few lines of the paragraph indented to make room for this first large letter.

name: capt-of
caption: Captions on more than floats

descriptions.text:
Defines a command \captionof for putting a caption to something that’s not a float.

Note that the caption package includes a \captionof command that is an extension of that provided by this package.

name: captcont
caption: Retain float number across several floats

descriptions.text:
The captcont package provides the ability to continue the numbering in your float environment (figure, table, etc.) with minimal overhead. This package adds three commands: \caption*, \captcont, and \captcont*. Along with the \caption command, these give full control over the caption numbering, caption text and the entries in the list-of pages.

The \caption and \captcont commands generate list-of page entries. The \caption and \caption* commands increment the figure or table counter.

Captcont also fully supports the subfigure package.

name: captdef
caption: Declare free-standing \caption commands

descriptions.text: The \DeclareCaption command defines a class of caption command associated with the counter specified to the command. These commands are free-standing (i.e., don't need to be inside a float environment). The package uses \DeclareCaption to define \figcaption and \tabcaption, which can be used outside figure or table environments.

name: caption
caption: Customising captions in floating environments

descriptions.text:
The caption package provides many ways to customise the captions in floating environments like figure and table, and cooperates with many other packages. Facilities include rotating captions, sideways captions, continued captions (for tables or figures that come in several parts). A list of compatibility notes, for other packages, is provided in the documentation.

The package also provides the caption outside float facility, in the same way that simpler packages like capt-of do.

The package supersedes caption2.

name: caption2
caption: Superseded version of the caption package

descriptions.text:
Extends caption (version 1) capabilities for figures and tables, such as the caption width, style, and font. Many aspects are tunable as options.

Note that the original caption package now stands at version 3 and supersedes this version.

name: carbohydrates
caption: Carbohydrate molecules with chemfig

descriptions.text: This package offers macros that make the preparation of exercise sheets for teaching carbohydrate chemistry a lot less tedious. It uses chemfig for drawing the formulas. Different representation models (Fischer, Haworth, chair…) are supported as well as alpha, beta, and chain isomers.

name: card
caption: Print visiting cards

descriptions.text: The package produces 10 visiting cards in credit card format (European standard) per A4 page.

topics.details: typeset cards for business, filing, etc.

name: card-set
caption: Typeset text for cardfile cards

descriptions.text: The package (a LaTeX 2.09 style) allows you to print text formatted for cardfile cards. Text longer than a single card may be created, and will be boxed up for several different cards.

topics.details: typeset cards for business, filing, etc.

name: cardgame
caption: Typeset custom playing cards for printing

descriptions.text: The cardgame package allows you to define cards, which have various attributes like image, text, and a bunch of layout features. You can then include those cards as images or, more importantly, generate a document containing all of the cards you defined laid out optimally for printing and cutting. You can optionally create card lists for your game's manual, and you can create multiple copies of cards and automatically print the correct number of back sides.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: carlisle
caption: David Carlisle’s small packages

descriptions.text:
Many of David Carlisle’s more substantial packages stand on their own, or as part of the LaTeX latex-tools set; this set contains:

  • Making dotless j characters for fonts that don’t have them;
  • A method for combining the capabilities of longtable and tabularx;
  • An environment for including Plain TeX in LaTeX documents;
  • A jiffy to remove counters from other counters’ reset lists (now obsolete as it has been incorporated into the LaTeX format);
  • A jiffy to create slashed characters for physicists.

name: carlito
caption: Support for Carlito sans-serif fonts

descriptions.text: The package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Carlito family of sans serif fonts, designed by Lukasz Dziedzic of the tyPoland foundry and adopted by Google for ChromeOS as a font-metric compatible replacement for Calibri.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: carolmin
caption: Carolingian Miniscule manuscript book-hand font

descriptions.text:
The carolmin and allcmin packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Carolingian Miniscules manuscript book-hand used between the 8th and 12th century AD. The font consists of minuscules and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided. (Note that the carolmin font is also available in Adobe Type 1 format.)

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: carolmin-t1
caption: Adobe Type 1 format of Carolingian Minuscule fonts

descriptions.text:
The bundle offers Adobe Type 1 format versions of Peter Wilson's Carolingian Minuscule font set (part of the bookhands collection).

The fonts in the bundle are ready-to-use replacements for the Metafont originals.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: carom-billiards
caption: Environment to typeset annotated French billiard tables

descriptions.text: The package provides a new environment together with a collection of TikZ macros designed to facilitate the creation of French billiards table diagrams.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: cartonaugh
caption: A LuaLaTeX package for drawing karnaugh maps with up to 6 variables

descriptions.text:
This package, a fork of 2pi’s karnaugh-map package, draws karnaugh maps with 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 variables. It also contains commands for filling the karnaugh map with terms semi-automatically or manually. Last but not least it contains commands for drawing implicants on top of the map.

The name cartonaugh is a portmanteau of cartographer and karnaugh.

The package needs LuaLaTeX and depends on TikZ, xparse, and xstring.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: cascade
caption: Constructions with braces to present mathematical demonstrations

descriptions.text: The LaTeX package cascade provides a command \Cascade to do constructions to present mathematical demonstrations with successive braces for the deductions.

name: CascadiaCode
caption: The Cascadia Code font with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX

descriptions.text:
Cascadia Code is a monospaced font by Microsoft.

This package provides the Cascadia Code family of fonts with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX.

Adding \usepackage{cascadia-code} to the preamble of your document will activate Cascadia Code as the typewriter font (\ttdefault).

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: cascadiamono-otf
caption: Fontspec support for the OpenType font CascadiaMono

copyright.owner: C. Pierquet (with help from D. Flipo)

descriptions.text:
Support for the OpenType font CascadiaMono (so with LuaLaTeX/XeTeX and fontspec), which is a variant of CascadiaCode, but without ligatures.

  • \setmonofont{CascadiaMono} for regular version,
  • \setmonofont{CascadiaMono-SemiLight} for semilight version.
  • \setmonofont{CascadiaMono-Light} for light version,
  • \setmonofont{CascadiaMono-ExtraLight} for extralight version.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cascadilla
caption: Typeset papers conforming to the stylesheet of the Cascadilla Proceedings Project

descriptions.text: The class provides an extension of the standard LaTeX article class that may be used to typeset papers conforming to the stylesheet of the Cascadilla Proceedings Project, which is used by a number of linguistics conference proceedings (e.g., WCCFL).

name: cascover
caption: Make cassette covers

descriptions.text: A straightforward package.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: cases
caption: Numbered cases environment

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX environment numcases to produce multi-case equations with a separate equation number for each case. There is also a subnumcases environment which numbers each case with the overall equation number plus a letter [8a, 8b, etc.].

name: casiofont
caption: Support for the Casio ClassWiz font

descriptions.text: This package provides support for the Casio ClassWiz font, available from the Casio web site. The font itself is not included in the distribution. The package requires compilation with XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts

name: cassette
caption: Typeset cassette box inserts

descriptions.text:
The macros typeset into a set of boxes that are assembled to produce an insert that will fold to fit in a standard Philips cassette box. The body font used is pandora.

A requirement for fonts to provide both CD and Dolby logos are written into the macros; the user will probably need to edit the macros to remove that.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: cassette-shipunov
caption: Print labels for audio cassettes

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX2e class file (the only other cassette package on CTAN is cassette, written for Plain TeX.

The class is part of the shipunov bundle.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: cassette209
caption: A LaTeX 209 document style for cassette inserts

descriptions.text: A style (LaTeX 2.09 equivalent of class) for laying out information on a standard cassette tape insert.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: casslbl
caption: Typeset cassette labels

descriptions.text: A set of macros for typesetting cassette labels, using Plain TeX. Examples of use are provided.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: casyl
caption: Typeset Cree/Inuktitut in Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics

descriptions.text: The bundle constitutes a font (as Metafont source) and LaTeX macros for its use within a document.

name: catalan
caption: Catalan hyphenation patterns

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Catalan

name: catalanbib
caption: Bibliographic styles for use in Catalan

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: El paquet catalanbib conté diversos estils bibliogràfics per fer servir el BibTeX en català: els estils estàndard – adaptats a les convencions tipogràfiques catalanes – (caplain.bst, caunsrt.bst, caabbrev.bst i caalpha.bst) i altres quatre estils autor-data (caauda{0-3}.bst).

The catalanbib package includes several Catalan bibliographic styles for BibTeX: the standard ones – adapted to the Catalan typographical conventions – (caplain.bst, caunsrt.bst, caabbrev.bst, and caalpha.bst), and also four author-date styles (caauda{0-3}.bst).

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Catalan

name: catchfile
caption: Catch an external file into a macro

descriptions.text: This package catches the contents of a file and puts it in a macro. It requires e-TeX. Both LaTeX and plain TeX are supported.

name: catchfilebetweentags
caption: Catch text delimited by docstrip tags

descriptions.text:
This package (built using the facilities of catchfile) provides a macro \catchfilebetweentags acts like the original \catchfile but only extracts a portion of the file instead of the complete file. The extracted portion can be delimited by strings or by docstrip tags:

%<*tag> .... %</tag>

(comments in the caught region may be included or dropped).

name: catcodes
caption: Generic handling of TeX category codes

descriptions.text:
The bundle deals with category code switching; the packages of the bundle should work with any TeX format (with the support of the plainpkg package).

The bundle provides:

  • stacklet.sty, which supports stacks that control the use of different catcodes;
  • actcodes.sty, which deals with active characters; and
  • catchdq.sty, which provides a simple quotation character control mechanism.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: catdoc
caption: Text extractor for word files

descriptions.text: A filter which extracts ASCII text from MS-Word files, optionally with some TeX control sequences (for those characters, which have special meaning for TeX).

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

name: catdvi
caption: A DVI to plain text translator

descriptions.text: A DVI to plain text translator capable of generating ASCII, Latin-1, Latin-9 and UTF-8 (Unicode) output, and recognising T1 and other LaTeX encodings (as well as Knuth's original encodings and those of AMS and other fonts). Catdvi aims to become a superior replacement for the dvi2tty utility; the present version outperforms dvi2tty in some areas and is inferior to it in other areas.

topics.details: derive plain text from a TeX document

name: catechis
caption: Macros for typesetting catechisms

descriptions.text:
The macros include:

  • format for question-and-answer;
  • comments on answers;
  • lengthier explanations of answers;
  • citations.

The formatting of all the macros is highly (and simply) customizable.

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

name: catoptions
caption: Preserving and recalling standard catcodes

descriptions.text: The package changes package loading internals so that all subsequently loaded packages can rely on normal/standard catcodes of all ASCII characters. The package defines canonical control sequences to represent all the visible ASCII characters. It also provides robust option parsing mechanisms (XDeclareOption, XExecuteOptions and XProcessOptions, which will be used by \documentclass if the package has already been loaded). The package also provides a range of other TeX programming tools.

name: catppuccinPalette
caption: Provides (x)colors of catppuccin theme

descriptions.text: Catppuccin is a nice pastel theme in four flavours/styles (Latte, Frappé, Macchiato, Mocha). This package defines these themes as xcolor colors.

name: causets
caption: Draw causal set (Hasse) diagrams

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package uses TikZ to generate (Hasse) diagrams for causal sets (causets) to be used inline with text or in mathematical expressions. The macros can also be used in the tikzpicture environment to annotate or modify a diagram, as shown with some examples in the documentation.

name: cbcoptic
caption: Coptic fonts and LaTeX macros for general usage and for philology

descriptions.text: CBcoptic is a bundle of files for typesetting Coptic philological text with the proper fonts and hyphenation. The fonts are based on, but much extend, the fonts of the original coptic bundle. The CBcoptic bundle includes font description files, Metafont sources and equivalent Adobe Type 1 fonts in pfb format. The bundle also includes a package that provides some macros of philological interest.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: cbe
caption: Bibliography style for Council of Biology Editors format

descriptions.text:
The CBE format is used by Evolution, American Naturalist, and lots of other journals.

The style is derived from apalike.bst in the BibTeX bundle, adopting further features from astron.bst; use with the LaTeX package that comes with astron.

name: cbfonts-fd
caption: LaTeX font description files for the CB Greek fonts

descriptions.text:
The package provides font description files for all the many shapes available from the cbfonts collection. The files provide the means whereby the NFSS knows which fonts a LaTeX user is requesting.

The package depends on cbgreek-complete.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cbgreek-complete
caption: Complete set of Greek fonts

descriptions.text:
This bundle presents the whole of Beccari’s original Greek font set, which use the Lispiakos font shape derived from the shape of the fonts used in printers’ shops in Lispia. The fonts are available both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format, and at the same wide set of design sizes as are such font sets as the EC fonts.

Please note that this package needs the complementary cbfonts-fd package to work properly.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: cc-pl
caption: Polish extension of Computer Concrete fonts

descriptions.text:
These Metafont sources rely on the availability of the Metafont Polish fonts and of the Metafont sources of the original Concrete fonts.

Adobe Type 1 versions of the fonts are included.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: ccaption
caption: Continuation headings and legends for floats

descriptions.text: A package providing commands for continuation captions, unnumbered captions, and also a non-specific legend heading for any environment. Methods are also provided to define captions for use outside float (e.g., figure and table) environments, and to define new float environments and Lists of Floats. Tools are provided for specifying your own captioning styles.

name: ccfonts
caption: Support for Concrete text and math fonts in LaTeX

descriptions.text: LaTeX font definition files for the Concrete fonts and a LaTeX package for typesetting documents using Concrete as the default font family. The files support OT1, T1, TS1, and Concrete mathematics including AMS fonts (Ulrik Vieth's concmath).

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cchess
caption: Chinese chess

descriptions.text: Macros and a font for typesetting Chinese Chess board diagrams. The font is distributed as Metafont source.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: ccicons
caption: LaTeX support for Creative Commons icons

descriptions.text: The package provides the means to typeset Creative Commons icons, in documents licensed under CC licences. A font (in Adobe Type 1 format) and LaTeX support macros are provided.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: CClicenses
caption: Typeset Creative Commons licence logos

descriptions.text: The cclicenses package helps users typesetting Creative Commons logos in LaTeX. It defines some commands useful to quickly write these logos, related to CC licences versions 1.0 and 2.0.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: ccool
caption: A key-value document command parser

descriptions.text: This package provides a key-value interface, \Ccool, on top of xparse’s document command parser. Global options control input processing and its expansion. By default, they are set to meet likely requirements, depending on context: the selected language, and which of text and math mode is active. These options can be overridden inline. This versatility could find its use, for example, to encode notational conventions (such as \Real → \mathbb{R}) at the point where they are introduced in the document (Let R denote real numbers). Polymorphic commands can be generated by parameterizing the keys (for instance, one parameter value for style, another for a property). User input to \Ccool can optionally be serialized. This can useful for typesetting documents sharing the same notation.

name: cd
caption: Typeset CD covers

descriptions.text: Normal usage will ordinarily require no more than a simple data file per cover; the package will make a full insert for a CD case (it copes with both normal and slim cases).

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

name: cdcmd
caption: Expandable conditional commands for LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides some conditional commands, just like the styledcmd package. The difference is that cdcmd can define expandable conditional commands.

name: cdcover
caption: Typeset CD covers

descriptions.text: The CD-cover class will typeset front and back cover sheets for CD jewel cases, or an entire paper cover, or a label for a plastic slip-cover.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: cdlabeler
caption: Take user text and typeset it to fit a CD label

descriptions.text: The package’s operation is described in comments in the file itself; a simple test file is provided.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: C.D.P. Bundle
caption: Business letters in the Italian style

descriptions.text: The C.D.P. Bundle can be used to typeset high-quality business letters formatted according to Italian style conventions. It is highly configurable, and its modular structure provides you with building blocks of increasing level, by means of which you can compose a large variety of letters. It is also possible to write letters divided into sections and paragraphs, to include floating figures and tables, and to have the relevant indexes compiled automatically. A single input file can contain several letters, and each letter will have its own table of contents, etc., independent from the other ones.

name: cea
caption: Produce papers for Computers and Electronics in Agriculture

descriptions.text: The package provides an unofficial LaTeX 2.09 style option for the Elsevier journal.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: cell
caption: Bibliography style for Cell

descriptions.text: This is an apa-like style (cf. apalike.bst in the BibTeX distribution), developed from the same author's JMB style. A supporting LaTeX package is also provided.

name: cellprops
caption: Accept CSS-like selectors in tabular, array, …

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: This package reworks the internals of tabular, array, and similar constructs, and adds a \cellprops command accepting CSS-like selectors and properties. It depends on mdwtab, xcolor, expl3, and xparse.

name: cellspace
caption: Ensure minimal spacing of table cells

descriptions.text:
It is well known that high or deep cells tend to touch the \hlines of a tabular. This package provides a modifier S acting on usual column types so that to ensure a minimal distance that can be controlled through two parameters \cellspacetoplimit and \cellspacebottomlimit.

The approach employed by this package is noticeably simpler than that of tabls, which considers the dimensions of each entire row; whereas you can ask the cellspace only to look at the cells of potentially difficult columns.

The package depends on ifthen, array, calc, and xkeyval.

name: cellular
caption: Cellular table construction

descriptions.text: Cellular tables are ruled tables with spanned cells; the present package achieves that, and includes several tricks for dealing with the idiosyncrasies of printers of the time when it was written.

name: cellwise
caption: Building tables one cell at a time

descriptions.text:
The package provides the means to build tables from free-formated cells, one cell at a time. The basic command is

\thiscell{<column>}{<line>}{<definitions>}

name: celtic
caption: A TikZ library for drawing celtic knots

descriptions.text: The package provides a TikZ library for drawing celtic knots.

name: censor
caption: Tools for producing redacted documents

descriptions.text: This package provides simple tools for creating redacted documents with blacked-out text. Its tools are useful both for creating documents in a restricted environment (for redacted release in an unrestricted environment) as well as in an unrestricted environment (for eventual transfer and completion in the restricted environment).

name: centeredline
caption: A macro for centering lines

descriptions.text:
This package provides a macro \centeredline{...} which allows to conveniently center a line inside a paragraph while allowing usage therein of \verb or other macros changing catcodes.

It works nicely in list environments, and material whose natural width exceeds the current linewidth will get properly centered too.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: centerlastline
caption: Paragraphs with last line centered, known as <q>Spanish</q> paragraphs

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package provides a command \centerlastline and an environment centerlastline that typeset Spanish paragraphs, that is paragraphs without indentation, and last line centered, useful to finish a large paragraph of text at the end of chapters, prologues, etc.

name: centernot
caption: Centred \not command

descriptions.text:
The package provides \centernot that prints the symbol \not on the following argument. Unlike the default \not command, the symbol is horizontally centered.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: cep
caption: Compression tools for PostScript

descriptions.text: Compression utilities for PostScript files, written in AWK and PostScript (to be processed by gawk and Ghostscript) to compress bitmap EPS files down to 10 percent of the original size.

name: cesenaexam
caption: A class file to typeset exams

descriptions.text: This LaTeX document class has been designed to typeset exams.

name: cfgguide
caption: Documentation of LaTeX configuration options

descriptions.text:
Documentation of techniques used to vary the configuration of a LaTeX installation.

Part of a set of documentation that also covers LaTeX3 methods for document authors, font handling, class and package writing, typesetting Cyrillic, and LaTeX font encodings, modification of LaTeX.

name: cfr-initials
caption: LaTeX packages for use of initials

descriptions.text:
This is a set of 23 tiny packages designed to make it easier to use fonts from the initials package in LaTeX, e.g. with the lettrine package.

It is a response to comments on an answer at TeX StackExchange requesting sample package files for others to copy. I had previously assumed these were too trivial to be of interest, but if they would be useful, then I would prefer them to be generally available via CTAN.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cfr-lm
caption: Enhanced support for the Latin Modern fonts

descriptions.text:
The package supports a number of features of the Latin Modern fonts which are not easily accessible via the default (La)TeX support provided in the official distribution. In particular, the package supports the use of the various styles of digits available, small-caps and upright italic shapes, and alternative weights and widths. It also supports variable width typewriter and the quotation font. Version 2.004 of the Latin Modern fonts is supported.

By default, the package uses proportional oldstyle digits and variable width typewriter but this can be changed by passing appropriate options to the package. The package also supports using (for example) different styles of digits within a document so it is possible to use proportional oldstyle digits by default, say, but tabular lining digits within a particular table.

The package requires the official Latin Modern distribution, including its (La)TeX support. The package relies on the availability of both the fonts themselves and the official font support files. The package also makes use of the nfssext-cfr package.

Only the T1 and TS1 encodings are supported for text fonts. The set up of fonts for mathematics is identical to that provided by Latin Modern.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: chalk-annotate
caption: Chalk-textured annotations for Beamer presentations

descriptions.text: This package provides pre-rendered PNG overlays with natural chalk grain and opacity variation for emphasizing text and other content in Beamer slides. It offers six annotation styles: ellipse, underline, box with fill and border, arrow, and strikethrough. Each style is available in five colors: red, blue, green, orange, and purple. The resulting annotations look more realistic than pure TikZ decorations. The package works with XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: changebar
caption: Generate changebars in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: Identify areas of text to be marked with changebars with the \cbstart and \cbend commands; the bars may be coloured. The package uses drivers to place the bars; the available drivers can work with dvitoln03, dvitops, dvips, the emTeX and TeXtures DVI drivers, and VTeX and pdfTeX.

name: changelayout
caption: Change the layout of individual pages and their text

descriptions.text: The package is an extension of the changepage package to permit the user to change the layout of individual pages and their texts.

name: changelog
caption: Typesetting keepachangelog.com style changelogs

descriptions.text:
This package provides a changelog environment (which itself provides a version environment) to represent a changelog. The package supports multiple authors, unreleased changes, and yanked (revoked) releases.

Inspired by keepachangelog.com.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: changepage
caption: Margin adjustment and detection of odd/even pages

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands to change the page layout in the middle of a document, and to robustly check for typesetting on odd or even pages. Instructions for use are at the end of the file.

The package is an extraction of code from the memoir class, whose user interface it shares. It is intended the this package will eventually replace the chngpage package, which is distributed with the package.

name: changes
caption: Manual change markup

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to manually markup changes of text, such as additions, deletions, or replacements. Changed text is shown in a different color; deleted text is striked out. Additionally, text can be highlighted and/or commented. The package allows free definition of additional authors and their associated color. It also allows you to change the markup of changes, authors, highlights or comments.

A Python script is provided for removing the changes.

name: chappg
caption: Page numbering by chapter

descriptions.text: The package provides for chapterno-pageno or chaptername-pageno page numbering. Provision is made for front- and backmatter in book class.

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

name: chapref
caption: Bibliography details per chapter

descriptions.text: The package provides for a separate bibliography section in each chapter. (It is assumed that each chapter is in its own \included file.)

topics.details: multiple BibTeX bibliographies in a document

name: chapterbib
caption: Multiple bibliographies in a document

descriptions.text:
The package allows a bibliography per \included file, or per unit defined by its cbunit or \cbinput directives. A package option is provided to force all these bibliographies to be in \sections (rather than \chapters, as would normally happen in book- or report-like classes).

The package is distributed as part of the cite bundle of packages.

topics.details: multiple BibTeX bibliographies in a document

name: chapterfolder
caption: Package for working with complicated folder structures

descriptions.text: This package simplifies working with folder structures that match the chapter/section/subsection structure. It provides macros to define a folder that contains the file for a chapter/section/subsection, and provides macros that allow inclusion without using the full path, rather the path relative to the current folder of the chapter/section/subsection. It makes easy changing the name of a folder, for example.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: char2path
caption: A LaTeX package that converts characters into TikZ paths

descriptions.text: This TikZ-based LaTeX package provides an easy way to convert characters to TikZ-paths representing these characters.

name: CharisSIL
caption: CharisSIL fonts with support for all LaTeX engines

descriptions.text: This package provides the CharisSIL family of fonts adapted by SIL International from Bitstream Charter in TrueType format, with support for LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: font with adaptations to several languages
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: charter
caption: Charter fonts

descriptions.text: A commercial text font donated for the common good. Support for use with LaTeX is available in freenfss, part of psnfss.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: chbar
caption: Change bar marks in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: This package creates change bars without the use of \special commands (unlike the LaTeX package changebar).

name: chbibref
caption: Change the Bibliography/References title

descriptions.text: Defines a single command, \setbibref, which sets whichever of \bibname and \refname is in use. (\bibname is used in book.cls and report.cls, and \refname is used in article.cls.)

name: cheatsheet
caption: A simple cheatsheet class

descriptions.text: The package provides a clean, multi-column design intended for cheat sheets. It imports the most useful packages and encloses the document in a multicol environment.

name: check
caption: A syntax checker and tidier

descriptions.text: The checker provides syntax checking and automatic labelling, together with some support for German documents.
