topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: check-parens
caption: Check parentheses in LaTeX

descriptions.text: A simple program written in C++, prompted by difficulty of spotting missing braces.

name: checkcites
caption: Check citation commands in a document

copyright.owner: Enrico Gregorio, Paulo Roberto Massa Cereda

descriptions.text: The package provides a lua script written for the sole purpose of detecting undefined and unused references from LaTeX auxiliary or bibliography files.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: checkend
caption: Extend <q>improperly closed environment</q> messages

descriptions.text:
When an environment is left open, LaTeX gives an error at the end of the document. However it only informs about the first of them, while the rest are shown with meaningless errors:

(\end occurred inside a group at level N)

This package replaces these errors with more useful messages which show which environments (in reverse order) were not closed. There are no user macros: just use the package.

name: checklab
caption: A patch for the label-checking code

descriptions.text:
Patch for the kernel label-checking code at end document, to produce an explicit message (albeit a somewhat inscrutable one) for each label that it thinks has changed (and how it has changed). This is useful if you are developing macros that use labels in odd ways.

One of a series of fragments designed for use by package writers and others.

name: checklistings
caption: Pass verbatim contents through a compiler and reincorporate the resulting output

descriptions.text:
This package augments the fancyvrb and listings packages to allow the source code they contain to be checked by an external tool (like a compiler). The external tool's messages can be automatically reincorporated into the original document.

The package does not focus on a specific programming language, but it is designed to work well with languages and compilers in the ML family.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: chem-journal
caption: Various BibTeX formats for journals in Chemistry

descriptions.text: Various BibTeX formats for journals in Chemistry, including Reviews in Computational Chemistry, Journal of Physical Chemistry, Journal of Computational Chemistry, and Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics.

name: chemarr
caption: Arrows for chemists

descriptions.text:
Very often chemists need a longer version of reaction arrows (\rightleftharpoons) with the possibility to put text above and below. Analogous to amsmath's \xrightarrow and \xleftarrow this package provides the macro \xrightleftharpoons. The package requires amsmath. To use it, \usepackage{chemarr}, then \xrightleftharpoons[below]{above} .

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: chemarrow
caption: Arrows for use in chemistry

descriptions.text: This bundle consists of a font (available as Metafont source, MetaPost source, and generated type 1 versions), and a package to use it. The arrows in the font are designed to look more like those in chemistry text-books than do Knuth's originals.

name: chembst
caption: A collection of BibTeX files for chemistry journals

descriptions.text: The package offers a collection of advanced BibTeX style files suitable for publications in chemistry journals. Currently, style files for journals published by the American Chemical Society, Wiley-VCH and The Royal Society of Chemistry are available. The style files support advanced features such as automatic formatting of errata or creating an appropriate entry for publications in Angewandte Chemie where both English and German should be cited simultaneously.

name: chemcompounds
caption: Simple consecutive numbering of chemical compounds

descriptions.text: The chemcompounds package allows for a simple consecutive numbering of chemical compounds. Optionally, it is possible to supply a custom name for each compound. The package differs from the chemcono package by not generating an odd-looking list of compounds inside the text.

name: chemcono
caption: Support for compound numbers in chemistry documents

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package for using compound numbers in chemistry documents. It works like \cite and the \thebibliography, using \fcite and \theffbibliography instead. It allows compound names in documents to be numbered and does not affect the normal citation routines.

name: chemexec
caption: Creating (chemical) exercise sheets

descriptions.text: The package provides environments and commands that the author needed when preparing exercise sheets and other teaching material. In particular, the package supports the creation of exercise sheets, with separating printing of solutions

name: chemfig
caption: Draw molecules with easy syntax

descriptions.text:
The package provides the command \chemfig{<code>}, which draws molecules using the TikZ package. The <code> argument provides instructions for the drawing operation.

While the diagrams produced are essentially 2-dimensional, the package supports many of the conventional notations for illustrating the 3-dimensional layout of a molecule.

The package uses TikZ for its actual drawing operations.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: chemformula
caption: Command for typesetting chemical formulas and reactions

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command to typeset chemical formulas and reactions in support of other chemistry packages (such as chemmacros).

The package used to be distributed as a part of chemmacros.

name: chemformula-ru
caption: Using the chemformula package with babel-russian settings

descriptions.text:
The chemformula package and babel-russian settings (russian.ldf) both define macros named \ch .

The package chemformula-ru undefines babel’s macro to prevent an error when both packages are loaded together.

Optionally it redefines the \cosh macro to print the hyperbolic cosine in Russian notation and/or defines a new macro \Ch for that purpose.

name: chemgreek
caption: Upright Greek letters in chemistry

descriptions.text:
The package provides upright Greek letters in support of other chemistry packages (such as chemmacros).

The package used to be distributed as a part of chemmacros.

name: chemmacros
caption: A collection of macros to support typesetting chemistry documents

descriptions.text:
The bundle offers a collection of macros and commands which are intended to make typesetting chemistry documents faster and more convenient. Coverage includes some nomenclature commands, oxidation numbers, thermodynamic data, newman projections, etc.

The package relies on the following supporting packages:

  • chemformula, providing a command for typesetting chemical formulae and reactions (doing a similar task to that of mhchem);
  • chemgreek, offering support for use of greek letters; and
  • ghsystem, providing for the UN globally harmonised chemical notation.

The packages are written using current versions of the experimental LaTeX 3 coding conventions and the LaTeX 3 support packages.

name: chemnum
caption: A method for numbering chemical compounds

descriptions.text:
The package defines a \label- and \ref-like commands for compound numbers.

The package requires LaTeX3 packages expl3 (from the l3kernel bundle) as well as xparse and l3keys2e (from the l3packages bundle).

name: chemobabel
caption: Convert chemical structures from ChemDraw, MDL molfile or SMILES using Open Babel

descriptions.text:
This package provides a way to convert and include chemical structure graphics from various chemical formats, such as ChemDraw files, MDL molfile or SMILES notations using Open Babel.

To use this LaTeX package, it is necessary to enable execution of the following external commands via latex -shell-escape.

  • obabel (Open Babel)
  • inkscape or rsvg-convert (for SVG -> PDF/EPS conversion)
  • pdfcrop or ps2eps (optional; for cropping large margins of PDF/EPS)

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: chempid
caption: Draw Piping and Instrumentation diagrams using TikZ via PGF

descriptions.text: A humble LaTeX package that allows you to draw Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&ID) or block diagrams quickly and efficiently. It contains pre-built assets in PGF to create P&ID drawings. We noticed that, with the diminishing compile time on Overleaf, it became increasingly difficult to use TikZ to this end. Therefore, we chose for PGF because it is faster to compile than TikZ objects. The objects themselves have been made in accordance with the ISO 10628-2 standard.

name: chemplants
caption: Symbology to draw chemical plants with TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package offers tools to draw simple or barely complex schemes of chemical processes. The package defines several standard symbols and styles to draw process units and streams. The guiding light of the package is the UNICHIM regulation.

All of the symbols and styles are defined using tools of the TikZ package, thus a basic knowledge of the logic of this powerful tool is required to profitably use chemplants.

name: chemscheme
caption: Support for chemical schemes

descriptions.text:
The chemscheme package consists of two parts, both related to chemical schemes. The package adds a scheme float type to the LaTeX default types figure and table. The scheme float type acts in the same way as those defined by the LaTeX kernel, but is intended for chemical schemes. The package also provides a method for adding automatic numbering of chemicals to schemes.

The package is distributed as part of the chemstyle bundle.

name: chemschemex
caption: Typeset and cross-reference chemical schemes based on TikZ code

descriptions.text: The package provides a comfortable means of typesetting chemical schemes, and also offers automatic structure referencing.

name: chemsec
caption: Automated creation of numeric entity labels

descriptions.text: Packages provides creation of sequential numeric labels for entities in a document. The motivating example is chemical structures in a scientific document. The package can automatically output a full object name and label on the first occurrence in the document and just labels only on subsequent references.

name: chemstruct
caption: Structural organic chemistry

descriptions.text: An ingenious package that will also work with Plain TeX. There are signs that it may have been (in part) inspiration for XyMTeX.

name: chemstyle
caption: Writing chemistry with style

descriptions.text:
Chemstyle has been developed as a successor to the LaTeX package provided by the rsc bundle. The package provides an extensible system for formatting chemistry documents according to the conventions of a number of leading journals. It also provides some handy chemistry-related macros.

Chemstyle is much enhanced compared to its predecessor, and users of rsc are strongly encouraged to migrate (all of the additional macros in the rsc LaTeX package are present in chemstyle).

The package chemscheme is distributed with chemstyle; chemstyle itself incorporates ideas that come from the trivfloat package; the documentation uses the auto-pst-pdf package.

name: chemsym
caption: Macros for typing chemical symbols

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Provides some basic support for typesetting chemical formulae, avoiding direct use of maths mode.

name: chemtex
caption: Structural chemistry

descriptions.text: The package was a very early demonstration of the use of TeX for graphical purposes; it is seldom if ever used now (21st century), but represented ground-breaking effort when first released.

name: cheq
caption: Adobe chess font

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: The font itself is presented as Macintosh stuffit (both in printer and screen formats), and (for some reason) as a .ps file, which from the documentation sounds as if it ought to be a .pfa file. Metrics (both AFM and TeX .pl files), and a simple package for generating images of pieces, are provided.

topics.details: fonts for typesetting chess problems and diagrams

name: cherokee
caption: A font for the Cherokee script

descriptions.text:
The Cherokee script was designed in 1821 by Segwoya.

The alphabet is essentially syllabic, only 6 characters (a e i o s u) correspond to Roman letters: the font encodes these to the corresponding roman letter. The remaining 79 characters have been arbitrarily encoded in the range 38–122; the cherokee package provides commands that map each such syllable to the appropriate character; for example, Segwoya himself would be represented \Cse\Cgwo\Cya.

The font is distributed as Metafont source; it works very poorly in modern environments, and could do with expert attention (if you are interested, please contact the CTAN team for details).

name: chess
caption: Fonts for typesetting chess boards

descriptions.text:
The original (and now somewhat dated) TeX chess font package.

Potential users should consider skak (for alternative fonts, and notation support), texmate (for alternative notation support), or chessfss (for flexible font choices).

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
fonts for typesetting chess problems and diagrams

name: chess-problem-diagrams
caption: A package for typesetting chess problem diagrams

descriptions.text: This package provides macros to typeset chess problem diagrams including fairy chess problems (mostly using rotated images of pieces) and other boards.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: chessboard
caption: Print chess boards

descriptions.text:
This package offers commands to print chessboards. It can print partial boards, hide pieces and fields, color the boards and put various marks on the board. It has a lot of options to place pieces on the board. Using exotic pieces (e.g., for fairy chess) is possible.

The documentation includes an example of an animated chessboard, for those whose PDF viewer can display animations.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: chessfss
caption: A package to handle chess fonts

descriptions.text:
This package offers commands to use and switch between chess fonts. It uses the LaTeX font selection scheme (nfss).

The package doesn't parse, format and print PGN input like e.g. the packages skak or texmate; the aim of the package is to offer writers of chess packages a bundle of commands for fonts, so that they don't have to implement all these commands for themselves. A normal user can use the package to print e.g. single chess symbols and simple diagrams.

The documentation contains also a section about installation of chess fonts.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: chessmin
caption: Minimal chess diagrams

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Defines a macro that takes a delimited string to define a board layout. The board is drawn using chess symbols crudely assembled using blocks; the author remarks that the job is done better with Tutelaers’ chess package, with its associated fonts; modern users have a wide range to choose from.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: chet
caption: LaTeX layout inspired by harvmac

descriptions.text:
The package aims to streamline the work of typesetting, and to provide the look and feel of harvmac for readers.

The package name stands for Class for High Energy Theory, as the majority of individuals using harvmac for their papers were primarily working in high energy theory, a subfield of theoretical physics.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: chextras
caption: A companion package for the Swiss typesetter

descriptions.text: The package simplifies the preparation of Swiss documents and letters by setting up linguistic and common packages. While it is a useful addition to the chletter document class, it is not tied to it and may be used as a general purpose package.

name: chgbar
caption: Draw change bars in the margin

descriptions.text: Defines macros \chgbarbegin and \chgbarend to mark the extent of changes to the document. The change bar is drawn continuously between the lines containing the two macros, but there are issues due to the timing of glue set in the vertical stretchability of the page.

name: chhaya
caption: Linguistic glossing in Marathi language

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: This package provides macros for linguistic glossing as per the rules given by Mumbai University.
मुंबई विद्यापीठाच्या छायालेखन नियमावलीस अनुसरून भाषावैज्ञानिक छायांगांचे संक्षेप पुरवणारा आज्ञासंच.

name: chicago
caption: A <q>Chicago</q> bibliography style

descriptions.text:
Chicago is a BibTeX style that follows the B reference style of the 13th Edition of the Chicago manual of style; a LaTeX package (to LaTeX 2.09 conventions) is also provided.

The style was derived from the newapa style.

name: chicago-annote
caption: Chicago-based annotated BibTeX style

descriptions.text: This is a revision of chicagoa.bst, using the commonly-used annote field in place of the original’s annotation.

name: chicagoa
caption: <q>Chicago</q> bibliography style with annotations

descriptions.text: This is a modification of the author’s chicago style, to support an annotation field in bibliographies.

name: chicagolinks
caption: <q>Chicago</q> bibliography style that allows annotations

descriptions.text: This bibliography style is intended to extend the Chicago bibliography style so that it can be annotated and at the same allowing DOI and URL fields.

name: chickenize
caption: Use Lua callbacks for <q>interesting</q> textual effects

descriptions.text: The package allows manipulations of any LuaTeX document (it is known to work with Plain LuaTeX and LuaLaTeX). Most of the package’s functions are merely for fun or educational use, but some functions (for example, colorstretch for visualising the badness and font expansion of each line, and letterspaceadjust doing what its name says) could be useful in a normal LuaTeX document.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
LuaTeX and packages that require it
support for variations of typographic style

name: chifoot
caption: Chicago-style footnote formatting

descriptions.text: A very short snippet. Will set the footnotes to be conformant with the Chicago style, so the footnotes at the bottom of the page are now marked with a full-sized number, rather than with a superscript number.

name: childdoc
caption: Directly compile \include’d child documents

descriptions.text: This LaTeX2e package enables the direct compilation of document sections included by \include to individual files.

topics.details: include complete documents in other documents

name: china2e
caption: Font and macros for Chinese calendar

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package to produce Chinese calendar symbols of the old Chinese lunisolar calendar. The associated font is distributed as Metafont source.

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas
typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: ChineseJFM
caption: Luatexja-jfm files for Chinese typesetting

descriptions.text: ChineseJFM is a series of luatexja-jfm files for better Chinese typesetting, providing quanjiao, banjiao, and kaiming three styles and other fancy features. It can be used for both horizontal and vertical writing mode in Simplified/Traditional Chinese or Japanese fonts.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: chinesechess
caption: Typeset Chinese chess with l3draw

descriptions.text: This LaTeX3 package based on l3draw provides macros and an environment for Chinese chess manual writing.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: chitex
caption: A Chinese TeX system

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
ChiTeX provides the means for typesetting Chinese in a TeX system, including the necessary fonts.

The bundle provides installation images for either Unix systems (FreeBSD or Linux, using TeX Live), or for Windows systems (using MiKTeX 2.9). In all cases, the TeX distribution should be installed before installing ChiTeX.

name: Chivo
caption: Using the free Chivo fonts with LaTeX

descriptions.text: This work provides the necessary files to use the Chivo fonts with LaTeX. Chivo is a set of eight fonts provided by Héctor Gatti & Omnibus Team under the Open Font License (OFL), version 1.1. The fonts are copyright (c) 2011-2019, Omnibus-Type.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: chkfloat
caption: Warn whenever a float is placed <q>to far away</q>

descriptions.text: The package checks for floats that are placed too far from their origin. It was motivated by a question on the question and answer page.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: chklref
caption: Check for problems with labels in LaTeX

descriptions.text: It is quite common that after modifying a TeX file, many unused labels remain in it. The purpose of chklref is to automatically find these useless labels. It also looks for non starred mathematical environments with no labels and advises the user to use a starred version instead.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: chktex
caption: Check for errors in LaTeX documents

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text: The program reports typographic and other errors in LaTeX documents. Filters are also provided for checking the LaTeX parts of CWEB documents.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: chletter
caption: Class for typesetting letters to Swiss rules

descriptions.text:
The class enables composition of letters fitting into Swiss C5 & C6/5 windowed envelopes. No assumption is made about the language used.

The class is based on the standard LaTeX classes and is compatible with the LaTeX letter class. It is not limited to letters and may be used as a generic document class; it is used with the chextras package.

name: chngcntr
caption: Change the resetting of counters

descriptions.text: Defines commands \counterwithin (which sets up a counter to be reset when another is incremented) and \counterwithout (which unsets such a relationship).

name: chngpage
caption: Change the page layout in the middle of a document

descriptions.text: The package provides broadly similar functionality to changepage, with which it is distributed. It is, however, considered obsolete, and should not be used in new documents.

name: chomsky
caption: Macros to typeset parsing trees

descriptions.text:
Macros for typesetting parsing trees that (apparently) don't rely on any other packages (the trees are drawn in LaTeX picture mode).

The macros were originally advertised for use with LaTeX 2.09, but will probably work with current LaTeX.

name: chordbars
caption: Print chord grids for pop/jazz tunes

descriptions.text: This Tikz-based music-related package is targeted at pop/jazz guitar/bass/piano musicians. They usually need only the chords and the song structure. This package produces rectangular song patterns with one square per bar, with the chord shown inside the square. It also handles the song structure by showing the bar count and the repetitions of the patterns.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: chordbox
caption: Draw chord diagrams

descriptions.text: This package provides two macros for drawing chord diagrams, as may be found for example in chord charts/books and educational materials. They are composed as TikZ pictures and have several options to modify their appearance.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: chroma
caption: Chroma: a reference book of LaTeX colours

descriptions.text:
This reference book presents several lists of colours and their respective parameters in a number of colour models. The lists are constructed either by parameters or by name.

Colours by parameters displays systematic series of colours, based on 3-tuples of numbers that are interpreted as colour parameters in the rgb, cmy, and hsb colour models.

Colours by name displays sets of colours that have been given specific names such that LaTeX users do not have to care about their parametrisation. However, as soon as there is the intention to use these colours outside the LaTeX world (e.g., website construction or drawing programs), the parameters suddenly gain importance. For each colour name, we display:

  • the colour itself plus the name of the underlying model,
  • a 50%-tint (mixture with white),
  • a 50%-tone (mixture with gray),
  • a 50%-shade (mixture with black), and
  • the complementary colour.

Additionally, for the base colours defined by the xcolor package, also all 50%-mixes of base colour pairs are included.

name: chronology
caption: Provides a horizontal timeline

descriptions.text: A timeline package that allows labelling of events with per-day granularity. Other features include relative positioning with unit specification, adjustable tick mark step size, and scaling to specified width.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: chronos
caption:
TikZ-based package for drawing customisable timelines
           with support for colour schemes, styles and memoization

descriptions.text:
The package supports drawing timelines and aims to be highly customisable. Extensive configuration options are offered via a standard key-value interface based on pgfkeys. Custom colour schemes and styles are supported, and the package includes documented examples of each. Memoization works out-of-the-box if the memoize package is loaded.

The code was developed as a result of questions concerning difficulties in customising the output of existing packages for drawing timelines, which sometimes eschew pgfkeys and are often challenging to configure, even when based on PGF/TikZ.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: chronosys
caption: Drawing time-line diagrams

descriptions.text: Macros to produce time line diagrams. Interfaces for Plain TeX, ConTeXt and LaTeX are provided.

name: chs-physics-report
caption: Physics lab reports for Carmel High School

descriptions.text:
This package may optionally be used by students at Carmel High School in Indiana in the United States to write physics lab reports for FW physics courses. As many students are beginners at LaTeX, it also attempts to simplify the report-writing process by offering macros for commonly used notation and by automatically formatting the documents for students who will only use TeX for mathematics and not typesetting.

The package depends on amsmath, calc, fancyhdr, geometry, graphicx, letltxmacro, titlesec, transparent, and xcolor.

name: chscite
caption: Bibliography style for Chalmers University of Technology

descriptions.text: The package, heavily based on the harvard package for Harvard-style citations, provides a citation suite for students at Chalmers University of Technology that follows given recommendations.

name: churchslavonic
caption: Typeset documents in Church Slavonic language using Unicode

descriptions.text:
The package provides fonts, hyphenation patterns, and supporting macros to typeset Church Slavonic texts.

It depends on the following other packages: fonts-churchslavonic, hyph-utf8, intcalc, etoolbox, and xcolor.

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: chuushaku
caption: Flexible book notes in Japanese

descriptions.text:
This style file is designed for compiling book notes in Japanese as part of the body text. (Chuushaku means booknotes in Japanese.)

The remember picture feature automatically calculates coordinates, eliminating the need for manual adjustment of note positions.

The main packages used in chuushaku.sty are TikZ, amsmath, framed, and calc.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: ciad-beamertheme
caption: A beamer theme for creating modern presentations

descriptions.text:
The CIAD Beamer Theme, class and packages constitute a comprehensive LaTeX presentation theme designed according to the guidelines and recommandations of the Connaissance et Intelligence Artificielle Distribuees (CIAD UR 7533) research laboratory at the Université de Technologie Belfort Montbéliard and Université Bourgogne Europe in France.

It provides a professional, visually consistent presentation style with an extensive set of high-level commands that emulate the ease of use found in PowerPoint’s Smart Objects and other graphical layout tools.

This Beamer Theme, class and packages could be easily extended and adapted to reach the requirements and recommandations of your own institution.

ciad-beamertheme is part of the larger project TeX-templates.

documentation.details: Package documentation and example of use

name: cid
caption: Fonts defined by character identifier

descriptions.text:
CID-keyed fonts were developed by Adobe to handle character sets containing large numbers of glyphs, notably for East Asian languages (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.). The glyphs are addressed by number rather than name, and organized into so-called collections.

Several of Adobe’s CID mapping files are distributed as part of ConTeXt. In TeX Live, they are in the directory texmf-dist/fonts/cid.

See the Wikipedia entry, among other places, for more information.

name: cidarticle
caption: A class for submissions to the <q>Commentarii informaticae didacticae</q> (CID)

descriptions.text: The cidarticle bundle is used for writing articles to be published in the Commentarii informaticae didacticae (CID). The LaTeX class file is based on the class used for the Lecture Notes in Informatics (LNI) (https://github.com/gi-ev/LNI).

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: cinzel
caption: LaTeX support for Cinzel and Cinzel Decorative fonts

descriptions.text: Cinzel and Cinzel Decorative fonts, designed by Natanael Gama Natanael Gama), find their inspiration in first century roman inscriptions, and are based on classical proportions. Cinzel is all-caps (similar to Trajan and Michelangelo), but is available in three weights (Regular, Bold, Black). There are no italic fonts, but there are Decorative variants, which can be selected by the usual italic-selection commands in the package’s LaTeX support.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: circ
caption: Macros for typesetting circuit diagrams

descriptions.text:
Several electrical symbols like resistor, capacitor, transistors etc., are defined. The symbols can be connected with wires. The package also contains an American resistor symbol for those of us on that side of the Atlantic.

The package also has simple facilities for producing optics diagrams; however, no-one would deny that the PSTricks pst-optic package, or the MetaPost makecirc package do the job better.

name: circle
caption: Maths mode circles for temporal logic

descriptions.text: Provides circles in math mode that can be used for the nextstep operator of temporal logic, in conjunction with \Box and \Diamond (latexsym) or \square and \lozenge (amssymb). LaTeX circles \circ and \bigcirc are not of the right size. The circles are taken from the font lcircle10. The package contains some hacks to approximate the right size and this solution is definitely not sufficient to give a high quality output.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: circledsteps
caption: Typeset circled numbers

descriptions.text: This package generates circled numbers (or other kinds of markers or small text) to mark steps in procedures, exercises, and so on.

name: circledtext
caption: Create circled text

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package provides a macro \circledtext to typeset circled text. Its starred version can produce an inverted version.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: Circuit_macros
caption: M4 macros for electric circuit diagrams

descriptions.text:
A set of m4 macros for drawing high-quality electric circuits containing fundamental elements, amplifiers, transistors, and basic logic gates to include in TeX, LaTeX, or similar documents. Some tools and examples for other types of diagrams are also included.

The macros can be evaluated to drawing commands in the pic language, which is very easy to understand and which has a good power/complexity ratio. Pic contains elements of a simple programming language, and is well-suited to line drawings requiring parametric or conditional components, fine tuning, significant geometric calculations or repetition, or that are naturally block structured or tree structured. (The m4 and pic processors are readily available for Unix and PC machines.)

Alternative output macros can create TeX output to be read by pstricks, TikZ commands for use by the pgf bundle, or SVG.

name: CircuiTikZ
caption: Draw electrical networks with TikZ

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of macros for naturally typesetting electrical and (somewhat less naturally, perhaps) electronic networks.

It is designed as a tool that is easy to use, with a lean syntax, native to LaTeX, and directly supporting PDF output format. It has therefore been based on the very impressive PGF/TikZ package.

name: circularglyphs
caption: A circular glyphs alphabet

descriptions.text:
Circular Glyphs is a graphic alphabet of substitution based on a geometric construction using circles and arcs on a grid. The designs are all based on circular arcs, divided into four quadrants.

It is inspired by Star Trek and used by the Bynar and Borg cultures depicted there.

name: cirth
caption: Fonts for Cirth

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: This is a font to represent the runic Cirth script devised by Tolkien for his Sindarin language. The font is provided as Metafont source.

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

name: cistercian
caption: Display cistercian numerals

descriptions.text: A TikZ-based package to display cistercian numerals. After loading the package, the macro \cistercian{<number>} can be used to display cistercian numerals. The numerals can be customised via TikZ options.

name: citation-style-language
caption: Bibliography formatting with Citation Style Language

descriptions.text: The Citation Style Language (CSL) is an XML-based language that defines the formats of citations and bibliography. There are currently thousands of styles in CSL including the most widely used APA, Chicago, Vancouver, etc. The citation-style-language package is aimed to provide another reference formatting method for LaTeX that utilizes the CSL styles. It contains a citation processor implemented in pure Lua (citeproc-lua) which reads bibliographic metadata and performs sorting and formatting on both citations and bibliography according to the selected CSL style. A LaTeX package (citation-style-language.sty) is provided to communicate with the processor.

name: cite
caption: Improved citation handling in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package supports compressed, sorted lists of numerical citations, and also deals with various punctuation and other issues of representation, including comprehensive management of break points. The package is compatible with both hyperref and backref.

The package is (unsurprisingly) part of the cite bundle of the author’s citation-related packages.

name: cite-bundle
caption: Citation management bundle

descriptions.text:
A collection of packages related to managing citations:

  • cite, which supports compressed, sorted lists of numerical citations, and also deals with various punctuation and other issues of representation;
  • drftcite, which prints citation keys rather than numbers;
  • overcite, which prints citation numbers in a superscript position; and
  • chapterbib, which permits multiple bibliographies, one per \included file in a document.

name: citeall
caption: Cite all entries of a bbl created with BibLaTeX

descriptions.text: This small package allows to cite all entries of a bbl-file created with BibLaTeX (v1.9).

name: citeref
caption: Add reference-page-list to bibliography-items

descriptions.text: The package does its job without using the indexing facilities, and needs no special \cite-replacement package.

name: citeright
caption: Specify accurate natbib citations for diverse naming conventions

descriptions.text:
This package provides the command \citeright for aliasing in-text citations and specifying their appearance in the list of references.

It is specifically tailored for use with the natbib package and is compatible with citation managers such as BibDesk and JabRef.

The package is intended to provide a means for respecting the diverse naming conventions of cited authors and, in this way, decolonizing academia.

name: citesidx
caption: Produce a citation list for the bibliography

descriptions.text:
The list of citations may appear as a list of page numbers in each cited entry in the bibliography, or in the index.

A modern implementation of the same concept is backref (part of the hyperref distribution), that produces hypertext links from the bibliography to each citation.

name: CJ
caption: BibTeX style for Computer Journal

descriptions.text: Deals with the requirements of the Computer Journal (published by the British Computer Society). These requirements are not met by custom-bib, and this file has been derived from a near approximation produced by custom-bib.

name: cje
caption: LaTeX document class for CJE articles

descriptions.text: The cje article class allows authors to format their papers to Canadian Journal of Economics style with minimum effort. The class includes options for two other formats: review (double spaced, for use at the submission stage) and proof (used by the typesetters to prepare the proof authors will receive for approval).

name: CJHebrew
caption: Typeset Hebrew with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The cjhebrew package provides Adobe Type 1 fonts for Hebrew, and LaTeX macros to support their use. Hebrew text can be vocalised, and a few accents are also available. The package makes it easy to include Hebrew text in other-language documents.

The package makes use of the e-TeX extensions to TeX, so should be run using an e-LaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

name: cjk
caption: CJK language support

descriptions.text:
CJK is a macro package for LaTeX, providing simultaneous support for various Asian scripts in many encodings (including Unicode):

  • Chinese (both traditional and simplified),
  • Japanese,
  • Korean and
  • Thai.

A special add-on feature is an interface to the Emacs editor (cjk-enc.el) which gives simultaneous, easy-to-use support to a bunch of other scripts in addition to the above – Cyrillic, Greek, Latin-based scripts, Russian and Vietnamese are supported.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)
support for typesetting, and documentation in Thai

name: cjk-fonts
caption: Chinese/Japanese/Korean bitmap fonts

descriptions.text:
Fonts to go with the cjk macro package for Chinese, Japanese and Korean with LaTeX2e.

The package aims to supersede HLaTeX fonts bundle.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: cjk-gs-integrate
caption: Tools to integrate CJK fonts into Ghostscript

descriptions.text: This script searches a list of directories for CJK fonts, and makes them available to an installed Ghostscript. In the simplest case, with sufficient privileges, a run without arguments should result in a complete setup of Ghostscript.

name: cjk-ko
caption: Extension of the CJK package for Korean typesetting

descriptions.text:
The package supports typesetting UTF-8-encoded modern Korean documents with the help of the LaTeX2e CJK package. It provides some enhanced features focused on Korean typesetting culture, one of them being allowing line-break between Latin and CJK characters.

The package requires nanumtype1 fonts.

name: cjkpunct
caption: Adjust locations and kerning of CJK punctuation marks

descriptions.text: The package serves as a companion package for CJK.

name: cjs-rcs-article
caption: Article class for The Canadian Journal of Statistics

copyright.owner: Statistical Society of Canada / Société canadienne de statistique

descriptions.text: The document class cjs-rcs-article and its companion bibliographic styles cjs-rcs-en and cjs-rcs-fr typeset manuscripts immediately in accordance with the presentation rules of The Canadian Journal of Statistics. The package also contains the official Author guidelines for The Canadian Journal of Statistics.

documentation.details: Template for an article in English
Template for an article in French

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: cjw
caption: A bundle of packages and classes

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
The bundle contains:

  • a collection of support macros, offering general support, support for various areas of maths, and for typesetting of units,
  • a letter and envelope class,
  • an outlining package, and
  • a package that enables all of Plain TeX usage under LaTeX.

name: clara
caption: A serif font family

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text:
Clara is a type family created specially by Séamas Ó Brógáin for printing A Dictionary of Editing (2015).

The family includes italic, bold, bold italic, and small capitals, while the character set includes (monotonic) Greek, Cyrillic, ogham, phonetic and mathematical ranges, scribal abbreviations and other specialist characters.

The fonts also include some OpenType features (such as ligature substitution, small capitals, and old-style numerals) and variant forms for particular languages.

name: classes
caption: The source of LaTeX’s standard classes

descriptions.text: The article, report, and book classes of current LaTeX (and their class option files) all derive from a single source file, classes.dtx; its contents are extracted to the class files themselves in the course of installing LaTeX.

name: classico
caption: URW Classico fonts

descriptions.text:
The archive provides type 1 fonts with metrics and LaTeX support files. URW Classico is a revision for the URW++ foundry by Hermann Zapf of his very well-known Optima sans serif typeface.

The original fonts were made available for non-commercial distribution by Artifex software. URW++ has corrected the original fonts and added many accented glyphs.

The type 1 fonts and LaTeX support files (for traditional engines) were generated using otf2tfm, cfftot1, and autoinst.

font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: classics
caption: Cite classic works

descriptions.text:
The package provides a basic framework to cite classic works (specially from authors such as Homer, Plato, Aristotle, Descartes, Hume, and Kant) in accordance with traditional pagination systems.

It may be used in conjunction with other citation packages.

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: ClassicThesis
caption: A classically styled thesis package

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text:
This package provides an elegant layout designed in homage to Bringhurst’s The Elements of Typographic Style. It makes use of a range of techniques to get the best results achievable using TeX.

Included in the bundle are templates to make thesis writing easier.

name: classif2
caption: Biological classification tables

descriptions.text:
The package defines an environment classif that simplifies the process of typesetting classification tables.

The package is part of the shipunov bundle.

name: classlist
caption: Record classes used in a document

descriptions.text:
Load this package before \documentclass:

\RequirePackage{classlist} \documentclass[some,options]{whatever}

After doing this, \MainClass contains the name of the first loaded class, \ClassList contains a set of triples <class name>, <options directly requested>, and <version requested>. (The package may also be loaded after \documentclass, in which case some information is not available.)

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: classpack
caption: XML mastering for LaTeX classes and packages

descriptions.text: The package provides an experiment in using XML (specifically DocBook 5) to mark up and maintain LaTeX classes and packages. XSLT 2 styleheets generate the .dtx and .ins distribution files expected by end users.

name: ClawXiv
caption: Provenance typesetting for human–AI collaborative writing

descriptions.text: The clawxiv package provides LaTeX environments for typesetting text according to its authorial provenance in documents that mix human and AI contributions. Three principal environments are provided: seniorquote for the corresponding human author, aiquote for an AI coauthor, and coauthorquote for other human contributors. Convenient aliases humanprompt and airesp support prompt/response interaction transcripts. The package is part of the ClawXiv framework for archiving human–AI co-authored papers with full provenance tracking. A white paper is available at ClawXiv

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: cleanthesis
caption: A clean LaTeX style for thesis documents

descriptions.text: The package offers a clean, simple, and elegant LaTeX style for thesis documents.

name: clearsans
caption: Clear Sans fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
Clear Sans was designed by Daniel Ratighan at Monotype under the direction of the User Experience team at Intel’s Open Source Technology Center. Clear Sans is available in three weights (regular, medium, and bold) with corresponding italics, plus light and thin upright (without italics). Clear Sans has minimized, unambiguous characters and slightly narrow proportions, making it ideal for UI design. Its strong, recognizable forms avoid distracting ambiguity, making Clear Sans comfortable for reading short UI labels and long passages in both screen and print.

The fonts are available in both TrueType and Type 1 formats.

name: clefval
caption: Key/value support with a hash

descriptions.text: This package provides only two macros viz. \TheKey and \TheValue to define then use pairs of key/value and gives a semblance of a hash. Syntax: \TheKey{key}{value} to define the value associated to the key, does not produce text; \TheValue{key} to return the value linked to the key. Both arguments of \TheKey are moving as LaTeX defines the term and we have sometimes to protect them.

name: cleveref
caption: Intelligent cross-referencing

descriptions.text:
The package enhances LaTeX’s cross-referencing features, allowing the format of references to be determined automatically according to the type of reference. The formats used may be customised in the preamble of a document; babel support is available (though the choice of languages remains limited: currently Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Russian, Spanish and Ukrainian).

The package also offers a means of referencing a list of references, each formatted according to its type. In such lists, it can collapse sequences of numerically-consecutive labels to a reference range.

name: cleveref-forward
caption: Forward-referencing functionality for cleveref

descriptions.text:
This package aims at providing the forward-referencing functionality for the package cleveref.

It is derived from the package cleveref-usedon, with several fixes and enhancements.

name: cleveref-icelandic
caption: Icelandic grammatical declension for cleveref cross-references

descriptions.text: The cleveref-icelandic package extends cleveref with Icelandic declension support, allowing cross-references to figures, tables, equations, and sections to appear in the correct grammatical case (nominative, accusative, dative, genitive) in both singular and plural. Case can be specified explicitly by name (nom/acc/dat/gen or Icelandic abbreviations nf/þf/þgf/ef), by number (0–3), or automatically inferred from a preposition argument. Built-in declension tables are provided for the four most common reference types. Additional reference types and prepositions can be declared in the document preamble using \DeclareIcrefType and \DeclareIscrefPreposition.

topics.details: support for typesetting the Icelandic language

name: cleveref-usedon
caption: Adds forward-referencing functionality to the cleveref package

descriptions.text:
Imagine you are reading a long mathematical text such as a text book or a thesis.

There are plenty of supplementary lemmas, propositions, theorems and/or exercises throughout the whole text.

You ask yourself Gosh, while Lemma 1.12 is certainly an interesting result, where is this result used later on in this long text? I really would find that helpful to decide why I should read the proof.

You can, of course, use the PDF search function of your viewer to look up the string Lemma 1.12, but wouldn’t it be more helpful if Lemma 1.12 already indicated all or at least its most useful/crucial applications via an info message?

This is what this package tries to address: The info message Used on p. 40, 43-45 and 101. would then be printed to the header of Lemma 1.12.

This is done by extending the \cref and \Cref commands and giving them an optional argument UsedOn. Every time you wish to record a reference in the used on page list, you would simply type \cref[UsedOn]{<LabelName>}. If you use \cref without this optional argument, this reference won’t be recorded in this page list.

name: clicks
caption: Slide Deck Animation

descriptions.text: With the help of this package you can simulate animation in your slide deck, making it look similar to what PowerPoint can do.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: clip
caption: A language-independent literate programming tool

descriptions.text: The CLiP approach to literate programming relies on coding style. As a result, code extraction is completely independent of the text processing environment. (CLiP may even be used in combination with a wordprocessor.) Equally, addition the CLiP mechanism is independent of programming languages as well, and the CLiP style is easily adapted to any language.

name: clipboard
caption: Copy and paste into and across documents

descriptions.text: The clipboard package provides a basic framework for copying and pasting text and commands into and across multiple documents. It replaces the copypaste package.

name: clistmap
caption: Map and iterate over LaTeX3 clists

descriptions.text: This package provides a key-based interface for defining templates whose job is to partition LaTeX3 clists and map differentiatedly across its components.

name: clock
caption: Graphical and textual clocks for TeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text: Features graphical clocks (with a classical 12h dial and two hands) and text clocks (in 24h format) which can show system time or any time the user desires. Works with both TeX and LaTeX. The clock faces (appearances of the dial) are easily expandable; the default uses a custom Metafont font.

name: clojure-pamphlet
caption: A simple literate programming tool based on clojure’s pamphlet system

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: The Clojure pamphlet system is a system based on the Clojure literate system. In the Clojure's pamphlet system you have your main LaTeX file, which can be compiled regularly. This file contains documentation and source code (just like in other forms of literate programming). These code snippets are wrapped in the chunk environment, hence they can be recognized by the tangler in order to extract them. Chunks can be included inside each other by the getchunk command (which will be typeset accordingly). Finally, the LaTeX file will be run through the tangler to get the desired chunk of code.

name: closefrm
caption: Tidy up after reading a MetaPost file

descriptions.text:
Defines a closefrom macro to complement the readfrom primitive. It operates by repeatedly reading from a file until reaching EOF, which has the side-effect of closing the file.

The macro might be useful to avoid running out of read files when using the MetaPost graph package to process many data files that contain extra junk at the end. (In such circumstances, reading the files will stop short of the end, so leaving the file open.)

name: cloze
caption: A LuaLaTeX package for creating cloze texts

descriptions.text:
This is a LuaTeX or LuaLaTeX package for generating cloze texts. The main feature of the package is that the formatting doesn’t change when using the hide and show options.

There are the commands \cloze, \clozefix, \clozefil, \clozenol, \clozestrike and the environments clozepar and clozebox to generate cloze texts.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: clrdblpg
caption: Control pagestyle of pages left blank by \cleardoublepage

descriptions.text: This tiny package allows easy manipulation of the headers and footers on pages left blank by \cleardoublepage. By default, LaTeX has no easy facilities for this. This package uses more or less the algorithm listed in the fancyhdr package documentation, with some better indentation and added flexibility.

name: clrscode
caption: Typesets pseudocode as in Introduction to Algorithms

descriptions.text: This package allows you to typeset pseudocode in the style of Introduction to Algorithms, Second edition, by Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, and Stein. The package was written by the authors. You use the commands the same way the package's author did when writing the book, and your output will look just like the pseudocode in the text.

name: clrscode3e
caption: Typesets pseudocode as in Introduction to Algorithms

descriptions.text: This package allows you to typeset pseudocode in the style of Introduction to Algorithms, Third edition, by Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, and Stein. The package was written by the authors. Use the commands the same way the package’s author did when writing the book, and your output will look just like the pseudocode in the text.

name: clrstrip
caption: Place contents into a full width colour strip

descriptions.text: This lightweight package provides the colorstrip environment, that places its contents into a full page width colour strip.

name: clsguide
caption: Documentation of LaTeX class and package writing

descriptions.text:
Documentation of commands (other than font-handling commands) that are useful when writing a LaTeX class or package.

Part of a set of documentation that also covers LaTeX3 methods for document authors, font handling, typesetting Cyrillic, LaTeX font encodings, configuration options and modification of LaTeX.

name: cluttex
caption: An automation tool for running LaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This is another tool for the automation of LaTeX document processing, like latexmk or arara.

The main feature of this tool is that it does not clutter your working directory with .aux or .log or other auxiliary files.

It has of course the usual features of automation tools: It automatically re-runs (La)TeX for cross-references. MakeIndex, BibTeX, Biber, or makeglossaries will be executed if a corresponding option is set. Furthermore, cluttex can watch input files for changes (using an external program).

name: cm
caption: Computer Modern fonts

descriptions.text:
Knuth's final iteration of his re-interpretation of a c.19 Modern-style font from Monotype. The family is comprehensive, offering both sans and roman styles, and a monospaced font, together with mathematics fonts closely integrated with the mathematical facilities of TeX itself.

The base fonts are distributed as Metafont source, but autotraced PostScript Type 1 versions are available (one version in the AMS fonts distribution, and also the BaKoMa distribution).

The Computer Modern fonts have inspired many later families, notably the European Computer Modern and the Latin Modern families.

name: cm-afm
caption: Adobe Font Metrics for the CM fonts

descriptions.text: A set of AFM files, derived from the Computer Modern sources; the purpose of creating the files was to make the fonts available to such applications as fontinst.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: cm-gf
caption: Generate GF format for CM

descriptions.text:
A Makefile to generate GF files for the CM fonts.

Note that GF format is typically not used nowadays, except as an intermediate stage, so this package is of little more than academic interest.

name: cm-lgc
caption: Type 1 CM-based fonts for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic

descriptions.text:
The fonts are converted from Metafont sources of the Computer Modern font families, using textrace. Supported encodings are: T1 (Latin), T2A (Cyrillic), LGR (Greek) and TS1. The package also includes Unicode virtual fonts for use with Omega.

The font set is not a replacement for any of the other Computer Modern-based font sets (for example, cm-super for Latin and Cyrillic, or cbgreek for Greek), since it is available at a single size only; it offers a compact set for general working. The fonts themselves are encoded to external standards, and virtual fonts are provided for use with TeX.
