descriptions.text: The package solves two problems: floats in a twocolumn document come out in the right order and allowed float positions are now [tbp]. The package actually merges facilities from fixltx2e and stfloats.

name: dblfnote
caption: Double-column footnotes

descriptions.text:
The package sets the footnotes of a single-column document in two columns; the package offers a range of parameters to determine the exact appearance of the two columns.

The package is part of the yafoot bundle of footnote facilities.

name: dblfont
caption: Blackboard bold font package

descriptions.text:
The dblfont package defines a means of accessing the AMS fonts’ Blackboard Bold letters. The package has largely been superseded by macros in the amsfonts bundle.

The package is part of the bosisio bundle.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: DB_process
caption: Process database output

descriptions.text: Parse the output from a database, delimited by either a tab or comma, and apply a user-defined macro to each line.

topics.details: read, process and convert CSV data

name: dbshow
caption: A package to store and display data with custom filters, orders, and styles

descriptions.text:
The package provides four core functions:

  1. data storage and display
  2. data filtering
  3. data sorting
  4. data display

All data is saved once and then you can display these data with custom filters, orders and styles. The package can be used, for example, to record and display something you’d like to review, maybe the question you always answered incorrectly or some forgettable knowledge. But obviously, the package is much more powerful and extensible for more interesting tasks depending on the individual.

topics.details: prepare data for use within TeX
select data from sets in the TeX file

name: dccpaper
caption: Typeset papers for the International Journal of Digital Curation

copyright.owner: Digital Curation Centre, University of Edinburgh

descriptions.text:
The LaTeX class ijdc-v14 produces camera-ready papers and articles suitable for inclusion in the International Journal of Digital Curation, with applicability from volume 14 onwards; a legacy class ijdc-v9 is provided for papers and articles written for volumes 9-13.

The similar idcc class can be used for submissions to the International Digital Curation Conference, beginning with the 2015 conference.

As of August 2023 these classes are no longer officially supported for new submissions to the IJDC and IDCC, but nevertheless they continue to be maintained to support existing documents.

name: dco
caption: Use the DC fonts with old-style numerals

descriptions.text: The package provides virtual fonts and support files, to use the (now obsolete) DC fonts with all digits replaced by oldstyle digits.

name: dcolumn
caption: Align on the decimal point of numbers in tabular columns

descriptions.text:
The dcolumn package makes use of the array package to define a D column format for use in tabular environments.

This package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: dcounter
caption: Support dynamic counters

descriptions.text:
Counters declared as dynamic are created at the time of their first use and they receive at that moment the count style which was established by the \countstyle command. Special use of the \countstyle command with an optional parameter allows modification of the subordination of existing counters.

This package is part of the ncctools bundle.

name: DCpic
caption: Commutative diagrams in a LaTeX and TeX documents

descriptions.text: DCpic is a package for typesetting Commutative Diagrams within a LaTeX and TeX documents. Its distinguishing features are: a powerful graphical engine, the PiCTeX package; an easy specification syntax in which a commutative diagram is described in terms of its objects and its arrows (morphism), positioned in a Cartesian coordinate system.

name: ddphonism
caption: Dodecaphonic diagrams: twelve-tone matrices, clock diagrams, etc

descriptions.text:
This music-related package focuses on notation from the Twelve-Tone System, also called Dodecaphonism. It provides LaTeX algorithms to generate common dodecaphonic diagrams based off a musical series, or row sequence, of arbitrary length.

The package requires TikZ.

name: de-macro
caption: Expand private macros in a document

descriptions.text:
De-macro is a Python script that helps authors who like to use private LaTeX macros (for example, as abbreviations). A technical editor or a cooperating author may balk at such a manuscript; you can avoid manuscript rejection misery by running de-macro on it.

De-macro will expand macros defined in \(re)newcommand or \(re)newenvironment commands, within the document, or in the document’s private package file.

name: debate
caption: Debates between reviewers

descriptions.text: This package helps to organize debates between multiple reviewers of a paper within the text.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: decimal
caption: LaTeX package for the English raised decimal point

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package should be used by people who need the traditional English raised decimal point, instead of the American-style period.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: decimalcomma
caption: Comma for decimal numbers

descriptions.text:
This small package offers a new definition of the comma , as an active character. It ensures the correct spacing in mathematical mode when using the comma either as a decimal separator or as a list separator.

With this package, the comma behaves similarly to ncccomma, but the code is lighter, and several compatibility issues have been fixed.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: decision-table
caption: An easy way to create Decision Model and Notation decision tables

descriptions.text:
The decision-table package allows for an easy way to generate decision tables in the Decision Model and Notation (DMN) format. This package ensures consistency in the tables (i.e. fontsize), and is thus a better alternative to inserting tables via images.

The decision-table package adds the \dmntable command, with which tables can be created. This command expands into a tabular, so it can be used within a table or figure environment. Furthermore, this allows labels and captions to be added seamlessly. It is also possible to place multiple DMN tables in one table/figure environment.

The package relies on nicematrix and l3keys2e.

name: declare
caption: Declare register names locally

descriptions.text:
These macros provide a method of locally allocating registers without interference with previously allocated registers; thus \declarecount allocates a count for local use, in exactly the same way that \newcount allocations one for global use. The sequence

{... \declarecount\foo ... \newcount\bar ...}

is of course a logical error; any \new* command should be issued before the corresponding \declare* command.

name: decorule
caption: Decorative swelled rule using font character

descriptions.text:
The package implements a decorative swelled rule using only a symbol from a font installed with all distributions of TeX, so it works independently, without the need to install any additional software or fonts.

This is the packaged version of the macro which was originally published in the Typographers’ Inn column in TUGboat 31:1 (2010).

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.
control the weight of rules, etc., in text

name: decsci
caption: BibTeX style for the journal Decision Sciences

descriptions.text: Generated by custom-bib.

name: dectab
caption: Align columns on a decimal point

descriptions.text: The package defines the command \dec, which allows a construct such as ...& \dec -1.461 &... in a tabular c column; the column will then be centred on the decimal point in the number.

name: default
caption: Provide default parameters for TeX macros

descriptions.text: The command \setdefault defines default values for the arguments of an existing macro; the macro, thus adjusted, is called with square brackets around arguments which are overriding the default. (This is the same scheme as is used in LaTeX.)

name: deflist
caption: A variation on the description environment

descriptions.text: The command deflist evnironment takes an argument, whose width is taken as the maximum width of labels in a description-like environment

name: defoldfonts
caption: Define old font commands

descriptions.text: In 1994, with LaTeX2e, the old font commands \rm, \sf, \tt, \bf, \it, \sl, and \sc became obsolete. This package defines them, and also the deprecated KOMA-Script command \sfb.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: defstring
caption: Define macros as verbatim macros

descriptions.text:
The command \defstring defines its first argument (a control sequence name) as the content of its second argument, with category code other, with surrounding braces added.

The package uses the maybeload and redefine packages.

name: degrade
caption: Degrade JPEG images on the fly, prior to inclusion

descriptions.text: Degrade is a LaTeX package that degrades JPEG images on the fly to decrease the size of the resulting PostScript or PDF file. It uses the convert utility from the ImageMagick bundle as well as jpeg2ps (if you're producing PostScript output).

name: dehyph
caption: German hyphenation patterns for traditional orthography

descriptions.text:
The package provides older hyphenation patterns for the German language. Please note that by default only pdfLaTeX uses these patterns (mainly for backwards compatibility).

The older packages ghyphen and gnhyph are now bundled together with dehyph, and are no longer be updated.

Both XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX use the current German hyphenation patterns taken from Hyphenation patterns in UTF-8, and using the Experimental hyphenation patterns for the German language package it is possible to make pdfLaTeX use the new German patterns as well.

name: dehyph-exptl
caption: Experimental hyphenation patterns for the German language

copyright.owner: Stephan Hennig, Werner Lemberg, Günter Milde,     Sander van Geloven, Georg Pfeiffer, Gisbert W. Selke, Tobias Wendorf,     Keno Wehr

descriptions.text: Dieses Paket enthält experimentelle Trennmuster für die deutsche Sprache. Die Trennmuster decken das in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz gebräuchliche Standarddeutsch in der traditionellen und reformierten Rechtschreibung ab und können mit den Paketen Babel und hyphsubst aus dem Oberdiek-Bündel verwendet werden.

The package provides experimental hyphenation patterns for the German language, covering both traditional and reformed orthography. The patterns can be used with packages Babel and hyphsubst from the Oberdiek bundle.

name: dejavu
caption: LaTeX support for the DejaVu fonts

descriptions.text:
The package contains LaTeX support for the DejaVu fonts, which are derived from the Vera fonts but contain more characters and styles.

The fonts are included in the original TrueType format, and in converted Type 1 format.

The (currently) supported encodings are: OT1, T1, IL2, TS1, T2*, X2, QX, and LGR.

The package doesn't (currently) support mathematics. More encodings and/or features are expected.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

name: dejavu-otf
caption: Support for the ttf and otf DejaVu fonts

descriptions.text:
This package supports the free ttf-fonts from the DejaVu project which are available from GitHub or already part of your system (Windows/Linux/...), and the OpenType version of TeXGyre Math, which is part of any TeX distribution. The following font files are supported:

  • DejaVuSans-BoldOblique.ttf
  • DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf
  • DejaVuSansCondensed-BoldOblique.ttf
  • DejaVuSansCondensed-Bold.ttf
  • DejaVuSansCondensed-Oblique.ttf
  • DejaVuSansCondensed.ttf
  • DejaVuSans-ExtraLight.ttf
  • DejaVuSansMono-BoldOblique.ttf
  • DejaVuSansMono-Bold.ttf
  • DejaVuSansMono-Oblique.ttf
  • DejaVuSansMono.ttf
  • DejaVuSans-Oblique.ttf
  • DejaVuSans.ttf
  • DejaVuSerif-BoldItalic.ttf
  • DejaVuSerif-Bold.ttf
  • DejaVuSerifCondensed-BoldItalic.ttf
  • DejaVuSerifCondensed-Bold.ttf
  • DejaVuSerifCondensed-Italic.ttf
  • DejaVuSerifCondensed.ttf
  • DejaVuSerif-Italic.ttf
  • DejaVuSerif.ttf
  • texgyredejavu-math.otf

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: delarray
caption: Delimiters for arrays

descriptions.text:
Add delimiters (parentheses etc.) around arrays (nesting brackets are automatically inserted).

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle.

name: deleq
caption: Flexible numbering of equations

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Offers more flexible numbering of equations and recycled equations, including partial equation numbers (3a, 3b, etc.).

name: delig
caption: Disable misplaced ligatures in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
DeLig disables misplaced ligatures in LaTeX documents, using a dictionary approach.

With its original fonts, LaTeX always uses ligatures for the letter combinations ff, fi, fl, ffi and ffl.

This is not always correct in the German language, e.g., the word Auflage may not be printed with an fl-ligature, that is, the fl-ligature in Auflage must be disabled.

This may be accomplished by using the babel-package and the two symbols |": Auf"lage.

The Java program DeLig does this job automatically for you, using a ligature word list. Please note that DeLig is only as good as the ligature word list file DeLig.list it relies on.

This version is intended for German language texts only.

DeLig is partially based on the Perl script rmligs by Björn Jacke, in particular the wordlist data is based on his igerman98 dictionary.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: delim
caption: Simplify typesetting mathematical delimiters

descriptions.text: The package permits simpler control of delimiters without excessive use of \big… commands (and the like).

name: delimseasy
caption: Delimiter commands that are easy to use and resize

descriptions.text:
This package provides commands to give a consistent, easy-to-remember, easy to edit way to control the size and blackness of delimiters: append 1–4 bs to command for larger sizes; prepend B for boldface.

These commands reduce the likelihood of incomplete delimiter pairs and typically use fewer characters than the LaTeX default.

name: delimset
caption: Typeset and declare sets of delimiters with convenient size control

descriptions.text: delimset is a LaTeX2e package to typeset and declare sets of delimiters in math mode whose size can be adjusted conveniently.

name: delimtxt
caption: Read and parse text tables

descriptions.text: This experimental package can read and parse text tables delimited by user-defined tokens (e.g., tab). It can be used for serial letters and the like, making it easier to export the data file from MS-Excel/MS-Word

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: delvierre
caption: LaTeX journal article class and example template for Delvierre

descriptions.text: delvierre is a LaTeX journal article class and template bundle for preparing manuscripts for Delvierre publications. The package provides the delvierre> document class, a sample manuscript source, package documentation, and an example graphical abstract asset. It is intended for pdfLaTeX-based journal article preparation.

name: democodetools
caption: A deprecated package for LaTeX code documentation

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This package is no longer supported, fully deprecated. Use (for instance) codedescribe or doctools.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: denisbdoc
caption: A personal dirty package for documenting packages

descriptions.text: A personal dirty package for documenting classes and packages.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: dental-palmer
caption: Typeset Zsigmondy-Palmer dental notation with TikZ

descriptions.text: The dental-palmer distribution provides the palmer LaTeX package for typesetting Zsigmondy-Palmer dental notation using TikZ. It provides the \Palmer command with a key-value interface for alignment, spacing (gap-ratio), midline-bar suppression (no-vert), and quadrant-order control (no-reverse), plus \palmerset for document-wide defaults. It is intended for dental professionals, educators, and researchers preparing clinical and academic documents.

name: deproc
caption: Macros for DECUS proceedings articles

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 (or even earlier) documentstyle that is based on the article style. An example document is included in the distribution.

name: derivative
caption: Nice and easy derivatives

descriptions.text:
Typesetting derivatives and differentials in a consistent way are clumsy and require care to ensure the preferred formatting. Several packages have been developed for this purpose, each with its own features and drawbacks, with the most ambitious one being diffcoeff. While this package is comparable to diffcoeff in terms of features, it takes a different approach. One difference is this package provides more options to tweak the format of the derivatives and differentials. However, the automatic calculation of the total order isn't as developed as the one in diffcoeff.

This package makes it easy to write derivatives and differentials consistently with its predefined commands. It also provides a set of commands that can define custom derivatives and differential operators. The options follow a consistent naming scheme making them easy to use and understand.

name: desclist
caption: Extended <q>description</q> lists

descriptions.text:
The package implements a desclist environment, which is similar to the description environment, but offers more flexibility in formatting labels. The package also modifies the description environment to provide an optional parameter that is a prototype for evaluation of the hanging indentation of the list.

This package is part of the ncctools bundle.

name: designcon
caption: Develop DesignCon papers

descriptions.text: The bundle includes a class file (based on article) and two skeleton documents (one for straight LaTeX and one for Lyx).

name: detex
caption: Strip TeX from a source file

descriptions.text:
Detex is a program to remove TeX constructs from a text file. It recognizes the \input command.

The program assumes it is dealing with LaTeX input if it sees the string \begin{document} in the text. In this case, it also recognizes the \include and \includeonly commands.

The author now considers this program to be retired and Piotr Kubowicz’s OpenDetex as its successor.

topics.details: derive plain text from a TeX document

name: detexfaq
caption: German TeX FAQ

descriptions.text: The PDF document is automatically extracted from the home website.

name: deutschesmuseum
caption: A LaTeX class for contributions to Deutsches Museum publications

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX class for contributions to Deutsches Museum publications.

name: devanagari
caption: Typeset Devanagari

descriptions.text:
Frans Velthuis’ preprocessor for Devanagari text, and fonts and macros to use when typesetting the processed text. The macros provide features that support Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi, Nepali, and other languages typically printed in the Devanagari script.

The package provides fonts, in both Metafont and Type 1 formats.

Users of modern TeX distributions may care to try the XeTeX based package, which is far preferable for users who can type Unicode text.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: devanagari-omega
caption: Typeset Devanagari with Omega

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent
Omega and packages that use it

name: development
caption: BibTeX style file for the journal Development

descriptions.text: Here is a BibTeX style file for biologists interested in submitting an article to the journal `Development'.

name: dfg-crc
caption: Create DFG Collaborative Research Centre proposals and CVs

descriptions.text: The dfg-crc LuaLaTeX class supports preparation of Collaborative Research Centre proposals and CV sections for the German Research Foundation (DFG). Structured metadata drives project and person references, project heads, staff and funding tables, proposal-wide totals, collaboration plots, Gantt charts, and reusable project templates. The bundle is an independent, unofficial template and is not published, endorsed, or maintained by the DFG.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
typeset proposals to funding bodies, etc

name: dfgproposal
caption: Support for writing proposals to the DFG

descriptions.text:
The class is a specialisation of the proposal class, for writing proposals to the German Research Council (DFG). Examples of its use are provided elsewhere in the bundle.

The class is distributed as part of the proposal class bundle, and depends on the author’s stex bundle.

topics.details: typeset proposals to funding bodies, etc

name: dhua
caption: German abbreviations using thin space

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands for those abbreviations of German phrases for which the use of thin space is recommended. Setup commands \newdhua and \newtwopartdhua are provided, as well as commands for single cases (such as \zB for z. B., saving the user from typing such as z.\,B.).

To typeset the documentation, the niceverb package, version 0.44, or later, is required.

Das Paket dhua stellt Befehle für sog. mehrgliedrige Abkürzungen bereit, für die schmale Leerzeichen (Festabstände) empfohlen werden (Duden, Wikipedia).

In die englische Paketdokumentation sind deutsche Erläuterungen eingestreut.

name: diabetes-logbook
caption: A logbook for people with type one diabetes

descriptions.text:
Initially a logbook for me, a person with type one diabetes mellitus, this evolved over time into a TeX project, making it prettier and/or easier to use. I’ve made it simple to use, while not forgoing the document’s beauty or the speed of input. The logbook, with slight commenting out and editing, could be used as a journal by anybody, although the template and graphing functionality are set up for people using insulin injections and blood glucose teststrips, as well as counting/estimating carbs, protein, and fat.

Note: The names of the package’s files are not constructed using the long diabetes-logbook, but the acronym dmlb (for diabetes mellitus log book).

name: diadia
caption: Package to keep a diabetes diary

descriptions.text:
The diadia package allows you to keep a diabetes diary. Usually, this means keeping record of certain medical values like blood sugar, blood pressure, pulse or weight. It might also include other medical, pharmaceutical or nutritional data (HbA1c, insulin doses, carbohydrate units). The diadia package supports all of this plus more – simply by adding more columns to the data file! It is able to evaluate the data file and typesets formatted tables and derived plots. Furthermore, it supports medication charts and info boxes.

Supported languages: English, German. Feel free to provide other translation files!

name: diagbox
caption: Table heads with diagonal lines

descriptions.text:
The package’s principal command, \diagbox, takes two arguments (texts for the slash-separated parts of the box), and an optional argument with which the direction the slash will go, the box dimensions, etc., may be controlled.

The package also provides \slashbox and \backslashbox commands for compatibility with the slashbox package, which it supersedes.

diagbox depends on e-TeX as well as the packages array, calc, fp, keyval, and pict2e.

name: diagmac
caption: A diagram drawing package

descriptions.text:
The package comes in two parts: first, some macros that are generally applicable to drawing diagrams in LaTeX; and second, macros specific to drawing category theory diagrams.

The package was written for LaTeX 2.09, but continues to work under LaTeX2e; however, an updated version, that uses pict2e, is also available.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: diagmac2
caption: Diagram macros, using pict2e

descriptions.text: This is a development of the long-established diagmac package, using pict2e so that the restrictions on line direction are removed.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: diagnose
caption: A diagnostic tool for a TeX installation

descriptions.text: Provides macros to assist evaluation of the capabilities of a TeX installation (i.e., what extensions it supports). An example document that examines the installation is available.

name: diagramf
caption: Labelled diagrams in Metafont

descriptions.text: The package provides a means of labelling diagrams each produced as a Metafont character in a font which is produced using the diagramf.mf Metafont package. LaTeX passes data to Metafont (by ordinary LaTeX file-writing mechanisms), and Metafont writes stuff into its log-file, which must then be extracted into a different file so that LaTeX can see it.

name: diagxy
caption: Diagram macros by Michael Barr

descriptions.text:
Diagxy is a general diagramming package, useful for diagrams in a number of mathematical disciplines.

Diagxy is a development of an earlier (successful) package to use the facilities of the xypic bundle.

name: dialogl
caption: Macros for constructing interactive LaTeX scripts

descriptions.text: Gathers together a bunch of code and examples about how to write macros to carry on a dialogue with the user.

name: dialogue
caption: Quote short scripted dialogue in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package defining the dialogue environment for citing short passages of scripted dialogue.

The package is part of the frankenstein bundle of packages.

name: dice
caption: A font for die faces

descriptions.text: A Metafont font that can produce die faces in 2D or with various 3D effects.

name: dichokey
caption: Construct dichotomous identification keys

descriptions.text: The package can be used to construct dichotomous identification keys (used especially in biology for species identification), taking care of numbering and indentation of successive key steps automatically. An example file is provided, which demonstrates usage.

name: dichromacy
caption: Simulation of color vision deficiency, using LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text: Simulate color vision deficiencies, including protanopia, deuteranopia, and tritanopia, in LuaLaTeX documents. This package provides a few simple commands that allow you to control both the type of color deficiency, and the severity of the simulation.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: dickimaw
caption: Books and tutorials from the <q>Dickimaw LaTeX Series</q>

descriptions.text:
The package provides some of the books and tutorials that form part of the Dickimaw LaTeX Series.

Only the A4 PDF of each book is detailed here. Other formats, such as HTML or screen optimized PDF, are available from the package home page.

Books included are:

  • LaTeX for Complete Novices: an introductory guide to LaTeX.
  • Using LaTeX to Write a PhD Thesis: a follow-on from LaTeX for Complete Novices geared towards students who want to use LaTeX to write their PhD thesis.
  • Creating a LaTeX minimal example: describes how to create a minimal example, which can be used as a debugging aid when you encounter errors in your LaTeX documents.

documentation.details: Using LaTeX to Write a PhD Thesis

name: DictSym
caption: DictSym font and macro package

descriptions.text:
This directory contains the DictSym Type1 font designed by Georg Verweyen and all files required to use it with LaTeX on the Unix or PC platforms.

The font provides a number of symbols commonly used in dictionaries. The accompanying macro package makes the symbols accessible as LaTeX commands.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: didactic
caption: Tools for writing teaching material

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros and environments useful for writing teaching material. It provides more semantic environments on top of the standard definition, theorem, and friends: for instance, exercise, activity and question. These are suitably colour-coded when used with Beamer. They occur as normal text in handouts produced by beamerarticle (same style as definition usually has).

It also provides macros for typesetting code listings and output side by side.

Finally, it modifies the appearance of beamer (Berlin-based theme) and memoir (Tufte style layout), if loaded. It is designed to be used with beamer to produce slides and beamerarticle with memoir to produce notes and handouts from the same source.

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: didec
caption: Fixed-point arithmetic with two decimal places

copyright.owner: Prof. Dr. Dr. Thomas F. Sturm

descriptions.text:
This package supports fixed-point arithmetic with two decimal places (di-decimal) which is typical for financial transactions in many currencies.

The intended use case is (personal) bookkeeping.

name: diffcoeff
caption: Write differential coefficients easily and consistently

descriptions.text:
This package allows the easy and consistent writing of ordinary, partial and other derivatives of arbitrary (algebraic or numeric) order. For mixed partial derivatives, the total order of differentiation is calculated by the package. Optional arguments allow specification of points of evaluation (ordinary derivatives), or variables held constant (partial derivatives), and the placement of the differentiand (numerator or appended).

The package is built on xtemplate and the configurability it enables, extending to differentials (including simple line elements) and jacobians.

name: digestif
caption: Editor plugin for LaTeX, ConTeXt etc

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: Digestif is a code analyzer, and a language server, for LaTeX, plain TeX, ConTeXt and Texinfo. It provides context-sensitive completion, documentation, code navigation, and related functionality to any text editor that speaks the LSP protocol.

topics.details: package will use LuaTeX facilities if available
plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

name: digicap-pro
caption: Creates captions to digital photos

descriptions.text:
The digicap-pro package creates captions to digital photos or graphics and selectively places them on top with a selected opacity. Captions can be static or they can be rollovers.

As a bonus, the document author can create a photo album complete with thumbnail versions of the photos, which when clicked, the fullsize photo appears with caption and title.

Adobe Distiller is required.

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: digiconfigs
caption: Writing <q>configurations</q>

descriptions.text: In Stochastic Geometry and Digital Image Analysis some problems can be solved in terms of so-called configurations. A configuration is basically a square matrix of \circ and \bullet symbols. This package provides a convenient and compact mechanism for displaying these configurations.

name: dijkstra
caption: Dijkstra algorithm for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This small package uses the Dijkstra algorithm for weighted graphs,directed or not: the search table of the shortest path can be displayed, the minimum distance between two vertices and the corresponding path are stored in macros.

This packages depends on simplekv.

topics.details: finite-state machines, automata, labelled graphs, etc.

name: dimnum
caption: Commands for dimensionless numbers

descriptions.text: This package simplifies the calling of Dimensionless Numbers in math or text mode.

topics.details: macros for defining abbreviations in documents

name: din1505
caption: Bibliography styles for German texts

descriptions.text: A set of bibliography styles that conformt to DIN 1505, and match the original BibTeX standard set (plain, unsrt, alpha and abbrv), together with a style natdin to work with natbib.

name: dinat
caption: Bibliography style for German texts

descriptions.text: Bibliography style files intended for texts in german. They draw up bibliographies in accordance with the german DIN 1505, parts 2 and 3.

name: dinbrief
caption: German letter DIN style

descriptions.text:
Implements a document layout for writing letters according to the rules of DIN (Deutsches Institut für Normung, German standardisation institute). A style file for LaTeX 2.09 (with limited support of the features) is part of the package. Since the letter layout is based on a German standard, the user guide is written in German, but most macros have English names from which the user can recognize what they are used for. In addition there are example files showing how letters may be created with the package.

A graphical interface for use of the dinbrief is provided in the dinbrief-GUI bundle.

name: dinbrief-gui
caption: GUI for LaTeX package dinbrief

descriptions.text: Graphical user interface for the LaTeX package dinbrief. The GUI is available as a Windows executable, as a Tcl/Tk script, and as Tclkit. It's small, fast, and for just writing letters, it's better-featured than any word processor!

name: dingbat
caption: Two dingbat symbol fonts

descriptions.text:
The fonts (ark10 and dingbat) are specified in Metafont; support macros are provided for use in LaTeX.

An Adobe Type 1 version of the fonts is available in the niceframe fonts bundle.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: directory
caption: An address book using BibTeX

descriptions.text: A package for LaTeX and BibTeX that facilitates the construction, maintenance and exploitation of an address book-like database.

topics.details: lists of addresses, for a personal directory (or the like)

name: directtex
caption: TeX for the Macintosh

descriptions.text: DirectTeX Pro contains a shell, an integrated text editor, an integrated tool to view and print DVI files, TeX 3.14159, Metafont 2.718, BibTeX, MakeIndex, dvips, all TeX and Metafont related tools like DVIType, GFToPK,... No other software is needed for typesetting and printing TeX documents.

name: dirtree
caption: Display trees in the style of windows explorer

descriptions.text:
This package is designed to emulate the way windows explorer displays directory and file trees, with the root at top left, and each level of subtree displaying one step in to the right.

The macros work equally well with Plain TeX and with LaTeX.

name: dirtreex
caption: Directory tree rendering for LaTeX with TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package provides a self-contained tool for rendering directory trees in an optionally breakable, fully styleable frame. Built directly on TikZ and zref, it works natively without requiring tcolorbox, dirtree, shell escape, or external scripts.

Its main features include automatically tracked depth, so that \dir and \file commands can be nested naturally; breakable frames whose borders, background, and vertical connection lines continue across page boundaries; extensive customization with per-tree and per-entry settings for line colors, line widths, and elbow radii; and CJK-friendly operation with ctex and LuaTeX.

name: dirtytalk
caption: A package to typeset quotations easier

descriptions.text: The package provides a macro to typeset quotations, using the command \say{stuff}. The quotation mark glyphs are inserted by the macro; nested quotations are detected.

name: disser
caption: Class and templates for typesetting dissertations in Russian

descriptions.text:
Disser comprises a document class and set of templates for typesetting dissertations in Russian. One of its primary advantages is a simplicity of format specification for titlepage, headers and elements of automatically generated lists (table of contents, list of figures, etc).

Bibliography styles, that conform to the requirements of the Russian standard GOST R 7.0.11-2011, are provided.

name: ditaa
caption: Use ditaa diagrams within LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: With this package ditaa (DIagrams Through Ascii Art) diagrams can be embedded directly into LaTeX files.

name: dithesis
caption: A class for undergraduate theses at the University of Athens

descriptions.text:
The class conforms to the requirements of the Department of Informatics and Telecommunications at the University of Athens regarding the preparation of undergraduate theses, as of Sep 1, 2011.

The class is designed for use with XeLaTeX; by default (on a Windows platform), the font Arial is used, but provision is made for use under Linux (with a different sans-serif font).

name: divine
caption: LaTeX support for the divine font

descriptions.text: The package provides support files for the Divine Font Family from the T-26 foundry.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: djgpp
caption: DJGPP-based version of TeX for MS-DOS

descriptions.text: This is a port of the Web2C distribution to use the DJGPP 2.01 environment.

name: dk-bib
caption: Danish variants of standard BibTeX styles

descriptions.text:
Dk-bib is a translation of the four standard BibTeX style files (abbrv, alpha, plain and unsrt) and the apalike style file into Danish.

The files have been extended with URL, ISBN, ISSN, annote and printing fields which can be enabled through a LaTeX style file.

Dk-bib also comes with a couple of Danish sorting order files for BibTeX8.

topics.details: support for typesetting, or documentation in Danish

name: dkhyphen
caption: Danish hyphenation patterns

topics.details: support for typesetting, or documentation in Danish

name: dktools
caption: Tools and libraries by Dirk Krause

descriptions.text:
This bundle, which provides a number of tools and libraries by Dirk Krause, is no longer available on CTAN. It is now available only at its SourceForge project page.

The project does not contain any LaTeX packages, but source code to build executable programs. During the last years, many programs unrelated to LaTeX have been added. Therefore, the CTAN is no longer a suitable place to host the entire project.

The programs related to LaTeX are:

  • wxdkdraw: Minimalistic drawing program for use with LaTeX
  • wxd2lat: Convert wxdkdraw drawings to PDF+TeX, EPS+TeX, TeX (PGF)
  • bmpp: Convert PNG, JPEG, TIFF to PDF, PS, EPS
  • fig2lat: Convert *.fig to PS(+TeX), PDF(+TeX), PGF
  • dk-t2l: Convert plain text to LaTeX
  • plpdftex: Output driver for octpgfpl to produce PDF+TeX

name: dlfltxb
caption: Macros related to <q>Introdktion til LaTeX</q>

descriptions.text:
The bundle contains various macros either used for creating the author’s book Introduktion til LaTeX (in Danish), or presented in the book as code tips.

The bundle comprises:

  • dlfltxbcodetips: various macros helpful in typesetting mathematics;
  • dlfltxbmarkup: provides macros used throughout, for registering macro names, packages etc. in the text, in the margin and in the index, all by using categorised keys (note, a configuration file may be used; a sample is included in the distribution);
  • dlfltxbtocconfig: macros for the two tables of contents that the book has;
  • dlfltxbmisc: various macros for typesetting LaTeX arguments, and the macro used in the bibliography that can wrap a URL up into a BibTeX entry.

Interested parties may review the book itself on the web at the author’s institution (it is written in Danish).

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book
support for typesetting, or documentation in Danish

name: dlrg-templates
caption: Templates for the German Lifesaving Association (DLRG)

descriptions.text: This bundle provides templates for members of the German Lifesaving Association (DLRG). This includes the letter template, presentations, specialist publications and press releases. These templates are based on the current cooperative design. They can be adapted to the local structure with simple settings.

name: dmfonts
caption: Virtual fonts to provide T1 encoding

descriptions.text:
A set of virtual fonts to provide a simulacrum of the DC (i.e., prototype Computer Modern T1-encoded) fonts, from previously existing resources such as Knuth's Computer Modern.

The similar AE set, based on the final version of T1-fonts specification, is recommended in place of this obsolete package.

name: dmhgener
caption: Equation, figure (etc.) numbering and referencing

descriptions.text: The file provides a set of macros for numbering equations, figures and tables, and also a method for citing these objects and for citing things in separate documents. All references are numbered per chapter, and a chapter command is provided that deals with the chapter number. (Section and subsection commands are also provided, but with no provision for numbering.)

name: dnaseq
caption: Format DNA base sequences

descriptions.text:
Defines a means of specifying sequences of bases. The bases may be numbered (per line) and you may specify that subsequences be coloured.

For a more vanilla-flavoured way of typesetting base sequences, the user might consider the seqsplit package.

name: dnsrecord
caption: Typeset DNS records, zone files, propagation tables, and DNSSEC chains

descriptions.text: A comprehensive LaTeX package for typesetting DNS (Domain Name System) data in technical documents. Provides 22 color-coded record type commands (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, PTR, SRV, CAA, DNSKEY, DS, RRSIG, NSEC, NSEC3, TLSA, HTTPS, SVCB, SPF, DKIM, DMARC), seven environments for zone file tables, propagation status displays, DNSSEC chain-of-trust diagrams, DNS health check reports, email authentication summaries, latency comparisons, and provider tables. Includes utility commands for formatting domains, IPs, TTLs with human-readable conversion, DNS response codes, and query flags. Designed for network engineers, system administrators, security researchers, and computer science academics writing papers, theses, and operational documentation.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: do-it-yourself-tex
caption: Back to Plain XeTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides a collection of easily modifiable forms, macros and sample texts for use with plain TeX/XeTeX.

Plain TeX, as demonstrated by the myriad of articles and books dating from before the advent of LaTeX, is capable of producing fine typography. It has the advantage of not being as obscure as far as macros, font designation etc. are concerned, and this package is intended to be another contribution to the repertoire in terms of macros, forms and examples.

XeTeX, which works without the necessity of further manipulation of classical TeX documents, has the further advantage of understanding Unicode, for which many open source fonts are available. In additon, XeTeX’s immediate output is an extended variant of DVI format, which is ordinarily processed by a tightly bound processor (called xdvipdfmx) that produces PDF, i.e. if you type: xetex file_01.tex, you obtain: file_01.pdf.

This package provides easily modifiable forms and macros which illustrate how plain XeTeX can be used to produce high quality texts with such features as precise font designations, imported images, marginal notes, colour, right to left texts and syllabics. Real examples are provided in both the TeX and PDF versions. A set of shell files, font tables, and an HTML page with links to font sources are also provided.

topics.details: package will use XeTeX facilities if available
XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: doafter
caption: Do things after a group

descriptions.text:
The doafter package provides a \doafter command that allows you to execute a single token (typically a command) after a TeX group (either between braces or \begingroup/\endgroup) and all its \aftergroup-saved stuff.

The package is part of the mdwtools bundle.

name: doc
caption: Format LaTeX documentation

descriptions.text:
The package provides definitions that are necessary to format the documentation of LaTeX kernel and package source files (Literate LaTeX), which incorporate both the documentation and the code.

This package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: doc-pictex
caption: A summary list of PicTeX documentation

descriptions.text: A summary of available resources providing (or merely discussing) documentation of PicTeX.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: docarc
caption: Multi-user distributed bibliographic database system

descriptions.text:
Document Archive is a bibliographic database system (which can also store document files) that runs over the Web to allow multiple users (e.g., a workgroup) to access the same bibliographic data. One may use the command line interface to replace .bib-files (required citations are downloaded automatically) or a web browser (a Mozilla plugin is provided) to easily browse through the stored documents.

The package may be downloaded via its home page on Sourceforge.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: docassembly
caption: Use the Acrobat JavaScript API

descriptions.text:
This package defines the docassembly environment in which JavaScript code can be written to execute once and only once the newly created PDF in the Acrobat application. The package also defines a series of helper commands to execute security restricted JavaScript methods.

The package depends on acrotex-js.

name: docbytex
caption: Creating documentation from source code

descriptions.text: The package creates documentation from C source code, or other programming languages.

name: docext
caption: Extension for documenting the LaTeX source files

descriptions.text:
This package is an extension for documenting LaTeX source files.

It provides an environment codedemo for typesetting the code within a verbatim and a demo environment at the same time.

It fixes the errors of the doc package under the engines pTeX and upTeX, and the classes book and report (or any class that uses the titlepage environment in \maketitle).

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: doclicense
caption: Support for putting documents under a license

descriptions.text:
This package allows you to put your document under a license and include a link to read about the license or include an icon or image of the license.

Currently, only Creative Commons is supported, but this package is designed to handle all kinds of licenses.

name: docmfp
caption: Document non-LaTeX code

descriptions.text: Extends the doc package to cater for documenting non-LaTeX code, such as Metafont or MetaPost, or other programming languages.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: docmute
caption: Input files ignoring LaTeX preamble, etc

descriptions.text: Input or include stand-alone LaTeX documents, ignoring everything but the material between \begin{document} and \end{document}.

topics.details: include complete documents in other documents

name: docshots
caption: TeX samples next to their PDF snapshots

descriptions.text: This package helps you render TeX examples from your DTX documentation and then embed PDF snapshots into it, next to the source TeX code.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: docstrip
caption: Remove comments from file

descriptions.text:
The package prepares a LaTeX kernel or package source file for actual use, by removing the documentation and meta-data. The package can conditionally include parts of the source file, generate many files from a single source, and generate a single output from several source files.

The package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: docsurvey
caption: A survey of LaTeX documentation

descriptions.text: A survey of programming-related documentation for LaTeX. Included are references to printed and electronic books and manuals, symbol lists, FAQs, the LaTeX source code, CTAN and distributions, programming-related packages, users groups and online communities, and information on creating packages and documentation.

topics.details: document reviewing subjects relevant for TeX users

name: doctools
caption: Tools for the documentation of LaTeX code

descriptions.text: The package provides a collection of tools for use either in an ordinary LaTeX document, or within a .dtx file.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: documentation
caption: Documentation support for C, Java and assembler code

descriptions.text: The package provides a simple means of typesetting computer programs such that the result is acceptable for inclusion in reports, etc.

name: docutils
caption: Helper commands and element definitions for Docutils LaTeX output

descriptions.text:
The package is intended for use with LaTeX documents generated from reStructuredText sources with Docutils.

When generating LaTeX documents, specify this package with the stylesheet configuration option, e.g.

rst2latex --stylesheet=docutils exampledocument.txt

name: dogma
caption: Metrics and LaTeX support for Dogma Font from Emigre Graphics

descriptions.text: This package provides metric files and LaTeX support for the Dogma font family from Emigre Graphics, designed by Zuzana Licko in 1994. It has everything you need to typeset in this font – except, of course, the font itself.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: doi
caption: Create correct hyperlinks for DOI numbers

descriptions.text: You can hyperlink DOI numbers to doi.org. However, some publishers have elected to use nasty characters in their DOI numbering scheme (<, >, _ and ; have all been spotted). This will either upset (La)TeX, or your PDF reader. This package contains a single user-level command \doi{}, which takes a DOI number, and creates a correct hyperlink to the target of the DOI.

name: doibanner
caption: Generate DOI banners and links

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package to generate DOI banners and links.

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

name: doipubmed
caption: Special commands for use in bibliographies

descriptions.text: The package provides the commands \doi, \pubmed and \citeurl. These commands are primarily designed for use in bibliographies. A LaTeX2HTML style file is also provided.

name: domaincoloring
caption: Draw colored represenations of complex functions

descriptions.text:
Domain coloring is a technique to visualize complex functions by assigning a color to each point of the complex plane z=x+iy.

This package calculates with the help of Lua any complex function to visualize its behaviour. The value of the complex function(z) can be described by radius and angle which can be two values of the hsv-color model, which then defines the color of each point in the complex plane z=x+iy.

topics.details: plot a representation of a function
LuaTeX and packages that require it
converting graphics files from MetaPost output or (E)PS to embeddable PDF

name: domitian
caption: Drop-in replacement for Palatino

descriptions.text:
The Domitian fonts are a free and open-source OpenType font family, based on the Palatino design by Hermann Zapf (1918-2015), as implemented in Palladio, the version distributed as part of URW's free Core 35 PostScript fonts (2.0).

Domitian is meant as a drop-in replacement for Adobe's version of Palatino. It extends Palladio with small capitals, old-style figures and scientific inferiors. The metrics have been adjusted to more closely match Adobe Palatino, and hinting has been improved.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: dos-dc
caption: A distribution of the DC fonts for emTeX

descriptions.text: Documentation, such as it is, may be found in the distribution.

name: dosepsbin
caption: Deal with DOS binary EPS files

descriptions.text:
A Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) file may given in a special binary format to support the inclusion of a thumbnail. This file format, commonly known as DOS EPS format starts with a binary header that contains the positions of the possible sections:

  • PostScript (PS);
  • Windows Metafile Format (WMF); and
  • Tag Image File Format (TIFF).

The PS section must be present and either the WMF file or the TIFF file should be given.

The package provides a Perl program that will extract any of the sections of such a file, in particular providing a text-form EPS file for use with (La)TeX.

topics.details: manipulating images for inclusion in documents

name: dot2tex
caption: Convert graphs generated by Graphviz to LaTeX friendly formats

descriptions.text:
Dot2tex is a tool for converting graphs rendered by Graphviz to formats that can be used with LaTeX.

The purpose of dot2tex is to give graphs generated by Graphviz a more LaTeX friendly look and feel. This is accomplished by converting xdot output from Graphviz to a series of TikZ and PGF, or PSTricks commands. This approach allows:

  • Typesetting labels with LaTeX, allowing mathematical notation;
  • Using native PSTricks and PGF/TikZ commands for drawing arrows; and
  • Using backend specific styles to customize the output.

Dot2tex requires a Python interpreter v2.4 or better.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: dot2texi
caption: Create graphs within LaTeX using the dot2tex tool

descriptions.text: The dot2texi package allows you to embed graphs in the DOT graph description language in your LaTeX documents. The dot2tex tool is used to invoke Graphviz for graph layout, and to transform the output from Graphviz to LaTeX code. The generated code relies on the TikZ and PGF package or the PSTricks package. The process is automated if shell escape is enabled.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: dotarrow
caption: Extendable dotted arrows

descriptions.text: The package can draw dotted arrows that are extendable, in the same was as \xrightarrow.

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: dotlessi
caption: Provides dotless i’s and j’s for use in any math font

descriptions.text: The package provides two commands: \dotlessi and \dotlessj, which give access to dotless i's and j's in math mode. They are intended for symbols in non English languages.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: dotlessj
caption: Generates a dot-less j

descriptions.text:
If you are using a font set without a dotless j (\j and \jmath) then this package will fake one. It requires the LaTeX color package. It does not require any explicit PostScript support.

The package is part of the carlisle bundle.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: dotseqn
caption: Flush left equations with dotted leaders to the numbers

descriptions.text:
The package provides a different format for typesetting equations, one reportedly used in old style Britsh books: equations aligned on the left, with dots on the right leading to the equation number.

In default of an equation number, the package operates much like the fleqn class option (no leaders).

name: dottex
caption: Use dot code in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The dottex package allows you to encapsulate dot and neato files in your document (dot and neato are both part of graphviz; dot creates directed graphs, neato undirected graphs). If you have shell-escape enabled, the package will arrange for your files to be processed at LaTeX time; otherwise, the conversion must be done manually as an intermediate process before a second LaTeX run.

name: doublecol
caption: Double-column page macros for Plain TeX

descriptions.text: These macros are derived from Knuth’s macros (separately transcribed here), by an unknown hand.

topics.details: more than one column on the page

name: doublespace
caption: Double space environment

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX 2.09 package that defines a spacing environment which you can use anywhere in your document.

This package should no longer be used: it has serious bugs, and is no longer maintained. It is superseded by setspace.

name: doublestroke
caption: Typeset mathematical double stroke symbols

descriptions.text:
A font based on Computer Modern Roman useful for typesetting the mathematical symbols for the natural numbers (N), whole numbers (Z), rational numbers (Q), real numbers (R) and complex numbers (C); coverage includes all Roman capital letters, 1, h and k. The font is available both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format, and LaTeX macros for its use are provided.

The fonts appear in the blackboard bold sampler.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: doulossil
caption: A font for typesetting the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)

descriptions.text: This package provides the IPA font Doulos SIL in TrueType format.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: dow
caption: Calculate day of week from a numeric date

descriptions.text:
Defines two macros:

  • \dowcomp, which calculates the day of the week as a number in the range 0–6, returning the result in a counter \dow, and
  • \dayname, which uses \dowcomp to produce the (English) name of the week day.

name: dowith
caption: Apply a command to a list of items

descriptions.text:
The package provides macros for applying a command to all elements of a list without separators, such as \DoWithAllIn{<cmd>}{<list-macro>} , and also for extending and reducing macros storing such lists. Applications in mind belonged to LaTeX, but the package should work with other formats as well. Loop and list macros in other packages are discussed.

A further package, domore, is also provided, which enhances the functionality of dowith.

name: download
caption: Allow LaTeX to download files using an external process

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to download files (using cURL or wget), from within a document.

To run the external commands, LaTeX (or whatever) needs to be run with the --shell-escape flag; this creates a tension between your needs and the security implications of the flag; users should exercise due caution.

topics.details: run an external program from within a document

name: dox
caption: Extend the doc package

descriptions.text: The doc package provides LaTeX developers with means to describe the usage and the definition of new macros and environments. However, there is no simple way to extend this functionality to other items (options or counters, for instance). The DoX package is designed to circumvent this limitation.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: dozenal
caption: Typeset documents using base twelve numbering (also called <q>dozenal</q>)

descriptions.text:
The package supports typesetting documents whose counters are represented in base twelve, also called dozenal. It includes a macro by David Kastrup for converting positive whole numbers to dozenal from decimal (base ten) representation. The package also includes a few other macros and redefines all the standard counters to produce dozenal output.

Fonts, in Roman, italic, slanted, and boldface versions, provide ten and eleven (the Pitman characters preferred by the Dozenal Society of Great Britain). The fonts were designed to blend well with the Computer Modern fonts, and are available both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts with specific small application areas

name: DPcircling
caption: Decorated text boxes using TikZ

descriptions.text:
This simple package provides four types of text decorations using TikZ. You can frame your text with circles, rectangles, jagged rectangles, and fan-shapes. The baseline will be adjusted properly according to the surroundings. You can use these decorations both in text mode and in math mode. You can specify line color, line width, width, and height using option keys.

Note: The DP in the package name stands for Decorated Packets.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: dpfloat
caption: Support for double-page floats

descriptions.text: Provides fullpage and leftfullpage environments, that may be used inside a figure, table, or other float environment. If the first of a 2-page spread uses a leftfullpage environment, the float will only be typeset on an even-numbered page, and the two floats will appear side-by-side in a two-sided document.

name: dprogress
caption: LaTeX-relevant log information for debugging

descriptions.text:
The package logs LaTeX’s progress through the file, making the LaTeX output more verbose. This helps to make LaTeX debugging easier, as it is simpler to find where exactly LaTeX failed.

The package outputs the typesetting of section, subsection and subsubsection headers and (if amsmath is loaded) details of the align environment.

name: dps
caption: Create a <q>matching</q> game with a hidden message

descriptions.text:
Das Puzzle Spiel is a LaTeX package (dps) for creating a puzzle, a message actually, and a series of questions and answers. The document consumer matches the questions with the answers. With each match, another letter appears in the puzzle. Upon completion of all questions, the message hidden in the puzzle is revealed. The puzzle is primarily designed for the screen, but you can optionally create the game for paper.

The package itself is distributed as a zip file embedded in the package documentation.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: drac
caption: Declare active character substitution, robustly

descriptions.text:
The package provides macros \DeclareRobustActChar and \ReDeclareRobActChar. One uses \DeclareRobustActChar in the same way one would use \DeclareRobustCommand; the macro \protects the active character when it appears in a moving argument.

\ReDeclareRobActChar redefines an active character previously defined with \DeclareRobustActChar, in the same way that \renewcommand works for ordinary commands.

name: draft
caption: A LaTeX 2.09 style for supporting work on drafts

descriptions.text: The package marks \label, \cite, \ref, \index and \glossary commands with a small mark in the text and with a marginal note of the label, citation or whatever itself.

name: draftcopy
caption: Identify draft copies

descriptions.text:
Places the word DRAFT (or other words) in light grey diagonally across the background (or at the bottom) of each (or selected) pages of the document.

The package uses PostScript \special commands, and may not therefore be used with pdfLaTeX. For that usage, consider the wallpaper or draftwatermark packages.

name: draftfigure
caption: Replace figures with a white box and additional features

descriptions.text: With this package you can control the outcome of a figure which is set to draft and modify the display with various options.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: drafthead
caption: Mark <q>DRAFT</q> in page headers

descriptions.text: Sets up page headers including date and time and the string DRAFT, using myheadings page style.

name: draftmark
caption: Put draft marks on selected pages

descriptions.text:
The package can place selected watermarks on a selection of pages. The user may specify content, colour, position and orientation for each watermark.

The package makes use of the atbegshi package.

name: draftwatermark
caption: Put a grey textual watermark on document pages

descriptions.text:
The package provides a means to add a watermark (typically a light gray piece of text) on every page or on the first page of a document. Typical usage may consist in writing words such as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL across document pages.

The package performs a similar function to that of draftcopy, but its implementation is output device independent.

As of December 2020, the package relies on the new shipout hooks directly provided by LaTeX. For users of older versions of LaTeX, the package also provides a legacy version of itself (that is automatically loaded, currently being at release 2.3) which relies on the everypage package. Note that this legacy version will progressively lag behind in terms of features.

topics.details: separate printing, under (or over) the page as a whole

name: drama
caption: Production-style stage script in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package that defines macros for typesetting a basic production-style stage script; the package is not fully debugged.

The package is not supported, and is distributed as one of the frankenstein bundle’s appendices.

name: dramatist
caption: Typeset dramas, both in verse and in prose

descriptions.text: This package is intended for typesetting drama of any length. It provides two environments for typesetting dialogues in prose or in verse; new document divisions corresponding to acts and scenes; macros that control the appearance of characters and stage directions; and automatic generation of a dramatis personae list.

name: dratex
caption: General drawing macros

descriptions.text: A low level (DraTex.sty) and a high-level (AlDraTex.sty) drawing package written entirely in TeX.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: drawing
caption: Simple drawings with Metafont

descriptions.text: A system for producing drawings using Metafont glyphs (or sequences of glyphs, tiled together using the verbatim package).

name: Drawing-with-Metapost
caption: How to draw technical diagrams with MetaPost

descriptions.text: This project provides a document that discusses how to draw technical diagrams with John Hobby’s MetaPost language. It includes over 200 illustrations created with MetaPost, complete with source code as inspiration and examples.

name: drawmatrix
caption: Draw visual representations of matrices in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides macros to visually represent matrices. Various options allow to change the visualizations, e.g., drawing rectangular, triangular, or banded matrices.

name: drawmgr
caption: Macros for centralized management of graphics scripts

descriptions.text: This package provides a tool for collectively managing drawing scripts, which allows users to organize drawing scripts into modules and call them on demand in documents.

name: drawstack
caption: Draw execution stacks

descriptions.text: This simple LaTeX package provides support for drawing execution stack (typically to illustrate assembly language notions). The code is written on top of TikZ.

name: drcaps
caption: Simple dropped capitals

descriptions.text:
The package offers simple macros for dropped capitals, in a couple of forms.

The package is part of the shipunov bundle.

topics.details: drop capitals and flow text around them

name: drftcite
caption: Print the bibliography in <q>draft</q> mode

descriptions.text:
The package arranges that the tags are printed instead of the numbers for \cite and \bibitem.

Drftcite is distributed with the cite bundle of packages.

name: drm
caption: A complete family of fonts written in Metafont

descriptions.text: The package provides access to the DRM (Don's Revised Modern) family of fonts, which includes a variety of optical sizes in Roman (in four weights), italic, and small caps, among other shapes, along with a set of symbols and ornaments. It is intended to be a full-body text font, but its larger sizes can also be used for simple display purposes, and its significant body of symbols can stand on its own. It comes complete with textual (old-style) and lining figures, and even has small-caps figures. It also comes with extensible decorative rules to be used with ornaments from itself or other fonts, along with an extremely flexible ellipsis package.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: droid
caption: LaTeX support for the Droid font families

descriptions.text:
The Droid typeface family was designed in the fall of 2006 by Steve Matteson, as a commission from Google to create a set of system fonts for its Android platform. The goal was to provide optimal quality and comfort on a mobile handset when rendered in application menus, web browsers and for other screen text. The Droid family consists of Droid Serif, Droid Sans and Droid Sans Mono fonts, licensed under the Apache License Version 2.0.

The bundle includes the fonts in both TrueType and Adobe Type 1 formats.

The package does not support the Droid Pro family of fonts, available for purchase from the Ascender foundry.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: droit-fr
caption: Document class and bibliographic style for French law

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a toolkit intended for students writing a thesis in French law.

It features:

  • a LaTeX document class;
  • a bibliographic style for BibLaTeX package;
  • a practical example of french thesis document; and
  • documentation.

The class assumes use of biber and BibLaTeX.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: drop
caption: Dropped capitals at the start of a paragraph (LaTeX 2.09)

descriptions.text:
The macros drop and enlarge the first letter(s) of a paragraph; there is no automation of the font used – the user is prompted for a font name.

The dropping and (especially) lettrine packages, for LaTeX2e, offer far more sophistication and facilities.

topics.details: drop capitals and flow text around them

name: dropcaps
caption: Use dropped capitals to start a paragraph

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: While this package still works as originally intended (as far as it goes), the more sophisticated lettrine package is recommended for the job, nowadays.

topics.details: drop capitals and flow text around them

name: dropping
caption: Drop first letter of paragraphs

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: The package provides A LaTeX2e macro for dropping the first character(s) (or word(s)) of a paragraph, extending the LaTeX 2.09 package dropcaps and automatically taking care of finding the font name. Now largely superseded by lettrine.

topics.details: drop capitals and flow text around them

name: drs
caption: Typeset Discourse Representation Structures (DRS)

descriptions.text:
The package draws Discourse Representation Structures (DRSs). It can draw embedded DRSs, if-then conditions and quantificational duplex conditions (with a properly scaled connecting diamond). Formatting parameters allow the user to control the appearance and placement of DRSs, and of DRS variables and conditions.

The package is based on DRS macros in the covington package.

name: drv
caption: Derivation trees with MetaPost

descriptions.text:
A set of MetaPost macros for typesetting derivation trees (such as used in sequent calculus, type inference, programming language semantics…).

No MetaPost knowledge is needed to use these macros.

name: dsptricks
caption: Macros for Digital Signal Processing plots

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of LaTeX macros (based on PSTricks) for plotting the kind of graphs and figures that are usually employed in digital signal processing publications.

DSPTricks provides facilities for standard discrete-time lollipop plots, continuous-time and frequency plots, and pole-zero plots.

The companion package DSPFunctions (dspfunctions.sty) provides macros for computing frequency responses and DFTs, while the package DSPBlocks (dspblocks.sty) supports DSP block diagrams.

topics.details: package using PStricks for graphical output

name: DSSerif
caption: A double-struck serifed font for mathematical use

descriptions.text: DSSerif is a mathematical font package with double struck serifed digits, upper and lower case letters, in regular and bold weights. The design was inspired by the STIX double struck fonts, which are sans serif, but starting from a Courier-like base.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: dtk
caption: Document class for the journal of DANTE

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a class and style file for typesetting Die TeXnische Komödie – the communications of the German TeX Users Group DANTE e.V. The arrangement means that the class may be used by article writers to typeset a single article, as well as to produce the complete journal.

name: dtk-1.32
caption: Document class for the journal of DANTE

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a class and style file for typesetting Die TeXnische Komödie – the communications of the German TeX Users Group DANTE e.V. The arrangement means that the class may be used by article writers to typeset a single article as well as to produce the complete journal.

Version 1.32 is superseded by a totally rewritten dtk bundle.

name: dtk-bibliography
caption: Bibliography of <q>Die TeXnische Komödie</q>

descriptions.text:
This package contains the bibliography for Die TeXnische Komödie, the journal of the German-speaking TeX User Group.

It is updated on a quarterly basis.

topics.details: document reviewing subjects relevant for TeX users

name: dtl
caption: Tools to dis-assemble and re-assemble DVI files

descriptions.text:
DTL (DVI Text Language) is a means of expressing the content of a DVI file, which is readily readable by humans. The DTL bundle contains an assembler dt2dv (which produces DVI files from DTL files) and a disassembler dv2dt (which produces DTL files from DVI files).

The DTL bundle was developed so as to avoid some infelicities of dvitype (among other pressing reasons).

topics.details: create and/or process text representation of a DVI file

name: dtxdescribe
caption: Describe additional object types in dtx source files

descriptions.text:
The doc package includes tools for describing macros and environments in LaTeX source .dtx format. The dtxdescribe package adds additional tools for describing booleans, lengths, counters, hooks, sockets, plug, keys, packages, classes, options, files, commands, arguments, and other objects, and also works with the standard document classes as well, for those who do not wish to use the .dtx format.

Each item is given a margin tag similar to \DescribeEnv, and is listed in the index by itself and also by category. Each item may be sorted further by an optional class. All index entries except code lines are hyperlinked.

The dtxexample environment is provided for typesetting example code and its results. Contents are displayed verbatim along with a caption and cross-referencing. They are then input and executed, and the result is shown.

Environments are also provided for displaying verbatim or formatted source code, user-interface displays, and sidebars with titles.

Macros are provided for formatting the names of inline LaTeX objects such as packages and booleans, as well as program and file names, file types, internet objects, the names of certain programs, a number of logos, and inline dashes and slashes.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: DTX gallery
caption: A small collection of minimal DTX examples

descriptions.text:
A collection of files that demonstrate simple things that are possible with the flexible and under-appreciated docstrip file format. Each file of the collection is provided as a .dtx file and as the corresponding .pdf.

The set is intended as a companion to Scott Pakin’s excellent and influential dtxtut example of producing LaTeX packages in this way.

topics.details: code that serves as examples of TeX programming

name: dtxgen
caption: Creates a template for a self-extracting .dtx file

descriptions.text: The bash script dtxgen creates a template for a self-extracting .dtx file. It is useful for those who plan to create a new Documented LaTeX Source (.dtx) file.

name: dtxtut
caption: Tutorial on writing .dtx and .ins files

descriptions.text: This tutorial is intended for advanced LaTeX2e users who want to learn how to create .ins and .dtx files for distributing their homebrewed classes and package files.

name: ducksay
caption: Draw ASCII art of animals saying a specified message

descriptions.text:
The package draws ASCII art of animals saying a specified message. The following macros are available:

  • \ducksay
  • \duckthink
  • \DefaultAnimal
  • \AddAnimal
  • \DucksayOptions

Multi-line messages are now fully supported. The package comes with two versions, choosable with the version key.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: duckuments
caption: Create duckified dummy content

descriptions.text:
The package provides facilities to create duckified dummy contents. It was inspired by the question Getting ducks in example images on TeX Stack Exchange.

The following macros are available:

  • \duckument[key=val] – print a short duckument
  • \blindduck[key=val] – print a paragraph
  • \ducklist(*){environment} – create a list of type environment
  • \ducklistlist(*){environment} – create nested lists
  • \duckitemize – ducklist{itemize}
  • \duckenumerate – ducklist{enumerate}
  • \duckdescription – ducklist{description}
  • \duckumentsCreateExampleFile
  • \duckumentsDrawRandomDucks

The package works with pdfTeX, LuaTeX, and XeTeX.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: duerer
caption: Computer Duerer fonts

descriptions.text:
These fonts are designed for titling use, and consist of capital roman letters only. Together with the normal set of base shapes, the family also offers an informal shape. The distribution is as Metafont source.

LaTeX support is available in the duerer-latex bundle.

name: duerer-LaTeX
caption: LaTeX support for the Duerer fonts

descriptions.text: LaTeX support for Hoenig’s Computer Duerer fonts, using their standard fontname names.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: duotenzor
caption: Drawing package for circuit and duotensor diagrams

descriptions.text: This is a drawing package for circuit and duotensor diagrams within LaTeX documents. It consists of about eighty commands, calling on TikZ for support.

name: duplicat
caption: Make duplicate page numbers distinct

descriptions.text:
The package arranges that all pages’ numbers are distinct (as far as output drivers is concerned), by using \count 1 as a running page number. (Dvips distinguishes such duplicates anyway, so that the package is not necessary if you are using dvips for output.

The package is part of the piff bundle.

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

name: dutchcal
caption: A reworking of ESSTIX13, adding a bold version

descriptions.text:
