name: gentl-gr
caption: Modern Greek translation of the Gentle Introduction to TeX

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

name: gentle
caption: A Gentle Introduction to TeX

descriptions.text: The Gentle Introduction is the longest-established comprehensive free tutorial on the use of plain TeX.

name: gentombow
caption: Generate Japanese-style crop marks

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides a LaTeX package for generating Japanese-style crop marks (called tombow in Japanese) for practical use in self-publishing.

The bundle contains the following packages:

  • gentombow.sty: Generate crop marks (called tombow in Japanese) for practical use in self-publishing. It provides the core tombow feature if not available.
  • pxgentombow.sty: Superseded by gentombow.sty; kept for compatibility only.
  • bounddvi.sty: Set papersize special to DVI file. Can be used on LaTeX/pLaTeX/upLaTeX (with DVI output mode) with dvips or dvipdfmx drivers.

topics.details: select pages to be output, etc.

name: geometry
caption: Flexible and complete interface to document dimensions

descriptions.text:
The package provides an easy and flexible user interface to customize page layout, implementing auto-centering and auto-balancing mechanisms so that the users have only to give the least description for the page layout. For example, if you want to set each margin 2cm without header space, what you need is just \usepackage[margin=2cm,nohead]{geometry}.

The package knows about all the standard paper sizes, so that the user need not know what the nominal real dimensions of the paper are, just its standard name (such as a4, letter, etc.).

An important feature is the package’s ability to communicate the paper size it’s set up to the output (whether via DVI \specials or via direct interaction with pdf(La)TeX).

name: geometry-de
caption: German documentation for the geometry package

descriptions.text:
German translation of the geometry documentation, by Hans-Martin Haase of the University of Jena.

Note: This used to be an independent package, but has become part of the main geometry package in January 2020.

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language

name: geomsty
caption: Macros used in typesetting a geometry book

descriptions.text:
Geomsty is a LaTeX 2.09 document style, loosely based on the standard book and article styles.

It provides: inclusion of PostScript figures, and of TeX text within figures; automatic creation of index entries and cross-references where appropriate; no need to worry about fragile commands in almost all situations; greater versatility in defining theorem-like environments; proofing aids such as version numbers and a running index.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: geophysics
caption: Articles for the journal Geophysics

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: The rules implemented are taken from Instructions to authors, Geophysics, January 1986.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: georgian
caption: Support for typesetting in Georgian

descriptions.text: The bundle provides fonts, babel and LaTeX NFSS support, for typesetting text written in Georgian.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: georgian-stanier
caption: A Georgian font

descriptions.text:
The package provides fonts for the Mxedruli alphabet for writing Georgian; the font is available in two shapes – upright and italic.

The fonts are distributed as Metafont source; they work poorly in modern environments, and could do with expert attention (if you are interested, please contact the CTAN team for details).

documentation.details: Readme about the italic shape font

name: geradwp
caption: Document class for the Cahiers du GERAD series

descriptions.text: This package provides the geradwp class, a class based on article and compatible with LaTeX. With this class, researchers at GERAD will be able to write their working paper while complying to all the presentation standards required by the Cahiers du GERAD series.

name: german
caption: Support for German typography

descriptions.text: Supports the old German orthography (alte deutsche Rechtschreibung).

name: germbib
caption: German variants of standard BibTeX styles

descriptions.text:
A development of the (old) german.sty, this bundle provides German packages, BibTeX styles and documentary examples, for writing documents with bibliographies.

The author has since developed the babelbib bundle, which (he asserts) supersedes germbib.

name: germdoc
caption: A collection of documentation available in German

descriptions.text:
Packages covered are:

  • g-brief;
  • german.sty;
  • picinpar; and
  • script (the predecessor of koma-script.

The packages are not collected in this way, on CTAN; this entry provides a convenient reference point.

name: germkorr
caption: Change kerning for German quotation marks

descriptions.text:
The package germcorr has to be loaded after the package german.

It brings some letters like T nearer to german single and double quotes even when that letter wears a standard accent like "`\.T"'.

name: geschichtsfrkl
caption: BibLaTeX style for historians

descriptions.text: The package provides a BibLaTeX style, (mostly) meeting the requirements of the History Faculty of the University of Freiburg (Germany).

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: getargs
caption: A flexible list-parsing macro with configurable parsing character

descriptions.text:
This short package provides a flexible list-parsing macro with the ability to configure the parsing character, as well as the macro names in which the parsed list items are placed. The name of the parsing macro is \getargs.

It is a significant improvement over similarly named macros in the same author’s stringstrings and readarray packages. It is the author’s intent to eventually have the parsers of those other packages point to this package, to achieve a measure of uniformity.

Note: This package has been withdrawn by its author in July 2016. It will be replaced by the forthcoming listofitems package.

name: getfiledate
caption: Find the date of last modification of a file

descriptions.text: The package fetches from the system the date of last modification or opening of an existing file, using the function \pdffilemoddate (present in recent versions of pdfTeX); the user may specify how the date is to be presented.

name: getitems
caption: Gathering items from a list-like environment

descriptions.text: This package provides a \gatheritems command to parse a list of data separated by \item tokens. This makes it easier to define custom environments which structure their data in the same way that itemize or enumerate do.

name: getmap
caption: Download OpenStreetMap maps for use in documents

descriptions.text:
The package provides a simple interface to OpenStreetMap, and to Google Maps map images. In the simplest case, it is sufficient to specify the address you need (if you don’t, the package will use its own default).

The package loads the map image using an external lua script (invoked via \write 18: LaTeX must be running with \write 18 enabled).

The (external) lua script may be used from the command line; a bash version is provided.

topics.details: map production and geographical data usage

name: getoptk
caption: Define macros with sophisticated options

descriptions.text:
The package provides a means of defining macros whose options are taken from a dictionary, which includes options which themselves have arguments.

The package was designed for use with Plain TeX; its syntax derives from that of the \hbox, \hrule, etc., TeX primitives.

name: getrefs
caption: BibTeX style to sort by <q>journal</q> entries of references

descriptions.text: A BibTeX style file to sort entries by source (e.g., journal), thus facilitating the retrieval of references from a library. A LaTeX document template is provided.

name: gettitlestring
caption: Clean up title references

descriptions.text: Cleans up the title string (removing \label commands) for packages (such as nameref) that typeset such strings.

name: gfdl
caption: Support for using GNU Free Documentation License in LaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: The GFDL (GNU Free Documentation License) is a popular license used for programming manuals, documentations and various other textual works too, but using this license with LaTeX is not very convenient. This package aims to help users in easily using the license without violating any rules of the license. With a handful of commands, users can rest assured that their document will be perfectly licensed under GFDL.

name: gfnotation
caption: Typeset Gottlob Frege’s notation in plain TeX

descriptions.text: The package implements macros for plain TeX to typeset the notation invented by Gottlob Frege in 1879 for his books Begriffsschrift and Grundgesetze der Arithmetik (two volumes). The output styles of both books are supported.

name: GFS
caption: The GFS font collection

descriptions.text:
The Greek Font Society has made a large number of fonts publicly available, and this collection reflects those that have been adapted, by Tsolomitis and others, for use with LaTeX. The collection comprises:

  • GFS Artemisia, a relatively modern general-purpose font;
  • GFS Baskerville, based on Baskerville’s classic font;
  • GFS Bodoni, based on Bodoni’s 19th century work;
  • GFS Didot, based on Didot’s 1805 font;
  • GFS Neo-Hellenic, a version of a font developed in Britain in the early 20th century; and
  • GFS Porson, developed from the early 19th century font based on Porson’s writing.

The fonts, except Baskerville and Porson, support the Latin alphabet as well as the Greek alphabet. Neo Hellenic has been matched to the existing CM bright set of mathematics fonts.

topics.details: listing a set of related fonts
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: GFS Artemisia
caption: A modern Greek font design

descriptions.text:
GFS Artemisia is a relatively modern font, designed as a general purpose font in the same sense as Times is nowadays treated. The present version has been provided by the Greek Font Society.

The font supports the Greek and Latin alphabets. LaTeX support is provided, using the OT1, T1 and LGR encodings.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: GFS Baskerville
caption: A Greek font, from one such by Baskerville

descriptions.text: The font is a digital implementation of Baskerville’s classic Greek font, provided by the Greek Font Society. The font covers Greek only, and LaTeX support provides for the use of LGR encoding.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: GFS Bodoni
caption: A Greek and Latin font based on Bodoni

descriptions.text:
Bodoni's Greek fonts in the 18th century broke, for the first time, with the Byzantine cursive tradition of Greek fonts. GFS Bodoni resurrects his work for general use.

The font family supports both Greek and Latin letters. LaTeX support of the fonts is provided, offering OT1, T1 and LGR encodings. The fonts themselves are provided in Adobe Type 1 and OpenType formats.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: GFS Complutum
caption: A Greek font with a long history

descriptions.text: GFS Complutum derives, via a long development, from a minuscule-only font cut in the 16th century. An unsatisfactory set of majuscules were added in the early 20th century, but its author died before he could complete the revival of the font. The Greek Font Society has released this version, which has a new set of majuscules.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: GFSDidot
caption: A Greek font based on Didot’s work

descriptions.text:
The design of Didot’s 1805 Greek typeface was influenced by the neoclassical ideals of the late 18th century. The font was brought to Greece at the time of the 1821 Greek Revolution, by Didot’s son, and was very widely used. The present version is provided by the Greek Font Society.

The font supports the Greek alphabet, and is accompanied by a matching Latin alphabet based on Zapf’s Palatino. LaTeX support is provided, using the OT1, T1, TS1, and LGR encodings.

font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: GFSDidotClassic
caption: The classic version of GFSDidot

descriptions.text: The classic version of GFSDidot provided for Unicode TeX engines.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: GFS NeoHellenic
caption: A font in the Neo-Hellenic style

descriptions.text:
The NeoHellenic style evolved in academic circles in the 19th and 20th century; the present font follows a cut commissioned from Monotype in 1927. The present version was provided by the Greek Font Society.

The font supports both Greek and Latin characters, and has been adjusted to work well with the cmbright fonts for mathematics support. LaTeX support of the fonts is provided, offering OT1, T1 and LGR encodings.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: GFSNeohellenicMath
caption: A math font in the Neo-Hellenic style

descriptions.text:
The GFSNeohellenic font, a historic font first designed by Victor Scholderer, and digitized by George Matthiopoulos of the Greek Font Society (GFS), now has native support for Mathematics.

The project was commissioned to GFS by the Department of Mathematics of the University of the Aegean, Samos, Greece. The Math Table was constructed by the Mathematics Professor A. Tsolomitis. A useful application is in beamer documents since this is a Sans Math font.

The GFSNeohellenic fontfamily supports many languages (including Greek), and it is distributed (both text and math) under the OFL license.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: GFS Porson
caption: A Greek font, originally from Porson

descriptions.text:
Porson is an elegant Greek font, originally cut at the turn of the 19th Century in England. The present version has been provided by the Greek Font Society.

The font supports the Greek alphabet only. LaTeX support is provided, using the LGR encoding.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: GFS Solomos
caption: A Greek-alphabet font

descriptions.text:
Solomos is a font which traces its descent from a calligraphically-inspired font of the mid-19th century.

LaTeX support, for use with the LGR encoding only, is provided.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: ghab
caption: Typeset ghab boxes in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package defines a command \darghab that will typeset its argument in a box with a decorated frame. The width of the box may be set using an optional argument.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: ghostscript
caption: Freely available PostScript interpreter

descriptions.text:
Ghostscript is a freely available PostScript interpreter which is available for many platforms. It is a near-essential complement to a TeX installation, used in many utilities, including PostScript/PDF viewers such as gv and GSview.

Ghostscript is no longer held on CTAN: please see the home page for downloads.

name: ghsystem
caption: Globally harmonised system of chemical (etc) naming

descriptions.text: The package provides the means to typeset all the hazard and precautionary statements and pictograms in a straightforward way. The statements are taken from EU regulation 1272/2008.

name: gia-handout
caption: A LaTeX class for typesetting publications of the German Informatics Association

descriptions.text: This class provides a layout for publications of the Gesellschaft für Informatik e.V. (GI), following its corporate design. (The abbreviation GIA stands for German Informatics Association.)

name: gillcm
caption: Alternative unslanted italic Computer Modern fonts

descriptions.text:
This is a demonstration of the use of virtual fonts for unusual effects: the package implements an old idea of Eric Gill.

The package was written for the author’s talk at TUG 2010.

name: gillius
caption: Gillius fonts with LaTeX support

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Gillius and Gillius No. 2 families of sans serif fonts and condensed versions of them, designed by Hirwen Harendal. According to the designer, the fonts were inspired by Gill Sans.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: gincltex
caption: Include TeX files as graphics (.tex support for \includegraphics)

descriptions.text:
The package builds on the standard LaTeX packages graphics and/or graphicx and allows external LaTeX source files to be included, in the same way as graphic files, by \includegraphics. In effect, then package adds support for the .tex extension.

Some of the lower level operations like clipping and trimming are implemented using the adjustbox package which includes native pdfLaTeX support and uses the pgf package for other output formats.

name: gindex
caption: Formatting indexes

descriptions.text: This package provides a way to generate the format of index entries from within LaTeX.

name: ginpenc
caption: Modification of inputenc for German

descriptions.text: If the inputenc is used and German umlauts are input directly, they are converted to the LICR representation \"a (etc.). This breaks the sort algorithm of makeindex, for instance. Ginpenc converts umlauts and the sharp-s to the short forms defined by babel, e.g., "a instead, if the text is typeset in German.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: git-latexdiff
caption: Call latexdiff on two Git revisions of a file

descriptions.text: git-latexdiff is a tool to graphically visualize differences between different versions of a LaTeX file. Technically, it is a wrapper around git and latexdiff.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: gitfile-info
caption: Get git metadata for a specific file

descriptions.text: If you are using git to control versions of LaTeX-files, you may want to show yourself or other users or devs the current version of the file, information about the author and last edited date. All packages for git known make that kind of information available for the whole repository. But sometimes you have a lot of files within the same repository in different versions, from different authors etc. Perhaps you also split up a big project in small files and want to show within the document who had edited what. This package gives you the opportunity to do so.

name: gitinfo
caption: Access metadata from the git distributed version control system

descriptions.text:
The package makes it possible to incorporate git version control metadata into documents.

For memoir users, the package provides the means to tailor page headers and footers to use the metadata.

Note this version is now deprecated, but is kept on the archive, pro tem, for continuity for existing users. All new repositories should use gitinfo2.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: gitinfo-lua
caption: Display git project information in your LaTeX projects

descriptions.text:
This project aims to display git project information in PDF documents. It is mostly written in Lua for executing the git commands, thereby making this package only applicable for LuaLaTeX with shell escape enabled.

If LuaLaTeX isn’t working for you, you could try gitinfo2 instead.

For LaTeX, a set of standard macros is provided for displaying basic information or setting the project directory, and a set of advanced macros for formatting commits and tags.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
support for keeping track of document development

name: gitinfo2
caption: Access metadata from the git distributed version control system

descriptions.text:
The package makes it possible to incorporate git version control metadata into documents.

For memoir users, the package provides the means to tailor page headers and footers to use the metadata.

gitinfo2 is a new release of gitinfo. The changes to version 2 are not backward-compatible, and the package name has been changed to avoid impact on existing users’ repositories. All new repositories should use this version of the package.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: gitlog
caption: Typesetting git changelogs

descriptions.text:
This package allows git change log history to be incorporated into LaTeX documents; the log data is obtained from the git distributed version control system.

The current release (0.0.beta) is a proof-of-concept release to allow users an early evaluation and to attract ideas and support. Requests and suggestions, as well as code contributions are welcome.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: gitstatus
caption: Include Git information in the document as watermark or via variables

descriptions.text:
If your LaTeX-document is version-controlled with git, you might encounter situations, where you want to include some information of your git-repository into your LaTeX-document- e.g. to keep track on who gave you feedback on which version of your document.

This git-information can be included on every page by a watermark or (for custom needs) via provided variables.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.
separate printing, under (or over) the page as a whole

name: gitver
caption: Get the current git hash of a project and typeset it in the document

descriptions.text:
This package will get a description of the current git version of the document and store it in a command \gitVer. If memoir or fancyhdr are in use, it will also add this to the document footers unless the option noheader is passed.

The package also defines a command \versionBox which outputs a box containing the version and date of compilation.

The package requires hyperref, catchfile, pdftexcmds, and datetime.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: gkpmac
caption: The macros used in <q>Concrete Mathematics</q>

descriptions.text: The macros seem to have been updated since the book was published, but the changes are very small, in some cases merely of notation.

name: gl-tree
caption: Linguistic trees with a preprocessor

descriptions.text:
Trees are described by a \tree command followed by a parenthesised outline of the tree to be typeset. Possible output includes TeX commands, possibly using PostScript \specials to do the more difficult things (like sloped lines).

The preprocessors are specified (mostly) as lex tables; a Makefile is provided.

name: GladTeX
caption: LaTeX equations in HTML

descriptions.text:
GladTeX is a utility that enables LaTeX equations within HTML code. You write HTML code as usual, but in addition you can include equations within the special tags <EQ>..</EQ>, as if within $$..$$ in LaTeX. Then you run gladtex, which replaces the equations by images. Features include image alignment (baseline of equations agree with baseline of text), GIF and PNG support, transparent backgrounds and antialiasing.

Additionally, GladTeX can aid the creation of accessible documents for the blind by providing the LaTeX equation in the alt attribute of an image. It also comes with a library which allows embedding GladTeX into other applications.

name: gleitobjekte
caption: Tutorial from a DANTE meeting in November 1997

descriptions.text: The script of a tutorial held at the November 1997 DANTE meeting. Topics covered include floats and their placement, captions, inclusion of graphics, lettering of graphics, layout of tables and large amounts of numerical data.

name: glhyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for Galician

descriptions.text:
Development of the patterns was based on the schema developed by Javier Bezos for the CervanTeX patterns for Spanish.

The package includes a script for generating UTF-8 patterns, and UTF-8 patterns themselves (which patterns are also now part of hyph-utf8).

name: glmatrix
caption: Macros for linear algebra calculations using scalars, vectors, and matrices

descriptions.text: This package provides macros for linear algebra calculations with scalars, vectors, and matrices. Its structure is based on the JavaScript library glmatrix.js, and it similarly provides several convenience functions often used in computer graphics contexts, like creating a translation matrix.

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: globalvals
caption: Declare global variables

descriptions.text: This package allows the user to declare a variable which can then be used anywhere else in a document, including before it was declared.

name: glonti
caption: Virtual fonts for T2A-encoded fonts

descriptions.text: The package makes a T2A-encoded font family from the cm and the cmcyr fonts, by means of a set of virtual fonts.

topics.details: fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

name: glosmathtools
caption: Mathematical nomenclature tools based on the glossaries package

descriptions.text:
This package can be used to generate a mathematical nomenclature (also called list of symbols or notation). It is based on the glossaries package.

Its main features are:

  • symbol categories (e.g.: latin, greek)
  • automatic but customizable symbol sorting
  • easy subscript management
  • easy accentuation management
  • abbreviation support (with first use definition)
  • bilingual nomenclatures (for bilingual documents)
  • bilingual abbreviations

The documentation is based on the ulthese class.

The package itself depends on glossaries, amsmath, amsfonts, and etoolbox.

name: gloss
caption: Create glossaries using BibTeX

descriptions.text: A glossary package using BibTeX with \cite replaced by \gloss.

name: gloss-occitan
caption: Polyglossia support for Occitan

descriptions.text: Occitan language description file for polyglossia

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: glossaries
caption: Create glossaries and lists of acronyms

descriptions.text:
The glossaries package supports acronyms and multiple glossaries, and has provision for operation in several languages (using the facilities of either babel or polyglossia). New entries are defined to have a name and description (and optionally an associated symbol). Support for multiple languages is offered, and plural forms of terms may be specified. An additional package, glossaries-accsupp, can make use of the accsupp package mechanisms for accessibility support for PDF files containing glossaries.

The user may define new glossary styles, and preambles and postambles can be specified. There is provision for loading a database of terms, but only terms used in the text will be added to the relevant glossary.

The package uses an indexing program to provide the actual glossary; either makeindex or xindy may serve this purpose, and a Perl script is provided to serve as interface.

This package requires the mfirstuc package.

The package supersedes the author’s glossary package (which is now obsolete).

name: glossaries-accsupp
caption: Accessibility support for glossaries

descriptions.text:
The package provides an interface between glossaries package, and the PDF accessibility support package accsupp.

The package is distributed as part of the glossaries bundle.

name: glossaries-danish
caption: Danish language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Danish language module for glossaries package.

topics.details: support for typesetting, or documentation in Danish

name: glossaries-dutch
caption: Dutch language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Dutch language module for glossariesr package.

name: glossaries-english
caption: English language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: English language module for glossariesr package.

name: glossaries-estonian
caption: Estonian language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: This package provides the Estonian language module for the glossaries package.

name: glossaries-extra
caption: An extension to the glossaries package

descriptions.text:
This package provides improvements and extra features to the glossaries package. Some of the default glossaries.sty behaviour is changed by glossaries-extra.sty. See the user manual glossaries-extra-manual.pdf for further details.

glossaries-extra.sty requires the glossaries package and, naturally, all packages required by glossaries.sty.

name: glossaries-finnish
caption: Finnish language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Finnish language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-french
caption: French language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: French language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-german
caption: German language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: German language module for the glossaries package.

name: glossaries-irish
caption: Irish language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Irish language module for glossariesr package.

topics.details: support for typesetting the Irish (gaelic) language

name: glossaries-italian
caption: Italian language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Italian language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-magyar
caption: Magyar language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Magyar language module for glossariesr package.

name: glossaries-norsk
caption: Norsk Bokmål language module for the glossaries Package

descriptions.text: This package adds Norwegian Bokmål translations for the glossaries package. These will be loaded automatically when the babel package is loaded with the option norsk.

name: glossaries-nynorsk
caption: Nynorsk language module for the glossaries package

descriptions.text: Norwegian Nynorsk language module for the glossaries package.

name: glossaries-polish
caption: Polish language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Polish language module for the glossaries package.

name: glossaries-portuges
caption: Portuges language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Portuges language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-serbian
caption: Serbian language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Serbian language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-slovene
caption: Slovene language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Slovene language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-spanish
caption: Spanish language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Spanish language module for glossaries package.

name: glossaries-swedish
caption: Swedish language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Swedish language module for the glossaries package.

name: glossaries-ukrainian
caption: Ukrainian language module for glossaries package

descriptions.text: Ukrainian language module for the glossaries package.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Ukrainian

name: glossary
caption: Create a glossary

descriptions.text:
The package supports generation of a glossary with makeindex. It has a certain amount of flexibility allowing the user to customize the format of the glossary and define new glossary-style objects so that you can have more than one type of glossary in your document.

The package is no longer supported; the author urges users to switch to use of its replacement, the glossaries package. Migration support is available, within the newer package.

name: glosstex
caption: Prepare glossaries in LaTeX

descriptions.text: GlossTeX is a tool for the automatic preparation of glossaries, lists of acronyms and sorted lists in general for use with LaTeX and MakeIndex. GlossTeX combines the functionality of acronym and nomencl and provides some new features. Various binaries are available in the bin subdirectory.

name: glotex
caption: A glossary processor

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
Glotex is supplied as C source (and as a DOS executable), and a supporting package is provided (whose detection of current language is inadequate for current usage).

The bundle is distributed with idxtex.

name: gmdoc
caption: Documentation of LaTeX packages

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package and an example class for documenting (La)TeX packages, document classes, .dtx etc., providing hyperlinks. The package is believed to be compatible with doc and permits minimal markup of code (the macrocode environment is no longer necessary). The package provides automatic detection of definitions (detecting such things as \def, \newcommand, \DeclareOption etc.).

The package needs hyperref and the author’s three basic packages: gmutils, gmverb and gmiflink.

As a bonus (and as an example of doc compatibility) driver files are provided that may be used to typeset the LaTeX Base.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: gmdoc-enhance
caption: Some enhancements to the gmdoc package

descriptions.text: This package provides some enhancements for the gmdoc package: nicer formatting for multiple line inline comments, an ability to comment out some code, and a macro to input other files in normal LaTeX mode.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: gmeometric
caption: Change page size wherever it’s safe

descriptions.text:
Changing the size of the typeset area is well-known to be a dangerous operation in TeX documents. This package identifies the circumstances where the \geometry command of the geometry package may safely be used, (other, of course, than in the preamble of a document) and provides a mechanism for using it.

The package makes use of the author’s gmutils package.

name: gmiflink
caption: Simplify usage of \hypertarget and \hyperlink

descriptions.text: Three hyperref-based macros that simplify usage of \hypertarget and \hyperlink: one argument instead of the same one twice. Also \gmiflink and \gmifref which typeset plain text instead of generating an error or printing ?? if there is no respective hypertarget or label.

name: gmp
caption: Enable integration between MetaPost pictures and LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package allows integration between MetaPost pictures and LaTeX. The main feature is that passing parameters to the MetaPost pictures is possible and the picture code can be put inside arguments to commands, including \newcommand.

topics.details: support tools and macros for MetaPost programming

name: gmutils
caption: Support macros for other packages

descriptions.text:
Miscellaneous macros used by others of the author’s packages.

Contents of the package: \newgif and other globals; \@ifnextcat and \@ifXeTeX; \(Re)storeMacro(s) to override redefinitions; \afterfi and friends; commands from relsize, etc.; almost an environment or redefinition of \begin (\begin* doesn't check if the argument environment is defined).

name: gmverb
caption: A variant of LaTeX \verb, verbatim and shortvrb

descriptions.text:
A redefinition of \verb and verbatim so that long lines are breakable before \ and after { with % as hyphen. Allows you to define your own verbatim-like environments (subject to a size limit) and allows you to declare any single character as a shorthand as in the \MakeShortVerb command of the shortvrb package of the LaTeX distribution.

The package depends on the gmutils package.

name: gmverse
caption: A package for typesetting (short) poems

descriptions.text: A redefinition of the verse environment to make the \\ command optional for line ends and to give it a possibility of optical centering and right-hanging alignment of lines broken because of length.

name: gnu-freefont
caption: A Unicode font, with rather wide coverage

descriptions.text: The package provides a set of outline (i.e. OpenType) fonts covering as much as possible of the Unicode character set. The set consists of three typefaces: one monospaced and two proportional (one with uniform and one with modulated stroke).

topics.details: fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

name: gnuplot
caption: General purpose plotting program

descriptions.text: Generate almost any type of chart you wish and save it in LaTeX format or as PDF (or in any of a dozen other formats).

topics.details: graphics generator whose output is good for use with TeX

name: gnuplottex
caption: Embed Gnuplot commands in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package allows you to include Gnuplot graphs in your LaTeX documents.

The gnuplot code is extracted from the document and written to .gnuplot files. Then, if shell escape is used, the graph files are automatically processed to graphics or LaTeX code files which will then be included in the document. If shell escape isn't used, the user will have to manually convert the files by running gnuplot on the extracted .gnuplot files.

name: go
caption: Fonts and macros for typesetting go games

descriptions.text: The macros provide for nothing more complicated than the standard 19x19 board; the fonts are written in Metafont.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: go-make
caption: A make variant for LaTeX documents

copyright.owner: David J. Musliner and The University of Michigan

descriptions.text:
Go automates the processing of a LaTeX document, according to a file .gorc in the same directory as the document. Has facilities for previewing the document, with a continuous preview mode.

Go is set up to deal with LaTeX 2.09 documents; it would need some attention to prepare it for use with modern documents.

name: gobble
caption: More gobble macros for PlainTeX and LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The LaTeX package gobble includes several gobble macros not included in the LaTeX kernel. These macros remove a number of arguments after them, a feature regulary used inside other macros. This includes gobble macros for optional arguments.

The LaTeX package gobble-user provides these macros at the user level, i.e. using names without @ so that these can be used without \makeatletter and \makeatother.

The same macros are provided inside .tex files for use with plain-TeX or other TeX formats. However, the gobble macros for optional macros require \@ifnextchar to be defined.

name: goblin
caption: Tolkien’s goblin alphabet

descriptions.text:
The font covers the alphabet that Tolkien designed for the book The Father Christmas Letters.

The font is distributed as Metafont source; it works very poorly in modern environments, and could do with expert attention (if you are interested, please contact the CTAN team for details).

topics.details: font for an ‘invented’ language or script

name: gofonts
caption: GoSans and GoMono fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the GoSans and GoMono families of fonts designed by the Bigelow & Holmes foundry for the Go project.

GoSans is available in three weights: Regular, Medium, and Bold (with corresponding italics). GoMono is available in regular and bold, with italics.

Notes on the design may be found at https://blog.golang.org/go-fonts.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font with adaptations to several languages

name: gost
caption: BibTeX styles to format according to GOST

descriptions.text:
BibTeX styles to format bibliographies in English, Russian or Ukrainian according to GOST 7.0.5-2008 or GOST 7.1-2003.

Both 8-bit and Unicode (UTF-8) versions of each BibTeX style, in each case offering a choice of sorted and unsorted. Further, a set of three styles (which do not conform to current standards) are retained for backwards compatibility.

name: gothic
caption: A collection of old German-style fonts

descriptions.text:
A collection of fonts that reproduce those used in old German printing and handwriting. The set comprises Gothic, Schwabacher and Fraktur fonts, a pair of handwriting fonts, Sütterlin and Schwell, and a font containing decorative initials.

In addition, there are two re-encoding packages for Haralambous’s fonts, providing T1, using virtual fonts, and OT1 and T1, using Metafont.

topics.details: listing a set of related fonts
font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: gotoh
caption: An implementation of the Gotoh sequence alignment algorithm

descriptions.text: This package calculates biological sequence alignment with the Gotoh algorithm. The package also provides an interface to control various settings including algorithm parameters.

name: gpdata
caption: Cause MetaPost graph package to ignore <q>#</q>-comments

descriptions.text:
This file modifies the Grdln_ routine of the MetaPost graph package, so that it can parse and ignore comment lines in data files starting with a # sign, similar to the conventions in Gnuplot.

Note that the graph package will still interpret an empty line as end of data (even if it precedes any data).

name: gplot
caption: CGM-based graphics support

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

name: grabbox
caption: Read an argument into a box and execute the code afterwards

descriptions.text: The package provides the command \grabbox, which grabs an argument into a box and executes the code afterwards.

name: gradback
caption: Gradient backgrounds for dvips output

descriptions.text: There being no documentation, this package is really for the determined user only: there is some description of arguments to the package's command in comments in the package file.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers
decorate/confuse text by adding a background

name: gradient-text
caption: Decorate text with linear gradient colors

descriptions.text: This package enables writers to conveniently decorate text with linear gradient colors. The RGB values of the first and the last character are specified as parameters while the rest of the text is colored automatically.

name: gradientframe
caption: Simple gradient frames around objects

descriptions.text: The package provides a means of drawing graded frames around objects. The gradients of the frames are drawn using the color package.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: grading-scheme
caption: Typeset grading schemes in tabular format

descriptions.text: This package aims at an easy-to-use interface to typeset grading schemes in tabular format, in particular grading-schemes of exercises of mathematical olympiads where multiple solutions have to be graded and might offer mutual exclusive ways of receiving points.

name: gradstudentresume
caption: A generic template for graduate student resumes

descriptions.text: The package offers a template for graduate students writing an academic CV. The goal is to create a flexible template that can be customized based on each specific individual's needs.

name: grafcet
caption: Draw Grafcet/SFC with TikZ

descriptions.text: The package provides a library (GRAFCET) that can draw Grafcet Sequential Function Chart (SFC) diagrams, in accordance with EN 60848, using Pgf/TikZ.
L'objectif de la librairie GRAFCET est de permettre le tracé de grafcet selon la norme EN 60848 à partir de Pgf/TikZ.

name: grafik
caption: EPS graphics under Windows

descriptions.text: A guide (in German) on how to produce EPS graphics files for use with LaTeX on MS Windows platforms.

name: grant
caption: Classes for formatting federal grant proposals

descriptions.text:
LaTeX classes for formatting federal grant proposals:

  • grant: Base class for formatting grant proposals
  • grant-arl: Army Research Laboratory
  • grant-darpa: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
  • grant-doe: Department of Energy
  • grant-nih: National Institutes of Health
  • grant-nrl: Naval Research Laboratory
  • grant-nsf: National Science Foundation
  • grant-onr: Office of Naval Research

topics.details: typeset proposals to funding bodies, etc

name: graph35
caption: Draw keys and screen items of several Casio calculators

descriptions.text: This package defines commands to draw the Casio Graph 35 / fx-9750GII calculator (and other models). It can draw the whole calculator, or parts of it (individual keys, part of the screen, etc.). It was written to typeset documents instructing students how to use their calculator.

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: GraphBase
caption: A platform for combinatorial algorithms

descriptions.text: A cweb program developed (presumably) in pursuit of work on The Art of Computer Programming .

topics.details: graphics generator whose output is good for use with TeX

name: graphbox
caption: Extend graphicx to improve placement of graphics

descriptions.text:
Graphbox is an extension of the standard graphicx LaTeX2e package to allow the placement of graphics relative to the current position using additional optional arguments of \includegraphics.

For example, changing the vertical alignment is convenient for using graphics as elements of (mathematical) formulae. Options for shifting, smashing and hiding the graphics may be useful in support, for example, of the beamer framework.

name: GraphConv
caption: Convert graph files to PSTricks

descriptions.text: Graph is a very easy to use program to create simple graphs. GraphConv is a small Windows program to convert Graph files to PStricks code.

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

name: grapher
caption: Create graphs, state machine and data flow diagrams

descriptions.text: Grapher is a python script; you provide it with a specification (in python) of a diagram, and grapher emits gpic code that can be translated to LaTeX and used to typeset the diagram in your document.

topics.details: graphics generator whose output is good for use with TeX

name: graphfig
caption: Simpler graphic, subfigure and float

descriptions.text:
This package combines the tools of the graphic, subfigure and float packages in a way that makes their use simpler and more robust. The Figure environment (capitalized) differs from the standard LaTeX figure environment by the addition of a mandatory argument to specify the caption and an optional argument to be used as a label. These ensure that the \label command appears after the \caption command to avoid the common labelling error. The commands \graphfig and \graphfig* have the additional advantage that the image will be automatically centered horizontally.

The package is part of the bosisio bundle.

name: graphicp
caption: An enhanced version of graphics

descriptions.text:
An extension of the standard LaTeX graphics package, with features to speed it up and to improve its accuracy. (In particular, the calculations relating to bounding boxes are performed in an out-of-line Perl script, which means that the operation is potentially more robust, and the calculations are more accurate than can be achieved within TeX itself.

The package works under Plain TeX as well as LaTeX.

name: graphics
caption: Standard LaTeX graphics

descriptions.text:
The package was designed to accommodate all needs for inclusion of graphics in LaTeX documents, replacing many earlier packages used in LaTeX 2.09. The package aims to give a consistent interface to including the file types that are understood in your output, by use of printer drivers (now known, simply, as drivers). The distribution of the package contains several drivers, but others (for example, pdfTeX) are distributed separately. The package also offers several means of manipulating graphics in the course of inserting them into a document (for example, rotation and scaling).

For extended documentation see epslatex.

The package is part of the graphics bundle, which is one of the collections in the LaTeX required set of packages.

name: graphics-cfg
caption: Sample configuration files for LaTeX color and graphics

descriptions.text:
This bundle includes color.cfg and graphics.cfg files that set default driver options for the color and graphics packages.

It contains support for defaulting the new LuaTeX option which was added to graphics and color in the 2016-02-01 release. The LuaTeX option is only used for LuaTeX versions from 0.87, older versions use the pdfTeX option as before.

name: graphics-def
caption: Colour and graphics option files

descriptions.text:
This bundle is a combined distribution consisting of dvips.def, pdftex.def, luatex.def, xetex.def, dvipdfmx.def, and dvisvgm.def driver option files for the LaTeX graphics and color packages.

It is hoped that by combining their source repositories at https://github.com/latex3/graphics-def it will be easier to coordinate updates.

name: graphics-pln
caption: LaTeX-style graphics for Plain TeX users

descriptions.text:
The Plain TeX graphics package is mostly a thin shell around the LaTeX graphicx and color packages, with support of the LaTeX-isms in those packages provided by miniltx (which is the largest part of the bundle).

The bundle also contains a file picture.tex, which is a wrapper around the autopict.sty, and provides the LaTeX picture mode to Plain TeX users.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: graphicscache
caption: Cache includegraphics calls

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides caching of \includegraphics calls, with several useful effects:

  • Recompilations are much faster (10x speedup observed).
  • Images can be postprocessed with ghostscript before inclusion, thus:
    • Automatic downscaling to specified DPI
    • Automatic JPEG compression with configurable quality
    • Much smaller files (e.g. 10MB instead of 150MB)!

Note: Due to the one-by-one invocation of pdflatex and ghostscript for each graphics element, the first compilation is typically slower than usual.

Note: graphicscache needs the \write18 call (also called shell escape). This is a security risk if you have untrusted TeX sources.

graphicscache supports pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX; XeLaTeX is not supported.

topics.details: run an external program from within a document

name: graphicx
caption: Enhanced support for graphics

descriptions.text:
The package builds upon the graphics package, providing a key-value interface for optional arguments to the \includegraphics command. This interface provides facilities that go far beyond what the graphics package offers on its own.

For extended documentation, see epslatex.

The package is part of the latex-graphics bundle, which is one of the collections in the LaTeX required set of packages.

name: graphicx-psmin
caption: Reduce size of PostScript files by not repeating images

descriptions.text:
The package is an extension of the standard latex-graphics bundle and provides a way to include repeated PostScript graphics (ps, eps) only once in a PostScript document. This leads to smaller PostScript documents when having, for instance, a logo on every page. The package only works when post-processed with dvips, which should be version 5.95b or later.

The difference for a resulting distilled PDF file is minimal (as Ghostscript and Adobe Distiller only include a single copy of each graphics file, anyway).

name: graphicxbox
caption: Insert a graphical image as a background

descriptions.text: The package defines two new commands \graphicxbox and \fgraphicxbox, which are companions to \colorbox and \fcolorbox of the Standard LaTeX color package. The \graphicxbox command inserts a graphical image as a background rather than a background color, while \fgraphicxbox does the same thing, but also draws a colored frame around the box.

name: graphicxpsd
caption: Adobe Photoshop Data format (PSD) support for graphicx package

descriptions.text: This package provides Adobe Photoshop Data format (PSD) support for the graphicx package with the sips (Darwin/macOS) or convert (ImageMagick) command.

name: GraphicxSP
caption: An extension of the graphicx package

descriptions.text: GraphicxSP embeds a graphic file in a PDF document in such a way that the author may re-use that same graphics without significantly increasing the file size. GraphicxSP also supports the Adobe transparency model.

name: graphpap
caption: For producing graph paper

descriptions.text:
This file defines the \graphpaper command which makes a grid of lines.

This file is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: graphpaper
caption: A LaTeX class to generate several types of graph papers

descriptions.text: Graphpaper is a LaTeX document class which allows to print several types of graph papers: bilinear (millimeter paper), semilogarithmic, bilogarithmic, polar, log-polar, Smith charts. It is based on the picture environment and its extensions.

name: GraphTeX
caption: Graphs theory and related diagrams in a TeX document

descriptions.text: GraphTeX is a Perl library (graphtex.pl) along with a preprocessor (gt) which can be used to generate TeXdraw commands producing graphs and related diagrams inside a TeX document. A graph can be typeset by writing a .gt source file which resembles a matrix environment.

topics.details: graphics generator whose output is good for use with TeX

name: graphviz
caption: Write graphviz (dot+neato) inline in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: The package allows inline use of graphviz code, in a LaTeX document.

name: Gratzer-Color-Scheme
caption: Colors definitions, theorems, corollaries, lemmas, and propositions

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package introduces the Grätzer Color Scheme for math publications, which colors theorems and corollaries red, lemmas and propositions blue, definitions green.

name: gray
caption: Fonts for gray-scales

descriptions.text: The font is discussed in the Metafont book, by Knuth.

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

name: grayhints
caption: Produce <q>gray hints</q> to a variable text field

descriptions.text:
The package provides JavaScript code snippets to create gray hints. Gray hints, as the author terms them, are text that appears initially in a text field that gives a short hint as to what the contents of the text field should be. For example, a text field might contain the hint First Name, or a date field might read yyyy/mm/dd. As soon as the field comes into focus, the hint disappears. It reappears when the field is blurred and the user did not enter any text into the field.

The package works for dvips/Distiller, pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: grchyph
caption: Hyphenation for classical Greek, under XeTeX

descriptions.text: These patterns are written in Unicode to work with XeTeX; they will not work with a standard TeX installation.

name: greek-fontenc
caption: LICR macros and encoding definition files for Greek

descriptions.text: LICR macros for characters from the Greek script and encoding definition files for Greek text font encodings.

name: greek-inputenc
caption: Greek encoding support for inputenc

descriptions.text: Input encoding definition files for UTF-8, Macintosh Greek, and ISO 8859-7 enabling the use of literal characters for Greek letters and symbols with 8-bit TeX engines (pdfLaTeX).

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: greek-makeindex
caption: Makeindex working with Greek

descriptions.text: Makeindex is resolutely stuck with Latin-based alphabets, so will not deal with Greek indexes, unaided. This package provides a Perl script that will transmute the index of a Greek document in such a way that makeindex will sort the entries according to the rules of the Greek alphabet.

name: greek4cbc
caption: A Greek font from 394BC

descriptions.text: Provides a Greek monumental font as used on a stele in Athens in 394BC. The font consists of majuscules only and is in Adobe Type 1 format. This is one of a series of archaic fonts.

documentation.details: Sample of Greek C4 BCE font

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: greek6cbc
caption: A Greek font from the sixth century BC

descriptions.text:
This Greek font (in Type 1 format) is typical of the writing used in the 6th century BC.

It is one of a series of archaic fonts.

documentation.details: Sample of Greek C6 BCE font:

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: greekctr
caption: Represent counters by letters of the Greek alphabet

descriptions.text:
The commands \greek and \Greek use (mathematical) Greek letters (or upper case Latin letters, where appropriate), to enumerate numbers up to 24. Numbers 25 and above are represented with \omega/\Omega, and provoke an error message.

The package is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

name: greekdates
caption: Provides ancient Greek day and month names, dates, etc

descriptions.text: The package provides easy access to ancient Greek names of days and months of various regions of Greece. In case the historical information about a region is not complete, we use the Athenian name of the month. Moreover commands and options are provided, in order to completely switch to the ancient way, commands such as \today.

name: greekinfo3
caption: Overview of systems, packages, and fonts for Greek TeX

descriptions.text: The document Twenty-five years of Greek TeXing provides an updated perspective of all available systems, packages, and fonts for typesetting Greek texts using TeX/LaTeX.

name: greektex
caption: Fonts for typesetting Greek/English documents

descriptions.text: The fonts are based on Silvio Levy’s classical Greek fonts; macros and Greek hyphenation patterns for the fonts’ encoding are also provided.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: greektex-fd
caption: LaTeX font definition files for GreekTeX

descriptions.text: FD files for the three families of fonts of the GreekTeX bundle, in a U encoding (for the roman, sans and teletype families), and again as an OML encoding for the roman family.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: greektonoi
caption: Facilitates writing/editing of multiaccented greek

descriptions.text: The greektonoi mapping extends the betababel package or the babel polutonikogreek option to provide a simple way to insert ancient Greek texts with diacritical characters into your document using a similar method to the commonly used Beta Code transliteration, but with much more freedom. It is designed especially for the XeTeX engine and it could also be used for fast and easy modification of monotonic greek texts to polytonic. The output text is natively encoded in Unicode, so it can be reused in any possible way. The greektonoi package provides, in addition to inserting greek accents and breathings, many other symbols used in greek numbers and arithmetic or in the greek archaic period. It could be used with greektonoi mapping or indepedently.

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: greenpoint
caption: The Green Point logo

descriptions.text: A Metafont-implementation of the logo commonly known as Der Grüne Punkt (The Green Point). In Austria, it can be found on nearly every bottle. It should not be confused with the Recycle-logo, implemented by Ian Green.

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

name: gregoriotex
caption: Engraving Gregorian Chant scores

descriptions.text: Gregorio is a software application for engraving Gregorian Chant scores on a computer. Gregorio’s main job is to convert a gabc file (simple text representation of a score) into a GregorioTeX file, which makes TeX able to create a PDF of your score.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: grfext
caption: Manipulate the graphics package’s list of extensions

descriptions.text: This package provides macros for adding to, and reordering the list of graphics file extensions recognised by package graphics.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: grffile
caption: Extended file name support for graphics (legacy package)

descriptions.text:
The original package extended the file name processing of package graphics to support a larger range of file names.

The base LaTeX code now supports multiple dots and spaces, and this package by default is a stub that just loads graphicx.

However, \usepackage{grffile}[=v1] may be used to access version 1(.18) of the package if that is needed.

name: grfguide
caption: LaTeX standard graphics and color packages documentation

descriptions.text: Documentation of the LaTeX Graphics bundle. The guide discusses using graphics in LaTeX, including documentation on the use of colour (the color package).

topics.details: documentation of techniques for using graphics

name: grfpaste
caption: Include fragments of a dvi file

descriptions.text: Provides a mechanism to include fragments of dvi files with the graphicx package, so that you can use \includegraphics to include dvi files. The package requires the dvipaste program.

name: grid
caption: Grid typesetting in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package helps to enables grid typesetting in double column documents. Grid typesetting (vertical aligning of lines of text in adjacent columns) is a difficult task in LaTeX, and the present package is no more than an attempt to help users to achieve it in a limited way. An example document, grid.tex, is provided with simple instructions to typeset it using the package.

The package needs a lot more work: this is only a beginning…

topics.details: typeset, snapping lines of text to a grid

name: grid-system
caption: Page organisation, modelled on CSS facilities

descriptions.text:
The package provides the means for LaTeX to implement a grid system as known from CSS grid systems.

The facility is useful for creating box layouts as used in brochures.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: gridpapers
caption: Graph paper backgrounds and color schemes

descriptions.text:
This package provides many preset yet customizable graph paper backgrounds. Some of the preset patterns include standard quadrille or graph pattern, dot grid, hexagons, isometric or triangular grid, squares with 45° light cone lines, ruled, and more. Pattern sizes can be controlled via package options. There are several preset color palletes, and colors can be overridden.

The package uses the PGF/TikZ package, and the geometry package to control page size.

topics.details: decorate/confuse text by adding a background

name: gridset
caption: Grid, a.k.a. in-register, setting

descriptions.text: Grid setting – also known as strict in-register setting – is something, that should be done for a lot of documents but is not easy using LaTeX. The package helps to get the information needed for grid setting. It does not implement auto grid setting, but there is a command \vskipnextgrid, that moves to the next grid position. This may be enough under some circumstances, but in other circumstances it may fail. Thus gridset is only one more step for grid setting, not a complete solution.

topics.details: typeset, snapping lines of text to a grid

name: gridslides
caption: Free form slides with blocks placed on a grid

descriptions.text:
This package allows creating free form slides with blocks placed on a grid. The blocks can be filled with text, equations, figures etc. The resulting slides are similar to the ones produced with LaTeX beamer, but more flexible.

Sequential unconvering of elements is supported. A compiler script is provided which compiles each slide separately, this way avoiding long compile times.

name: grkfinst
caption: Install Greek Type 1 fonts

descriptions.text:
This is a plug-in for fontinst, for installing Greek Type 1 fonts for use with (La)TeX using the LGR encoding.

For Unicode fonts to use with Omega, see the author’s ofntinst bundle.

topics.details: Omega and packages that use it
convert a font to a form usable with TeX

name: grnumalt
caption: Ancient Greek (Athenian) numbers

descriptions.text: The package implements a numbering system that was used in ancient Athens, producing the Athenian numeral for any positive number. The package’s \athnum command can (in principle) be used to provide alternative typeset display of the value of counters.

name: grtimes
caption: Typeset Greek text with Times New Roman Greek

descriptions.text:
The bundle assumes you have run ttf2mf to produce Metafont source from the (Monotype) Times New Roman TrueType font that you (otherwise, legally) own. (The translation may be steered by a file within the this package.)

The package grtimes, in the bundle, allows the user to typeset monotonic Greek text using these Metafont-specified fonts.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: grundgesetze
caption: Typeset Frege’s Grundgesetze der Arithmetik

copyright.owner: Josh Parsons, Marcus Rossberg, J.J. Green, Richard Kimberly Heck, Agustín Rayo

descriptions.text: The package defines maths mode commands for typesetting Gottlob Frege’s concept-script in the style of his Grundgesetze der Arithmetik (Basic Laws of Arithmetic).

name: grverb
caption: Typesetting Greek verbatim

descriptions.text: The package provides verbatim typesetting, in the context of the Greek option in babel. The package uses the public domain Greek-CourierPlain font, and the font itself (in Type 1 format), metrics and a font map entry for its use are provided.

name: GS1
caption: Typeset EAN barcodes using TeX rules, only

descriptions.text: The (LaTeX3) package typesets EAN-8 and EAN-13 barcodes, using the facilities of the rule-D package.

name: gsemthesis
caption: Geneva School of Economics and Management PhD thesis format

descriptions.text:
The class provides a PhD thesis template for the Geneva School of Economics and Management (GSEM), University of Geneva, Switzerland.

The class provides utilities to easily set up the cover page, the front matter pages, the page headers, etc., conformant to the official guidelines of the GSEM Faculty for writing PhD dissertations.

name: gsftopk
caption: Convert <q>Ghostscript fonts</q> to PK files

descriptions.text: Designed for use with xdvi and dvips this utility converts Adobe Type 1 fonts to PK bitmap format. It should not ordinarily be much used nowadays, since both its target applications are now capable of dealing with Type 1 fonts, direct.

topics.details: convert a font to a form usable with TeX

name: gsview
caption: View PostScript under MS-Windows or OS/2

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
GSView is a graphical interface for the Ghostscript interpreter of PostScript and PDF, under Windows, OS/2 or Unix-alike systems. GSview was inspired by Tim Theisen’s X11 Ghostview program (the current X11 derivative of that is gv).

GSview is no longer available from CTAN: it should be retrieved from its home page.

topics.details: application for viewing a typeset document on screen

name: gtex-letter
caption: A Gnome assistant to ease the writing of LaTeX letters

descriptions.text:
A good looking interface, based on the gnome-desktop. Serial letters are supported. Multiple letter headers can be accessed from within the application. Standard openings and default closings can be configured. These openings can be configured to adopt to the sex of the addressee automatically.

You can choose from three different user interfaces. Novice is very easy for the beginner, intermediate is the standard way, expert is straight forward, all on one big page.

The application can swallow text you pipe into it, being it the address or the text of the letter. A special non-interactive mode lets you produce standard-letters in an extremely efficient way.

gtex-letter connects to the gnome-address-book from the gnome-pim package.

gtex-letter is implemented in python and based on gnome.

name: gtl
caption: Manipulating generalized token lists

descriptions.text: The package provides tools for simple operations on lists of tokens which are not necessarily balanced. It is in particular used a lot in the unravel package, to go through tokens one at a time rather than having to work with entire braced groups at a time.

name: gtrcrd
caption: Add chords to lyrics

descriptions.text: The package provides the means to specify guitar chords to be played with each part of the lyrics of a song. The syntax of the macros reduces the chance of failing to provide a chord where one is needed, and the structure of the macros ensures that the chord specification appears immediately above the start of the lyric.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: gtrlib.largetrees
caption: Library for genealogytree aiming at large trees

descriptions.text:
The main goal of this package is to offer additional database fields and formats for the genealogytree package, particularly for typesetting large trees.

The package depends on genealogytree and etoolbox.

name: gu
caption: Typeset crystallographic group-subgroup-schemes

descriptions.text: The package simplifies typesetting of simple crystallographic group-subgroup-schemes in the Bärnighausen formalism. It defines a new environment stammbaum, wherein all elements of the scheme are defined. Afterwards all necessary dimensions are calculated and the scheme is drawn. Currently two steps of symmetry reduction are supported.

topics.details: typeset material to do with crystallography

name: guarani
caption: Guarani support

descriptions.text: This is an (unfinished) package for support of Guarani, which is the main language spoken in Paraguay. The bundle provides Babel support for writing in Guarani, together with an inputenc definition file for a windows Guarani code page.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines
extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages
support for a language whose support is not otherwise catalogued

name: gudea
caption: The Gudea font face with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides the Gudea family of fonts designed by Agustina Mingote, with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: guia-bibtex
caption: Guia casi completa de BibTeX

descriptions.text: The document is an (as-complete-as-possible) manual about the use of BibTeX with LaTeX, in Spanish.

name: guide-latex-fr
caption: A french guide on LaTeX – for beginners or advanced users

descriptions.text: If you want to start from scratch and learn how to type good-looking reports with LaTeX, and if you’re French, then I know it can be really hard to do it by yourself. That’s why I put all the knowledge I acquired into this guide. It can help a lot to learn the bases or to move forward and use LaTeX to type more handsome documents. Lots of examples are provided all along this guide.

Si tu ne connais rien à LaTeX, si tu veux apprendre à rédiger des rapports élégants sous LaTeX, et si en plus tu es Français, je sais exactement ce que tu ressens: c’est extrêmement dur de commencer tout seul, en autodidacte. C’est pourquoi j’ai réuni toutes mes connaissances actuelles sur LaTeX dans ce guide. Il peut donc t’aider à apprendre les bases ou aller plus loin dans ton utilisation de LaTeX. Des exemples détaillés sont fournis tout le long du guide.

name: GuIT-corso
caption: Introduzione al mondo di LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This material provides everything is necessary to give a LaTeX course in Italian. The course is divided into four lessons and it has been written for people without any previous knowledge of LaTeX. It has been successfully tested on Windows and *nix platforms.

The class guitbeamer is needed to run the presentations. Documentation is only available in Italian.

Viene qui presentato il materiale realizzato per il corso Introduzione al mondo di LaTeX tenuto dai membri del Gruppo Utilizzatori Italiani di TeX e destinato a chiunque abbia in animo di organizzare un corso ma non trovi il tempo e/o la voglia necessaria per allestire tutto il materiale. Il corso è articolato in quattro lezioni ed è rivolto a discenti senza alcuna conoscenza pregressa di LaTeX e/o linguaggi di programmazione. Esso può essere svolto sia per piattaforme Windows che *nix, essendo stato sperimentato con successo su entrambi i sistemi.

Le presentazioni a video sono realizzate sulla base della classe guitbeamer sviluppata da Emiliano Giovanni Vavassori e disponibile su CTAN.

name: guitar
caption: Guitar chords and song texts

descriptions.text: (La)TeX macros for typesetting guitar chords over song texts. The toolbox package is required. Note that this package only places arbitrary TeX code over the lyrics. To typeset the chords graphically (and not only by name), the author recommends use of an additional package such as gchords by K. Peeters.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: guitarchordschemes
caption: Guitar Chord and Scale Tablatures

descriptions.text:
This package provides two commands (\chordscheme and \scales).

With those commands it is possible to draw schematic diagrams of guitar chord tablatures and scale tablatures. Both commands know a range of options that allow wide customization of the output.

The package's drawing is done with the help of TikZ.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: guitartabs
caption: A class for drawing guitar tablatures easily

descriptions.text:
This package provides is a simple LaTeX2e class that allows guitarists to create basic guitar tablatures using LaTeX. Create music and do not be bothered with macro programming.

The class depends on the LaTeX packages geometry, harmony, inputenc, intcalc, musixtex, tikz, and xifthen, as well as the article class.

topics.details: chord notations, as for song books

name: GuITbeamer
caption: Beamer-based class for GuIT presentations

descriptions.text: The guitbeamer class is written to simplify the preparation of presentations on LaTeX to members of GuIT. The class is based on beamer.

name: GuITlogo
caption: Macros for typesetting the GuIT logo

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands useful to correctly write the logo of Gruppo Utilizzatori Italiani di TeX (Italian TeX User Group), using the default document color or any other color the user may ever choose, in conformity with the logo’s scheme as seen on the group’s website https://www.guitex.org. Likewise, commands are provided that simplify the writing of the GuIT acronym’s complete expansion, of the addresses of the group’s internet site and public forum, and the meeting GuITmeeting and the magazine Ars TeXnica’s logo.

Optionally, using hyperref, the outputs of the above cited commands can become hyperlinks to the group’s website https://www.guitex.org.

The Documentation is available in Italian only.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: gurmukhi
caption: Support for Gurmukhi

descriptions.text: TeX support for Gurmukhi (a Punjabi language), including a converter from US-ASCII to Gurmukhi.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: gurmukhi-singh
caption: Support for Gurmukhi in TeX

descriptions.text: A preprocessor (provided as C source) for Gurmukhi text expressed in a Latin alphabet, Metafont source of a Gurmukhi font, and plain TeX macros (derived from Devanagari macros).

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: gurps
caption: Typeset Generic Universal Role Playing System (GURPS) materials

descriptions.text:
This package supports typesetting Generic Universal Role Playing System (GURPS) materials. It provides many convenience commands (e.g. \gurps, \SJGamesOnlinePolicy) as well as limited NPC building capabilities with a character environment.

The package requires the use of LuaLaTeX as several of the internal calculations are in Lua.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: GUTenberg
caption: French TeX Users Group information

descriptions.text: This directory contains files with information about the French TeX Users Group GUTenberg.

name: gv
caption: An X front end for Ghostscript

descriptions.text:
GNU gv enables the user to view and navigate through PostScript and PDF documents on an X display by providing a user interface for the Ghostscript interpreter.

Devlopment of gv was based on ghostview 1.5 (which CTAN does not hold).

topics.details: application for viewing a typeset document on screen

name: gv-savepos
caption: A patch to gv to save positions

descriptions.text:
A patch against the sources of gv (version 3.6.2), to record the coordinates of the cursor in a file.

Such a file simplifies the process of preparing images using packages such as pinlabel.

topics.details: application for viewing a typeset document on screen

name: gzt
caption: Bundle of classes for <q>La Gazette des Mathématiciens</q>

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides two classes and BibLaTeX styles for the French journal La Gazette des Mathématiciens :

  • gzt for the complete issues of the journal, aimed at the Gazette’s team,
  • gztarticle, intended for authors who wish to publish an article in the Gazette. This class’s goals are to
    • faithfully reproduce the layout of the Gazette, thus enabling the authors to be able to work their document in actual conditions, and
    • provide a number of tools (commands and environments) to facilitate the drafting of documents, in particular those containing mathematical formulas.

name: h2020proposal
caption: LaTeX class and template for EU H2020 RIA proposal

descriptions.text: This package consists of a class file as well as FET and ICT proposal templates for writing EU H2020 RIA proposals and generating automatically the many cross-referenced tables that are required.

topics.details: typeset proposals to funding bodies, etc

name: ha-prosper
caption: Patches and improvements for prosper

descriptions.text: HA-prosper is a patch for prosper that adds new functionality to prosper based presentations. Among the new features you will find automatic generation of a table of contents on each slide, support for notes and portrait slides.
