The available styles demonstrate how to expand the functionality of prosper even further.

name: hackalloc
caption: Make allocations local

descriptions.text: The package makes all allocation (\newcount, \newdimen, etc.) local.

name: hackthefootline
caption: Footline selection and configuration for LaTeX beamer’s standard themes

descriptions.text:
This package is taking over, defining and redefining different footlines. Configuration is provided via using key-value syntax.

It depends on the pgfkeys used for providing the configuration keys.

Optional features require the following LaTeX packages: appendixnumberbeamer, calc, etoolbox, and numprint.

name: hacm
caption: Font support for the Arka language

descriptions.text:
The package supports typesetting hacm, the alphabet of the constructed language Arka.

The bundle provides nine official fonts, in Adobe Type 1 format.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font for an ‘invented’ language or script

name: hadith
caption: An easy way to typeset Hadith text using XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides an easy way to typeset Hadith text (with full Arabic diacritics/tashkeel) from the canonical collections of Islamic tradition in XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX documents. It is modeled after the quran package and follows the same architecture: text data in .def files, macros in .sty.

The package currently includes seven collections (36,390 hadiths total): Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami at-Tirmidhi, Sunan an-Nasa’i, Sunan Ibn Majah, and Muwatta Malik. English translations and hadith authenticity grades are included.

Key features include on-demand chapter loading to avoid TeX memory limits, case-insensitive collection names, inline citation commands, and metadata commands for section/chapter names.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Arabic

name: hagenberg-thesis
caption: Collection of LaTeX classes, style files and example documents for academic manuscripts

descriptions.text: This is a collection of modern LaTeX classes, style files and example documents for authoring Bachelor, Master, Diploma, or PhD theses and related academic manuscripts in English and German. Pre-configured English and German documents are available. They are easy to use even for LaTeX beginners, and compatible with LaTeX distributions for Windows, macOS, and Linux. The document classes are immediately usable and convenient to customize.

name: halftone
caption: Knuth’s halftone font and its uses

descriptions.text: Knuth’s font is of course distributed as Metafont source. Macros that demonstrate usage of the font to produce actual printable pictures are also provided.

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

name: halloweenmath
caption: Scary and creepy math symbols with AMS-LaTeX integration

descriptions.text: The package defines a handful of commands for typesetting mathematical symbols of various kinds, ranging from large operators to extensible arrow-like relations and growing arrow-like math accents that all draw from the classic Halloween-related iconography (pumpkins, witches, ghosts, cats, and so on) while being, at the same time, seamlessly integrated within the rest of the mathematics produced by (AmS-)LaTeX.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material
construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: hamnosys
caption: A font for sign languages

descriptions.text:
The Hamburg Notation System, HamNoSys for short, is a system for the phonetic transcription of signed languages. This package makes HamNoSys available in XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

The package provides a Unicode font for rendering HamNoSys symbols as well as three methods for entering them.

name: handin
caption: Light weight template for creating school submissions using LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package is for students creating school submissions using LaTeX. It is especially suitable for math, physics, statistics and the like. It can easily be used for creating exercises, too.

name: handout
caption: Create handout for auditors of a talk

descriptions.text:
In some fields of scholarship, a beamer does not offer good support when giving a talk in a proceeding. For example, in classical philology, the main sources are text, and it will be better to distribute a handout to the audience with extracts of the texts about which we will talk.

The package supports preparation of such handouts when writing the talk.

name: handoutWithNotes
caption: Create Handouts with notes from your LaTeX beamer presentation

descriptions.text: This package provides pgfpages layouts to place notes next to the scaled slides.

name: hands
caption: Pointing hand font

descriptions.text: Provides right- and left-pointing hands in both black-on-white and white-on-black realisation. The font is distributed as Metafont source.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: handstroke
caption: Eye-catching hand-drawn underline

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides the \handstroke command, which underlines a word or a phrase with a line that looks as if it were drawn by hand.

A straight, ruler-perfect rule blends into the text and is easy to overlook, whereas an uneven, hand-drawn handstroke stands apart from the page and catches the reader’s eye. The line can optionally be tinted in any color.

name: hang
caption: Environments for hanging paragraphs and list items

descriptions.text: This package provides environments for hanging paragraphs and list items. In addition, it defines environments for labeled paragraphs and list items.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: hangcaption
caption: Hanging layout for captions

descriptions.text: The hangcaption package redefines the caption command to produce captions with hanging indentation. While this package will work with current LaTeX, its effects are better achieved by one of the many functions of the caption package.

name: hanging
caption: Hanging paragraphs

descriptions.text:
The hanging package facilitates the typesetting of hanging paragraphs.

The package also enables typesetting with hanging punctuation, by making punctuation characters active. This facility is best suppressed (it can interfere with other packages) – there are package options for suppressing each individual punctuation character. Real attempts at hanging punctuation should nowadays use the microtype package, which takes advantage of the support offered in recent versions of pdfTeX.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: hanoi
caption: Tower of Hanoi in TeX

descriptions.text: The Plain TeX program (typed in the shape of the towers of Hanoi) serves both as a game and as a TeX programming exercise. As a game it will solve the towers with (up to) 15 discs (with 15 discs, 32767 moves are needed).

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: hanzibox
caption: Boxed Chinese characters with Pinyin above and translation below

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX package written to simplify the input of Chinese with Hanyu Pinyin and translation. Hanyu Pinyin is placed above Chinese with the xpinyin package, and the translation is placed below.

The package can be used as a utility for learning to write and pronounce Chinese characters, for Chinese character learning plans, presentations, exercise booklets and other documentation work.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: happy4th
caption: A firework display in obfuscated TeX

descriptions.text: The output PDF file gives an amusing display, as the reader pages through it.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
TeX code as a source of humour

name: har2nat
caption: Replace the harvard package with natbib

descriptions.text:
This small package allows a LaTeX document containing the citation commands provided by the Harvard package to be compiled using the natbib package. Migration from harvard to natbib thus can be achieved simply by replacing

\usepackage{harvard}

with

usepackage{natbib} usepackage{har2nat}

It is important that har2nat be loaded after natbib, since it modifies natbib commands.

name: haranoaji
caption: Harano Aji Fonts

descriptions.text:
Harano Aji Fonts (Harano Aji Mincho and Harano Aji Gothic) are fonts obtained by replacing Adobe-Identity-0 (AI0) CIDs of Source Han fonts (Source Han Serif and Source Han Sans) with Adobe-Japan1 (AJ1) CIDs.

There are 14 fonts, 7 weights each for Mincho and Gothic.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: haranoaji-extra
caption: Harano Aji Fonts

descriptions.text:
Harano Aji Fonts (Harano Aji Mincho and Harano Aji Gothic) are fonts obtained by replacing Adobe-Identity-0 (AI0) CIDs of Source Han fonts (Source Han Serif and Source Han Sans) with Adobe-Japan1 (AJ1) CIDs.

There are 14 fonts, 7 weights each for Mincho and Gothic.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: hardwrap
caption: Hard wrap text to a certain character length

descriptions.text:
The package facilitates wrapping text to a specific character width, breaking lines by words rather than, as done by TeX, by characters.

The primary use for these facilities is to aid the generation of messages sent to the log file or console output to display messages to the user. Package authors may also find this useful when writing out arbitrary text to an external file.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: harmony
caption: Typeset harmony symbols, etc., for musicology

descriptions.text: The package harmony.sty uses the packages ifthen and amssymb from the amsfonts bundle, together with the LaTeX font lcirclew10 and the font musix13 from musixtex.

name: harnon-cv
caption: A CV document class with a vertical timeline for experience

descriptions.text: The class offers another modern, neat, design, and provides a simple means of adding an experience timeline.

name: harpoon
caption: Extra harpoons, using the graphics package

descriptions.text: Provides over- and under-harpoon symbol commands; the harpoons may point in either direction, with the hook pointing up or down. The covered object is provided as an argument to the commands, so that they have the look of accent commands.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: harvard
caption: Harvard citation package for use with LaTeX2e

descriptions.text:
This is a re-implementation, for LaTeX2e, of the original Harvard package. The bundle contains the LaTeX package, several BibTeX styles, and a Perl package for use with LaTeX2HTML.

Harvard is an author-year citation style (all but the first author are suppressed in second and subsequent citations of the same entry); the package defines several variant styles:

  • apsr.bst for the American Political Science Review;
  • agsm.bst for Australian Government publications;
  • dcu.bst from the Design Computing Unit of the University of Sydney;
  • kluwer.bstwhich aims at the format preferred in Kluwer publications;
  • nederlands.bst which deals with sorting Dutch names with prefixes (such as van) according to Dutch rules,
  • together with several styles whose authors offer no description of their behaviour.

name: harvard-obsolete
caption: The Harvard bibliography style family

descriptions.text:
There are two primary forms of citation in the Harvard style, dependent upon whether the reference is used as a noun or parenthetically. The citations themselves are in author-date style, with authors after the first suppressed in repeat citations.

The three original bibliography styles are agsm.bst (for Australian Government publications), dcu.bst (from the Design Computing Unit of the University of Sydney) and kluwer.bst (aiming at the format preferred in Kluwer publications).

This package is no longer recommended for use: the harvard package for current LaTeX should be used instead.

name: harveyballs
caption: Create Harvey Balls using TikZ

descriptions.text: The package provides 5 commands (giving symbols that indicate values from none to full).

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: harvmac
caption: Macros for scientific articles

descriptions.text: Known as Harvard macros, since written at that University.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: hatching
caption: MetaPost macros for hatching interior of closed paths

descriptions.text: The file hatching.mp contains a set of MetaPost macros for hatching interior of closed paths. Examples of usage are included.

name: hausarbeit-jura
caption: Class for writing <q>juristische Hausarbeiten</q> at German Universities

descriptions.text: The class was developed for use by students writing legal essays (juristische Hausarbeit) at German Universities. It is based on jurabook and jurabib and makes it easy for LaTeX beginners to get a correct and nicely formatted paper.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: havannah
caption: Diagrams of board positions in the games of Havannah and Hex

descriptions.text: This package defines macros for typesetting diagrams of board positions in the games of Havannah and Hex.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: hawkdraw
caption: Draw vector graphics using l3draw with a simple syntax

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package allows the user to use a simple syntax similar to TikZ to generate vector graphic output based on l3draw and related LaTeX3 modules such as l3fp which provides very precise calculations. The syntax is meant to be simple and flexible but also coherent and logical with the aim of allowing the user to quickly draw graphics. The package name relates to the quickness and agility of hawks and the preciseness of their eyesight.

The package intends to define a set of user-level commands that can be used for drawing simple graphics. It does not aim be a substitute for the TikZ package or to offer a similar scope of application.

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

name: hcbundle
caption: Replacement for the LaTeX classes

descriptions.text: A set of replacements for the default LaTeX classes, based upon the Koma-Script bundle and the seminar class. Includes hcart, hcreport, hcletter, and hcslides.

name: hduThesiS
caption: LaTeX class for bachelor and MPhil theses in Hangzhou Dianzi University

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX template for graduation theses from Hangzhou Dianzi University. It supports the formatting of bachelor and MPhil degree theses.

name: he-le-na
caption: Support for Serbian typesetting

descriptions.text: The package contains a number of commands defining Serbian abbreviations, and a large number of hyphenation exceptions.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: he-she
caption: Alternating pronouns to aid gender-neutral writing

descriptions.text: The package implements a version of semi-automatic pronoun switching for writing gender-neutral (and possibly annoying) prose. It has upper- and lowercase versions of switching pronouns for all case forms, plus anaphoric versions that reflect the current gender choice.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: headerfooter
caption: Define the layouts of page headers and footers

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
Defines (for LaTeX 2.09) the common model of left, centre, right entries for both odd and even pages.

This, and similar packages, are now superseded by fancyhdr.

name: Hebdomon
caption: A document class for report writing in university settings

descriptions.text: This package provides a documentclass for streamlining document creation in LaTeX. It does not overwrite any TeX or LaTeX commands so the user could use their own macros or other commands as they wish.

documentation.details: Package documentation and example of use

name: hebrew-fonts
caption: Input encodings, font encodings and font definition files for Hebrew

descriptions.text: A collection of input encodings, font encodings and font definition files for the Hebrew language.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines
documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: hebtex
caption: Support for Hebrew and other right-to-left languages

descriptions.text: A comprehensive collection of fonts, macros, and support material for typesetting Hebrew and other right-to-left languages.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

name: hecthese
caption: A class for dissertations and theses at HEC Montréal

descriptions.text:
This package provides the hecthese class, a class based on memoir and compatible with LaTeX.

Using this class, postgraduate students at HEC Montréal will be able to write their dissertation or thesis while complying with all the presentation standards required by the University.

This class is meant to be as flexible as possible; in particular, there are very few hardcoded features except those that take care of the document’s layout.

Dissertations and theses at HEC Montréal can be written on a per-chapter or per-article basis. Documents that are written on a per-article basis require a bibliography for each of the included articles and a general bibliography for the entire document. The hecthese class takes care of these requirements.

name: hellas
caption: Typeset bibliographies which include Greek

descriptions.text: Hellas is a BibTeX style, based on the standard plain style, for typesetting databases that containing both Greek and non-Greek bibliographic records. For most bibliographic record types there is an equivalent record type whose name begins with the prefix gr-. These gr-something records may have fields translator and original-title in addition to the fields one might expect in a standard BibTeX record.

name: helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation
caption: Beautiful in-line microtonal just intonation accidentals

descriptions.text:
The Helmholtz-Ellis JI Pitch Notation (HEJI), devised in the early 2000s by Marc Sabat and Wolfgang von Schweinitz, explicitly notates the raising and lowering of the untempered diatonic Pythagorean notes by specific microtonal ratios defined for each prime. It provides visually distinctive logos distinguishing families of justly tuned intervals that relate to the harmonic series. These take the form of strings of additional accidental symbols based on historical precedents, extending the traditional sharps and flats. Since its 2020 update, HEJI ver. 2 (HEJI2) provides unique microtonal symbols through the 47-limit.

This package is a simple LaTeX implementation of HEJI2 that allows for in-line typesetting of microtonal accidentals for use within theoretical texts, program notes, symbol legends, etc.

Documents must be compiled using XeLaTeX.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: helvet
caption: Load Helvetica, scaled

descriptions.text:
The package provides a means of loading Helvetica (and its clones), scaled so that it matches Times Roman (to some extent).

The package is delivered as part of the psnfss bundle, which is itself part of the LaTeX required set of packages.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: hep
caption: A <q>convenience wrapper</q> for High Energy Physics packages

descriptions.text: Loads the author’s hepunits and hepnicenames packages, and a selection of others that are useful in High Energy Physics papers, etc.

name: hep-acronym
caption: An acronym extension for glossaries

descriptions.text:
The hep-acronym package provides an acronym macro based on the glossaries package.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-acronym}.

name: hep-bibliography
caption: An acronym extension for glossaries

descriptions.text:
The hep-bibliography package extends the BibLaTeX package with some functionality mostly useful for high energy physics. In particular it makes full use of all BibTeX fields provided by Discover High-Energy Physics.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-bibliography}.

name: hep-float
caption: Convenience package for float placement

descriptions.text:
The hep-float package redefines some LaTeX float placement defaults and defines convenience wrappers for floats.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-float}.

name: hep-font
caption: Latin modern extended by computer modern

descriptions.text:
The hep-font package loads standard font packages and extends the usual Latin Modern implementations by replacing missing fonts with Computer Modern counterparts.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-font}.

name: hep-gen
caption: Generic macros for quantum physics

descriptions.text: Provides macros for slashed variables, Dirac bra-ket notation and normal ordered products.

name: hep-graphic
caption: Extensions for graphics, plots and feynman graphs in high energy physics

descriptions.text: The hep-graphic package collects convenience macros that modify the behaviour of the TikZ, pgfplots, and TikZ-Feynman packages and ensure that the generated graphics look consistent.

name: hep-math
caption: Extended math macros

descriptions.text:
The hep-math package provides some additional features beyond the mathtools and amsmath packages.

To use the package place \usepackage{hep-math} in the preamble

name: hep-math-font
caption: Extended Greek and sans-serif math

descriptions.text:
The hep-math-font package adjust the math fonts to be sans-serif if the document is sans-serif. Additionally Greek letters are redefined to be always italic and upright in math and text mode respectively. Some math font macros are adjusted to give more consistently the naively expected results.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-math-font}.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: hep-paper
caption: Publications in High Energy Physics

descriptions.text:
This package aims to provide a single style file containing most configurations and macros necessary to write appealing publications in High Energy Physics. Instead of reinventing the wheel by introducing newly created macros, hep-paper preferably loads third party packages as long as they are light-weight enough.

For usual publications it suffices to load the hep-paper package, without optional arguments, in addition to the article class.

name: hep-reference
caption: Adjustments for publications in High Energy Physics

descriptions.text: This package makes some changes to the reference, citation and footnote macros to improve the default behavior of LaTeX for High Energy Physics publications.

name: hep-text
caption: List and text extensions

descriptions.text:
The hep-text package extends LaTeX lists using the enumitem package and provides some text macros.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-text}.

name: hep-title
caption: Extensions for the title page

descriptions.text:
The hep-title package extends the title macros of the standard classes with macros for a preprint, affiliation, editors, and endorsers.

The package is loaded with \usepackage{hep-title}.

name: hepnames
caption: Pre-defined high energy particle names

descriptions.text:
Hepnames provides a pair of LaTeX packages, heppennames and hepnicenames, providing a large set of pre-defined high energy physics particle names built with the hepparticles package. The packages are based on pennames.sty by Michel Goossens and Eric van Herwijnen.

Heppennames re-implements the particle names in pennames.sty, with some additions and alterations and greater flexibility and robustness due to the hepparticles structures, which were written for this purpose.

Hepnicenames provides the main non-resonant particle names from heppennames with more friendly names.

name: HEPparticles
caption: Macros for typesetting high energy physics particle names

descriptions.text:
HEPparticles is a set of macros for typesetting high energy particle names, to meet the following criteria:

1. The main particle name is a Roman or Greek symbol, to be typeset in upright font in normal contexts.

2. Additionally a superscript and/or subscript may follow the main symbol.

3. Particle resonances may also have a resonance specifier which is typeset in parentheses following the main symbol. In general the parentheses may also be followed by sub- and superscripts.

4. The particle names are expected to be used both in and out of mathematical contexts.

5. If the surrounding text is bold or italic then the particle name should adapt to that context as best as possible (this may not be possible for Greek symbols).

A consequence of point 5 is that the well-known problems with boldness of particle names in section titles, headers and tables of contents automatically disappear if these macros are used.

name: hepthesis
caption: A class for academic reports, especially PhD theses

descriptions.text:
Hepthesis is a LaTeX class for typesetting large academic reports, in particular PhD theses. It was originally developed for typesetting the author’s high-energy physics PhD thesis and includes some features specifically tailored to such an application. In particular, hepthesis offers:

  • Attractive semantic environments for various rubric sections;
  • Extensive options for draft production, screen viewing and binding-ready output;
  • Helpful extensions of existing environments, including equation and tabular; and
  • Support for quotations at the start of the thesis and each chapter.

The class is based on scrbook, from the KOMA-Script bundle.

documentation.details: Part of a thesis, seen as for printing

name: Hepunits
caption: A set of units useful in high energy physics applications

descriptions.text: Hepunits is a LaTeX package built on the SIunits package which adds a collection of useful HEP units to the existing SIunits set. These include the energy units \MeV, \GeV, \TeV and the derived momentum and mass units \MeVoverc, \MeVovercsq and so on.

name: here
caption: Emulation of obsolete package for <q>here</q> floats

descriptions.text:
Provides the H option for floats in LaTeX to signify that the environment is not really a float (and should therefore be placed here and not float at all). The package emulates an older package of the same name, which has long been suppressed by its author.

The job is done by nothing more than loading the float package, which has long provided the option in an acceptable framework.

name: hereapplies
caption: A LaTeX package for referencing groups of pages that share something in common

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: Here Applies is a LaTeX package that allows to collect groups of labels and reference them altogether. It can be used for creating informal glossaries that cross-link concepts to their applications, or simply mentioning multiple pages that share something in common.

name: heria
caption: A LaTeX class for Horizon Europe RIA and IA grant proposals

descriptions.text:
This class facilitates the preparation of Research and Innovation Action (RIA) and Innovation Action (IA) funding proposals for the European Commission’s Horizon Europe program.

The class is a conversion of the official Part B template into LaTeX; it preserves the formatting and most of the instructions of the original version, and has the additional feature that tables (listing the participants, work packages, deliverables, etc.) are programmatically generated according to data supplied by the user.

topics.details: typeset proposals to funding bodies, etc

name: heros-otf
caption: Using the OpenType fonts TeX Gyre Heros

descriptions.text:
This package can only be used with LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX. It does the font setting for the OpenType font TeX Gyre Heros.

The condensed versions of the fonts are also supported. The missing typefaces for slanted text are also defined.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: hershey
caption: Experiments with the Hershey fonts

descriptions.text:
The Hershey fonts were developed by the US government, and are freely available. The present bundle shows the outcome of some work on making the fonts usable as system fonts, with a view (eventually) to their use in typesetting programs.

The directory contains a number of Metafont sources, but not all will actually compile.

name: hershey-mp
caption: MetaPost support for the Hershey font file format

descriptions.text:
This package provides MetaPost support for reading jhf vector font files, used by (mostly? only?) the so-called Hershey Fonts of the late 1960s.

The package does not include the actual font files, which you can probably find in the software repository of your operating system.

topics.details: use, and support for use, of MetaPost
support tools and macros for MetaPost programming

name: heuristica
caption: Fonts extending Utopia, with LaTeX support files

descriptions.text:
The fonts extend the utopia set with Cyrillic glyphs, additional figure styles, ligatures and Small Caps in Regular style only.

Macro support, and maths fonts that match the Utopia family, are provided by the Fourier and the Mathdesign font packages.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
support languages written using Cyrillic alphabets
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

name: hex
caption: Print a counter in hexadecimal

descriptions.text: Defines a macro \hex that takes a counter name as argument.

name: hexboard
caption: For drawing Hex boards and games

descriptions.text: hexboard is a package for LaTeX that should also work with LuaTeX and XeTeX, that provides functionality for drawing Hex boards and games. The aim is a clean, clear design with flexibility for drawing different sorts of Hex diagrams.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: hexdump
caption: Read and typeset ASCII hexdump files

descriptions.text:
The main macro reads an ASCII hexdump file and puts it, verbatim, into the document. Additional macros provide, e.g., for a Directory of Dumps.

The package uses moreverb’s facilities, so depends on that package.

name: hexdumptikz
caption: Display hexdumps in LaTeX with the help of TikZ

descriptions.text:
Showing hexdumps is a common task in some fields. The most rudimentary form doing this in LaTeX is using a simple listings package. But often just showing the data is not enough. Instead, it needs to be annotated and explained.

This package offers exactly this feature by drawing each byte as a TikZ node. Note that this package explicitly aims to also support hexdumps with larger addresses (thinking of 64-bit addresses/offsets) here.

name: hexgame
caption: Provide an environment to draw a hexgame-board

descriptions.text: Hex is a mathematical game invented by the Danish mathematician Piet Hein and independently by the mathematician John Nash. This package defines an environment that enables the user to draw such a game in a trivial way.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: hf-tikz
caption: A simple way to highlight formulas and formula parts

descriptions.text: The package provides a way to highlight formulas and formula parts in both documents and presentations, us TikZ.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: hfbright
caption: The hfbright fonts

descriptions.text: These are Adobe Type 1 versions of the OT1-encoded and maths parts of the Computer Modern Bright fonts.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: hfoldsty
caption: Old style numerals with EC fonts

descriptions.text: The hfoldsty package provides virtual fonts for using oldstyle (0123456789) figures with the European Computer Modern fonts. It does a similar job as the eco package by Sebastian Kirsch but includes a couple of improvements, i.e., better kerning with guillemets, and support for character protruding using the pdfcprot package.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: HFUTExam
caption: Exam class for Hefei University of Technology (China)

descriptions.text: 该文档类提供了合肥工业大学考试试卷模板， 点击下方 Download 来下载所有文件。
This package provides an exam class for Hefei University of Technology (China).

name: hfutthesis
caption: LaTeX Thesis Template for Hefei University of Technology

descriptions.text: This project is based on the HFUT_Thesis LaTeX template of Hefei University of Technology compiled on the basis of ustctug/ustcthesis, in accordance with the latest version of Hefei University of Technology Graduate Dissertation Writing Specifications and Hefei University of Technology Undergraduate Graduation Project (Thesis) Work Implementation Rules.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: hge
caption: An <q>Old English</q> font

descriptions.text: This is a derivative, in Metafont, of the Old English font in the (free) Hershey collection.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: hhline
caption: Better horizontal lines in tabulars and arrays

descriptions.text:
The command \hhline produces a line like \hline, or a double line like \hline\hline, except for its interaction with vertical lines. The command takes a preamble (rather like the preamble of a tabular environment), and this specifies whether there are to be one or two horizontal lines, and what happens when the horizontal line meets a vertical one.

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: hhtensor
caption: Print vectors, matrices, and tensors

descriptions.text: This package provides commands for vectors, matrices, and tensors with different styles – arrows (as the LaTeX default), underlined, and bold.

name: hideanswer
caption: Generate documents with and without answers by toggling a switch

descriptions.text: This package can generate documents with and without answers from a single file by toggling a switch. However, it can only be used to create documents to be printed on paper.

name: hideproofs
caption: Defines a starred proof environment that hides proofs in draft mode

descriptions.text:
This package introduces an alternate proof environment, proof*, which conditionally hides or shows its contents based on the document mode (draft, final, or default). This is useful for omitting formal proofs from draft versions while retaining them in final documents.

The motivation for this package is to reduce the clutter in large files by omitting long proofs, allowing authors to focus their attention on results or proofs that are currently works in progress.

name: hieroglf
caption: The <q>poor man’s</q> Egyptian Hieroglyphic font

descriptions.text:
The hieroglf bundle provides a Type 1 rendition of some of the ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs. Hieroglyphic writing was used between about 3000 BC and 400 AD.

The bundle is based on Serge Rosmorduc's comprehensive hieroglyph package, but only provides about one tenth of his 650-odd hieroglyphs. Sufficient glyphs are provided for writing a few names like Cleopatra or Ptolomeny (together with cartouches) and some numbers, but the package is not for serious Egyptologists.

The bundle is part of a set of archaic fonts, and requires use of the oands fonts from that set.

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: hieroglyph
caption: Hieroglyph fonts and other support

descriptions.text: HieroTeX is a system for typesetting ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs. It contains a hieroglyphic font, a number of style files, and a helper program in C called sesh which allows one to type hieroglyphic texts using the manuel de codage, which is the current standard for encoding ancient Egyptian. The fonts in the base system are distributed as Metafont source, but Adobe type 1 versions are also provided.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

name: highlight
caption: Converts source code to syntax highlighted TeX or LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This is a program which converts source code to TeX and LaTeX with syntax highlighting. It is possible to add custom programming language definitions easily.

Highlight supports 100 programming languages and includes 50 colour themes. It features code reformatting and indenting.

name: highlightlatex
caption: Syntax highlighting for LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides extensive colored syntax highlighting for LaTeX. For this purpose it builds on the generic listings package.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: highlightx
caption: Highlight formulas or paragraphs

descriptions.text:
This package provides commands (in French or English) to highlight formulas or paragraphs with handwriting effect:

  • coded using soul and TikZ;
  • \SurlignerFormule and \SurlignerTexte in French;
  • \HighlightFormula and \HighlightText in English.

The code for highlighting paragraphs with a handwriting effect has been contributed by Antal Spector-Zabusky.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: hilowres
caption: Support high and low resolution versions of same picture

descriptions.text: A package to simplify the inclusion of low resolution versions of high resolution images, if each pair of files have the same basename (e.g., bird_low.eps and bird.eps). The package is a simple wrapper around the \includegraphics command of the graphicx package.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: hindawi-latex-template
caption: A LaTeX template for authors of the Hindawi journals

descriptions.text:
This package contains a LaTeX template for authors of the Hindawi journals. Authors can use this template for formatting their research articles for submissions.

The package has been created and is maintained by the Typeset team.

name: hindmadurai
caption: The HindMadurai font face with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides the HindMadurai family of fonts designed by the Indian Type Foundry, with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: histogr
caption: Draw histograms with the LaTeX picture environment

descriptions.text: This is a collection pf macros to draw histogram bars inside a LaTeX picture-environment.

name: historische-zeitschrift
caption: BibLaTeX style for the journal <q>Historische Zeitschrift</q>

descriptions.text:
The package provides citations according with the house style of the Historische Zeitschrift, a German historical journal. The scheme is a fullcite for the first citation and Author, Shorttitle (as note N, P) for later citations (P being the page number). For further details, see the description of the house style at the journal's site.

The package depends on BibLaTeX (version 3.3 or higher) as well as etoolbox (version 1.5 or higher).

name: histyle
caption: A <q>HighStyle</q> environment for TeX

descriptions.text:
Described as very rudimentary beginnings of HighStyle environment for [Plain] TeX. The package defines a bunch of macros and (LaTeX-like) environments in support of its aim.

(There's no documentation, to speak of, and no information about HighStyle, on which the package is supposedly based: there seems to be no information about HighStyle on the Web, either.)

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: hitec
caption: Class for documentation

descriptions.text: An article-based class designed for use for documentation in high-technology companies.

name: hitex
caption: A TeX extension writing HINT output for on-screen reading

descriptions.text:
An extension of TeX which generates HINT output.

The HINT file format is an alternative to the DVI and PDF formats which was designed specifically for on-screen reading of documents. Especially on mobile devices, reading DVI or PDF documents can be cumbersome. Mobile devices are available in a large variety of sizes but typically are not large enough to display documents formated for a4/letter-size paper. To compensate for the limitations of a small screen, users are used to alternating between landscape (few long lines) and portrait (more short lines) mode.

The HINT format supports variable and varying screen sizes, leveraging the ability of TeX to format a document for nearly-arbitrary values of \hsize and \vsize.

documentation.details: HiTeX documentation, in both PDF and HINT formats

name: hitex-def
caption: Support files for HiTeX

descriptions.text: Base support files for HiTeX, both plain and LaTeX,

name: hithesis
caption: Harbin Institute of Technology Thesis Template

descriptions.text: hithesis is a LaTeX thesis template package for Harbin Institute of Technology supporting bachelor, master, doctor dissertations.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: hitreport
caption: Harbin Institute of Technology Report LaTeX Template

descriptions.text: This package provides an assignment and experiment report template free of configuration designed for undergraduates on the three campuses of Harbin Institute of Technology.

name: hitszbeamer
caption: A beamer theme for Harbin Institute of Technology, ShenZhen

descriptions.text: This is a beamer theme designed for Harbin Institute of Technology, ShenZhen (HITSZ).

name: HITSZThesis
caption: A dissertation template for Harbin Institute of Technology, ShenZhen

descriptions.text: This package provides a dissertation template for Harbin Institute of Technology, ShenZhen (HITSZ), including bachelor, master and doctor dissertations.

name: HitType
caption: Typesetting Hittite cuneiform

descriptions.text:
This package allows for typing in Hittite cuneiform in LaTeX documents, using parsing based on the Latin transcriptions of the various signs. It also includes some formatting commands designed to allow for easy formatting of heterographic compounds, as well as shorthands for symbols commonly used in transcriptions.

The UllikummiA.ttf, UllikummiB.ttf, and UllikummiC.ttf files comprise the Ullikummi Hittite cuneiform fonts developed by Dr Sylvie Vanséveren, distributed with written permission from Dr Vanséveren, available on Hethitologie Portal Mainz at https://www.hethport.uni-wuerzburg.de/cuneifont/.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: hktex
caption: A TeX/LaTeX equivalent for Android

descriptions.text: The package offers formula parsing software written for mobile phones and tablets using the Android operating system. It is developed entirely with Google Eclipse and thus allows app developers and book writers to import the files easily.

name: hlatex
caption: Support for the Korean language

descriptions.text: Support for Korean documents written in Korean standard KSC codes for LaTeX2e.

name: HLaTeX fonts
caption: A collection of Korean (Hangul) fonts

descriptions.text:
A collection of fonts in Adobe Type 1 format for use with HLaTeX, Korean LaTeX.

The CJK fonts provide a replacement route to font support for Korean.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: hletter
caption: Flexible letter typesetting with flexible page headings

descriptions.text: The package permits the user to specify easily, with the aid of self defined key-words, letters (with a logo and private) and headings. The heading may include a footer and the letter provides commands to include a scanned signature and two signees. The package works with the merge package.

name: hlist
caption: Horizontal and columned lists

descriptions.text:
This plain TeX and LaTeX package provides the hlist environment in which \hitem starts a horizontal and columned item.

It depends upon the simplekv package.

name: hmtrump
caption: Describe card games

descriptions.text: This package provides a font with LuaLaTeX support for describing card games.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
fonts that provide collections of symbols
metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: hobby
caption: An implementation of Hobby’s algorithm for PGF/TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package defines a path generation function for PGF/TikZ which implements Hobby’s algorithm for a path built out of Bezier curves which passes through a given set of points. The path thus generated may by used as a TikZ to path.

The implementation is in LaTeX3.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers
graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: hobete
caption: Unofficial beamer theme for the University of Hohenheim

descriptions.text:
The package provides a beamer theme which features the Ci colors of the University of Hohenheim.

Please note that this is not an official Theme, and that there will be no support for it, from the University. Furthermore there is NO relationship between the University and this theme.

name: hobsub
caption: Construct package bundles

descriptions.text:
Heiko Oberdiek’s hobsub package (and hobsub-hyperref and hobsub-generic packages) defined a mechanism for concatenating multiple files into a single file for faster loading.

The disadvantage is that it introduces hard dependencies between the source files that are included and complicates distribution and updates.

It was principally used with hyperref but is not currently used in any standard packages in TeX Live.

The packages are still distributed as simple stubs that reference the included packages via \RequirePackage rather than copying their source.

The documented source of the original packages is available at github, but is not distributed to CTAN.

name: hoffset-voffset
caption: Calculate values for \hoffset and \voffset

descriptions.text: The bundle contains Pascal source, and a Windows executable.

name: hologo
caption: A collection of logos with bookmark support

descriptions.text: The package defines a single command \hologo, whose argument is the usual case-confused ASCII version of the logo. The command is bookmark-enabled, so that every logo becomes available in bookmarks without further work.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use
symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: holtpolt
caption: Typeset Maxwell’s non-commutative division

descriptions.text:
Defines two commands \holter and \polter that typeset Maxwell’ non-commutative division operations.

The package is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

name: holtxdoc
caption: Documentation macros for oberdiek bundle, etc

descriptions.text: These are personal macros, which are not necessarily useful to other authors (they are provided as part of the source of others of the author’s packages). Macros that may be of use to other authors are available separately, in package hypdoc.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: homework
caption: A LaTeX class for writing your homework

descriptions.text:
The current document class is for writing homework. It has the following features.

  • Simple and clear interface.
  • Built-in support for many theorem-type environments, already configured and ready to use.
  • Multilingual support.
  • Page numbers are of the form Page [current] of [total], which can help you ensure that there are no missing pages when you print your homework for submission.
  • Support writing problem statements and solutions (or proofs) in different colors.
  • Every statement and solution has its own QED symbol, in hollow or solid shape, respectively.
  • You can mark the unfinished parts, and a report shall be generated at the end of your document for reminding.

documentation.details: Example of an Exercise Sheet, with Answer

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: hook-pre-commit-pkg
caption: Pre-commit git hook for LaTeX package developers

descriptions.text:
This package provides a pre-commit git hook to check basic LaTeX syntax for the use of package developers.

It is installed by copying it into the .git/.hooks file.

It then checks the following file types: .sty, .dtx, .bbx, .cbx, and .lbx.

List of performed checks:

  • Each line must be terminated by a %, without a space before it. Empty lines are allowed, but not lines with nothing but spaces in them.
  • \begin{macro} and \end{macro} must be paired.
  • \begin{macrocode} and \end{macrocode} must be paired.
  • \begin{macro} must have a second argument.
  • One space must be printed between % and \begin{macro} or \end{macro}. % must be the first character in the line.
  • Four spaces must be printed between % and \begin{macrocode} or \end{macrocode}.
  • \cs argument must not start with a backslash.

name: hopatch
caption: Load patches for packages

descriptions.text: Hopatch provides a command with which the user may register of patch code for a particular package. Hopatch will apply the patch immediately, if the relevant package has already been loaded; otherwise it will store the patch until the package appears.

name: horoscop
caption: Generate astrological charts in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The horoscop package provides a unified interface for astrological font packages; typesetting with pict2e of standard wheel charts and some variations, in PostScript- and PDF-generating TeX engines; and access to external calculation software (Astrolog and Swiss Ephemeris) for computing object positions.

name: HPtfm2pl
caption: Create TeX PL files from HP AutoFont Support

descriptions.text: HP provides Autofont support files for all of the built-in printer fonts and all of the cartridges that it sells. Use HPtfm2pl to create PL files, and then pltotf to convert those to TFM files.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: hp2xx
caption: HP GL converter

descriptions.text: HP2xx is a versatile tool to convert vector-oriented graphics data given in Hewlett-Packard's HP-GL plotter language into a variety of popular graphics formats, both vector- and raster-oriented. HP2xx may also be used as an HP GL viewer on certain platforms.

name: hpgl2ps
caption: Translate HPGL to PostScript

descriptions.text: An ancient converter, which covers (most of) the language of DXY plotters, and RD-GL format (a superset of HPGL at the time the program was written). The converter doesn't cover all of the respective languages, but warns about things it doesn't understand.

topics.details: convert a foreign graphics format for use with TeX

name: hpsdiss
caption: A dissertation class

descriptions.text: The class was developed to typeset a dissertation at ETH Zürich. The requirements were to use A5 paper and 10pt type. A sample of the output is shown in the PDF documentation link.

name: href-ul
caption: Underscored LaTeX hyperlinks

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package makes hyperlinks underscored, just like on the web. The package uses hyperref and ulem.

name: hrefhide
caption: Suppress hyper links when printing

descriptions.text:
This package provides the command \hrefdisplayonly (additionally to \href provided by the hyperref package). While the (hyperlinked) text appears like an ordinary \href in the compiled pdf-file, the same text will be hidden when printing the text. Hiding is actually achieved by making the text the same colour as the background, thus preserving the layout of the rest of the text.

Further the commands \hycon and \hycoff (hyper-colour-on/off) can be used to simulate switching option ocgcolorlinks of the hyperref package on and off.

This package is possibly obsolete, see section 3: Alternatives in the documentation.

name: hrhyph
caption: Croatian hyphenation

descriptions.text:
Hyphenation patterns for the Croatian language for use with T1 encoding as supported in EC fonts.

Note that these patterns are no longer used by distributions; a version of the patterns, encoded in UTF-8, are the location of current development.

name: hrlatex
caption: LaTeX support for Croatian documents

descriptions.text: This package simplifies creation of new documents for the (average) Croatian user. As an example, a class file hrdipl.cls (designed for the graduation thesis at the University of Zagreb) and sample thesis documents are included.

name: hsindex
caption: An alternative index processor to imakeidx written with Haskell

descriptions.text:
HsIndex is an index generator that can be used with the LaTeX (LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, ...) processor in association with the imakeidx package.

HsIndex was made to compensate the absence and/or buggy version of xindy in Debian.

name: html2latex
caption: Convert HTML to LaTeX

descriptions.text: An HTML to LaTeX translator originally written in C, but now recast as a Perl module.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: htmlhelp
caption: HTML translation of VMS help files

descriptions.text: A series zip archives of HTML files derived from VMS help for BibTeX, LaTeX, makeindex and SliTeX.

name: hu-berlin-bundle
caption: LaTeX classes for the Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin

descriptions.text:
This package provides files according to the corporate design of the Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. This is not an official package by the university itself, and not officially approved by it.

More information can be found in the Humboldt University’s corporate design guideline and on the website https://www.hu-berlin.de/de/hu-intern/design.

At present, the bundle contains a letter class based on scrlttr2 and a package hu-berlin-base.sty which contains all relevant code for documents and documentclasses of the bundle.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: huawei
caption: Template for Huawei documents

descriptions.text: This unofficial package provides a class for creating documents for people working with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.

name: huaz
caption: Automatic Hungarian definite articles and suffixes

descriptions.text: In Hungarian there are two definite articles, a and az, which are determined by the pronunciation of the subsequent word. The definite article is az, if the first phoneme of the pronounced word is a vowel, otherwise it is a. The huaz package helps the user to insert automatically the correct definite article for cross-references and other commands containing text. Another service offered by the package is the automatic suffixing of numbers and cross-references, also based on their pronunciation.

name: huffman
caption: Drawing binary Huffman trees with MetaPost and METAOBJ

descriptions.text: This MetaPost package allows to draw general q-ary Huffman trees from two arrays : an array of strings, and an array of weights (numeric). It is based on the METAOBJ package which provides many tools to build trees in general.

name: huhyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for the Hungarian language

descriptions.text: This set of patterns is now superseded by those in the hungarian bundle.

name: hulipsum
caption: Hungarian dummy text (Lórum ipse)

descriptions.text:
Lorem ipsum is an improper Latin filler dummy text, cf. the lipsum package. It is commonly used for demonstrating the textual elements of a document template.

Lórum ipse is a Hungarian variation of Lorem ipsum. (Lórum is a Hungarian card game, and ipse is a Hungarian slang word meaning bloke.) With this package you can typeset 150 paragraphs of Lórum ipse.

All paragraphs are taken with permission from http://www.lorumipse.hu. Thanks to Lórum Ipse Lab (Viktor Nagy and Dávid Takács) for their work.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: humanbio
caption: Bibliography style for <q>Human Biology</q>

descriptions.text: A style derived from apalike in the BibTeX bundle, adopting further features from astron.bst; use with the LaTeX package that comes with astron.

name: humanist
caption: Humanist manuscript book-hand font

descriptions.text:
The humanist and allhmin packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Humanist manuscript book-hand used from the 14th century AD onwards. The font consists of uppercase and lowercase letters, digits and some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: humannat
caption: Bibliography style for <q>Human Nature</q> and <q>American Anthropologist</q>

descriptions.text: A style derived from apalike.bst in the BibTeX distribution, adopting further features from astron.bst; use with the LaTeX package that comes with astron.

name: huncial
caption: Fonts based on the half Uncial manuscript book-hand

descriptions.text:
The huncial and allhuncl packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Half Uncial manuscript book-hand used between the 3rd and 9th centuries. The font consists of minuscules and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks and ligatures. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: hungarian
caption: New Hungarian hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text: These patterns are a modern substitute for those in the huhyph package.

name: hust-beamer
caption: An unofficial 16:9 Beamer theme for Huazhong University of Science and Technology

descriptions.text:
The package provides an unofficial 16:9 Beamer theme for Huazhong University of Science and Technology. It provides coordinated cover, section, outline, content, and closing pages, a compact title system, itemized lists, semantic blue and pink boxes, and bundled vector HUST identity assets.

The package targets XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX and builds on beamer and Moloch.

name: hustthesis
caption: Unofficial thesis template for Huazhong University

descriptions.text: The package provides an Unofficial Thesis Template in LaTeX for Huazhong University of Science and Technology.

name: hustvisual
caption: Visual identity of Huazhong University of Science and Technology

descriptions.text: The package provides a collection of visual identity assets for Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST), implemented using LaTeX3 and TikZ.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: hvarabic
caption: Macros for RTL typesetting

descriptions.text:
This package provides some macros for right-to-left typesetting.

It uses by default the arabic fonts Scheherazade and ALM fixed, the only monospaced arabic font.

The package works with LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX, but not with pdfLaTeX or latex.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Arabic

name: hvdashln
caption: Horizontal and vertical dashed lines in arrays and tabulars

descriptions.text:
Definitions of horizontal and vertical dashed lines for the array and tabular environment. Instead of building partial horizontal dashed lines using Isozaki's \cline{2-3}, \hdashline fills the full width. The proportion of the dashed line is defined by the two parameters: \hdashlinewidth=2pt and \hdashlinegap=2pt, where the former defines the width of the dash and the latter sets their gap.

Note that this functionality has been re-implemented, for current LaTeX, in the package arydshln.

name: hvextern
caption: Write and execute external code, and insert the output

descriptions.text: This package allows to write MetaPost, TeX, ConTeXt, LaTeX, LuaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeTeX, XeLaTeX, Lua, Perl, or Python source code into an external file, run that file via shell-escape to create PDF, PNG, or text output, and include that output automatically into the main LaTeX document.

topics.details: manipulating images for inclusion in documents
run an external program from within a document

name: hvfloat
caption: Controlling captions, fullpage and doublepage floats

descriptions.text:
hvfloat

Placing figures/tables with various options, like rotating the image/table and/or caption. Placing object and caption side by side in one- and twocolumn mode. Fullpage objects with captions on the preceeding or following page in one- and twocolumn mode.

hvfloat-fps

Simple global placement setting for floats

name: hvindex
caption: Support for indexing

descriptions.text: The package simplifies the indexing of words using the \index command of makeidx. With the package, to index a word in a text, you only have to type it once; the package makes sure it is both typeset and indexed.

name: hvlogos
caption: Print TeX-related names as logo

descriptions.text:
This package is more or less an extension to Heiko Oberdiek’s package hologo. It prints TeX-related names as logos.

The package requires fetamont, hologo, dantelogo, and xspace.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: hvmath
caption: Support for using the Micropress HV-Math fonts (Helvetica Maths)

descriptions.text: Typeset math in a style that suits the Adobe Helvetica text fonts. Commercial (Adobe type 1) versions of the HV-Math fonts are available from Micropress; free bitmap versions of the fonts from the Micropress fonts directories.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: hvmath-fonts
caption: Bitmap versions of the Micropress HV-Math fonts (Helvetica Maths)

descriptions.text: This is the public part of the HV-Math font distribution: metrics, and a set of bitmap files. Actually to use the fonts, you probably also need the macros by Walter Schmidt.

topics.details: font distributed in an ad-hoc fashion

name: hvpygmentex
caption: Syntax-Highlighting of program code

descriptions.text: The package is based on pygmentex but provides an automatic run from within the document itself, with the option --shell-escape. It does not need the additional action by the user to run the external program pygmentize to create the code snippets.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: hvqrurl
caption: Insert a QR code in the margin

descriptions.text: This package allows to draw an URL as a QR code into the margin of a one- or twosided document. The following packages are loaded by default: qrcode, marginnote, url, xcolor and xkeyval.

name: hwemoji
caption: Unicode emoji support for pdfLaTeX with sequences

descriptions.text: This package provides direct support for Unicode emoji in pdfLaTeX, with full access to emoji sequences including but not limited to flag sequences, diversity modifier sequences, and tag sequences. Emojis are displayed through Twemoji digital assets, as licensed under the CC-BY 4.0.

name: hwkatakana
caption: Half-width katakana fonts

descriptions.text:
Half-width katakana Type 1 fonts in SJIS encoding are provided to integrate with the Wadalab fonts for use with, for example, the CJK package. Auxiliary files to use the font with Unicode UTF8 encoding are also provided. The origin of the font is the Wadalab gothic font katakana glyphs, which have been modified to make up the JIS X 0201 set of half-width katakana characters using Fontforge. The Wadalab fonts need to be available for this package to work.

Note: This package has now been included in the Wadalab fonts bundle so that this separate bundle is considered obsolete.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: hyacc-cm
caption: Hyphenation using 7-bit fonts

descriptions.text: A scheme for obtaining respectable hyphenation in the presence of accents, using only CM fonts (and in the absence of the MLTeX extensions).

name: hybrid-latex
caption: Allow active Python code in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: This is a collection of Python and Bash shell scripts that allows LaTeX documents to contain active Python code. The active code blocks are processed ahead of LaTeX and their results are accessible within the same LaTeX document. Thus a calculation that might otherwise be done in two documents, one using Python to do the maths, and a separate LaTeX document to record the results, can be consolidated into a single source.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: hycolor
caption: Implements colour for packages hyperref and bookmark

descriptions.text: This package provides the code for the color option that is used by packages hyperref and bookmark. It is not intended as package for the user.

name: hypbmsec
caption: Hypertext bookmarks in sectioning commands

descriptions.text:
Bookmark entries can be given as another argument to the LaTeX sectioning commands. The hyperref package is required to get the bookmarks, but the syntax works without it.

This package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: hypcap
caption: Adjusting the anchors of captions

descriptions.text:
The package offers a solution to the problem that when you link to a float using hyperref, the link anchors to below the float’s caption, rather than the beginning of the float.

Hypcap defines a separate \capstart command, which you put where you want links to end; you should have a \capstart command for each \caption command. Package options can be used to auto-insert a \capstart at the start of a float environment.

name: hypdestopt
caption: Hyperref destination optimizer

descriptions.text: This package supports hyperref’s pdfTeX driver. It removes unnecessary destinations and shortens the destination names or uses numbered destinations to get smaller PDF files.

name: hypdoc
caption: Hyper extensions for doc.sty

descriptions.text: This package adds hypertext features to the package doc that is used in the documentation system of LaTeX2e. Bookmarks are added and references are linked as far as possible.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: hypdvips
caption: Hyperref extensions for use with dvips

descriptions.text: The hypdvips package fixes some problems when using hyperref with dvips. It also adds support for breaking links, file attachments, embedded documents and different types of GoTo-links. The cooperation of hyperref with cleveref is improved, which in addition allows an enhanced back-referencing system.

name: hyper
caption: Hypertext cross referencing

descriptions.text:
Redefines LaTeX cross-referencing commands to insert \special commands for HyperTeX dvi viewers, such as recent versions of xdvi.

The package is now largely superseded by hyperref.

name: hyperbar
caption: Add interactive Barcode fields to PDF forms

descriptions.text:
The package extends the hyperref functionality for creating interactive forms to allow adding Barcode form fields supported by some modern PDF readers.

Currently, only pdfTeX is supported.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

name: hyperlatex
caption: A restricted LaTeX system that also produces HTML

descriptions.text:
HyperLaTeX defines a form of LaTeX that may be processed in the ordinary way with a latex command, for printed output. However, HyperLaTeX documents may also be processed by the program hyperlatex to produce good-quality HTML.

HyperLaTeX is not a LaTeX to HTML converter (see, for example, tth or latex2html for that). Rather, HyperLaTeX provides an environment where the author can prepare a document that may be converted to either print or HTML output.

name: hypernat
caption: Allow hyperref and natbib to work together

descriptions.text: Allows hyperref package and the natbib package with options numbers and sort&compress to work together. This means that multiple sequential citations (e.g [3,2,1]) will be compressed to [1-3], where the 1 and the 3 are (color-)linked to the bibliography.

name: hyperref
caption: Extensive support for hypertext in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The hyperref package is used to handle cross-referencing commands in LaTeX to produce hypertext links in the document. The package provides backends for the \special set defined for HyperTeX DVI processors; for embedded pdfmark commands for processing by Acrobat Distiller (dvips and Y&Y’s dvipsone); for Y&Y’s dviwindo; for PDF control within pdfTeX and dvipdfm; for TeX4ht; and for VTeX’s pdf and HTML backends.

The package is distributed with the backref and nameref packages, which make use of the facilities of hyperref.

The package depends on the author’s kvoptions, ltxcmds and refcount packages.

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: hyperxmp
caption: Embed XMP metadata within a LaTeX document

descriptions.text:
XMP (eXtensible Metadata Platform) is a mechanism proposed by Adobe for embedding document metadata within the document itself. The metadata is designed to be easy to extract, even by programs that are oblivious to the document's file format. Most of Adobe's applications store XMP metadata when saving files. Now, with the hyperxmp package, it is trivial for LaTeX document authors to store XMP metadata in their documents as well.

The package integrates seamlessly with hyperref and requires virtually no modifications to documents that already exploit hyperref's mechanisms for specifying PDF metadata. The current version of hyperxmp can embed the following metadata as XMP: title, authors, primary author's title or position, metadata writer, subject/summary, keywords, copyright, license URL, document base URL, document identifier and instance identifier, language, source file name, PDF generating tool, PDF version, and contact telephone number/postal address/email address/URL. Hyperxmp currently embeds XMP only within PDF documents; it is compatible with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, LaTeX+dvipdfm, and LaTeX+dvips+ps2pdf.

name: hypgotoe
caption: Links to embedded files

descriptions.text:
This experimental package is a first experiment for links to embedded files. It is named after the PDF action name /GoToE.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: hyph-utf8
caption: Hyphenation patterns expressed in UTF-8

descriptions.text:
Modern native UTF-8 engines such as XeTeX and LuaTeX need hyphenation patterns in UTF-8 format, whereas older systems require hyphenation patterns in the 8-bit encoding of the font in use (such encodings are codified in the LaTeX scheme with names like OT1, T2A, TS1, OML, LY1, etc).

The present package offers a collection of conversions of existing patterns to UTF-8 format, together with converters for use with 8-bit fonts in older systems. Since hyphenation patterns for Knuthian-style TeX systems are only read at iniTeX time, it is hoped that the UTF-8 patterns, with their converters, will completely supplant the older patterns.

name: hyphen-accent
caption: LaTeX 2.09 code for using DC fonts

descriptions.text: The bundle presents variants of the (pre-LaTeX2e) nfss, that may be used to typeset inflected Latin alphabet text using the DC fonts (the pre-release forrunners of the EC fonts), thus allowing hyphenation using the (then) new 8-bit hyphenation patterns.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: hyphen-spanish
caption: Standard hyphenation rules for Spanish

descriptions.text: This directory is a permanent place for the latest official release of the hyphenation patterns for the Spanish language, valid for XeTeX, LuaTeX, and pdfTeX, with the tools used to generate them.

name: hyphenat
caption: Disable/enable hyphenation

descriptions.text: This package can disable all hyphenation or enable hyphenation of non-alphabetics or monospaced fonts. The package can also enable hyphenation within words that contain non-alphabetic characters (e.g., that include underscores), and hyphenation of text typeset in monospaced (e.g., cmtt) fonts.

name: hyphenation-greek
caption: Hyphenation patterns for ancient and modern Greek

descriptions.text: Contains the hyphenation patterns for ancient Greek and modern Greek in polytonic (multi-accent) and monotonic (uni-accent) systems. The hyphenation patterns will work perfectly with the babel greek option or with Dryllerakis’ GreeKTeX. The patterns can easily be converted for use with the ibycus fonts (see the ibycus-babel package), or with Omega/Lambda (see the antomega package). For any other Greek package, the patterns will have to be re-coded.

name: hyphenex
caption: US English hyphenation exceptions file

descriptions.text:
Exceptions for American English hyphenation patterns are occasionally published in the TeX User Group journal TUGboat.

This bundle provides alternative Perl and Bourne shell scripts to convert the source of such an article into an exceptions file, together with a recent copy of the article and machine-readable files.

name: hyphsubst
caption: Substitute hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text:
A TeX format file may include alternative hyphenation patterns for a language with a different name. If the naming convention follows babel’s rules, then the hyphenation patterns for a language may be replaced by the alternative hyphenation patterns, provided in the format file.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: hypht1
caption: Additional hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text:
Additional hyphenation patterns which have to be loaded in conjunction with each normal set of patterns. The package contains patterns to allow hyphenation after an explicit - character, which are needed if you want to use (e.g.) the second hyphen character (\char127) of any T1-encoded font as \hyphenchar\font.

Usage details are described in comments in the file.

name: HyPlain
caption: Basic support for multiple languages in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: The package offers a means to set up hyphenation suitable for several languages and/or dialects, and to select them or switch between them while typesetting.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs
support for more than one (natural) language

name: i-ching
caption: An i-ching package

descriptions.text: A complete Plain TeX-based i-ching divination system, including an Adobe Type 1 font for the characters. Translations are derived from Alan Stanier's work in his iching package.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: iacrj
caption: A document class for IACR journal publications

copyright.owner: Joppe W. Bos and Kevin S. McCurley

descriptions.text:
The iacrj document class is used to produce publications for three IACR journals. It is intended as an eventual replacement for iacrcc.cls and iacrtrans.cls. It can be used to produce publications for IACR Communications in Cryptology, IACR Transactions on Symmetric Cryptology, and IACR Transactions on Cryptographic Hardware and Embedded Systems.

iacrj.cls is part of a larger set of tools for implementing a journal publishing workflow, and it depends on the metacapture.sty package. There is also a companion open source implementation of a publishing workflow written in Python that is used for this journal and provides a simplified workflow for copy editing and production. Further information on this workflow can be found in two articles that were published by the authors:

  • Lowering the Cost of Diamond Open Access Journals,
  • A LaTeX publishing workflow

name: iagproc
caption: Class for two column IAG Proceedings articles

descriptions.text: LaTeX2e class file for two column IAG Proceedings articles, like those for the Banff GGG2000 Symposium or the Thessaloniki IGGC 2002 meeting.

name: iahyphen
caption: Hyphenation patterns for Interlingua

descriptions.text: Interlingua is an international auxiliary language.

topics.details: support for a language whose support is not otherwise catalogued

name: iaria
caption: Write documents for the IARIA publications

descriptions.text: This package contains templates for the creation of documents for IARIA publications (International Academy, Research, and Industry Association) and implements the specifications for the IARIA citation style.

topics.details: prepare documents for a specific publisher

name: iaria-lite
caption: Write documents for the IARIA publications

descriptions.text:
This package provides a convenient environment for writing IARIA (International Academy, Research, and Industry Association) scholary publications.

It does not implement the specifications for the IARIA citation style, for which you have to use the iaria class.

topics.details: prepare documents for a specific publisher

name: ibarra
caption: LaTeX support for the Ibarra Real Nova family of fonts

descriptions.text: The Ibarra Real Nova is a revival of a typeface designed by Geronimo Gil for the publication of Don Quixote for the Real Academia de la Lengua in 1780. Joaquin Ibarra was the printer.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: ibm
caption: Metrics for IBM fonts

descriptions.text: These metrics (a TFM and a VF file) cover a font whose actual identity is unclear to the present cataloguer; it appears to be a variant of Times, but is not included in the package.

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: ibmres-tex
caption: A semi-automated approach to the production of resumes

descriptions.text: The package is designed to offer advice on creating effective resumés, and to provide a mechanism for generating one, based on a series of templates.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: ibrackets
caption: Intelligent brackets

descriptions.text: This small package provides a new definition of brackets [ and ] as active characters to get correct blank spaces in mathematical mode when using for open intervals. Instead of parenthesis: ]-\infty, 0[ is equivalent to (-\infty, 0).

name: ibycus-babel
caption: Use the Ibycus 4 Greek font with Babel

descriptions.text: The package allows you to use the Ibycus 4 font for ancient Greek with Babel. It uses a Perl script to generate hyphenation patterns for Ibycus from those for the ordinary Babel encoding, cbgreek. It sets up ibycus as a pseudo-language you can specify in the normal Babel manner. For proper hyphenation of Greek quoted in mid-paragraph, you should use it with elatex (all current distributions of LaTeX are built with e-TeX, so the constraint should not be onerous).

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: ibygrk
caption: Fonts and macros to typeset ancient Greek

descriptions.text:
Ibycus is a Greek typeface, based on Silvio Levy’s realisation of a classic Didot cut of Greek type from around 1800. The fonts are available both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format.

This distribution of ibycus is accompanied by a set of macro packages to use it with Plain TeX or LaTeX, but for use with Babel, see the ibycus-babel package.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: icehyph
