caption: Icelandic hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text: Hyphenation patterns for Icelandic; apparently designed for a modern encoding (by contrast with ishyph, whose encoding is not apparently published.

topics.details: support for typesetting the Icelandic language

name: icelandic
caption: Icelandic Fonts

descriptions.text:
Sources for Icelandic Fonts, together with some macro support, under Plain TeX and LaTeX 2.09.

The fonts seem not to compile correctly under current Metafont.

topics.details: support for typesetting the Icelandic language

name: iching
caption: A font for I Ching divinations

descriptions.text: A LaTeX file is provided to print out divinations, using the font (supplied as Metafont source). The \interpret macro in the LaTeX file is a simplified beast, in which significance is only accorded to one line in the hexagram.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: icite
caption: Indices locorum citatorum

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: The package is designed to produce from BibTeX or BibLaTeX bibliographical databases the different indices of authors and works cited which are called indices locorum citatorum. It relies on a specific \icite command and can operate with either BibTeX or BibLaTeX.

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: icomma
caption: Intelligent commas for decimal numbers

descriptions.text:
An intelligent comma, which yields proper spacing in decimal numbers as well as in mathematical expressions. In contrast to other known solutions, this package does not depend on the encoding of the CM maths fonts, and it works with decimal numbers of arbitrary length.

This package is part of the was bundle.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: icon-appr
caption: Creates icon appearances for form buttons

descriptions.text:
Use this package to create icon appearances for push buttons, check box buttons, and radio buttons form fields.

Package works for pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, dvips/distiller or dvips/ps2pdf; some techniques require Acrobat. Pdfmark-type drivers require, depending on the method used, aeb_pro or graphicxsp.

PDF Viewers: Adobe Reader DC, PDF-XChange Editor, and, of course Adobe Acrobat. SummatraPDF previews the icon buttons very well.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: icons
caption: TeX icons

descriptions.text: These are conversions of Knuth's icons (designed for the OpenWindows filemanager) for use in other systems.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: icsv
caption: Class for typesetting articles for the ICSV conference

descriptions.text: This is an ad-hoc class for typesetting articles for the ICSV conference, based on the earler active-conf by the same author.

name: idealfonts
caption: Font and LaTeX support for Textures users

descriptions.text: Consists of 2 files that might help Textures users: one to ease the use of the basic 35 Adobe fonts with the T1 font encoding with LaTeX; the other for people willing to automatically install the latest LaTeX version under Textures.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: IdeaVault
caption: Idea (concept) management package

descriptions.text:
This LuaLaTeX package provides tools for the management (i.e. creation and printing) of ideas (i.e. pieces of LaTeX code representing concepts).

It supports dependencies, nested idea printing and tags, and can be useful for writing rulebooks or handbooks with many definitions.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: identkey
caption: Typesetting bracketed dichotomous identification keys

descriptions.text: The package is for typesetting bracketed dichotomous identification keys.

name: idverb
caption: Inline verbatim identifiers

descriptions.text: Typeset identifiers (and other short things) verbatim, using the |identifier| notation. This package is part of the js-misc bundle.

name: idxcmds
caption: Semantic commands for adding formatted index entries

descriptions.text: The package provides commands for adding formatted index entries; it arises from the author’s work on large documents.

name: idxlayout
caption: Configurable index layout, responsive to KOMA-Script and memoir

descriptions.text: The idxlayout package offers a key-value interface to configure index layout parameters, e.g. allowing for three-column indexes or for parent items and their affiliated subitems being typeset as a single paragraph. The package is responsive to the index-related options and commands of the KOMA-Script and memoir classes.

name: idxtex
caption: An index processor

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
Idxtex is supplied as C source (and as a DOS executable), and a supporting package is provided (whose detection of current language is inadequate for current usage).

The bundle is distributed with glotex.

name: IEEEannot
caption: A sorting version of IEEEtran.bst

descriptions.text: IEEEannot is a LaTeX bibliography style to generate an annotated bibliography in the IEEE citation format. It should not be used in submissions to the IEEE.

name: IEEEconf
caption: Macros for IEEE conference proceedings

descriptions.text: The IEEEconf class implements the formatting dictated by the IEEE Computer Society Press for conference proceedings.

name: ieeepes
caption: IEEE Power Engineering Society Transactions

descriptions.text: Supports typesetting of transactions, as well as discussions and closures, for the IEEE Power Engineering Society Transactions journals.

name: IEEEtran
caption: Document class for IEEE Transactions journals and conferences

descriptions.text: The class and its BibTeX style enable authors to produce officially-correct output for the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) transactions, journals and conferences.

name: ieeetrantools
caption: Functionality from IEEEtran for use with other classes

descriptions.text: The package provides several commands from the IEEEtran class file so that they can be used under other LaTeX classes; the package should not be used in a document that uses that parent class. The user guide only covers the ways in which usage differs from that in the parent class; thus the documentation of that class should be regarded as part of the documentation for the package.

name: IEEJtran
caption: Unofficial bibliography style file for the Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan

descriptions.text: This package provides an unofficial BibTeX style for authors of the Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan (IEEJ) transactions journals and conferences.

name: ietfbibs
caption: Generate BibTeX entries for various IETF index files

descriptions.text: The package provides scripts to translate IETF index files to BibTeX files.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: iexec
caption: Execute shell commands and input their output

descriptions.text: With the help of the \iexec command, you can execute a shell command and then input its output into your document. This package also lets you use any special symbols inside your command.

name: ifacmtg
caption: Elsevier Science preprint style for IFAC meetings

descriptions.text: To prepare a paper for an IFAC meeting, using LaTeX, the author needs a bibliography style such as harvard.

name: ifallfalse
caption: Compare a string against a set of other strings

descriptions.text:
This package allows you to check whether a string is contained within another set of strings, and perform an action if it is not. This is done by using the allfalse environment and passing in a string and an action to be performed if the string is not contained in the set. Then, passing in a string to the \orcheck macro inside the respective allfalse environment adds that to the set of strings.

This package does not work with the LuaTeX engine.

name: ifdraft
caption: Detect <q>draft</q> and <q>final</q> class options

descriptions.text:
The package defines commands that switch according to the prevailing draft or final options; each command takes two arguments, the first for the true, the second for the false case. Commands are:

  • \ifdraft determines whether we're operating in draft (true) or final mode;
  • \ifoptiondraft determines whether a draft option has been given; and
  • \ifoptionfinal determines whether a final option has been given.

name: ifetex
caption: Provides \ifetex switch

descriptions.text:
The package provides the switch \ifetex which indicates whether e-TeX is available or not.

The package can be loaded as LaTeX package using \usepackage{ifetex} or in plain TeX using \input ifetex. In either case it aborts silently if the \ifetex macro is already defined.

The package’s test is whether \eTeXversion is defined as a primitive; if it is, the package assumes e-TeX features are available.

Please note, that ifetex is now part of iftex.

name: iffont
caption: Conditionally load fonts with fontspec

descriptions.text: This package provides a macro to select the first font XeLaTeX or LuaTeX can find in a comma separated list and, additionally, a number of macro tests.

name: ifis-macros
caption: Check if a given input string is a number or dimension for TeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: This package provides three macros: \ifisint, \ifisdim, and \ifisglue. They test if a given input string represents either a valid integer or a valid dimension or a valid (mu)glue specification for TeX.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: iflang
caption: Expandable checks for the current language

descriptions.text:
This package provides expandable checks for the current language based on macro \languagename or hyphenation patterns.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: ifluatex
caption: Provides the \ifluatex switch

descriptions.text:
The package looks for LuaTeX regardless of its mode and provides the switch \ifluatex; it works with Plain TeX or LaTeX.

The package has been integrated into the iftex bundle.

name: ifmslide
caption: Presentation slides for screen and printouts

descriptions.text: This package is used to produce printed slides with LaTeX and online presentations with pdfLaTeX. It is provided by the Institute of Mechanics (ifm) Univ. of Technology Darmstadt, Germany. It is based on ideas of pdfslide, but completely rewritten for compatibility with texpower and seminar. The manual describes all functions and provides a sample.

name: ifmtarg
caption: If-then-else command for processing potentially empty arguments

descriptions.text: This package provides a command for the LaTeX programmer for testing whether an argument is empty.

name: ifnextok
caption: Utility macro: peek ahead without ignoring spaces

descriptions.text:
The package deals with the behaviour of the LaTeX internal command \@ifnextchar, which skips blank spaces. This has the potential to surprise users, since it can produce really unwanted effects. A common example occurs with brackets starting a line following \\: the command looks for an optional argument, whereas the user wants the brackets to be printed.

The package offers commands and options for modifying this behaviour, maybe limited to certain parts of the document source.

name: ifoddpage
caption: Determine if the current page is odd or even

descriptions.text: The package provides an \ifoddpage conditional to determine if the current page is odd or even. The macro \checkoddpage must be used direct before to check the page number using a label. Two compiler runs are therefore required to achieve correct results. In addition, the conditional \ifoddpageoronside is provided which is also true in oneside mode where all pages use the odd page layout.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: ifpdf
caption: Provides the \ifpdf conditional

descriptions.text:
This package looks for pdfTeX in pdf mode and implements and sets the switch \ifpdf. The detection is based on the value of \pdfoutput (which the package will not change). The package works with plain or LaTeX formats. To use it with LaTeX simply \usepackage{ifpdf}. Then use \ifpdf ... \else ... \fi.

The package has been integrated into the iftex bundle.

name: ifplatform
caption: Conditionals to test which platform is being used

descriptions.text:
This package uses the (La)TeX extension -shell-escape to establish whether the document is being processed on a Windows or on a Unix-like system (Mac OS X, Linux, etc.), or on Cygwin (Unix environment over a windows system).

Booleans provided are:

  • \ifwindows,
  • \iflinux,
  • \ifmacosx and
  • \ifcygwin.

The package also preserves the output of uname on a Unix-like system, which may be used to distinguish between various classes of Unix systems.

name: ifptex
caption: Check if the engine is pTeX or one of its derivatives

descriptions.text: The ifptex package is a counterpart of ifxetex, ifluatex, etc. for the ptex engine. The ifuptex package is an alias to ifptex provided for backward compatibility.

name: ifsym
caption: A collection of symbols

descriptions.text: A set of symbol fonts, written in Metafont, offering (respectively) clock-face symbols, geometrical symbols, weather symbols, mountaineering symbols, electronic circuit symbols and a set of miscellaneous symbols. A LaTeX package is provided, that allows the user to load only those symbols needed in a document.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: iftex
caption: Am I running under pdfTeX, XeTeX or LuaTeX?

descriptions.text:
The package, which works both for Plain TeX and for LaTeX, defines the \ifPDFTeX, \ifXeTeX, and \ifLuaTeX conditionals for testing which engine is being used for typesetting.

The package also provides the \RequirePDFTeX, \RequireXeTeX, and \RequireLuaTeX commands which throw an error if pdfTeX, XeTeX or LuaTeX (respectively) is not the engine in use.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: ifthen
caption: Conditional commands in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
The package’s basic command is \ifthenelse, which can use a wide array of tests. Also provided is a simple loop command \whiledo.

Ifthen is a separate package within the LaTeX distribution; while it will always be present in a LaTeX distribution, a \usepackage command is always needed to load it.

name: ifthenx
caption: Extra tests for \ifthenelse

descriptions.text:
The package extends the ifthen package, providing extra predicates for the package’s \ifthenelse command.

The package is complementary to xifthen, in that they provide different facilities; the two may be loaded in the same document, as long as xifthen is loaded first.

name: ifvtex
caption: Detects use of VTeX and its facilities

descriptions.text:
The package looks for VTeX and sets the switch \ifvtex. In the presence of VTeX, the mode switches \ifvtexdvi, \ifvtexpdf and \ifvtexps are set; \ifvtexgex tells you whether GeX is operating.

The package has been integrated into the iftex bundle.

name: ifxetex
caption: Am I running under XeTeX?

descriptions.text:
A simple package which provides an \ifxetex conditional, so that other code can determine that it is running under XeTeX.

The package requires the e-TeX extensions to the TeX primitive set.

Please note that ifxetex is now part of the iftex bundle.

name: ifxptex
caption: Detect pTeX and its derivatives

descriptions.text: The package provides commands for detecting pTeX and its derivatives (e-pTeX, upTeX, e-upTeX, and ApTeX). Both LaTeX and plain TeX are supported.

name: igo
caption: Fonts and macro to typeset Go diagrams

descriptions.text: This package is based on the package go written in 1991 by Hanna Kołodziejska which provides typesetting facilities for Go games and positions. Although igo contains roughly the same commands as the original package and uses the fonts created by Kołodziejska, it has been improved in a number of ways. It uses command names less likely to conflict with standard AMS packages. It allows different board sizes to be used. It understands a standardized notation for board coordinates. And it provides a facility to work on more than one board. Moreover, a few commands were reworked to define positions or game sequences more conveniently.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: iitem
caption: Multiple level of lists in one list-like environment

descriptions.text:
The package defines multiple level lists within one list-like environment. instead of writing 

   \begin{enumerate}
    \item 1
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item 2
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item 3
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item 4
    \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
    \item 2.1
    \end{enumerate}
    \item 1.1
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item 2
    \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
this package allows you to write 
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item 1
   \iitem 2
   \iiitem 3
   \ivtem 4
   \iitem 2.1
   \item 1.1
   \iitem 2
  \end{enumerate}

name: ijc
caption: International Journal of Control style

descriptions.text: A version of the LaTeX 2.09 document style article, together with an appropriate BibTeX style.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: ijcai89
caption: Format papers for IJCAI 1989

descriptions.text: A package to format LaTeX 2.09 article-style documents in the format required for papers at the meeting. (An instructions for authors document is present in the distribution, but unfortunately it is incomplete.)

name: ijmart
caption: LaTeX Class for the Israel Journal of Mathematics

descriptions.text: The Israel Journal of Mathematics is published by The Hebrew University Magnes Press. This class provides LaTeX support for its authors and editors. It strives to achieve the distinct look and feel of the journal, while having the interface similar to that of the amsart document class. This will help authors already familiar with amsart to easily submit manuscripts for The Israel Journal of Mathematics or to put the preprints in arXiv with minimal changes in the LaTeX source.

name: ijqc
caption: BibTeX style file for the Intl. J. Quantum Chem

descriptions.text: ijqc.bst is a BibTeX style file to support publication in Wiley's International Journal of Quantum Chemistry. It is not in any way officially endorsed by the publisher or editors, and is provided without any warranty one could ever think of.

name: ijsra
caption: LaTeX document class for the International Journal of Student Research in Archaeology

descriptions.text: This is a document class called ijsra which is used for the International Journal of Student Research in Archaeology.

name: imac
caption: International Modal Analysis Conference format

descriptions.text: A set of files for producing correctly formatted documents for the International Modal Analysis Conference. The bundle provides a LaTeX package and a BibTeX style file.

name: image-gallery
caption: Create an overview of pictures from a digital camera or from other sources

descriptions.text: The class may be used to create an overview of pictures from a digital camera or from other sources. It is possible to adjust the size of the pictures and all the margins. The example file shows the usage.

name: imakeidx
caption: A package for producing multiple indexes

descriptions.text: The package enables the user to produce and typeset one or more indexes simultaneously with a document. The package is known to work in LaTeX documents processed with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. If makeindex is used for processing the index entries, no particular setting up is needed when TeX Live is used. Using xindy or other programs it is necessary to enable shell escape; shell escape is also needed if splitindex is used.

name: Imake-TeX
caption: An Imake system for TeX

descriptions.text:
Imake-TeX basically consists of a shell script texmkmf (TeX make makefile) and a template file TeX.tmpl. Their installation is (of course) performed with the help of Imake.

The generated Makefile has targets for creating dependency information, and for generating DVI and PostScript output.

name: imfellEnglish
caption: IM Fell English fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: Igino Marini has implemented digital revivals of fonts bequeathed to Oxford University by Dr. John Fell, Bishop of Oxford and Dean of Christ Church in 1686. This package provides the English family, consisting of Roman, Italic and Small-Cap fonts.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: imfellflowers
caption: IM Fell Flower OpenType fonts

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: The package provides two flower fonts in OpenType format by IM Fell, as revived by Igino Marini.

name: impatient
caption: Free edition of the book <q>TeX for the Impatient</q>

copyright.owner: Paul Abrahams, Kathryn Hargreaves, Karl Berry

descriptions.text:
TeX for the Impatient is a book (of around 350 pages) on TeX, Plain TeX and Eplain.

The book is also available in French and Chinese translations.

documentation.details: A copy of the book (French translation)
A copy of the book (Chinese translation)

name: impnattypo
caption: Typographic utilities inspired by the French Imprimerie Nationale

descriptions.text: The package provides useful macros implementing recommendations by the French Imprimerie Nationale.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: import
caption: Establish input relative to a directory

descriptions.text:
The commands \import{full_path}{file} and \subimport{path_extension}{file} set up input through standard LaTeX mechanisms (\input, \include and \includegraphics) to load files relative to the \import-ed directory.

There are also \includefrom, \subincludefrom, and * variants of the commands.

topics.details: manipulation of TeX macro file i/o

name: impose
caption: PostScript imposition and support utilities

descriptions.text: Impose is used for two-up printing of DSC-compliant PostScript (including that from Netscape, dvips, and FrameMaker). It makes an effort to remove white space from the printout by probing the original PostScript for the bounding box of the printed area. This makes the output much more aesthetically satisfying than does a simple layout of non-cropped original pages.

name: imprintmtshadow
caption: Support files for the Monotype Imprint Shadow fonts

descriptions.text: The fonts themselves are only available for purchase.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
support is for a font not available on CTAN

name: imsproc
caption: Typeset IMS conference proceedings

descriptions.text:
The class typesets papers for IMS (Iranian Mathematical Society) conference proceedings.

The class uses the XePersian package.

name: IMTEKda
caption: IMTEK thesis class

descriptions.text:
The class permits typesetting of diploma, bachelor’s and master’s theses for the Institute of Microsystem Technology (IMTEK) at the University of Freiburg (Germany).

The class is based on the KOMA-Script class scrbook. Included in the documentation is a large collection of useful tips for typesetting theses and a list of recommended packages.

name: incgraph
caption: Sophisticated graphics inclusion in a PDF document

copyright.owner: Prof. Dr. Dr. Thomas F. Sturm

descriptions.text:
The package provides tools for including graphics at the full size of the output medium, or for creating pages whose size is that of the graphic they contain. A principal use case is documents that require inclusion of (potentially many) scans or photographs. Bookmarking is especially supported.

The tool box has basic macros and a convenience user interface that wraps \includegraphics.

name: includeRnw
caption: Include .Rnw inside .tex

descriptions.text:
This package is for including .Rnw (knitr/sweave)-files inside .tex-files. It requires that you have R and the R-package knitr installed.

Note: This package will probably not work on Windows. It is tested only on OS X, and will probably also work on standard Linux distros.

topics.details: typeset reports, diagrams, etc., of statistics
include complete documents in other documents

name: includex
caption: Extended \include

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \includedoc, which allows you to include just the contents of one source file into another, ignoring text outside \begin{document} ... \end{document} in the included file. In other respects, the command behaves like the standard LaTeX command \include.

The package is not supported, and is distributed as one of the frankenstein bundle’s appendices. The package’s functionality is now provided by the newclude package.

topics.details: include complete documents in other documents

name: inconsolata
caption: A monospaced font, with support files for use with TeX

descriptions.text: Inconsolata is a monospaced font designed by Raph Levien. This package contains the font (in both Adobe Type 1 and OpenType formats) in regular and bold weights, with additional glyphs and options to control slashed zero, upright quotes and a shapelier lower-case L, plus metric files for use with TeX, and LaTeX font definition and other relevant files.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: inconsolata-nerd-font
caption: Inconsolata Nerd Font with support for XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
Inconsolata is a monospaced font designed by Raph Levien. It is already available via the inconsolata package. However, that package provides a pretty old version of the font. Additionally, the Nerd Font project extended the font by a huge amount of additional glyphs.

This package provides the Inconsolata Nerd Font in .ttf format as well as a convenient interface to load the font for the XeTeX and LuaTeX engines.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: indent
caption: Environments that change margins

descriptions.text:
Defines an environment indentation that adjusts its margins relative to the rest of the page.

Note that (unlike more modern packages such as changepage) the package does not employ a surrounding list environment, so that the user needs to create any necessary skip above or below the indented matter.

name: indentfirst
caption: Indent first paragraph after section header

descriptions.text: This minimalist package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: index
caption: Extended index for LaTeX including multiple indexes

descriptions.text: This is a reimplementation of LaTeX’s indexing macros to provide better support for indexing. For example, it supports multiple indexes in a single document and provides a more robust \index command. It supplies short hand notations for the \index command (^{word}) and a * variation of \index (abbreviated _{word}) that prints the word being indexed, as well as creating an index entry for it.

name: indextools
caption: Producing multiple indices

descriptions.text:
This package enables the user to produce and typeset one or more indices simultaneously.

The package is known to work in LaTeX documents processed with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. If makeindex is used for processing the index entries, no particular setup is needed when TeX Live is used. Using xindy or other programs, it is necessary to enable shell escape. Shell escape is also needed if splitindex is used.

This is a fork of imakeidx, with new features and fixed bugs.

name: indextra
caption: Enhanced index typesetting

descriptions.text: This package provides some enhanced features for typesetting indexes, notably: (1) Continuation text when entries or sub-entries continue from one page or column to the next. (2) An interface for accessing marks created from index entries, so that (for example) a running head can include the range of index entries that appears on the page.

name: indic-type1
caption: Indic Type 1 fonts converted from public Metafont sources

descriptions.text:
Adobe Type 1 version of public Metafont fonts (from CTAN) for 10 Indic scripts: Devanagari, Sanskrit, Gurmukhi/Punjabi, Bangla, Tamil, Sinhala, Malayalam, Kannada, Telugu, Tibetan.

The fonts derive from an accurate analytic conversion to outlines using MetaPost output, with subsequent optimization and autohinting with FontForge.

The package contains the PFB and map files for 122 fonts, the copies of the TFM files have been also included to allow testing the fonts without the original packages.

For font tables, proofsheet files and other information see the package home page.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: induni-om
caption: Omega fonts for characters used in study of Sanskrit

descriptions.text: The files are a comprehensive set of virtual fonts for the Latin glyphs used in the study of Sanskrit and similar languages. The virtual fonts are built for use with Omega, and use the URW look-alikes for Times, etc as base fonts.

topics.details: fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
Omega and packages that use it

name: indxcite
caption: Generate author index based on citations

descriptions.text: A package to automatically generate an Author Index based on citations made using BibTeX. It requires the use of the harvard and index packages and LaTeX2e.

name: infpic
caption: Macros to insert pictures in paragraphs

descriptions.text: Provides macros for placing pictures, and Metafont support for making the simple pictures in the first place.

name: infufrgs
caption: A LaTeX Class for INF/UFRGS Documents

descriptions.text: infufrgs is a LaTeX document class that formats theses, dissertations, monographs and research reports following the typographic and bibliographic standards required by the Institute of Informatics (INF) of the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), Porto Alegre, Brazil.

name: infwarerr
caption: Complete set of information/warning/error message macros

descriptions.text: This package provides a complete set of macros for information, warning and error messages. Under LaTeX, the commands are wrappers for the corresponding LaTeX commands; under Plain TeX they are available as complete implementations.

name: inhyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for Bahasa Indonesia

topics.details: support for a language whose support is not otherwise catalogued

name: initials
caption: Adobe Type 1 decorative initial fonts

descriptions.text: For each font, at least a .pfb and a .tfm file is provided, with an .fd file for use with LaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: inkpaper
caption: A mathematical paper template

descriptions.text:
InkPaper is designed to write mathematical papers,especially designed for

  1. Mathematics Students.
  2. ZJGS students.
  3. magazine editors.

NOTICE.This is not a Thesis class.

name: inline-images
caption: Inline images in base64 encoding

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command \inlineimg to dynamically create a file containing the inline image in base64 format, which is decoded and included in the source file.

Requirements

  • LaTeX must be run with option --shell-escape.
  • Program base64.

topics.details: manipulating images for inclusion in documents

name: inlinebib
caption: Citations in footnotes

descriptions.text: A BibTeX style and a LaTeX package that allow for a full bibliography at the end of the document as well as citation details in footnotes. The footnote details include op. cit. and ibid. contractions.

name: inlinedef
caption: Inline expansions within definitions

descriptions.text: The package provides a macro \Inline that precedes a \def or \gdef. Within the definition text of an inlined definition, keywords such as \Expand may be used to selectively inline certain expansions at definition-time. This eases the process of redefining macros in terms of the original definition, as well as definitions in which the token that must be expanded is deep within, where \expandafter would be difficult and \edef is not suitable. Another application is as an easier version of \aftergroup, by defining a macro in terms of expanded local variables, then ending the group with \expandafter\endgroup\macro.

name: inlinegraphicx
caption: Insert inline images, with automatic size/positioning

descriptions.text: Insert inline images (based on graphicx), with automatic size/positioning.

name: inlinelabel
caption: Assign equation numbers to inline equations

descriptions.text: This package can assign equation numbers to inline equations. When Japanese is supported, you can switch to circled equation numbers.

name: innerscript
caption: Small modifications to math formatting

descriptions.text: This package optionally modifies four aspects of TeX’s automatic math formatting to improve typesetting: (1) it adds extra space around relation and operation symbols in superscripts and subscripts; (2) it removes extra space around \left-\right delimiter pairs; (3) it adds extra space after right delimiters in certain situations; and (4) it forces \left and \right delimiters to completely cover their contents. Using LuaLaTeX is required.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: inputenc
caption: Accept different input encodings

descriptions.text:
The package translates various standard and other input encodings into a LaTeX internal language. The internal language is expressed entirely in TeX’s base encoding (standard ASCII printable characters, carriage control tokens and TeX control sequences, the latter mostly defined by LaTeX).

The package is part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: inputenx
caption: Enhanced input encoding handling

descriptions.text: This package deals with input encodings. It provides a wider range of input encodings using standard mappings, than does inputenc; it also covers nearly all slots. In this way, it serves as more uptodate replacement for package inputenc.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: inputfile
caption: Input LaTeX files, remembering the file name

descriptions.text: The package keeps the file name as the file is input; the name of the current file may be retrieved using the command \inputfilename.

name: inputnormalization
caption: Wrapper for XeTeX’s and LuaTeX’s input normalization

descriptions.text: This package provides a cross engine interface to normalizing input before it's read by TeX. It is based on XeTeX's \XeTeXinputnormalization primitive and lua-uni-algos for LuaTeX.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: inputtrc
caption: Trace which file loads which

descriptions.text:
The package produces screen/log messages of the form <current> INPUTTING <next> reporting LaTeX input commands (<current> and <next> being file names). The message is indented to reflect the level of input nesting.

Tracing may be turned on and off, and the unit of indentation may be adjusted.

The implementation somewhat resembles those of packages FiNK and inputfile.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: inriafonts
caption: Inria fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
Inria is a free font designed by Black[Foundry] for Inria research institute. The font is available for free. It comes as Serif and Sans Serif, each with three weights and matching italics.

Using these fonts with XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX is easy using the fontspec package; we refer to the documentation of fontspec for more information.

The present package provides a way of using them with LaTeX and pdfLaTeX: it provides two style files, InriaSerif.sty and InriaSans.sty, together with the PostScript version of the fonts and their associated files. These were created using autoinst.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: inrstex
caption: Extended Plain TeX for use with MLTeX

descriptions.text: INRSTeX supports the preparation of documents in several languages, using ordinary fonts. It is usable with any TeX system, but is most useful when using ordinary CM fonts with an MLTeX system. The macros include support for PostScript graphics.

name: insbox
caption: Insert pictures/boxes into paragraphs

descriptions.text:
The package provides convenient bundling of the \parshape primitive.

LaTeX users should note that this is a generic package, and should be loaded using \input .

topics.details: flow text round an insertion in the paragraph

name: inscrutable
caption: A response to Perl hackers’ silliness

descriptions.text: A sillier way to produce a simple message would be hard to imagine.

topics.details: TeX code as a source of humour

name: insdljs
caption: Insert document-level JavaScript in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
The package defines an insDLJS environment and an \OpenAction command which specifies action to be performed when the document is opened at page 1. Various other supporting and other macros are defined.

The package is part of the AcroTeX bundle.

name: inslrmaj
caption: Fonts based on the Insular Majuscule manuscript book-hand

descriptions.text:
The inslrmaj and allimaj packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Insular Majuscule manuscript book-hand used between the 6th and 9th centuries. The font consists of majuscules and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks and ligatures. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: inslrmin
caption: Fonts based on the Insular Minuscule manuscript book-hand

descriptions.text:
The inslrmin and allimin packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Insular Miniscules manuscript book-hand used from the 6th century onwards. The font consists of minuscules and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks and ligatures. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: Install-LaTeX-Guide-zh-cn
caption: A short introduction to LaTeX installation written in Chinese

descriptions.text: This package will introduce the operations related to installing TeX Live (introducing MacTeX in macOS), upgrading packages, and compiling simple documents on Windows 11, Ubuntu 24.04, and macOS systems, and mainly introducing command line operations.

name: installfont
caption: A bash script for installing a LaTeX font family

descriptions.text:
With this script you can install a LaTeX font family (PostScript Type 1, TrueType and OpenType formats are supported). Font series from light to ultra bold, and (faked) small caps and (faked) slanted shapes are supported, but not expert fonts.

The script will rename the fonts automatically (optional) or will otherwise expect the *.afm files and the font files (in PostScript Type1 format) named in the Karl Berry scheme (e.g. 5bbr8a.pfb). After running the script, you should have a working font installation in your local TeX tree.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: intcalc
caption: Expandable arithmetic operations with integers

descriptions.text: This package provides expandable arithmetic operations with integers, using the e-TeX extension \numexpr if it is available.

name: inter
caption: The inter font face with support for LaTeX, XeLaTeX, and LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the
    Inter Sans family of fonts (version 3.015), designed by Rasmus Andersson.
    Inter is a typeface specially designed for user interfaces with focus
    on high legibility of small-to-medium sized text on computer screens.
    The family features a tall x-height to aid in readability of mixed-case
    and lower-case text.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: interactiveanimation
caption: Create PDF files with branching animations

copyright.owner: Luis Gonzáles, Javier Toro and Pedro Linares

descriptions.text:
The package provides an interface to create PDF files with branching animations. Animations are built up as a set of concatenated interactive frames; frames may contain images, and buttons which may control the progress of the animation.

The package only works with pdflatex.

name: interactiveplot
caption: Provides an interface to create interactive 2D/3D functions inside a PDF file

descriptions.text: The package provides an interface to create interactive 2D/3D functions inside a PDF file. It requires pdfTeX 1.2 or later. The output can only be viewed in Adobe Reader 11.0 or later.

name: interactiveworkbook
caption: LaTeX-based interactive PDF on the Web

descriptions.text: The package interactiveworkbook gives the user the ability to write LaTeX documents which, ultimately, create interactive question-and-answer Portable Document Format (PDF) tutorials meant to be used by Internet students and that, in particular, freely use mathematical notation.

name: interchar
caption: Managing character class schemes in XeTeX

descriptions.text: The package manages character class schemes of XeTeX. Using this package, you may switch among different character class schemes. Migration commands are provided for make packages using this mechanism compatible with each others.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: interfaces
caption: Set parameters for other packages, conveniently

descriptions.text:
The package provides a small number of convenient macros that access features in other frequently-used packages, or provide interfaces to other useful facilities such as the pdfTeX \pdfelapsedtime primitive. Most of these macros use pgfkeys to provide a key-value syntax. The package also uses the package scrlfile from the Koma-Script bundle (for controlled loading of other files) and etoolbox.

The package is bundled with sub-packages containing actual interfaces: by default, the package loads all available sub-packages, but techniques are provided for the user to select no more than the interfaces needed for a job.

name: interlinear
caption: A package for creating interlinear glossed texts with customizable formatting

descriptions.text: The interlinear package facilitates the creation of interlinear glossed texts, commonly used in linguistic examples. It is based on the gb4e package and builds upon its functionality to provide enhanced features. It offers extensive customization options, allowing users to control font styles, formatting, and layout. With predefined styles and margin note customization, interlinear provides a flexible solution for presenting linguistic data.

name: interpol
caption: Add interpolation to MetaPost graph package

descriptions.text:
This file declares a new internal quantity interpolating and modifies the augment and Mreadpath routines of the MetaPost graph package (part of the base MetaPost distribution) to construct a path from data points using Bezier curves instead of polygons (line segments) when interpolating is set positive.

Use of this feature can lead to severe distortions if the data isn't suitable. Its usefulness may best be seen when plotting smooth functions evaluated numerically at discrete intervals.

name: interpreter
caption: Translate input files on the fly

descriptions.text:
The package preprocesses input files to a Lua(La)TeX run, on the fly.

The user defines Lua regular expressions to search for patterns and modify input lines (or entire paragraphs) accordingly, before TeX reads the material. In this way, documents may be prepared in a non-TeX language (e.g., some lightweight markup language) and turned into proper TeX for processing.

The source of the documentation is typed in such a lightweight language and is thus easily readable in a text editor (the PDF file is also available, of course); the transformation to TeX syntax via Interpreter’s functions is explained in the documentation itself.

Interpreter is implemented using the author’s gates (Lua version), and works for plain TeX and LaTeX, but not ConTeXt.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: interval
caption: Format mathematical intervals, ensuring proper spacing

descriptions.text:
When typing an open interval as $]a,b[$, a closing bracket is being used in place of an opening fence and vice versa. This leads to the wrong spacing in, say, $]-a,b[$ or $A\in]a,b[=B$. The package attempts to solve this using: 

      \interval{a}{b} -> [a,b]
      \interval[open]{a}{b} -> ]a,b[
      \interval[open left]{a}{b} -> ]a,b]

The package also supports fence scaling and ensures that the enclosing fences will end up having the proper closing and opening types. TeX maths does not do this job properly.

The package depends on pgfkeys.

name: intex
caption: Support typesetting and indexing words and phrases

descriptions.text:
The package adds functionality to LaTeX to ease typesetting and indexing of phrases, acronyms, and proper names in a consistent manner throughout documents of arbitrary length.

The package provides a processor mkintex, that processes an intermediate .itx file, generating appropriate entries for both LaTeX and makeindex.

name: intexgral
caption: A LaTeX package for typesetting integrals

descriptions.text: Typesetting integrals, although common in LaTeX, is not particularly practical. The way in which the different parts are managed often generates unreadable source code, making modifications laborious. The package therefore follows a simple philosophy: focus on the essential element of an integral, the integrand. Everything else (limits, differentials, symbols) can be modified using keys. These keys are designed to allow you to easily and quickly change the style of an integral. Additionally, the package provides various auxiliary macros to support some keys which can have lengthy inputs.

name: intopdf
caption: Embed non-PDF files into PDF with hyperlink

descriptions.text: The package allows to embed non-PDF files (e.g., BibTeX) into PDF with a hyperlink.

name: intro-scientific
caption: Introducing scientific/mathematical documents using LaTeX

descriptions.text: Writing Scientific Documents Using LaTeX is an article introducing the use of LaTeX in typesetting scientific documents. It covers the basics of creating a new LaTeX document, special typesetting considerations, mathematical typesetting and graphics. It also touches on bibliographic data and BibTeX.

name: inversepath
caption: Calculate inverse file paths

descriptions.text: The package calculates inverse relative paths. Such things may be useful, for example, when writing an auxiliary file to a different directory.

name: invertedparagraphs
caption: Indented text with negative paragraph indentation

descriptions.text:
Defines an environment that behaves like a list, except that instead of an item label, the paragraph starts at the left margin, but carries on indented.

The macros (gratuitously) load maybeload and redefine.

name: invoice
caption: Generate invoices

descriptions.text:
The package may be used for generating invoices. The package can deal with invisible expense items and deductions; output may be presented in any of 10 different languages. A long-standing bug has been removed. Numbers now can show the comma as decimal separator.

The package depends on the fp, calc and siunitx for its calculations.

name: invoice-class
caption: Produces a standard US invoice from a CSV file

descriptions.text: This class produces a standard US commercial invoice using data from a CSV file. Invoices can span multiple pages. The class is configurable for different shipping addresses.

topics.details: read, process and convert CSV data

name: invoice2
caption: Intelligent invoices with LaTeX3

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
Typeset invoices with automatic VAT and calculation of totals. Supports internationalization, invoices are typeset with booktabs for readability. Does not support separate projects per invoice.

Can be used as a replacement for invoice in most cases.

name: iodhbwm
caption: Unofficial template of the DHBW Mannheim

descriptions.text: This package provides an unofficial template of the DHBW Mannheim for the creation of bachelor thesis, studies or project work with LaTeX. The aim of the package is the quick creation of a basic framework without much effort.

name: ionumbers
caption: Restyle numbers in maths mode

descriptions.text:
ionumbers stands for input/output numbers.

The package restyles numbers in maths mode. If a number in the input file is written, e.g., as $3,231.44$ as commonly used in English texts, the package is able to restyle it to be output as $3\,231{,}44$ as commonly used in German texts (and vice versa). This may be useful, for example, if you have a large table and want to include it in texts with different output conventions without the need to change the table.

The package can also automatically group digits left of the decimal separator (thousands) and right of the decimal separator (thousandths) in triplets without the need of specifying commas (English) or points (German) as separators. E.g., the input $1234.567890$ can be output as $1\,234.\,567\,890$.

Finally, an e starts the exponent of the number. For example, $21e6$ may be output as $26\times10\,^{6}$.

name: iopart-num
caption: Numeric citation style for IOP journals

descriptions.text: A BibTeX style providing numeric citation in Harvard-like format. Intended for use with Institute of Physics (IOP) journals, including Journal of Physics.

name: ipa
caption: LaTeX macros for using WSUIPA fonts

descriptions.text: The package comprises alternative LaTeX support of the wsuipa fonts. On CTAN (and in the TeX Live distribution), these macros are to be found with the fonts themselves.

name: ipaex
caption: IPA (Japanese) fonts

descriptions.text: The fonts provide fixed-width glyphs for Kana and Kanji characters, proportional width glyphs for Western characters.

name: ipaex-type1
caption: IPAex fonts converted to Type-1 format Unicode subfonts

descriptions.text:
The package contains the IPAex Fonts converted into Unicode subfonts in Type1 format, which is most suitable for use with the CJK package.

Font conversion was done with ttf2pt1.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: ipsum
caption: Insert multilingual placeholder text

descriptions.text: This is a package to work with multilingual Lorem Ipsum dummy texts.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: iptconf
caption: Class for IPT conference proceedings at Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute

descriptions.text: his class provides a two-column, A4 document layout for papers submitted to the annual conference of the Institute of Physics and Technology (IPT / НН ФТІ) at Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute.

name: iran-bibtex
caption: Iran Manual of Style Citation Guide for BibTeX

descriptions.text:
The iran-bibtex package, designed for LaTeX, provides BibTeX styles in accordance with the guidelines outlined in the Iran Manual of Style (1st edn., 2016) – citation guide to Persian, and English information sources.

A collection of illustrative examples showcasing the usage of this package has been meticulously prepared and is accessible in the package’s GitHub repository under the examples sub-directory.

To facilitate alphabetical sorting of references, prioritizing Persian/Farsi items ahead of English/Latin ones, a dedicated file named iran-bibtex-cp1256fa.csf is provided for use with this package. This file, derived from the ascii.csf file, serves the purpose of arranging references in the desired order.

It is important to note that this package relies on the natbib package, which is automatically loaded.

name: is-bst
caption: Extended versions of standard BibTeX styles

descriptions.text:
The bundle contains an extended version (xbtxbst.doc) of the source of the standard BibTeX styles, together with corresponding versions of the standard styles.

The styles offer support for CODEN, ISBN, ISSN, LCCN, and PRICE fields, extended PAGES fields, the PERIODICAL entry, and extended citation label suffixing.

name: iscram
caption: A LaTeX class to publish article to ISCRAM conferences

descriptions.text: LaTeX class to publish article to ISCRAM (International Conference on Information Systems for Crisis Response and Management).

name: isf
caption: Access italic computer modern sans in LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
Provides LaTeX 2.09 (dynamic-loading) font tables for a font selection command \isf, giving access to Computer Modern Sans Serif Italic fonts. (The font is actually a slanted version.)

Note that these macros do not work with current LaTeX, but since the NFSS supports the fonts anyway, this is not a problem.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: ishyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for Icelandic

descriptions.text: These patterns are supposedly based on the encoding of the Icelandic Roman fonts, so are probably of little use nowadays without some translation process; the icehyph is probably a better bet, nowadays.

topics.details: support for typesetting the Icelandic language

name: isi2bib-vim
caption: Vim script to convert bib database from ISI to BibTeX format

descriptions.text: A script that enables Vim (a popular text editor) to convert a bibliographic database from ISI (Institute of Scientific Information, Web of Science) export format to BibTeX format.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: isi2bibtex
caption: Converter for ISI to BibTeX

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: iso
caption: Generic ISO standards typesetting macros

descriptions.text:
Generic class and package files for typesetting ISO International Standard documents. Several standard documents have been printed by ISO from camera-ready copy prepared using LaTeX and these files.

The class makes use of the isorot package, rather than use other mechanisms directly.

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves

name: ISO-TeX
caption: Display (La)TeX accented letters in GNU Emacs

descriptions.text:
GNU Emacs modes to display letters with standard TeX accents as the character they are supposed to represent (for example \'e would display as é. This provides an alternative approach to that provided by inputenc, in which the user types the desired character and (La)TeX transparently executes the commands needed to produce the character in the typeset output.

The package is said to be capable of working with GNU Emacs version 19 or later.

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

name: iso10303
caption: Typesetting the STEP standards

descriptions.text: Class and package files building on iso for typesetting the ISO 10303 (STEP) standards. Standard documents prepared using these packages have been published by ISO.

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves

name: iso209
caption: A document style for ISO standards

descriptions.text: An early predecessor of Wilson’s iso.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves

name: isodate
caption: Tune the output format of dates according to language

descriptions.text:
This package provides ten output formats of the commands \today, \printdate, \printdateTeX, and \daterange (partly language dependent).

Formats available are: ISO (yyyy-mm-dd), numeric (e.g. dd.\,mm.~yyyy), short (e.g. dd.\,mm.\,yy), TeX (yyyy/mm/dd), original (e.g. dd. mmm yyyy), short original (e.g. dd. mmm yy), as well as numerical formats with Roman numerals for the month.

The commands \printdate and \printdateTeX print any date. The command \daterange prints a date range and leaves out unnecessary year or month entries.

This package supports German (old and new rules), Austrian, US English, British English, French, Danish, Swedish, and Norwegian.

name: isodoc
caption: A LaTeX class for typesetting letters and invoices

descriptions.text:
The isodoc class can be used for the preparation of letters and invoices (and, in the future, similar documents). Documents are set up with options, thus making the class easily adaptable to user’s wishes and extensible for other document types.

The class is based on the NTG brief class by Victor Eijkhout, which implements the NEN1026 standard.

name: isolatin1
caption: An obsolete means to use ISO 8859-1 with TeX

descriptions.text:
The package represents an outdated mechanism for reading ISO Latin-1 (ISO/IEC 8859-1) by means of setting the printing glyphs in the upper half of the character set to category code active, and defining them all.

While this mechanism is broadly that employed by the standard LaTeX inputenc package, the standard package has several advantages, including a more satisfactory approach to undefined character codes, better integration with other input encodings and generally improved robustness.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
input encoding support for TeX engines

name: isomath
caption: Mathematics style for science and technology

descriptions.text: The package provides tools for a mathematical style that conforms to the International Standard ISO 80000-2 and is common in science and technology. It changes the default shape of capital Greek letters to italic, sets up bold italic and sans-serif bold italic math alphabets with Latin and Greek characters, and defines macros for markup of vector, matrix and tensor symbols.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: isonums
caption: Display numbers in maths mode according to ISO 31-0

descriptions.text: The package makes a quick hack to ziffer to display numbers in maths mode according to ISO 31-0, regardless of input format (European $1.235,7$ or Anglo-American $1,235.7$). The options [euro, anglo] control the global input format. Default input format is anglo. Documentation is included as comments to the text source.

name: isopt
caption: Writing a TeX length with a space between number and unit

descriptions.text: Writing a TeX length with \the writes the value and the unit without a space. Package isopt provides a macro \ISO which inserts a user defined space between number and unit.

name: isorot
caption: Rotation of document elements

descriptions.text: The package is for rotation of document elements. It is a combination of the lscape package and an extension of the rotating package. The package is designed for use with the iso class but may be used with any normal class.

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

name: isosigns
caption: ISO signs and colors according to the standards 7001, 7010 and 3864

descriptions.text:
The package provides safety colors (ISO 3864), safety signs (ISO 7010), and public information symbols (ISO 7001) from the ISO. It can be useful when creating instructions for chemical or physical experiments.

Note: This is not an official package from ISO.

topics.details: typeset documents about standards, or the standards themselves
create symbols, rather than select from a font
symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: isotope
caption: A package for typesetting isotopes

descriptions.text: The package provides a command \isotope for setting the atomic weight and atomic number indications of isotopes. (The naive way of doing the job with (La)TeX mathematics commands produces an unsatisfactory result.)

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

name: ispell
caption: Multi-platform spell checker

descriptions.text:
Ispell is a fast screen-oriented spelling checker that shows you your errors in the context of the original file, and suggests possible corrections when it can figure them out. Compared to UNIX spell, it is faster and much easier to use. Ispell can also handle languages other than English.

Ispell is now largely superseded by aspell, a package that seasoned ispell users will find a comfortable home.

name: isphysicalmath
caption: Simple way to write nice formulas

descriptions.text: This package helps users to write mathematical and physical contents according to scientific notation (international mainly), in an elegant way. It deals with the notation and formatting of formulas, quantities, numerical values, factors, dimensions, measurement units and also performs its activities in complex mathematical environments.

name: issuulinks
caption: Produce external links instead of internal ones

descriptions.text:
The PDF visualizer http://issuu.com/ISSUU is a popular service which shows PDF documents a page a time. Due to the way it is implemented, internal links in these documents are not allowed. Instead, they must be converted to external ones in the form http://issuu.com/action/page?page=PAGENUMBER.

The package patches hyperref to produce external links in the required form instead of internal links created by \ref, \cite and other commands.

Since the package redefines the internals of hyperref, it must be loaded it AFTER hyperref.

name: ist21
caption: Title page for the old BSI IST/21 committee

descriptions.text: A variant of the standard LaTeX 2.09 titlepage package, designed for the working papers, etc., of the committee. (The committee covered, at various times, standardisation of OSI architecture, OSI upper layers, distributed processing, databases and graphics.)

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: istgame
caption: Draw Game Trees with TikZ

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides macros based on TikZ to draw a game tree. The main idea underlying its core macros is the completion of a whole tree by using a sequence of simple parent-child tree structures, with no longer nested relations involved (like the use of grandchildren or great-grandchildren).

Using this package you can draw a game tree as easily as drawing a game tree with pen and paper.

This package depends on expl3, TikZ, and xparse.

The ist prefix stands for it’s a simple tree or In-Sung’s simple tree.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: ital
caption: Automatic italic correction

descriptions.text:
The package defines commands \ital and \slant that provide the requisite italic correction at the end of their argument, and the command \upright that provides italic correction in front of its argument as necessary. A command \emph is also provided, choosing between \ital and \upright according to the state of the surrounding text.

These facilities are (of course) provided in LaTeX2e, with different names as part of the distribution.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: italic
caption: Automatic italic correction for italic and slanted text

descriptions.text: The package defines commands \ital and \slant, somewhat simpler than those in ital, which package has wider coverage.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: iTe
caption: Interactive TeX editor

descriptions.text: iTe is an easy to use, interactive authoring tool for LaTeX and TeX documents. With iTe running inside emacs, it is possible to select arbitrary display fragments such as figures, equations, labels, captions, etc. These fragments can then be freely moved, rotated and scaled.

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

name: ithyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for the Italian language

descriptions.text: These hyphenation patterns for the Italian language are supposed to comply with the Recommendation UNI 6461 on hyphenation issued by the Italian Standards Institution (Ente Nazionale di Unificazione UNI).

name: itnumpar
caption: Spell numbers in words (Italian)

descriptions.text:
Sometimes we need to say Capitolo primo or Capitolo uno instead of Capitolo 1, that is, spelling the number in words instead of the usual digit form.

This package provides support for spelling out numbers in Italian words, both in cardinal and in ordinal form.

name: itrans-processor
caption: Transliteration of Indian Languages

descriptions.text:
Itrans is a pre-processor: it converts English-encoded text into various Indian Language scripts for printing or for display.

The input text to itrans is in a transliterated form: each letter in an Indian Script is assigned an English equivalent, and the English letters are used to represent what will eventually print out in the Indian Language Script.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: ivd2dvi
caption: Convert IVD-DVI files to DVI

descriptions.text: The TeX extension TeX-XeT (single hyphen: not to be confused with TeX--XeT) produces IVD-DVI files which extend DVI files with reflection commands for horizontal reversal of text. In general, IVD-DVI files cannot be processed by an ordinary DVI processor; ivd2dvi will convert such a file to DVI so that it can be processed by a normal DVI driver.

name: iwhdp
caption: Halle Institute for Economic Research (IWH) Discussion Papers

descriptions.text:
The document class is for creating Discussion Papers of the Halle Institute for Economic Research (IWH) in Halle, Germany.

The class offers options for both English and German texts.

name: iwona
caption: A two-element sans-serif font

descriptions.text:
Iwona is a two-element sans-serif typeface. It was created as an alternative version of the Kurier typeface, which was designed in 1975 for a diploma in typeface design at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

This distribution contains a significantly extended set of characters covering the following modern alphabets: latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats. For use with TeX the following encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2-Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi and nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for LaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: iwonamath
caption: LaTeX support for scaled Iwona math fonts

descriptions.text:
This package provides an interface to the Iwona math fonts by Janusz Marian Nowacki. It allows to use Iwona as math complement for sans serif fonts without native math.

The package allows font scaling, the choice of light and condensed versions, and the creation of multiple math versions.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: izhitsa
caption: Support for the old Russian font <q>Izhitsa</q>

descriptions.text: Includes Metafont code and LaTeX style file.

topics.details: fonts for a script or language now obsolete
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

name: jablantile
caption: Metafont version of tiles in the style of Slavik Jablan

descriptions.text: This is a small Metafont font to implement the modular tiles described by Slavik Jablan. For an outline of the theoretical structure of the tiles, see (for example) Jablan’s JMM 2006 Exhibit.

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

name: jabref
caption: Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases

descriptions.text:
JabRef is a graphical frontend to manage BibTeX (and BibLaTeX) databases having BibTeX as internal format. It offers quality checks for entries; fetching complete bibliographic information based on ISBN, DOI, PubMed-ID and arXiv-ID; searching across many online scientific catalogues such as CiteSeer, CrossRef, Google Scholar, IEEEXplore, INSPIRE-HEP, Medline PubMed, MathSciNet, Springer, arXiv, and zbMATH.

It allows for grouping entries (and storing the group information in the .bib file itself), advancing searching and filtering, finding duplicate entries, attaching and renaming PDFs (e.g., according to the BibTeX key), and generating BibTeX keys.

Since JabRef fully relies on BibTeX, additional information such as ranking, priority, printed-flag, and quality-assured-flag are stored in the BibTeX entry in the .bib file itself.

name: jacow
caption: A class for submissions to the proceedings of conferences on JACoW.org

descriptions.text: The jacow class is used for submissions to the proceedings of conferences on Joint Accelerator Conferences Website (JACoW), an international collaboration that publishes the proceedings of accelerator conferences held around the world.

name: jadetex
caption: Macros supporting Jade DSSSL output

descriptions.text: Macro package on top of LaTeX to typeset TeX output of the Jade DSSSL implementation.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: jamtimes
caption: Expanded Times Roman fonts

descriptions.text:
The package offers LaTeX support for the expanded Times Roman font, which has been used for many years in the Journal d'Analyse Mathématique.

Mathematics support is based on the Belleek fonts.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: japanese-mathformulas
caption: Compiling basic math formulas in Japanese using LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
This is a style file for compiling basic maths formulas in Japanese using LuaLaTeX.

\NewDocumentCommand allows you to specify whether the formula should be used within a sentence or on a new line.

The main packages used in japanese-mathformulas.sty are amsmath, amssymb, siunitx, ifthen, xparse, TikZ, mathtools, and graphics.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: japanese-otf
caption: Advanced font selection for platex and its friends

descriptions.text: The package contains pLaTeX support files and virtual fonts for supporting a wide variety of fonts in LaTeX using the pTeX engine.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: japanese-otf-uptex
caption: Support for Japanese OTF files in upLaTeX

descriptions.text: This bundle has been merged into japanese-otf.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: jas99
caption: BibTeX style for American Meteorological Society (AMS)

descriptions.text: This style is a development of newapa.bst, and is in its turn superseded by jas99_m.bst.

name: jas99_m
caption: BibTeX style for American Meteorological Society (AMS)

descriptions.text:
This style is based on an earlier style jas99; the package acquired a new name since the original authors (of jac99.bst) aren't contactable.

Modifications are simply for better conformance to the AMS’ requirements for journals Journal of Atmospheric Science, Journal of Applied Meteorology and Monthly Weather Review..

name: jasthesis
caption: A <q>standard</q> thesis class

descriptions.text: A class that produces theses in the format required by the University of Bristol (UK). This is close to the requirements of the standard BS 4821:1990.

name: JavaBib
caption: A BibTeX file manager written in Java

descriptions.text: JavaBib reads the whole BibTeX file into memory and presents an index to the file and editing and management facilities.

name: javadoc
caption: Documenting source code

descriptions.text:
The package processes source code in a manner based on the javadoc system for documenting Java (and other language) source; its output is LaTeX, via a doclet.

A package for processing this output is provided.

name: javaDVI
caption: DVI viewer and printer coded in Java

descriptions.text: javaDVI is a DVI viewer and printer coded in Java, and running under the Java RTE 1.3 using the BaKoMa True Type fonts. The fonts are included as a .zip file, a format suitable for use with javaDVI.

topics.details: convert DVI files for (direct) printing, etc.

name: javascript_TeXed
caption: Small MiKTeX-editor for Win32 Intel platform

descriptions.text:
A small editor for MiKTeX as an HTML application (~20kb). Works on MS-Windows with Internet Explorer 5.0 and later. You can run it as JS-TeX.hta from command line or start JS-TeX.hta filename.tex

If you have help for LaTeX in HTML you can use it by filling the HELP field in Options.

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

name: JavascriptHTTP
caption: Add buttons to a PDF to easily get and post web content

descriptions.text: This small package adds commands for LaTeX to create buttons with which to fetch content from the internet. The content can optionally be transformed with Javascript and displayed in textfields. For these interactive elements to work, a PDF using the commands provided by this package must be opened in Acrobat Pro.

topics.details: relies on availability of Adobe Acrobat, etc.

name: javatex
caption: A Java implementation of TeX

descriptions.text:
At root, this is a small TeX (memmax=64K), but a larger version may be built.

The implementation was in essence an experiment, and performance proved so poor that the author considers it unusable in practice.

name: jbact
caption: BibTeX style for biology journals

descriptions.text:
The style is a development of apalike.bst in the BibTeX bundle.

The style serves two journals – if the user executes \nocite{TitlesOn} , the style serves for the Journal of Theoretical Biology; otherwise it serves for the Journal of Molecular Biology.

name: JBibtexManager
caption: Managing citations in BibTeX format

descriptions.text: JBibtexManager is a front-end to BibTeX database. You can add, edit, sort and search. Furthermore, you can find and delete duplicate entries. You can customize BibTeX templates, fonts, colors and more. JBibtexManager is a java GUI for managing citations in BibTeX format. The citations are presented in a spreadsheet format and allows sorting based on year, journal, and key. Furthermore, it allows searching for text in the author and title fields, and allows printing in the spreadsheet format. Requires java 1.4 and should work on all platforms.

name: jcc
caption: BibTeX style file for J. Comp. Chem

descriptions.text:
jcc.bst is a BibTeX style for J. Comp. Chem. originally dating from 2000.

It is now modified to make it really compliant with the journal’s present style requirements, as: author’s initials after the name, authors’ names separated by ;, no brackets around the year…

name: jeep
caption: Modified LaTeX2.09 article and report styles

descriptions.text: A personal adaptation of LaTeX standard code, with adjustment of the default page size, code to allow the user to customise section headers, an early version of fancy headers, compact lists and table of contents.

name: jeopardy
caption: Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The jeopardy package allows to build a jeopardy game with pdfLaTeX. It is based on the jj_game class and exerquiz package, written by D. P. Story. The author of the game can use multichoice questions or fill-in questions. The answer for fill-in questions is either a mathematical formula or text string (see the documentation of exerquiz and \RespBoxMath and \RespBoxTxt commands to learn more about the capabilities). JavaScripts are written to record the score. If the score is greater than a given value, a hidden string is shown. The user should use the style with some screen presentation package, such as web.

The package is distributed with some example games, including both 1- and 2-player games.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: jetbrainsmono-otf
caption: Package (or only fontspec config files) support for the OpenType font JetBrains

copyright.owner: C. Pierquet (with help from D. Flipo)

descriptions.text:
Support for the OpenType font JetBrainsMono (so with LuaLaTeX/XeTeX and fontspec),with or without ligatures, and with weights versions.

  • jetbrainsmono or jetbrainscode for regular version,
  • jetbrainsmono-medium or jetbrainscode-medium for medium version,
  • jetbrainsmono-light or jetbrainscode-light for light version,
  • jetbrainsmono-extralight or jetbrainscode-extralight for extralight version,
  • jetbrainsmono-thin or jetbrainscode-thin for thin version.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: JeuxCartes
caption: Macros to insert playing cards

descriptions.text: This package provides macros to insert playing cards, single, or hand, or random-hand, Poker or French Tarot or Uno, from png files.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: jflap2tikz
caption: Convert JFlap file into a LaTeX file depicting the automaton using TikZ

descriptions.text: JFlap is an excellent piece of software for experimenting with finite state machines, Turing machines and for exploring many aspects of the theory of computation. JFLAP2TikZ is a script that converts a JFlap jff file representing a finite automaton, push down automaton, or Turing machine to LaTeX file depicting the automaton graphically using TikZ.

name: jfmutil
caption: Utility to process pTeX-extended TFM and VF

descriptions.text:
This program provides functionality to process data files (JFM and VF) that form logical fonts used in (u)pTeX. The functions currently available include:

  • The mutual conversion between Japanese virtual fonts (pairs of VF and JFM) and files in the ZVP format, which is an original text format representing data in virtual fonts. This function can be seen as a counterpart to the vftovp/vptovf programs.
  • The mutual conversion between VF files alone and files in the ZVP0 format, which is a subset of the ZVP format.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: jfontmaps
caption: Font maps and configuration tools for Japanese fonts

descriptions.text:
The package offers font maps, and supporting material, that make various Japanese fonts available to users of (u)ptex and related programs or formats.

The package does not ship any of the fonts mentioned in the documentation, but only map files for use with dvipdfmx; the user must obtain the other fonts separately. The first exception is that ipa and ipaex the respective fonts are shipped as part of the TeX Live distribution and are available for free. The other exception is that the Yu Mincho/Gothic fonts are available to Windows and MacOSX users, as part of their operating system distribution.

This package has now been superseded by ptex-fontmaps.

name: jhep
caption: Class for JHEP

descriptions.text: A LaTeX class used to typeset manuscripts in JHEP style.

name: jIEEEtran
