The comments are shown in the margins alongside the text; different styles for the comments may be used; the styles are selected using package options.

The package is based on the package todonotes, and depends heavily on Lua, so it can only be used with LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: luatruthtable
caption: Generate truth tables of boolean values in LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides an easy way for generating truth tables of boolean values in LuaLaTeX. The time required for operations is no issue while compiling with LuaLaTeX. The package supports nesting of commands for multiple operations. It can be modified or extended by writing custom Lua programs.

There is no need to install Lua on users system as TeX distributions (TeX Live or MiKTeX) come bundled with LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: luavlna
caption: Prevent line breaks after single letter words, units, or academic titles

descriptions.text:
In some languages, like Czech or Polish, there should be no single letter words at the end of a line, according to typographical norms. This package handles such situations using LuaTeX’s callback mechanism. In doing this, the package can detect languages used in the text and insert spaces only in parts of the document where languages requiring this feature are used.

Another feature of this package is the inclusion of non-breakable space after initials (like in personal names), after or before academic degrees, and between numbers and units.

The package supports both plain LuaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

BTW: vlna is the Czech word for wave or curl and also denotes the tilde which, in TeX, is used for unbreakable spaces.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style
LuaTeX and packages that require it
support for typesetting, and documentation in Slovak

name: luaxml
caption: Lua library for reading and serialising XML files

descriptions.text: LuaXML is a pure Lua library for reading and serializing XML files. The current release is aimed mainly at support for the odsfile package. The documentation was created by automatic conversion of original documentation in the source code.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: lucida
caption: Metrics, etc., for Lucida Bright and Lucida Math

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides metric, virtual font, and map files, to use the Lucida font sets with current LaTeX/dvips/dvipdfm or pdfLaTeX. The metrics support T1, TS1, and LY1 encodings (note: there is no support for the OT1 encoding).

Note that macro support (at all levels above the .fd files), and support for use of the fonts for typesetting maths, is provided separately in the PSNFSS Lucida extension.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: lucida-otf
caption: Support for the Lucida Bright fonts (OpenType)

descriptions.text:
This package supports the non-free fonts from Bigelow & Holmes which are available from the TUG office for a special price for members of any TeX user group.

See https://tug.org/lucida

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: lucidabr
caption: PSNFSS support for Lucida Type 1 fonts

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros for using the Bigelow and Holmes Lucida fonts, in Type 1 format, with LaTeX.

Metrics and other font support files are provided separately in the Lucida package.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: lucide-admonitions
caption: Provides environments for rendering admonition boxes in multiple languages

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package for rendering admonition boxes with Lucide icons. It provides predefined box types inspired by MkDocs and Zensical, with customizable icons, colors, and titles.

The package supports standard LaTeX and KOMA-Script classes, and offers optional box titles and page-breaking support via tcolorbox. Titles can be automatically translated into multiple languages using the translations package.

name: lucide-icons
caption: Use lucide-icons through LaTeX commands

descriptions.text: This package provides commands like twemojis which allow to use Lucide-Icons through LaTeX commands. The implementation relies on images (PDF from SVG) and should work on every installation.

name: luciole
caption: Luciole OpenType fonts for LuaTeX and XeTeX

copyright.owner: Laurent Bourcellier, Jonathan Fabreguettes, Daniel Flipo

descriptions.text: This package provides four Unicode Math text fonts Luciole-*.ttf and a companion math font Luciole-Math.otf. These have been developed explicitly for visually impaired people and are the result of a two-year collaboration between the Centre Technique Régional pour la Déficience Visuelle (the Regional Technical Center for Visual Impairment) and the type-design studio typographies.fr. This project received a grant from the Swiss Ceres Foundation and support from the DIPHE laboratory at the Université Lumière Lyon 2.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: lucold
caption: Use old-style digits with Lucida fonts

descriptions.text: The package provides the means to switch the rendering of all the digits of a document from lining to old-style numbers, when using Lucida fonts. The switch affects all digits in text mode, or all digits in text and math mode. It works both for normal weight and boldface text and math; since the boldface old-style digits are in the Lucida Expert font set, you need it for the boldface digits. Includes a set of AWK programs used to automatically build .fd, .tfm, and .vf files from the existing Lucida PSNFSS distribution, and that may easily changed for the generation of different virtual files for whatever font.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: lug
caption: Create and edit TeX Local User Group web pages

descriptions.text:
lug can be used to maintain the TeX Local User Group web pages, currently located at www.ntg.nl/lug.

Without options specified, it reads key=value pairs, possibly embedded in the body of a mail as sent by a web form like here. You can feed the complete email (after saving it) to lug, or you can paste its content to standard input.

name: lutabulartools
caption: Some useful LuaLaTeX-based tabular tools

descriptions.text: This package provides some useful commands for tabular matter. It uses LuaLaTeX and offers the ability to combine the facilities of multirow and makecell with an easy to use syntax. It also adds some enhanced rules for the booktabs package.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: luwa-ul
caption: Provides underlines and other highlighting which can be used in vertical mode

descriptions.text: This package provides underlining and highlighting that remain intact even in vertical writing environments and when used together with ruby text. It internally uses lua-ul package, so it can be used only under LuaLaTeX.

name: LuwianType
caption: Typesetting package for Hieroglyphic Luwian

descriptions.text: This package allows for typing in Hieroglyphic Luwian in LaTeX documents, using relatively simple commands based on the Latin transcriptions of the various signs. It also includes some formatting commands designed to allow boustrophedon and columns, as well as shorthands for symbols commonly used in transcriptions.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

name: LuxiMono
caption: Free monospace fonts

descriptions.text: LuxiMono is a family of general-purpose monospaced (typewriter) fonts. This distribution contains the fonts in Adobe Type 1 format, and tfm, vf and LaTeX-related files are also provided.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: lwarp
caption: Converts LaTeX to HTML

descriptions.text:
This package converts LaTeX to HTML by using LaTeX to process the user’s document and generate HTML tags. External utility programs are only used for the final conversion of text and images. Math may be represented by SVG files or MathJax. Hundreds of LaTeX packages are supported, and their load order is automatically verified.

Documents may be produced by LaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and by several CJK engines, classes, and packages. A texlua script automates compilation, index, glossary, and batch image processing, and also supports latexmk. Configuration is semi-automatic at the first manual compile. Support files are self-generated. Print and HTML versions of each document may coexist.

Assistance is provided for HTML import into EPUB conversion software and word processors.

Requirements include the commonly-available Poppler utilities, and Perl. Detailed installation instructions are included for each of the major operating systems and TeX distributions. A quick-start tutorial is provided.

name: lwc-examples
caption: Examples from The LaTeX Web Companion

descriptions.text: The source of the examples printed in the book, together with necessary supporting files.

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

name: LXfonts
caption: Set of slide fonts based on CM

descriptions.text: The bundle contains the traditional slides fonts revised to be completely usable both as text fonts and mathematics fonts; they are fully integrated with the new operators, letters, symbols and extensible delimiter fonts, as well as with the AMS fonts, all redone with the same stylistic parameters.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: LXGW-fonts
caption: A CJK font family with a comprehensive character set

descriptions.text: The LXGW Font Family provides an open-source CJK font family with a comprehensive character set for Chinese (Simplified/Traditional), Cantonese, and Japanese. A fontset configuration of this font family for the ctex-kit is also provided in this package.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: lxmail
caption: A letter-generator that produces LaTeX output

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Lxmail is a DOS application that manages an address database, and uses it to produce LaTeX files for letters and (separately) for labels.

name: ly1
caption: Support for LY1 LaTeX encoding

descriptions.text: The Y&Y texnansi (TeX and ANSI, for Microsoft interpretations of ANSI standards) encoding lives on, even after the decease of the company; it is known in the LaTeX scheme of things as LY1 encoding. This bundle includes metrics and LaTeX macros to use the basic three (Times, Helvetica and Courier) Adobe Type 1 fonts in LaTeX using LY1 encoding.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: LydType
caption: Typing in the Lydian alphabet

descriptions.text:
This package aims to allow platform-agnostic typing in the Lydian alphabet using LaTeX, in particular as a way to deal with the fact that Overleaf does not support direct input of certain characters outside of a given Unicode range.

The package was developed for use with LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX, functionality with other compilers is not guaranteed.

The package includes the Noto Sans Lydian font as developed by Google.

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: LyLuaTeX
caption: Commands to include lilypond scores within a (Lua)LaTeX document

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros for the inclusion of LilyPond scores within LuaLaTeX. It calls LilyPond to compile scores, then includes the produced files.

Dependencies: currfile, environ, graphicx, luaotfload, luaoptions, luatexbase, metalogo, minibox, pdfpages, xkeyval.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: lyx
caption: Document processor based on LaTeX

descriptions.text:
LyX is an open source document processor that encourages an approach to writing based on the structure of your documents, not their appearance. LyX lets you concentrate on writing, leaving details of visual layout to the software.

LyX produces its output using LaTeX in the background; LyX is far more than a front-end to LaTeX, however. No knowledge of LaTeX is necessary to use LyX, but such knowledge sometimes helps explain the way LyX is behaving.

LyX is not provided on CTAN; potential users should go to the LyX home page for more information.

name: m-pictex
caption: Enable PicTeX to run with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
m-pictex used to be a ConTeXt MK II module making PicTeX available without e-TeX.

The ConTeXt code is no longer distributed. The LaTeX wrapper has not been needed since LaTeX switched to e-TeX 20 years ago.

However a LaTeX m-pictex.sty is available via the latex-context-ppchtex package. It simply loads PicTeX, for compatibility of old documents using m-pictex rather than pictex.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: M-Tx
caption: A preprocessor for pmx

descriptions.text: M-Tx is a preprocessor to pmx, which is itself a preprocessor to musixtex, a music typesetting system. The prime motivation to the development of M-Tx was to provide lyrics for music to be typeset. In fact, pmx now provides a lyrics interface, but M-Tx continues in use by those who prefer its language.

name: m3D
caption: Extension of plain MetaPost for 3D graphics

descriptions.text:
M3D is another extension of plain MetaPost for 3 dimensional graphics. While the author claims it should not be regarded as stable, he believes it has value simply as a source of ideas for those who wish to implement 3D graphics in MetaPost.

The package (stable or not) exhibits some interesting abilities, both in the package manual and in the gallery that comes with the distribution.

name: maad
caption: Mathematical Approximations and Documentation

descriptions.text: A document describing the parametrization of least-squares curve fitting, and showing how (using PicTeX) to display error bars.

name: mab2bib
caption: Converter tools: MAB to BibTeX and UTF-8 to LaTeX ASCII

descriptions.text: Simple Python scripts to convert MAB bibliography files into BibTeX and UTF-8 encoded text files into ASCII with LaTeX codes

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: macbibtex
caption: BibTeX for the Macintosh

descriptions.text: A port of BibTeX which is distributed with OzTeX for the Macintosh OS.

name: macfont
caption: Convert Apple type 1 fonts for use under Windows

descriptions.text: MacFont converts Macintosh Type 1 fonts into standard ASCII format. In order to use MacFont, you must transfer the resource forks of the Macintosh font onto your PC or workstation. This can generally be accomplished by archiving the font on the Macintosh and extracting the archive with macunpack or a similar non-Mac tool on your workstation.

topics.details: convert a font to a form usable with TeX

name: macrolist
caption: List operations for LaTeX2e

descriptions.text:
This package provides a list data structure and common list functions such as \macrolistadd, \macrolistremove, \macrolistforeach, as well as \macrolistremovelast (similar to C++’s pop_back) and \macrolistjoin (similar to Javascript’s arr.join).

Unlike most programming languages, the lists in this package are 1-indexed, meaning the first element is numbered 1, the second element numbered 2, and so on.

name: macros2e
caption: A list of internal LaTeX2e macros

descriptions.text: This document lists the internal macros defined by the LaTeX2e base files which can also be useful to package authors. The macros are hyper-linked to their description in source2e. For this to work both PDFs must be inside the same directory. This document is not yet complete in content and format and may miss some macros.

name: macroswap
caption: Swap the definitions of two LaTeX macros

descriptions.text: The package provides simple utility methods to swap the meaning (token expansion) of two macros by name.

name: mactex
caption: The TeX Live Mac distribution

descriptions.text:
MacTeX is a complete, easy-to-install TeX distribution for recent MacOS versions. The .pkg file is an install package for Apple’s installer. The mactex package contains all of TeX Live, with some GUI applications, and a recent version of Ghostscript. The basictex package contains a selected subset of packages, specified in TL’s scheme-small.

Beware: the download is large (over 5 Gbytes).

name: mactex-basic
caption: A basic TeX distribution for the Macintosh

descriptions.text: This package provides an (extremely) basic TeX distribution for MacOS X systems.

name: mactextras
caption: Extras for the MacTeX distribution

descriptions.text: MacTeXtras is a collection of auxiliary material for Macintosh machines, beyond what MacTeX provides; it is distributed as a .zip file, that contains extra programs, demos and documentation for MacTeX users.

name: mactotex
caption: Convert <q>Macintosh PostScript</q> for use with TeX

descriptions.text: The program cleans out all the irrelevant things that the MACOS applications used to add, and restructures so that the files can be used with TeX. The documentation talks about using psfig, but it doesn't seem likely that this is actually necessary, 15 years after the program was written.

name: mafr
caption: Mathematics in accord with French usage

descriptions.text:
The package provides settings and macros for typesetting mathematics with LaTeX in compliance with French usage. It comes with two document classes, fiche and cours, useful to create short high school documents such as tests or lessons.

The documentation is in French.

name: magaz
caption: Magazine layout

descriptions.text: The current version does special formatting for the first line of text in a paragraph. The package is part of a larger body of tools which remain in preparation.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style
layout of objects on the page

name: magic
caption: A font to go with the Magic(TM) game

descriptions.text: A small set of symbols appropriate to the game. The font is expressed in Metafont; unusually, the size-specific file magic12.mf is input by magic.mf, rather than the other way around.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: magicnum
caption: Access TeX systems’ <q>magic numbers</q>

descriptions.text: This package allows access to the various parameter values in TeX (catcode values), e-TeX (group, if and node types, and interaction mode), and LuaTeX (pdfliteral mode) by a hierarchical name system.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: magicthegathering
caption: LaTeX package for Magic: The Gathering typesetting

descriptions.text: The magicthegathering package provides LaTeX commands for typesetting Magic: The Gathering content: inline mana symbols, expansion-set icons, Scryfall-linked card names, sideboard-guide tables, plain-text deck-list import, and tournament match-result tracking.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material
create symbols, rather than select from a font
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: magicwatermark
caption: An easy and flexible way to set watermarks

descriptions.text: This package can flexibly set and clear watermarks. It is based on everypage and TikZ, encapsulated by LaTeX3. All watermark content is placed inside a TikZ node in the center of the page.

topics.details: separate printing, under (or over) the page as a whole
decorate/confuse text by adding a background

name: magra
caption: The Magra font face with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides the Magra family of fonts designed by FontFuror, with support for LaTeX and pdfLaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: mahjong
caption: Typeset Mahjong Tiles using MPSZ Notation

descriptions.text:
The mahjong package provides a LaTeX2e and LaTeX3 interface for typesetting mahjong tiles using an extended version of MPSZ algebraic notation.

Features include spaces, rotated, blank, and concealed tiles, as well as red fives. The size of the mahjong tiles can be controlled using a package option and an optional argument of \mahjong.

It is primarily aimed at Riichi (aka. Japanese) Mahjong but can be used to typeset any style of mahjong.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: mahjong-tiles
caption: A LaTeX package for typesetting Japanese/Riichi Mahjong tiles

descriptions.text: mahjong-tiles is a LaTeX package for typesetting Japanese/Riichi Mahjong tiles with compact MPSZ notation and extended commands. The package provides \mahjong{...} for inline hands and \mahjongriver{...} for discard rivers, while supports the manzu, pinzu, souzu, and honor suits, red fives(aka), face-down and blank tiles, gaps, called-meld rotation markers, stacked sideways tiles, concealed-kong shorthand, configurable tile size, and recoloured tile backs. mahjong-tiles is derived from Daniel Schmitz's mahjong package and keeps the general approach of rendering small PDF tile assets through a LaTeX parser, while adding notation conveniences and layout support for common Riichi Mahjong examples.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: mailing
caption: Macros for mail merging

descriptions.text: This package is for use when sending a large number of letters, all with the same body text. The package‘s \addressfile command is used to specify who the letter is to be sent to; the body of the \mailingtext command specifies the text of the letters, possibly using macros defined in the \addressfile.

name: mailmerge
caption: Repeating text field substitution

descriptions.text: The package mailmerge provides an interface to produce text from a template, where fields are replaced by actual data, as in a database. The package may be used to produce several letters from a template, certificates or other such documents. It allows access to the entry number, number of entries and so on.

name: maine-thesis
caption: A document class for University of Maine graduate theses

descriptions.text:
The maine-thesis class provides support for the formatting requirements for graduate theses of the Graduate School at The University of Maine. It sets default parameters for the report class, modifies captions, references, and the table of contents, and makes specific environments available.

The maine-thesis class reflects the guidelines published by the Graduate School at The University of Maine. The Graduate School at the University of Maine does not provide official support for any thesis style class or template.

name: make-env
caption: Print USPS standard envelopes

descriptions.text: The package prints USPS standard envelopes, using the author’s lettermac and zip packages.

name: make_latex
caption: LaTeX Makefile

descriptions.text: Make_latex is a library of make(1) rules for producing LaTeX documents; it has rules for running LaTeX enough times, for running BibTeX, for various format conversions and for printing final results.

name: make4ht
caption: A build system for tex4ht

descriptions.text: make4ht is a simple build system for tex4ht, a TeX to XML converter. It provides a command line tool that drives the conversion process. It also provides a library which can be used to create customized conversion tools.

name: makebarcode
caption: Print various kinds 2/5 and Code 39 bar codes

descriptions.text: The package contains macros for printing various 2/5 bar codes and Code 39 bar codes. The macros do not use fonts but create the bar codes directly using vertical rules. It is therefore possible to vary width to height ratio, ratio of thin and thick bars. The package is therefore convenient for printing ITF bar codes as well as bar codes for identification labels for HP storage media.

name: makebase
caption: Typeset counters in a different base

descriptions.text:
This package typesets a LaTeX counter such as page in an arbitrary base (default 16). It does not change font or typeface.

The package extends the functionality of the existing hex LaTeX 2.09 package and provides documentation. However, the author is not a mathematician, and suggestions for rewriting the code are welcomed.

Warning: this is alpha software and may contain bugs. Please report problems to the author.

name: makebox
caption: Defines a \makebox* command

descriptions.text: Define a \makebox* command that does the same as a \makebox command, except that the width is given by a sample text instead of an explicit length measure.

name: makecell
caption: Tabular column heads and multilined cells

descriptions.text:
This package supports common layouts for tabular column heads in whole documents, based on one-column tabular environment. In addition, it can create multi-lined tabular cells.

The Package also offers:

  • a macro which changes the vertical space around all the cells in a tabular environment (similar to the function of the tabls package, but using the facilities of the array)
  • macros for multirow cells, which use the facilities of the multirow package;
  • macros to number rows in tables, or to skip cells;
  • diagonally divided cells;
  • horizontal lines in tabular environments with defined thickness.

name: MakeCirc
caption: A MetaPost library for drawing electrical circuit diagrams

descriptions.text: MakeCirc is a MetaPost library that contains diverse symbols for use in circuit diagrams. MakeCirc offers a high quality tool, with a simple syntax. MakeCirc is completely integrated with LaTeX documents and with other MetaPost drawing/graphic. Its output is a PostScript file. MakeCirc only requires (La)TeX and MetaPost to work.

name: makecmds
caption: The new \makecommand command always (re)defines a command

descriptions.text: The package provides a \makecommand command, which is like \(re)newcommand except it always (re)defines a command. There is also \makeenvironment and \provideenvironment for environments.

name: makecookbook
caption: Make a Cookbook

copyright.owner: Terrence P. Murphy and Rosalie D’Amico

descriptions.text:
The makecookbook bundle contains the files needed to create a nice quality family cookbook in a form ready to submit to most print-on-demand companies. Modifiable choices have been made regarding standard book features such as trim size, margins, headers/footers, chapter heading formatting, front matter (copyright page, table of contents, etc.) and back matter (index). Commands and environments have been created to format the food stories and recipes. The user will need to:

  1. supply their own food stories and recipes(!), and
  2. install the needed fonts. We assume a LuaTeX compile.

Please note that no new document class or package is included here. Rather, we provide a modifiable preamble and a small number of other files that, together, fully support creation of all of the internal pages of a cookbook (i.e., everything except the cover art).

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: makedoc
caption: Preprocessing documentation with TeX

descriptions.text:
The package may be used to produce typeset documentation from a package file. The comments in the file are typeset (as appropriate) and the code is printed verbatim. This mechanism, the author suggests, is cleaner and easier to use than the docstrip-based mechanism commonly used.

The package is distributed as part of the author’s nicetext bundle.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: makedtx
caption: Perl script to help generate dtx and ins files

descriptions.text: The makedtx bundle is provided to help LaTeX2e developers to write the code and documentation in separate files, and then combine them into a single .dtx file for distribution. It automatically generates the character table, and also writes the associated installation (.ins) script.

name: makefonts
caption: Shell scripts to generate bitmaps from Metafont sources

descriptions.text:
This package contains shell scripts which generate PK files, based on the long-established script allcm.

Modern TeX distributions use Adobe Type 1 fonts for preference (if they allow bitmap forms at all), and will generate such bitmap fonts as are needed on-the-fly. These scripts are therefore most useful to those who have a principled objection to the use of outline fonts (or to the design of those available).

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

name: makeglos
caption: Include a glossary into a document

descriptions.text: The package provides the means to include a glossary into a document. The glossary is prepared by an external program, such as xindy or makeindex, in the same way that an index is made.

name: MakeGlossariesGUI
caption: Java GUI alternative to makeglossaries script

descriptions.text: The package provides a Java GUI alternative to the makeglossaries Perl script (supplied by the glossaries package). The package was designed for people who don’t want to use the command prompt but can’t get their editor to run makeglossaries. It can also be used as a diagnostic tool when there are problems with the document glossaries.

name: makegobbler
caption: Keep or drop some part of LaTeX source code

descriptions.text:
The makegobbler package provides a mechanism to selectively drop (gobble) or keep (ungobble) portions of LaTeX source code, either conditionally or unconditionally. The affected code is delimited by user-defined control sequences that act as explicit markers.

For example, you can define a conditional as follows: \newif\ifkeep

You can then make a portion of the source conditional like this: \keepfalse

\MGBkeep*\ifkeep\SomeArbitraryDelimitingControlSequence

Here, everything – including \fi#!{}_^$ – is dropped.

\SomeArbitraryDelimitingControlSequence

name: makeidx
caption: Standard LaTeX package for creating indexes

descriptions.text: Standard package for creating indexes; the package is available as part of the LaTeX distribution.

name: makeindex
caption: Process index output to produce typesettable code

descriptions.text: A general purpose hierarchical index generator; it accepts one or more input files (often produced by a text formatter such as TeX or troff), sorts the entries, and produces an output file which can be formatted. The formats of the input and output files are specified in a style file; by default, input is assumed to be an .idx file, as generated by LaTeX.

name: makeindexk
caption: Makeindex development sources

descriptions.text: The package contains the development sources of makeindex, which is now maintained as part of TeX Live.

name: makelabels
caption: Add a <q>\makelabels</q> feature to KOMA-Script letter classes and package

descriptions.text:
The standard letter class letter has a label feature. You can activate it using \makelabels. While in Germany window envelopes are common, printing labels is not common, and scrlttr2 has never supported label printing.

Using makelabels.lco does implement a \makelabels feature similar to the standard letter classes. Currently there are (almost) no configuration features for makelabels.lco. But you may use the envlab package after loading makelabels.lco to get various configuration features.

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

name: makeplot
caption: Easy plots from Matlab in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
Existing approaches to create EPS files from Matlab (laprint, mma2ltx, print -eps, etc.) aren't satisfactory; makeplot aims to resolve this problem.

Makeplot is a LaTeX package that uses the pstricks pst-plot functions to plot data that it takes from Matlab output files.

name: makeprog
caption: A literate system for TeX programming

descriptions.text:
A literate programming system strongly influenced by the ideas of Knuth's web system, but designed for processing TeX-based sources (documentation processing is provided in both Plain TeX and LaTeX).

In contrast to the LaTeX project’s doc and docstrip, but in common with Knuth's system, there is a separate program (makeprog) for producing code to run (equivalent to Knuth's tangle). However, makeprog doesn't rearrange code in the way that tangle does.

name: maker
caption: Include Arduino or Processing code in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
The first version of the package allows to include Arduino or Processing code using three different forms:

  1. writing the code directly in the LaTeX document
  2. writing Arduino or Processing commands in line with the text
  3. calling to Arduino or Processing files

All these options support the syntax highlighting of the official IDE.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: makerobust
caption: Making a macro robust (legacy package)

descriptions.text:
Heiko Oberdiek’s makerobust package defined a command with name \MakeRobustCommand that could be used to make fragile commands robust.

The LaTeX format has, since 2015, included a command \MakeRobust with the same syntax and behaviour. Also by 2019, almost all commands in LaTeX that may be used in a moving argument are already robust.

This package is now just a simple one-liner defining the name \MakeRobustCommand as an alias for \MakeRobust.

This package should not be used in any new documents.

name: makerobust209
caption: Make an existing LaTeX command robust

descriptions.text: The package provides a command \makerobust that converts the definition of a command to a robust one.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: makeshape
caption: Declare new PGF shapes

descriptions.text:
The package simplifies production of custom shapes with correct anchor borders, in PGF/TikZ; the only requirement is a PGF path describing the anchor border.

The package also provides macros that help with the management of shape parameters, and the definition of anchor points.

name: maketable
caption: Convert Word or Excel tables to TeX tabular structures

descriptions.text: MAKETABLE helps in converting tables in Word, Excel, etc. to a tabular structure for TeX. Copy your table in Word, Excel, etc. and paste it into a data grid in MAKETABLE. Click a button to convert the data grid to the tabular structure, then copy and paste it into your TeX editor.

name: Makor 2
caption: Typeset pointed Hebrew using Omega

descriptions.text:
Makor2 can be used to typeset Hebrew with vowels or liturgical accents, Yiddish, documents prepared using ArabTeX Hebrew conventions, Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia, and Old Hebrew.

Makor uses an intuitive interface – that is, you type characters on the keyboard according to more-or-less what they sound like, and Makor renders them in proper Hebrew.

topics.details: Omega and packages that use it
documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

name: malayalam-latex
caption: LaTeX for Malayalam

descriptions.text: Fonts (in Adobe Type 1 format), metrics and macros for typesetting Malayalam with LaTeX.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: malayalam-obsolete
caption: Fonts for typesetting Malayalam, with a pre-processor

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent
fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: malayalam-omega
caption: Typesetting Malayalam using Omega

descriptions.text: This package enables typesetting in the Indian language Malayalam using LaTeX on an Omega platform; UTF-8 source files are supported.

topics.details: Omega and packages that use it
support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: maltese
caption: Support input in Maltese

descriptions.text: Commands for input of Maltese characters, in the absence of the appropriate Unicode input mechanisms.

name: malvern
caption: A sans-serif font family

descriptions.text: The Malvern family is a broad family of sanserif fonts which includes Greek letters, diacritical marks and composites as well as the latin alphabet and some symbols. The font is supplied as a Metafont program.

name: mandel
caption: Compute the Mandelbrot set

descriptions.text: A tail-recursive macro to compute the set, and then to print it. The author claims the program took 5 minutes to run on his 66 MHz machine; on this cataloguer’s 2.4 GHz machine it takes about 1.1 seconds.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: mandi
caption: Macros for introductory physics and astronomy

descriptions.text:
The package contains commands for students and teachers of introductory physics. Commands for physical quantities intelligently handle SI units so the user need not do so. There are other features that should make LaTeX easy for introductory physics students.

The name of the package can be pronounced as M&I and refers to the physics textbook Matter & Interactions.

name: manfnt
caption: LaTeX support for the TeX book symbols

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package for easy access to the symbols of the Knuth's manual font, such as the Dangerous Bend and Manual-errata Arrow.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: manjutex
caption: Manju language support

descriptions.text:
Manju is a language of North East Asia, belonging to the Tungusic branch of the Altaic languages. Though it is virtually not spoken anymore, it survives in written form as Manju was the native language of the rulers of the Qing dynasty (1644–1911) in China. Large quantities of documents of the Imperial Archives survive, as well as some of the finest dictionaries ever compiled in Asia, like the Pentaglot, a dictionary comprising Manju, Tibetan, Mongolian, Uighur and Chinese.

ManjuTeX was developed on the basis of MonTeX, and provides all necessary characters for writing standard Manju as well as transliterated Tibetan texts, for which purpose a number of additional characters were created.

This catalogue entry describes the original ManjuTeX; its functionality has now been subsumed into monTeX, though the obsolete ManjuTeX remains on the archive.

name: manpage
caption: Man pages in LaTeX

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
The package provides a manpage environment that may be used as part of a document written using a LaTeX 2.09 documentstyle (examples are supplied that use report style).

The package has not been tested under current LaTeX.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation
package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: manual
caption: Knuth’s <q>manual</q> fonts

descriptions.text: Metafont (by Donald Knuth) and Adobe Type 1 (by Taco Hoekwater) versions of the font containing the odd symbols Knuth uses in his books. LaTeX support is available using the manfnt package

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: manual209
caption: A document style for manuals

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 document style, based on book, with modifications for manual generation and maintenance (including per-chapter page numbering, as in the chappg package).

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09
macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: Manuscript
caption: Emulate look of a document typed on a typewriter

descriptions.text: This package is designed for those who have to submit dissertations, etc., to institutions that still maintain the typewriter is the summit of non-professional printing.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: manyfoot
caption: Adds footnote levels to standard LaTeX’s footnote mechanism

descriptions.text:
Implements a command, \newfootnote, that adds footnote levels to standard LaTeX’s footnote mechanism. Footnotes of every additional level are automatically grouped together on a LaTeX2e output page and are separated from other levels by special vertical spaces. The command \newfootnote allows customisation of the way foonotes of additional level are represented in LaTeX2e documents. Two customisation styles are available now: the plain style is the ordinary LaTeX style of footnote representation; the para style causes footnotes to be typeset as a run-in paragraph.

This package is part of the ncctools bundle.

name: manyind
caption: Provides support for many indexes

descriptions.text:
This package provides support for many indexes, leaving all the bookkeeping to LaTeX and makeindex. No extra programs or files are needed. One runs latex and makeindex as if there is just one index. In the main file one puts commands like \setindex{main} to steer the flow.

Some features of makeindex may no longer work.

name: mapcodes
caption: Support for multiple character sets and encodings

descriptions.text: Mapcodes is an early package covering the same ground as the standard LaTeX inputenc. It provides for input in ISO Latin-1 and -2, IBM codepages 850 and 852, and HP, Macintosh and Atari encodings.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: maple
caption: Styles and examples for the MAPLE newsletter

name: marathi
caption: Typeset Marathi language using XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: लुआ-लाटेक् व झी-लाटेक् ह्यांच्यासह मराठीचा सुलभ वापर करण्यासाठी. लाटेक्-वरील मराठीच्या स्थानिकीकरणाचे काम ह्या आज्ञासंचामार्फत केले जाईल. expex व blindtext ह्या आज्ञासंचांचे स्थानिकीकरण तूर्तास ह्या आज्ञासंचामार्फत पुरवले जात आहे.

For conveniently typesetting Marathi language with LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX. This package will provide localizations needed for the Marathi language. Currently the package localizes package blindtext and package expex.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: Marcellus
caption: Marcellus fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Marcellus family of fonts, designed by Brian J. Bonislawsky.

Marcellus is a flared-serif family, inspired by classic Roman inscription letterforms. There is currently just a regular weight and small-caps. The regular weight will be silently substituted for bold.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: margbib
caption: Display bibitem tags in the margins

descriptions.text: The package redefines the thebibliography environment to place the citation key into the margin.

name: marginal
caption: Extensions to \marginpar handling

descriptions.text:
The package provides the commands

  • \showlostmarginals, to output lost marginal notes at the left of the page,
  • \enlargefreelist, to provide more free space for marginals and floats (see also morefloats); and
  • \onesidemarginals, to force all marginal notes onto the same side of the page, thus leaving space for twice as many notes.

The package was formerly part of the sttools bundle and has been withdrawn by the author in June 2015.

name: marginalia
caption: Marginal content anywhere with automatic adjustment for LuaLaTeX

descriptions.text: This LuaLaTeX package allows the placement of marginal content (such as notes) anywhere, without \marginpar’s limits, and automatically adjusts positions to prevent overlaps or content being pushed off the page, and offers key–value settings that allow fine-grained customization.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: marginfit
caption: Improved margin notes

descriptions.text:
This package fixes various bugs with the margin paragraph implementation of LaTeX. Those bugs include margin notes that are attached to the wrong side as well as those that stick out of the bottom of the page.

This package provides a drop-in replacement solution.

name: marginfix
caption: Patch \marginpar to avoid overfull margins

descriptions.text: Authors using LaTeX to typeset books with significant margin material often run into the problem of long notes running off the bottom of the page. A typical workaround is to insert \vshift commands by hand, but this is a tedious process that is invalidated when pagination changes. Another workaround is memoir’s \sidebar function, but this can be unsatisfying for short textual notes, and standard marginpars cannot be mixed with sidebars. This package implements a solution to make marginpars just work by keeping a list of floating inserts and arranging them intelligently in the output routine.

name: marginnote
caption: Notes in the margin, even where \marginpar fails

descriptions.text: This package provides the command \marginnote that may be used instead of \marginpar at almost every place where \marginpar cannot be used, e.g., inside floats, footnotes, or in frames made with the framed package.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: marginote
caption: Make numbered notes in the margin

descriptions.text:
The package places its argument the margin, numbering it using \fnsymbol sequence.

The same effect may be achieved using the footmisc package with the marginal option

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: maritime
caption: International maritime signal flags using TikZ

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX commands for drawing international maritime signal flags using TikZ (A-Z, NATO 0-9).

name: markdown
caption: Converting and rendering markdown documents inside TeX

descriptions.text: The package provides facilities for the conversion of markdown and YAML markup to plain TeX. These are provided both in form of a Lua module and in form of plain TeX, LaTeX, and ConTeXt macro packages that enable the direct inclusion of markdown and YAML documents inside TeX documents.

name: marnote
caption: Place text in the margin of a document

descriptions.text:
The package rotates a text (using dvips commands) and places it in the margin of a document. The position of the margin is assumed, rather than calculated, so the package will not work with other than the author’s original paper size (presumably letter). A command for writing a pale DRAFT diagonally across a page, is also provided.

The package apparently relies on PostScript code from the psfig bundle.

name: marvosym
caption: Martin Vogel’s Symbols (marvosym) font

descriptions.text:
Martin Vogel’s Symbol font (marvosym) contains the Euro currency symbol as defined by the European commission, along with symbols for structural engineering; symbols for steel cross-sections; astronomy signs (sun, moon, planets); the 12 signs of the zodiac; scissor symbols; CE sign and others.

The package contains both the original TrueType font and the derived Type 1 font, together with support files for TeX (LaTeX).

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: matapli
caption: Class for the french journal MATAPLI

descriptions.text: This is a class for the french journal MATAPLI of the Société de Mathématiques Appliquées et Industrielles (SMAI).

name: matc3
caption: Commands for MatematicaC3 textbooks

descriptions.text: The package provides support for the Matematica C3 project to produce free mathematical text books for use in Italian high schools.

name: matc3mem
caption: Class for MatematicaC3 textbooks

descriptions.text: The class is a development of memoir, with additions (specifically, mathematical extensions) that provide support for writing the books for the Matematica C3 project to produce free mathematical textbooks for use in Italian high schools.

name: match_parens
caption: Find mismatches of parentheses, braces, (angle) brackets, in texts

descriptions.text: Mismatches of parentheses, braces, (angle) brackets, especially in TeX sources which may be rich in those, may be difficult to trace. This little Ruby script helps you by writing your text to standard output, after adding a left margin to your text, which will normally be almost empty, but will clearly show any mismatches.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: math-e
caption: Examples from the book Typesetting Mathematics with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The bundle contains all the examples from the (English) book Typesetting Mathematics with LaTeX (UIT Press, Cambridge, 2010).

The examples are stand alone documents and may be separately processed with LaTeX or pdfLaTeX.

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

name: math-into-latex-4
caption: Samples from Math into LaTeX, 4th Edition

descriptions.text:
Samples for the book (More) Math into LaTeX, 4th edition.

In addition, there are two excerpts from the book:

  • A Short Course to help you get started quickly with LaTeX, including detailed instructions on how to install LaTeX on a PC or a Mac;
  • Math and Text Symbol Tables.

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

name: math-operator
caption: Predefined and new math operators

descriptions.text:
This package defines control sequences for roughly one hundred and fifty math operators, including special functions, probability distributions, pure mathematical constructions, and a variant of \overline.

The package also provides an interface for users to define new math operators similar to the amsopn package. New operators can be medium or bold weight, and they may be declared as \mathord or \mathop subformulas.

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: mathabx
caption: Three series of mathematical symbols

descriptions.text:
Mathabx is a set of 3 mathematical symbols font series: matha, mathb and mathx. They are defined by Metafont code and should be of reasonable quality (bitmap output). Things change from time to time, so there is no claim of stability (encoding, metrics, design).

The package includes Plain TeX and LaTeX support macros.

A version of the fonts, in Adobe Type 1 format, is also available.

name: mathabx-type1
caption: Outline version of the mathabx fonts

descriptions.text: This is an Adobe Type 1 outline version of the mathabx fonts.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: mathador
caption: LaTeX commands for the French game <q>Mathador</q>

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX package with graphic commands for the French game MATHADOR (by author Éric Trouillot and Réseau CANOPÉ).

The principle of the game is like this:

  • Roll the dice!
  • They give you one target number (between 0 and 99) and five numbers to use to reach it.
  • You can use the four arithmetic operations to get there.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: mathalpha
caption: General package for loading maths alphabets in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
Package mathalfa was renamed to mathalpha. For backward compatibility the old name will continue to be recognized in LaTeX documents.

The package provides means of loading maths alphabets (such as are normally addressed via macros \mathcal, \mathbb, \mathfrak and \mathscr), offering various features normally missing in existing packages for this job.

name: mathalphabets
caption: Chinese introduction to mathematical alphabets

descriptions.text: This is a Chinese introduction to mathematical alphabets including Greek alphabets, and Latin alphabets in script, calligraphic, fraktur, double stroke and blackboard bold fonts, and Hebrew alphabets. Furthermore, we will give some advice on how to use and read them.

name: mathastext
caption: Use the text font in maths mode

descriptions.text: The package uses a text font (usually the document’s text font) for the letters of the Latin alphabet needed when typesetting mathematics. (Optionally, other characters in the font may also be used). This facility makes possible (for a document with simple mathematics) a far wider choice of text font, with little worry that no specially designed accompanying maths fonts are available. The package also offers a simple mechanism for using many different choices of (text hence, now, maths) font in the same document. Of course, using one font for two purposes helps produce smaller PDF files.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathbbol
caption: Use the bbold fonts in mathematics

descriptions.text:
Macros for using the bbold fonts (including some related symbols taken from the stmaryrd fonts). The package itself needs two .fd files (to be found in the downloaded directory) to operate.

The file is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathcmd
caption: Mathematics support commands

descriptions.text:
The package provides refinements of the commands for typesetting integrals, sums, derivatives, limits and vector operators.

The package is part of the bosisio bundle.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathcommand
caption: \newcommand-like commands for defining math macros

descriptions.text:
This package provides functionalities for defining macros

  1. that have different behaviors depending on whether in math or text mode,
  2. that absorb Primes, Indices and Exponents (PIE) as extra parameters usable in the code; and
  3. it offers some iteration facilities for defining macros with similar code.

The primary objective of this package is to be used together with the knowledge package for a proper handling of mathematical notations.

name: mathcomp
caption: Text symbols in maths mode

descriptions.text: A package which provides access to some interesting characters of the Text Companion fonts (TS1 encoding) in maths mode.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathdesign
caption: Mathematical fonts to fit with particular text fonts

copyright.owner: Paul Pichaureau for the MathDesign Project

descriptions.text:
The Math Design project offers free mathematical fonts that match with existing text fonts.

To date, three free font families are available: Adobe Utopia, URW Garamond and Bitstream Charter. Three commercial fonts are also supported: Adobe Garamond Pro, Adobe UtopiaStd and ITC Charter.

Mathdesign covers the whole LaTeX glyph set, including AMS symbols and some extra. Both roman and bold versions of these symbols can be used. Moreover you can choose between three greek fonts (two of them created by the Greek Font Society).

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: mathdots
caption: Commands to produce dots in math that respect font size

descriptions.text: Redefines \ddots and \vdots, and defines \iddots. The dots produced by \iddots slant in the opposite direction to \ddots. All the commands are designed to change size appropriately in scripts, as well as in response to LaTeX size changing commands. The commands may also be used in plain TeX.

name: mathematica
caption: Support for fonts distributed with Mathematica

descriptions.text: Virtual TeX fonts that can be used with the PostScript fonts distributed with Mathematica 3.0. The archives use a TDS conforming directory structure. A style file for LaTeX2e is included, that enables use of the fonts and the new symbols from LaTeX2e.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: mathesatz-examples
caption: Examples from the book <q>Mathematiksatz mit LaTeX</q>

descriptions.text:
The bundle all the examples from the extended German version of the well-established Math mode, named Mathematiksatz mit LaTeX, available as a book and published in the DANTE Edition series.

A PDF version of each of the (many) examples in the directory is provided.

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

name: mathexam
caption: Package for typesetting exams

descriptions.text: The package can help you typeset exams (mostly in mathematics and related disciplines where students are required to show their calculations followed by one or more short answers). It provides commands for inclusion of space for calculations, as well as commands for automatic creation of answer spaces. In addition, the package will automatically create page headers and footers, and will let you include instructions and space for students to put their name.

name: mathfam256
caption: Extend math family up to 256 for pLaTeX/upLaTeX/Lamed

descriptions.text:
This package increases the upper limit of math symbols up to 256, using \omath... primitives. These primitives were originally introduced in Omega and are currently available in the following formats:

  • pLaTeX (runs on e-pTeX),
  • upLaTeX (runs on e-upTeX),
  • Lamed (runs on Aleph, successor of Omega).

topics.details: Omega and packages that use it

name: mathfixs
caption: Fix various layout issues in math mode

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX2e package to fix some odd behaviour in math mode such as spacing around fractions and roots, math symbols within bold text as well as capital Greek letters. It also adds some related macros.

topics.details: correct a problem, ahead of the “proper” fix

name: mathfont
caption: Use TrueType and OpenType fonts in math mode

descriptions.text: The mathfont package adapts unicode text fonts for math mode. The package allows the user to specify a default unicode font for different classes of math symbols, and it enables Unicode input in math mode. The package provides tools to change the font locally for math alphabet characters. When typesetting with LuaTeX, mathfont adds resizable delimiters, big operators, and a MathConstants table to text fonts.

name: mathformule
caption: A lightweight environment for single- and multiline numbered math

descriptions.text:
This package provides the LaTeX2e formule environment for both single-line and ampersand-aligned multiline display mathematics. A multiline display may use one overall equation number or configurable per-row subnumbers. Extensible left and right braces, optional mathematics outside a brace, and signed row- and brace-spacing corrections are supported.

The package shares LaTeX's standard equation counter and integrates with the usual numbering and cross-reference mechanisms.

name: mathgifg
caption: Support for Microsoft Georgia and ITC Franklin Gothic

descriptions.text:
The package offers LaTeX support for Microsoft Georgia and ITC Franklin Gothic fonts. Support is available both for text and mathematics.

The fonts are supplied, for example, with Microsoft Windows distributions. The distributed fonts are available in TrueType format; to use the package, a user must translate the fonts to Type 1 format (using, for example, ttf2pt1).

The maths support is very preliminary: much work remains on individual kerning and glyph placement ….

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathgreeks
caption: Use different Greek letter fonts in math mode

descriptions.text: The purpose of this package is to provide access to numerous Greek letter fonts for math mode, without altering other mathematical characters and symbols and without loading whole extensions that provide these fonts. Moreover, the chosen font or shape can be changed dynamically throughout the document.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathinst
caption: Merge font families to create mathematical font sets

descriptions.text: A set of Perl and fontinst scripts to integrate mathematical fonts for use by (La)TeX using a family of Roman types and a set of raw math fonts (such as Euler, or the commercial MathTime or Lucida New Math fonts). All fonts are properly scaled for compatibility with the Roman fonts.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: mathkit
caption: Generate maths fonts to match outline fonts

descriptions.text:
Creates Metafont for maths fonts that match Adobe Type 1 fonts (Times, Palatino, and others) for typesetting mathematics with TeX. The output also includes Plain TeX and LaTeX macros for using the fonts.

The bundle includes parameters for building fonts to match Adobe Times Roman and Palatino, and Monotype Baskerville.

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

name: mathlig
caption: Define maths <q>ligatures</q>

descriptions.text:
The package defines character sequences that behave like ligatures, in maths mode. Example definitions (chosen to show the package's flexibility, are:

  • \mathlig{->}{\rightarrow}
  • \mathlig{<-}{\leftarrow}
  • \mathlig{<->}{\leftrightarrow}

name: mathpartir
caption: Typesetting sequences of math formulas, e.g. type inference rules

descriptions.text:
The package provides macros for typesetting math formulas in mixed horizontal and vertical mode, automatically as best fit.

It provides an environment mathpar that behaves much as a loose centered paragraph where words are math formulas, and spaces between them are larger and adjustable. It also provides a macro \inferrule for typesetting fractions where both the numerator and denominator may be sequences of formulas that will be also typeset in a similar way. It can typically be used for typesetting sets of type inference rules or typing derivations. A macro inferrule for typesetting type inference rules.

name: mathpazo
caption: Fonts to typeset mathematics to match Palatino

descriptions.text:
The Pazo Math fonts are a family of PostScript fonts suitable for typesetting mathematics in combination with the Palatino family of text fonts. The Pazo Math family is made up of five fonts provided in Adobe Type 1 format (PazoMath, PazoMath-Italic, PazoMath-Bold, PazoMath-BoldItalic, and PazoMathBlackboardBold). These contain, in designs that match Palatino, glyphs that are usually not available in Palatino and for which Computer Modern looks odd when combined with Palatino. These glyphs include the uppercase Greek alphabet in upright and slanted shapes in regular and bold weights, the lowercase Greek alphabet in slanted shape in regular and bold weights, several mathematical glyphs (partialdiff, summation, product, coproduct, emptyset, infinity, and proportional) in regular and bold weights, other glyphs (Euro and dotlessj) in upright and slanted shapes in regular and bold weights, and the uppercase letters commonly used to represent various number sets (C, I, N, Q, R, and Z) in blackboard bold.

LaTeX macro support (using package mathpazo.sty) is provided in psnfss (a required part of any LaTeX distribution).

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: mathpple
caption: Use PostScript Palatino for typesetting maths

descriptions.text:
The package defined a scheme whereby mathematics used Palatino or (Palatino clone) fonts in mathematics, and other mathematical symbols, etc., were scaled to fit.

Mathpple is now rendered obsolete by mathpazo, which offers a better-designed set of mathematical fonts than mathpple could ever hope to provide. Mathpple is no longer distributed.

name: mathptm
caption: Adobe Times Roman (or equivalent) for text and maths

descriptions.text: The mathptm package is now obsolete, replaced by the newtx package, which does the same job, better.

name: mathptmx
caption: Use Times as default text font, and provide maths support

descriptions.text:
This package defines Adobe Times Roman (or equivalent) as default text font, and provides maths support using glyphs from the Symbol, Chancery and Computer Modern fonts together with letters, etc., from Times Roman. It supersedes both the original times and the mathptm packages.

The package is part of psnfss, but is reckoned to be obsolete. Users are recommended to switch to using newtx in its place.

name: mathpunctspace
caption: Control the space after punctuation in math expressions

descriptions.text: This package provides a mechanism to control the space after commas and semicolons in mathematical expressions.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: mathrsfs
caption: Support for using RSFS fonts in maths

descriptions.text:
Support use of the Raph Smith’s Formal Script font in mathematics. Provides a \mathscr command, rather than overwriting the standard \mathcal command, as in calrsfs.

The package is part of Jörg Knappen’s collection.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: maths-symbols
caption: Summary of mathematical symbols available in LaTeX

descriptions.text: A predecessor of the comprehensive symbols list, covering mathematical symbols available in standard LaTeX (including the AMS symbols, if available at compile time).

topics.details: lists of glyphs available from font(s)

name: mathsci2bibtex
caption: Convert Mathsci database information to BibTeX

descriptions.text: A Perl script for the job.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: mathscinet
caption: Retrieve references from MathSciNet in BibTeX format

descriptions.text: A Perl script that downloads references from MathSciNet in BibTeX format. The site has recently been redesigned, and this script works with the new layout.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: mathsemantics
caption: Semantic math commands in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides both syntactic and semantic helpers to typeset mathematics in LaTeX. The syntactic layer eases typesetting of formulae in general, while the semantic layer provides commands like \inner{x}{y} to unify typesetting of inner products. These not only unify typesetting of math formulae but also allow to easily adapt notation if a user prefers to.

The semantic layer is split into topics.

name: MathSpad
caption: A mathematics-capable word processor with LaTeX output

descriptions.text: An XWindows WYSIWYG structure editor implementing stencils which define two views of a document, the on-screen view and the output view (which might be LaTeX, TeX, HTML, troff).

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

name: mathspec
caption: Specify arbitrary fonts for mathematics in XeTeX

descriptions.text:
The mathspec package provides an interface to typeset mathematics in XeLaTeX with arbitrary text fonts using fontspec as a backend.

The package is under development and later versions might to be incompatible with this version, as this version is incompatible with earlier versions. The package requires at least version 0.9995 of XeTeX.

name: mathspic
caption: A Perl filter program for use with PiCTeX

descriptions.text: MathsPIC(Perl) is a development of the earlier MathsPIC(DOS) program, now implemented as a Perl script, being much more portable than the earlier program. MathsPIC parses a plain text input file and generates a plain text output-file containing commands for drawing a diagram. Version 1.0 produces output containing PiCTeX and (La)TeX commands, which may then be processed by plain TeX or LaTeX in the usual way. MathsPIC also outputs a comprehensive log-file. MathsPIC facilitates creating figures using PiCTeX by providing an environment for manipulating named points and also allows the use of variables and maths (advance, multiply, and divide). In short, it takes the pain out of PiCTeX. Both the original DOS version and the new Perl version are available.

name: mathstone
caption: Use Adobe Stone Serif and Stone Sans for typesetting maths

descriptions.text:
The package provides metric files and LaTeX support for Stone Sans and Stone Serif fonts from Adobe, in both maths and text modes. It has everything you need to typeset in this font – except the font itself. You need to purchase the fonts themselves: the pfb files are not included in the package. To use Greek letters, you need to install the package Mathdesign.

Three math versions (normal, semibold and bold) are provided for each font.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts
support is for a font not available on CTAN

name: mathstyle
caption: Manage mathematics typesetting style

descriptions.text:
The package performs two functions:

  • to make sub- and superscript operations macros, which has the effect of making their behaviour uniform and more readily understandable; and
  • to take advantage of the lack of infix operations (such as \over) in LaTeX to redesign the control of mathematical typesetting style, and to rationalise the way \mathchoice and dependent mechanisms work.

The package offers support for breqn and is part of the bundle of the same name.

name: mathtex
caption: A CGI program to use LaTeX to put mathematics on the web

descriptions.text:
MathTeX is a CGI program, written in C, that uses LaTeX and either dvipng or dvips/convert to emit GIF or PNG images of LaTeX mathematical expressions. Users can put mathematics directly in html pages with an <img> tag of the form <img src="/cgi-bin/mathtex.cgi?f(x)=\int_{-\infty}^xe^{-t^2}dt"> (see the package home page for a complete discussion).

MathTeX is a successor of the author's earlier mimeTeX; but mathTeX uses real LaTeX, where as mimeTeX uses its own built-in fonts, interpreter and rendering engine. Users who have LaTeX available on their server can obtain higher quality images and full LaTeX support with mathTeX. Users whose server doesn't offer LaTeX can continue to use mimeTeX. The two programs are plug-compatible, using the same <img> tag user interface, so migration is trivial.

The package home page carries extensive documentation of MathTeX.

topics.details: support for LaTeX(-alike) on the web, or feeding into other applications

name: mathtime-ltx
caption: LaTeX macros for using MathTime and MathTime Plus

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathtime-metrics
caption: MathTime AFM files

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathtime-pln
caption: Plain TeX macros for using MathTime and MathTime Plus

descriptions.text: Note that the (commercial) fonts themselves are now superseded, and no longer available. The package makes use of the mtmacs file that came with the fonts.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: mathtools
caption: Mathematical tools to use with amsmath

descriptions.text:
Mathtools provides a series of packages designed to enhance the appearance of documents containing a lot of mathematics. The main backbone is amsmath, so those unfamiliar with this required part of the LaTeX system will probably not find the packages very useful.

Mathtools provides many useful tools for mathematical typesetting. It is based on amsmath and fixes various deficiencies of amsmath and standard LaTeX. It provides:

  • Extensible symbols, such as brackets, arrows, harpoons, etc.;
  • Various symbols such as \coloneqq (:=);
  • Easy creation of new tag forms;
  • Showing equation numbers only for referenced equations;
  • Extensible arrows, harpoons and hookarrows;
  • Starred versions of the amsmath matrix environments for specifying the column alignment;
  • More building blocks: multlined, cases-like environments, new gathered environments;
  • Maths versions of \makebox, \llap, \rlap etc.;
  • Cramped math styles; and more...

Mathtools requires mhsetup.

name: MathTrip
caption: A trip to the wonderful world of mathematics

descriptions.text:
This document is a port (with a few additions) to LaTeX of the document https://www.tug.org/texshowcase/cheat.pdf produced and written in plain TeX. That original TeX document was written by Steve Seiden.

The purpose of the port to LaTeX is to make it possible to use the document to test some Unicode math fonts and unicode TeX more easily. This seems to be difficult with Plain TeX where the use of a font other than the Computer Modern fonts seems to be awfully complicated.

documentation.details: The document itself, compiled with luatex
The document itself, compiled with xetex

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
code that serves as examples of TeX programming

name: MathType
caption: Evaluation version of a commercial equation editor

descriptions.text:
MathType is a point and click mathematical equation editor. While its mouse-centric user interface is somewhat the opposite of TeX’s, it has a number of features that may be of interest to members of the TeX community:

  • It works with many Windows applications that TeX does not work directly with, such as word processors, presentation programs like PowerPoint, and many more. You can even place equations in flowcharts made with programs like Visio.
  • It can produce TeX and LaTeX code from its equations. This can be helpful to someone learning TeX or just to take advantage of MathType’s ability to work directly in mathematical notation in order to get the nested braces right on a particularly gnarly equation.
  • You can even type TeX language directly into the MathType window. This allows you to get the best of both the WYSIWYG editing and TeX worlds.
  • MathType can also produce GIF files for websites and blogs and EPS files for desktop publishing chores.

MathType does not require a product key for installation. Upon first launch, you will have an opportunity to begin a 30-day trial or to enter a purchased product key. If you decide to purchase MathType, you can use the Order MathType command within MathType itself to purchase a product key. You can also visit the Wiris website to learn more about MathType. If you have questions, email them to support@wiris.com.

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

name: matlab-prettifier
caption: Pretty-print Matlab source code

descriptions.text: The package extends the facilities of the listings package, to pretty-print Matlab and Octave source code. (Note that support of Octave syntax is not complete.)

name: matlabweb
caption: Literate programming system for Matlab

descriptions.text: Matlabweb is a literate programming system for the Matlab language. Similar to CWEB, it is created with a slightly modified version of the Spider system. Matlabweb can be used with plain TeX or LaTeX, the latter with help from the webfiles package.

name: matrix-skeleton
caption: A PGF/TikZ library that simplifies working with multiple matrix nodes

descriptions.text: The package provides a PGF/TikZ library that simplifies working with multiple matrix nodes. To do so, it correctly aligns groups of nodes with the content of the whole matrix. Furthermore, matrix.skeleton provides rows and columns for easy styling.

name: mattens
caption: Matrices/tensor typesetting

descriptions.text: The mattens package contains the definitions to typeset matrices, vectors and tensors as used in the engineering community for the representation of common vectors and tensors such as forces, velocities, moments of inertia, etc.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: mattex
caption: Import Matlab values to LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: The package provides macros and Matlab m-files that allow a user to export matlab variables to an intermediary file, and then import them to LaTeX for later use. This improves consistency and helps to prevent errors that might arise when manually copy-pasting.

name: maybeload
caption: Prevent reloading of files

descriptions.text: Defines a command \thisfileis, which will become \endinput if it's called for a second or subsequent time with a particular file name.

name: maybemath
caption: Make math bold or italic according to context

descriptions.text:
The \maybebm and \maybeit macros can be used in maths expressions to make the arguments typeset as bold or italic respectively if the surrounding context is appropriate. They are useful for writing user macros for use in general contexts.

\maybebm is especially appropriate when section titles contain math expressions, since the title will appear bold but the header and table of contents usually replicate the title in normal width. It uses the bm package to make things bold

\maybeit performs a similar role to \mathrm{} but the maths expression will be italicised if the surrounding text is. \maybeitsubscript is provided to shift subscripts to the left if the expression is italicised.

name: maze
caption: Generate random mazes

descriptions.text: This package can generate random square mazes of a specified size. The mazes generated by this package are natural and their solution is not too obvious. The output is based on the picture environment.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: mbboard
caption: Comprehensive blackboard bold fonts

descriptions.text: The distribution mbboard defines blackboard bold fonts for use with TeX either in text or maths mode; the fonts are specified in Metafont. The fonts cover upper and lower case roman letters (including ligatures), digits, and several maths-greek and hebrew letters.

name: mbenotes
caption: Notes in tables or images

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \tabnote, which stores notes for later processing by the command \thetabnotes, and a corresponding \imgnote for images.

The package is derived from mechanisms in the package endnotes.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: mboxfill
caption: Fill free space with a pattern

descriptions.text:
The package provides a convenient means of accessing the various leaders commands in TeX; define a box size, a filling object, and a sort of leader, and mboxfill will lay down an fill pattern.

The package is part of the ncctools bundle.

name: mcaption
caption: Put captions in the margin

descriptions.text:
The mcaption package provides an mcaption environment which puts figure or table captions in the margin. The package works with the standard classes and with the KOMA-Script document classes scrartcl, scrreprt and scrbook.

The package requires the changepage package.

name: mceinleger
caption: Creating covers for music cassettes

descriptions.text: A package for creating MC-covers on your own. It allows the creation of simple covers as well as covers with an additional page for more information about the cassette (table of contents e.g.). The rotating package is required.

topics.details: typeset badges, covers or labels for things (or people)

name: mcexam
caption: Create randomized Multiple Choice questions

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package automatically randomly permutes the order of questions as well as the answer options in different versions of a multiple choice exam/test.

Next to the exam versions themselves, the package also allows printing a concept version of the exam, a key table with the correct answers or points, and a document with solutions and explanations per exam version.

The package also allows writing an R code which processes the results of the exam and calculates the grades.
