topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: pygmentex
caption: Use Pygments to format code listings in documents

descriptions.text:
PygmenTeX is a Python-based LaTeX package that can be used for typesetting code listings in a LaTeX document using Pygments.

Pygments is a generic syntax highlighter for general use in all kinds of software such as forum systems, wikis or other applications that need to prettify source code.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: pyjupyter
caption: Lightweight environment for typesetting Python code

descriptions.text:
The pyjupyter package provides a lightweight and elegant environment for typesetting Python code in LaTeX documents with a visual style inspired by Jupyter notebooks.

It leverages the listings package for syntax highlighting and tcolorbox for structured, breakable frames. Key features include:

  • Full support for French accents and UTF-8 encoding.
  • Intelligent syntax highlighting for Python operators and keywords.
  • A dedicated numbered option for line numbering.
  • Seamless integration with TeXstudio via an included .cwl file for auto-completion.
  • Robust handling of Python comments (#) using an optional argument syntax.
  • Font selection.
  • Code size modification.

name: PyLuaTeX
caption: Execute Python code on the fly in your LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
PyLuaTeX allows you to execute Python code and to include the resulting output in your LaTeX documents in a single compilation run. LaTeX documents must be compiled with LuaLaTeX for this to work.

PyLuaTeX runs a Python InteractiveInterpreter (actually several if you use different sessions) in the background for on-the-fly code execution. Python code from your LaTeX file is sent to the background interpreter through a TCP socket. This approach allows your Python code to be executed and the output to be integrated in your LaTeX file in a single compilation run. No additional processing steps are needed. No intermediate files have to be written. No placeholders have to be inserted.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
call external code and process the result

name: pynotebook
caption: pynotebook presents (raw, Markdown or Python) codes (and execution with LuaLaTeX) as in a Jupyter Notebook

descriptions.text:
This package provides environments to (re)create a jupyter notebook with:

  • raw blocks;
  • markdown blocks (with full LaTeX support);
  • code blocks (python) with execution thanks to piton and PyLuaTeX (version > 0.7.0).

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: python
caption: Embed Python code in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package enables you to embed Python code in LaTeX, and insert the script’s output in the document.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: pythonhighlight
caption: Highlighting of Python code, based on the listings package

descriptions.text: Highlighting of Python code, based on the listings package.

name: pythonimmediate
caption: Library to run Python code

descriptions.text:
Just like PerlTeX or PyLuaTeX (and unlike PythonTeX or lt3luabridge), this only requires a single run, and variables are persistent throughout the run.

Unlike PerlTeX or PyLuaTeX, there is no restriction on compiler or script required to run the code.

There are also debugging functionalities: TeX errors result in Python traceback, and Python errors result in TeX traceback. Errors in code executed with the pycode environment give the correct traceback point to the Python line of code in the TeX file.

For advanced users, this package allows the user to manipulate the TeX state directly from within Python, so you don’t need to write a single line of TeX code.

CAUTION: In addition to this LaTeX package you need the Python pythonimmediate-tex package, which can be obtained from https://pypi.org/project/pythonimmediate-tex/.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: pythontex
caption: Run Python from within a document, typesetting the results

descriptions.text:
The package allows you to enter Python code within a LaTeX document, execute the code, and access its output in the original document. There is also support for Bash, JavaScript, Julia, Octave, Perl, R, Raku (Perl 6), Ruby, Rust, and SageMath.

Code is only executed when it has been modified, or when it meets user-specified criteria. Code may be divided into user-defined sessions, which automatically run in parallel.

Errors and warnings are synchronized with the LaTeX document, so that they refer to the document's line numbers. External dependencies can be tracked, so that code is re-executed when the data it depends on is modified. PythonTeX also provides syntax highlighting for code in LaTeX documents via the Pygments syntax highlighter.

The package provides a depythontex utility. This creates a copy of the document in which all Python code has been replaced by its output. This is useful for journal submissions, sharing documents, and conversion to other formats.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: pzccal
caption: Zapf Chancery as calligraphic math alphabet

descriptions.text:
The package establishes the Zapf Chancery font (pzcmi7t) as script (calligraphic) math alphabet \mathpzc. It provides options to scale the font and to configure the alias command name. By default, the package overwrites the predefined math alphabet command \mathcal.

The author has now declared the package obsolete, since he believes that the urwchancal package does the job better.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: Q-and-A
caption: Typesetting Q&A-style conversation made easier

descriptions.text:
Q-and-A is a LaTeX document class for you to typeset Q&A-style conversation. It turns simple pure text Q&A dialog into a carefully designed document.

Notably, it features two themes, ChatGPT-light and ChatGPT-dark, enabling you to format your Q&A dialog in a way that closely resembles the interface of ChatGPT.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language
LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: qbibman
caption: Graphical frontend to BibTool

name: qcircuit
caption: Macros to generate quantum ciruits

descriptions.text: The package supports those within the quantum information community who typeset quantum circuits, using xy-pic package, offering macros designed to help users generate circuits.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: QCM
caption: A LaTeX2e class for making multiple choice questionnaires

descriptions.text: QCM is a package for making multiple choices questionnaires under LaTeX2e (QCM is the French acronym for this style of test). A special environment allows you to define questions and possible answers. You can specify which answers are correct and which are not. QCM not only formats the questions for you, but also generates a form (a grid that your students will have to fill in), and a mask (the same grid, only with correct answers properly checked in). You can then print the mask on a slide and correct the questionnaires more easily by superimposing the mask on top of students’ forms. QCM can also typeset exam corrections automatically, and comes with support for AUC-TeX.

name: qdtexvpl
caption: Quick and dirty virtual font creation

descriptions.text: Qdtexvpl is a tool for quick and dirty creation of virtual fonts. You create a TeX file which contains the TeX code to be put into the virtual font, run TeX on the file, and feed the DVI file into qdtexvpl, which creates a VPL file. Finally, you use VPtoVF to create a TFM file and a VF file from the VPL file.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: qed
caption: Produce an <q>end-of-proof</q> mark

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: Produces end proof (and similar) mathematical marks, even at the end of displayed mathematics.

name: qfig
caption: DOS graphics program

descriptions.text: Qfig is a DOS graphics program to generate output for PicTeX and epic.

name: qfonts
caption: PostScript (Adobe Type 1) fonts in QX layout

descriptions.text:
IMPORTANT NOTICE: This package is now considered obsolete. Please use the TeX-Gyrefonts instead!

A collection of Type 1 fonts based on the URW++ fonts distributed with Ghostscript. The fonts are encoded according to QX layout which facilitates multilingual and technical typesetting using TeX, preserving usability in Windows applications.

The fonts have been superseded by the by the following TeX-Gyre fonts:

  • The Quasi-Bookman (qbk) fonts are now available as TeX-Gyre Bonum;
  • the Quasi-Chancery (qzc) fonts are now available as TeX-Gyre Chorus;
  • the Quasi-Courier (qcr) fonts are now available as TeX-Gyre Cursor;
  • the Quasi-Swiss and Quasi-Swiss-Condensed (qhv) fonts are now available as TeX-Gyre Heros;
  • the Quasi-Palatino (qpl) fonts are now available as TeX-Gyre Pagella; and
  • the Quasi-Times (qtm) fonts are now available as TeX-Gyre Termes.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: qm
caption: Commands for bras and kets and the like

descriptions.text: The commands (\bra and \ket, etc.) operate both in text and maths mode (the arguments are set as maths).

name: qms
caption: VMS tools for controlling QMS printers

topics.details: prepare data for use within TeX

name: qobitree
caption: LaTeX macros for typesetting trees

descriptions.text: Provides commands \branch and \leaf for specifying the elements of the tree; you build up your tree with those commands, and then issue the \tree command to typeset the whole.

name: qrbill
caption: Create QR bills using LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides support for creating QR-bills for the new Swiss payment standards.

This open source implementation is intended to offer a free option to support these regulations and can be adapted for international use.

Packages loaded by qrbill are expl3, fontspec (except if one is using a custom font setup), graphicx, scrbase, qrcode, iftex, l3keys2e, and numprint.

name: qrcode
caption: Generate QR codes in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package generates QR (Quick Response) codes in LaTeX, without the need for PSTricks or any other graphical package.

name: qrcodetikz
caption: Prettier QR codes

descriptions.text:
This package improves the display of QR codes provided by qrcode.

The Quick Response (QR) codes provided by package qrcode show white borders on each square (from little to very prominent, depending on the pdf viewer). This is because the QR code is printed square by square, not the connected regions of squares as such, and pdf screen viewers show these undesired borders.

This package overwrites the qrcode printing functions to fill connected regions of the QR code using TikZ, allowing prettier qrcodes on screen visualization, with possibility of customization.

name: qrcstamps
caption: Create QR codes using stamps

descriptions.text:
This package enables the document author to create QR Codes, the QR Code Symbology are cast onto a dynamic stamp annotation.

Adobe Distiller or ps2pdf can be used as the PDF creator, but the full Acrobat application is needed to perform post-creation tasks. Once the document is created and saved, it can be viewed by any appropriate PDF viewer.

topics.details: convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: qsharp
caption: Syntax highlighting for the Q# language

descriptions.text: The package provides syntax highlighting for the Q# language, a domain-specific language for quantum programming.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: qstest
caption: Bundle for unit tests and pattern matching

descriptions.text:
This is the public release of the qstest bundle (written for DocScape Publisher) (C) 2006, 2007 QuinScape GmbH.

The bundle contains the packages makematch for matching patterns to targets (with a generalization in the form of pattern lists and keyword lists), and qstest for performing unit tests, allowing the user to run a number of logged tests ensuring the consistency of values, properties and call sequences during execution of test code. Both packages make extensive use of in their package documentation, providing illustrated examples that are automatically verified to work as expected.

Check the README file for details.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: qsymbols
caption: Maths symbol abbreviations

descriptions.text: Provides macros for defining systematic mnemonic abbreviations, starting with ` for math symbols and \" for arrows, using standard symbols as well as those from the amsfonts bundle and the stmaryrd package.

name: qtree
caption: Draw tree structures

descriptions.text:
The package offers support for drawing tree diagrams, and is especially suitable for linguistics use. It allows trees to be specified in a simple bracket notation, automatically calculates branch sizes, and supports both DVI/PostScript and PDF output by use of pict2e facilities.

The package is a development of the existing qobitree package, offering a new front end.

name: qualitype
caption: The QualiType font collection

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text:
These 45 fonts were created by QualiType.

With the kind permisison of John Colletti, these fonts have been released as free and open-source.

topics.details: listing a set of related fonts
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

name: quantikz
caption: Draw quantum circuit diagrams

descriptions.text: The purpose of this package is to extend TikZ with the functionality for drawing quantum circuit diagrams.

name: quantum-chemistry-bonn
caption: Use consistent typesetting for quantum chemistry related software

descriptions.text: This package gives access to several commands related to quantum chemistry. This includes consistent formatting of names of QC programs, as well as methods such as density functionals. Furthermore, units of energy are set, and easy-to-use commands are provided. Lastly, the corporate design colors of the University of Bonn are defined.

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

name: quantumarticle
caption: Document class for submissions to the Quantum journal

authors.givenname: Quantum – the open journal for quantum science

copyright.owner: Verein zur Förderung des Open Access Publizierens in den Quantenwissenschaften

descriptions.text:
This package provides the preferred document class for papers to be submitted to Quantum – the open journal of quantum science. It is based on the widely used article document class and designed to allow a seamless transition from documents typeset with the article, revtex4-1, and elsarticle document classes. As a service to authors, the document class comes with a predefined bibilography style quantum.bst that is optimized to be used with the quantumarticle document class. Additionally, the quantumview documentclass is provided, which can be used as a proxy to typeset the HTML-only editorial pieces in Quantum Views in a LaTeX editor.

The quantumarticle document class also offers an option to remove the Quantum-related branding. In that way, users appreciating the esthetics of this document class can use it for their notes as well.

name: quantumcubemodel
caption: Representation of quantum states in the quantum cube model

descriptions.text: This package provides simple LaTeX commands to draw intuitive cube-based diagrams for quantum states of one, two, or three qubits. Inspired by Prof. B. Just’s educational framework, it supports amplitude-phase notation, gate transition visualizations (Hadamard, Pauli, CNOT, Toffoli). The package is ideal for teaching and documenting small quantum circuits.

name: quattrocento
caption: Quattrocento and Quattrocento Sans fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
The package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Quattrocento and Quattrocento Sans families of fonts, designed by Pablo Impallari; the fonts themselves are also provided, in both TrueType and Type1 format.

Quattrocento is a classic typeface with wide and open letterforms, and great x-height, which makes it very legible for body text at small sizes. Tiny details that only show up at bigger sizes make it also great for display use. Quattrocento Sans is the perfect sans-serif companion for Quattrocento.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: query-astro
caption: Querying astronomical databases in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The query-astro package is an experimental package developed to allow users to query astronomical databases directly from LaTeX. The query is performed by sending ADQL (Astronomical Data Query Language) instructions to a Table Access Protocol (TAP) service, so enabled \write18 is required. The result is then stored in a macro, which can be used in the document.

name: quickderivs
caption: Typeset derivatives and differentials with minimal input

descriptions.text: This is a small LaTeX package containing macros allowing one to typeset mathematical derivatives quickly, similar to esdiff.

name: quickreaction
caption: A simple and fast way to typeset chemical reactions

descriptions.text:
This package provides the quickreaction environment and the \quickarrow command to simplify the typesetting of chemical reactions.

It is based on the TikZ matrix of nodes and aligns all the reactants and products at the center of the TikZ box in which they are contained.

name: quicktype
caption: LaTeX package for quick typesetting

descriptions.text: Intended for the quick typesetting of basic documents using LaTeX using shortcuts to existing commands and specific commands for quick formatting and creation of tables and title pages with a graphic image.

name: quiver
caption: Draw commutative diagrams exported from https://q.uiver.app

descriptions.text:
quiver is a modern graphical editor for commutative and pasting diagrams, capable of rendering high-quality diagrams for screen viewing, and exporting to LaTeX.

This LaTeX package is intended to be used in conjunction with this editor, and provides the packages and styles that are used by diagrams exported from it.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: quiz2socrative
caption: Prepare questions for socrative quizzes

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX package for preparing multiple choice, true/false, and short answer questions.

Its main purpose is to offer a tool to easily insert rather complicated mathematical material in socrative quizzes (see https://socrative.com).

The package requires the following other LaTeX packages: calc, etoolbox, graphicx, ifthen, listofitems, moresize, TikZ, pgfmath, xcolor, and xparse.

name: quizztex
caption: Create quizzes like in TV shows

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package permits to create quizzes in the style of the TV shows « Qui veut gagner des millions ? » (Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?) or « Tout le monde veut prendre sa place ! ».

name: quotation
caption: Typeset an attributed quotation

descriptions.text: \quotation takes two arguments, the quotation itself, and the attribution. The quotation is set as a page-wide \align, so placement of \cr commands may be useful for best appearance.

name: quotchap
caption: Decorative chapter headings

descriptions.text: A package for creating decorative chapter headings with quotations. Uses graphical and coloured output and by default needs the Adobe standard font set (as supported by psnfss).

name: quote
caption: Match pairs of double-quote characters

descriptions.text: The package creates macros that match pairs of the ASCII double quote character to produce the left- and right-double quote ligatures that exist in standard-encoded TeX fonts.

name: quotes
caption: Smart double quotes in LaTeX input

descriptions.text:
A package to automatically translate the character " (ASCII double quote) to `` or '' so that opening and closing quotes are produced in the correct sequence.

The package is part of the bosisio collection.

name: quoting
caption: Consolidated environment for displayed text

descriptions.text: As an alternative to the LaTeX standard environments quotation and quote, the package provides a consolidated environment for displayed text. First-line indentation may be activated by adding a blank line before the quoting environment. A key-value interface (using kvoptions) allows the user to configure font properties and spacing and to control orphans within and after the environment.

name: quotmark
caption: Consistent quote marks

descriptions.text:
The package provides a means of ensuring consistent quote marks throughout your document. The style can be changed either via package option or command, and the package detects language selections (from the babel or ngerman packages), and uses the punctuation marks appropriate for the current language.

The author now considers the package obsolete, and recommends use of csquotes in its place.

name: quran
caption: An easy way to typeset any part of The Holy Quran

descriptions.text:
This package offers the user an easy way to typeset The Holy Quran. It has been inspired by the lipsum and ptext packages and provides several macros for typesetting the whole or any part of the Quran based on its popular division, including surah, ayah, juz, hizb, quarter, and page.

Besides the Arabic original, translations to English, German, French, and Persian are provided, as well as an English transliteration.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Arabic
dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: quran-bn
caption: Bengali translations to the quran package

descriptions.text:
The package is prepared for typesetting some Bengali translations of the Holy Quran.

It adds two Bengali translations to the quran package.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: quran-de
caption: German translations to the quran package

descriptions.text:
The package is prepared for typesetting some German translations of the Holy Quran.

It adds three more German translations to the quran package.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: quran-en
caption: English translation extension to the quran package

descriptions.text: This package is designed for typesetting multiple English translations of the Holy Quran. It adds 15 additional English translations to the quran package.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: quran-es
caption: Spanish Translations for the quran package

descriptions.text:
The package is designed for typesetting several Spanish translations of the Holy Quran.

It extends the quran package by adding three additional Spanish translations.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: quran-id
caption: Indonesian translation extension to the quran package

descriptions.text:
The package is prepared for typesetting some Indonesian translations of the Holy Quran.

It adds two Indonesian translations to the quran package.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: quran-ur
caption: Urdu translations to the quran package

descriptions.text:
The package is prepared for typesetting some Urdu translations of the Holy Quran.

It adds eight Urdu translations to the quran package.

topics.details: dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: QWorld
caption: Drawing string diagrams for monoidal categories and quantum theory in TeX

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package has been designed for the typesetting of graphical languages grounded in monoidal category theory and its extensions. It provides a declarative, LaTeX-native interface for rendering string diagrams, eliminating the need for any external graphics software or manual image management.

The package supports a wide spectrum of categorical structures frequently encountered in categorical quantum mechanics, algebraic structures, and diagrammatic reasoning, including but not limited to:

  • Monoidal and symmetric monoidal categories
  • Dual objects and pivotal / rigid categories
  • Dagger categories
  • Frobenius algebras and Hopf algebras
  • Braided, balanced, and ribbon categories

Internally, QWorld builds upon the TikZ graphics framework, but introduces a domain-specific layer of abstraction that aligns diagram syntax closely with categorical semantics. This design facilitates accurate and transparent visual representations of morphisms, tensor products, and composition, thereby supporting both formal exposition and pedagogical use.

QWorld is intended for researchers and educators working in categorical logic, quantum foundations, topological quantum field theory (TQFT), and related domains where graphical calculi constitute an essential mode of reasoning.

name: qyxf-book
caption: Book Template for Qian Yuan Xue Fu

descriptions.text:
qyxf-book is a LaTeX document class (template) developed by Qian Yuan Xue Fu (QYXF), a student club of Xi’an Jiaotong University (XJTU). Up to now, this template has been applied to academic counselling material (course helpers) written by members of QYXF, including

  • Solutions to University Physics
  • Notes on Computing Methods

Features of the template:

  • Minimalistic document style, as preferred for course helpers.
  • Several color schemes are offered, and it is easy to customize your own scheme.
  • Simple interfaces for users to customize the style of preface, main part and so on.

Currently the template is only designed for Chinese typesetting.

name: r_und_s
caption: Chemical hazard codes

descriptions.text:
The r_und_s package decodes the german R- und S-Sätze, which are numerically coded security advice for chemical substances into plain text. This is, e.g., used to compose security sheets or lab protocols and especially useful for students of chemistry.

There are four packages, giving texts in German, English, French and Dutch.

name: r2bib
caption: Convert refer and EndNote files to BibTeX

descriptions.text:
R2bib and EndNote2bib read files (respectively in refer and EndNote format) and produces a BibTeX reference list on the standard output.

Since refer files are inherently unstructured, r2bib only does a passable job (for example, it may need to invent a key for an entry, and it has to guess what BibTeX entry type to generate).

EndNote tags may not always match those recognised by EndNote2bib; a further filter program EndNoteTag is provided

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: ragged
caption: Generic ragged left and ragged right options

descriptions.text: Provides any TeX format (including LaTeX) with ragged left and ragged centre formatting of paragraphs while maintaining full control of hyphenation and degree of raggedness.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: ragged2e
caption: Alternative versions of <q>ragged</q>-type commands

descriptions.text: The package defines new commands \Centering, \RaggedLeft, and \RaggedRight and new environments Center, FlushLeft, and FlushRight, which set ragged text and are easily configurable to allow hyphenation (the corresponding commands in LaTeX, all of whose names are lower-case, prevent hyphenation altogether).

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: raggedr
caption: Set an entire document raggedright

descriptions.text: This package has been incorporated into ragged2e.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: rail
caption: Syntax specification in EBNF

descriptions.text: A C program and LaTeX package to draw syntax diagrams specified in EBNF.

name: rainbowbrackets
caption: Automatic coloring of nested parentheses

descriptions.text: The primary function of this package is to replicate a common feature found in many integrated development environments (IDEs), wherein matching parentheses at the same nesting level are assigned corresponding colors. This visual aid facilitates improved readability and cognitive parsing of complex expressions.

name: rake4latex
caption: A rake-based tool to compile LaTeX projects

descriptions.text:
The package provides a tool that compiles LaTeX-documents as often as needed, including makeindex and BibTeX calls.

A simple interface to the rake4latex-gem (Ruby/Rake) is provided, and an exe-file for windows (the exe-file requires no Ruby or Rake).

The gem itself is available at the RubyGems.

name: raleway
caption: Use Raleway with TeX(-alike) systems

descriptions.text: The package provides the Raleway family in an easy to use way. For XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX users the original OpenType fonts are used. The entire font family is included.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents

name: ran_toks
caption: Randomise token strings

descriptions.text:
The package provides means of randomising lists of tokens, or lists of chunks of tokens. Two mechanisms for defining chunks are provided:

  • the \ranToks command accepts an argument containing tokens to be randomised; and
  • the \bRTVToks/\eRTVToks commands delimit a collection of tokens for randomising; each group inside a rtVw constitutes one of these (typically larger) token sets.

name: randbild
caption: Marginal pictures

descriptions.text: Provides environments randbild to draw small marginal plots (using the packages pstricks and pst-plot), and randbildbasis (the same, only without the automatically drawn coordinate system).

name: randexam
caption: Make an exam paper and its randomized variants

descriptions.text:
This class helps you make an exam paper and its randomized variants.

It mainly focuses on making math exam papers, but you could use it to make other exam papers.

name: randintlist
caption: Creating random integer number lists, with repeating and sorting options

descriptions.text:
This package (like luarandom, but without the obligation to use LuaLaTeX) provides some macros for creating random integer number lists between a and b.

This list can have multiple numbers or not, and this list can be sorted or not.

name: random
caption: Generating <q>random</q> numbers in TeX

descriptions.text: Generates pseudo-random integers in the range 1 to 2^{31}. Macros are to provide random integers in a given range, or random dimensions which can be used to provide random real numbers, are also available.

name: randomlist
caption: Deal with database, loop, and random in order to build personalized exercises

descriptions.text:
The main aim of this package is to work on lists, especially with random operations.

The hidden aim is to build a personal collection of exercises with different data for each pupil.

name: randomwalk
caption: Random walks using TikZ

descriptions.text:
The randomwalk package provides a user command, \RandomWalk, to draw random walks with a given number of steps. Lengths and angles of the steps can be customized in various ways.

The package uses lcg for its random numbers and PGF/TikZ for its graphical output.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: randtext
caption: Randomise the order of characters in strings

descriptions.text:
The package provides a single macro \randomize{TEXT} that typesets the characters of TEXT in random order, such that the resulting output appears correct, but most automated attempts to read the file will misunderstand it.

This function allows one to include an email address in a TeX document and publish it online without fear of email address harvesters or spammers easily picking up the address.

name: rangecite
caption: Will turn a range of citations into something like [1..3]

descriptions.text: A jiffy that converts a range of citations into something like [1-3].

name: rangen
caption: Generate random integers, rational and decimal numbers

descriptions.text: The package generates random integers, rational numbers, and decimal numbers. The package uses the lcg package to generate random integers, and then builds rational numbers and decimal numbers from the generated integers.

name: rank-2-roots
caption: Draw (mathematical) rank 2 root systems

descriptions.text:
This package concerns mathematical drawings arising in representation theory. The purpose of this package is to ease drawing of rank 2 root systems, with Weyl chambers, weight lattices, and parabolic subgroups.

Required packages are tikz, etoolbox, expl3, pgfkeys, pgfopts, xparse, and xstring.

name: ransom
caption: A <q>very bad typewriter</q> font

descriptions.text: This font was developed for Metafont-for-SAIL, and the sources are no longer available (they wouldn't help much even if we had them). It is (just about) possible to use the fonts – available solely as a fixed-size 300dpi copy – as they are.

topics.details: font distributed in an ad-hoc fashion
fonts designed more for fun than for actual use

name: ratex
caption: A package for German lawyers

descriptions.text: RATeX is a newly developed bundle of packages and classes provided for German lawyers. Now in the early beginning it only contains rtklage, a class to make lawsuits.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: ratexdb
caption: Database reports using LaTeX and Ruby

descriptions.text:
This is a compatible rewrite of LaTeXDB (by Hans-Georg Eßer) in Ruby.

It is a preprocessor which performs SQL queries on a database and creates LaTeX code for the resulting rows. Ratexdb implements a few improvements, e.g. regexp postprocessing, command-line options, some protection against SQL injection, replacement of LaTeX reserved characters.

ratexdb is no longer being developed; it's replacement is nlatexdb.

name: rawfonts
caption: Low level font compatibility mode for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A package to define the low-level font commands that existed in LaTeX 2.09, for the benefit of old documents (or packages) that used them.

Since this is potentially an expensive operation (loading lots of fonts), the package allows you to chop and choose:

\usepackage[only,tenrm,sevsf]{rawfonts}

will load just \tenrm and \sevsf. (This facility uses the somedefs package).

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: rawprint
caption: Print raw Russian text

descriptions.text: A package for quick and dirty printing of raw (i.e., non-TeX) Russian texts by persons who do not have Russian printer fonts (but have Cyrillic TeX). It makes various symbols normal letters and converts the unisex quote character " into Russian-style « and » quotes.

name: rbt-mathnotes
caption: Rebecca Turner’s personal macros and styles for typesetting mathematics notes

descriptions.text: Styles for typesetting mathematics notes. Includes document classes for typesetting homework assignments and formula cheat sheets for exams. Several examples are included, along with rendered PDFs.

name: rccol
caption: Decimal-centered optionally rounded numbers in tabular

descriptions.text:
The rccol package provides decimal-centered numbers: corresponding digits and decimal separators aligned. Furthermore, rounding to the desired precision is possible.

The package makes use of the fltpoint package (as well as the LaTeX required array package).

name: rcs
caption: Use RCS (revision control system) tags in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
The rcs package utilizes the inclusion of RCS supplied data in LaTeX documents. It's upward compatible to *all* rcs styles I know of.

In particular, you can easily

  • access values of every RCS field in your document
  • put the checkin date on the titlepage
  • put RCS fields in a footline

You can typeset revision logs. Not in verbatim -- real LaTeX text! But you need a configurable RCS for that. Refer to the user manual for more detailed information.

You can also configure the rcs package easily to do special things for any keyword.

This bundle comes with a user manual, an internal interface description, full documentation of the implementation, style information for AUC-TeX, and test cases.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: rcs-multi
caption: Typeset RCS version control in multiple-file documents

descriptions.text:
The package enables the user to typeset version control information provided by RCS keywords (e.g., $ID: ... $) in LaTeX documents that contain multiple TeX files.

The package is based on the author’s svn-multi package.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: rcs-pln
caption: RCS data in Plain TeX documents

descriptions.text: Provides commands \RCSdate and \RCSrevision which take $-delimited RCS entries; these set up commands \thedate and \therevision for use in the document. Also provides a \Draft command.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: rcsinfo
caption: Support for the revision control system

descriptions.text:
A package to extract RCS (Revision Control System) information and use it in a LaTeX document.

For users of LaTeX2HTML rcsinfo.perl is included.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: ReadableCV
caption: A highly readable and good looking CV and letter class

descriptions.text: This class provides, what I have found, to be an extremely attractive and highly readable CV which will lead to your CV being read rather than disregarded.

name: readarray
caption: Read, store and recall array-formatted data

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to input formatted data into elements of a 2-D or 3-D array and to recall that data at will by individual cell number. The data can be but need not be numerical in nature. It can be, for example, formatted text.

While the package can be used for any application where indexed data is called for, the package proves particularly useful when elements of multiple arrays must be recallable and dynamically combined at time of compilation, rather than in advance.

name: readprov
caption: Provides GetFileInfo without the need to load the file

descriptions.text:
The package provides a \GetFileInfo command (as in the LaTeX standard doc package, but without the need to load the doc package). The package also provides new robust (expandable) variants of \GetFileInfo, even without loading the file itself (reading the file is stopped when the requisite information is found). So, for example, you can describe packages that are incompatible with each other or with packages that your document uses, or even report about class files (that are plainly not loadable).

Files examined in this way also enter the output of \listfiles.

The package is part of the fileinfo bundle.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: realboxes
caption: Variants of common box-commands that read their content as real box and not as macro argument

descriptions.text:
The package uses the author’s package collectbox to define variants of common box related macros which read the content as real box and not as macro argument. This enables the use of verbatim or other special material as part of this content.

The provided macros have the same names as the original versions but start with an upper-case letter instead. The long-form macros, like \Makebox, can also be used as environments, but not the short-form macros, like \Mbox. However, normally the long form uses the short form anyway when no optional arguments are used.

name: realcalc
caption: Macros for real arithmetic calculations

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: There are known problems with this package; an alternative is fp (a LaTeX package, only).

name: realhats
caption: Put real hats on symbols instead of ^

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package makes \hat put real hats on symbols.

The package depends on amsmath, calc, graphicx, ifthen, lcg, and stackengine.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: realscripts
caption: Access OpenType subscript and superscript glyphs

descriptions.text:
This small package replaces \textsuperscript and \textsubscript commands by equivalent commands that use OpenType font features to access appropriate glyphs if possible.

The package also patches LaTeX’s default footnote command to use this new \textsuperscript for footnote symbols.

The package requires fontspec running on either XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

The package holds functions that were once parts of the xltxtra package, which now loads realscripts by default.

topics.details: position sub- and superscripts (left and right sides)

name: realtranspose
caption: The <q>real</q> way to transpose a Matrix

copyright.owner: Lars Quentin, Matthew Scroggs, Adam Townsend

descriptions.text: With realtranspose you can notate the transposition of a matrix by rotating the symbols 90 degrees. This is an homage to the realhats package.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: rebuttal
caption: Markup for structured journal and conference paper rebuttals

descriptions.text: This package provides means for writing structured journal and conference paper rebuttals.

name: rec-thy
caption: Commands to typeset recursion theory papers

descriptions.text: This package is designed to help mathematicians publishing papers in the area of recursion theory (aka Computability Theory) easily use standard notation. This includes easy commands to denote Turing reductions, Turing functionals, c.e. sets, stagewise computations, forcing and syntactic classes.

name: recipe
caption: A LaTeX class to typeset recipes

descriptions.text: The layout design is relatively straightforward (and traditional: see sample output under documentation); the class uses the Bookman and the BrushScript-Italic fonts.

name: recipebook
caption: Typeset 5.5″ x 8″ recipes for browsing or printing

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX2e class for typesetting recipes. It is designed for typesetting one or two recipes per page, with dimensions of 5.5″ x 8.5″.

The hyperlinked table of contents (ToC) and page numbers make browsing recipes convenient, and the pages can be joined together or printed two per sheet to normal letterpaper easily.

The size was chosen to work in half-page 3-ring binder cover sheets.

name: recipecard
caption: Typeset recipes in note-card-sized boxes

descriptions.text: The recipecard class typesets recipes into note card sized boxes that can then be cut out and pasted on to note cards. The recipe then looks elegant and fits in the box of recipes.

name: recorder-fingering
caption: Package to display recorder fingering diagrams

descriptions.text: This package provides support for generating and displaying fingering diagrams for baroque fingering recorders and the tin whistle. Standard fingerings are provided for recorders in both C and F, and the tin whistle in D, along with methods to create and display alternate fingerings for trills, etc.

name: rectopma
caption: Recycle top matter

descriptions.text: Saves the arguments of \author and \title for reference (after \maketitle) in a document. (\maketitle simply disposes of the information, in the standard classes and some others.)

name: recycle
caption: A font providing the <q>recyclable</q> logo

descriptions.text: This single-character font is provided as Metafont source, and in Adobe Type 1 format. It is accompanied by a trivial LaTeX package to use the logo at various sizes.

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: redefine
caption: Conditional macro, etc., definitions

descriptions.text: Defines commands ewdef, ewgdef and ewlet that warn the user if a command is redefined using them (if operating under LaTeX, ewcommand is similarly modified). In addition ewif, ewbox, ewcount, ewdimen, ewtoks are modified to detect an error if a conditional or register name is reused.

name: redis
caption: A Hebrew font

descriptions.text: The font is in Metafont format; a version of it seems to appear in the HebTeX distribution.

topics.details: documentation in and support for typesetting Hebrew

name: REdit
caption: Menu-based editor

descriptions.text: REdit (written in Turbo Pascal for DOS) aims to simplify work with LaTeX with menus to insert commands. This should be convenient for beginners, in particular.

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

name: refcheck
caption: Check references (in figures, table, equations, etc)

descriptions.text: The package checks references in a document, looking for numbered but unlabelled equations, for labels which are not used in the text, for unused bibliography references. It can also display label names in text near corresponding numbers of equations and/or bibliography references.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: refcount
caption: Counter operations with label references

descriptions.text:
Provides commands \setcounterref and \addtocounterref which use the section (or whatever) number from the reference as the value to put into the counter, as in: 

      ...\label{sec:foo}
      ...
      \setcounterref{foonum}{sec:foo}
Commands \setcounterpageref and \addtocounterpageref do the corresponding thing with the page reference of the label.

No .ins file is distributed; process the .dtx with plain TeX to create one.

name: refenums
caption: Define named items and provide back-references with that name

descriptions.text: The package provides commands to define enumerable items with a number and a long name, which can be referenced later with the name or just the short form. For instance, Milestone M1: Specification created can be defined and later on be referenced with M1 or M1 (Specification created). The text in the references is derived from the definition and also rendered as hyperlink to the definition.

name: refer
caption: Convert a BibTeX bibliography to refer format

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

name: refer-tools
caption: Convert between refer format and BibTeX format

descriptions.text:
Various tools, mostly packaged as Unix shar archives:

  • ref2bib, an awk script for converting Refer format bibliographies to BibTeX format;
  • refer2bibtex, a Perl script for the same conversion;
  • refer.bst, a tool to convert a BibTeX database to Refer format, using BibTeX itself;
  • tex2refer, an awk-based script for the same conversion;
  • refer-to-bibtex, a GNU-emacs program to convert Refer format bibliographies to BibTeX format;
  • tib-to-bibtex, a C program to convert tib format bibliographies to BibTeX format.

name: references
caption: Bibliographic software supporting LaTeX/BibTeX

descriptions.text: The package comprises bibliographic software supporting preparation of scientific manuscripts, storage of bibliographic data of articles in periodicals, books and articles in books. The package supports the TeX/LaTeX/BibTeX setup as well as commercial word processors. Bibliographic data in the MEDLINE format may be imported. References may be retrieved by keywords, authors’ or editors’ names, date of publication, strings in the title of an article, in a book title or in journal names. Lists of references may be supplied in a (user-defined) formats.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: reflectgraphics
caption: Techniques for reflecting graphics

descriptions.text: The package provides a macro for reflecting images, in a number of different ways, in pursuit of more striking graphics in a document.

name: refman
caption: Format technical reference manuals

descriptions.text: Document classes (report- and article-style) for writing technical reference manuals. It offers a wide left margin for notes to the reader, like some of the manuals distributed by Adobe.

name: refreshpdf
caption: Refresh PDF files <q>remotely</q>

descriptions.text:
Refreshpdf is an applescript that will ensure the current copy of a PDF file is open in Acrobat reader; this may require that it instructs reader to close and re-open the file.

Users of non-Macintosh X11-based systems may use the commands from the xpdfopen package.

topics.details: view, or control viewing of, PDF

name: refstyle
caption: Advanced formatting of cross references

descriptions.text: The package provides a consistent way of producing references throughout a project. Enough flexibility is provided to make local changes to a single reference. The user can configure their own setup. The package offers a direct interface to varioref (for use, for example, in large projects such as a series of books, or a multivolume thesis written as a series of documents), and name references from the nameref package may be incorporated with ease. For large projects such as a series of books or a multi volume thesis, written as freestanding documents, a facility is provided to interface to the xr package for external document references.

name: regcount
caption: Display the allocation status of the TeX registers

descriptions.text: Adds a macro \rgcounts which displays the allocation status of the TeX registers. The display is written into the .log file as it is a bit verbose. An automatic call to \rgcounts is done at \begin{document} and \end{document}.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: regexpatch
caption: High level patching of commands

descriptions.text: The package generalises the macro patching commands provided by P. Lehmann’s etoolbox. The difference between this package and its sibling xpatch is that this package sports a very powerful \regexpatchcmd based on the l3regex module of the LaTeX3 experimental packages.

name: register
caption: Typeset programmable elements in digital hardware (registers)

descriptions.text:
This package is designed for typesetting the programmable elements in digital hardware, i.e., registers. Such registers typically have many fields and can be quite wide; they are thus a challenge to typeset in a consistent manner. Register is similar in some aspects to the bytefield and bitpattern packages. Anyone doing hardware documentation using LaTeX should examine those packages.

Register requires version 2001/07/25 or newer of the float package.

An example Perl module and script are provided, to convert the register specifications into structures suitable for, say, a pre-silicon test environment.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: register-transfer-level
caption: Easily generate high-quality, publication-ready RTL diagrams

descriptions.text: Register-Transfer-Level is a TikZ-based package designed to easily generate high-quality, publication-ready Register Transfer Level (RTL) diagrams. It aims to simplify the tedious process of drawing digital hardware architectures by providing parametric components and smart routing capabilities.

name: regstats
caption: Information about register use

descriptions.text: The package will report number of used registers (counter, dimen, skip, muskip, box, token, input, output, math families, languages, insertions), and will compare the number to the maximum available number of such registers.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: regulatory
caption: Flexible drafting of legal documents, especially in Dutch

descriptions.text: This package aims to simplify the writing process, especially for Dutch legal authors. It has also been implemented in English and can be expanded to include other languages. The package offers macros for typical legal structures and contains a referencing system.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: relatese
caption: General report helper package

descriptions.text:
relatese is a small helper package for scientific reports.

It provides a simplified way of loading commonly used package setups that enhance the standard LaTeX system, with options to load modules for page layout, mathematics, figures, tables, scientific writing, references, and draft tools.

name: reledmac
caption: Typeset scholarly editions

descriptions.text:
A package for typesetting scholarly critical editions, replacing the established ledmac and eledmac packages. Ledmac itself was a LaTeX port of the plain TeX EDMAC macros.

The package supports indexing by page and by line numbers, and simple tabular- and array-style environments.

The package is distributed with the related reledpar package.

name: reledpar
caption: Typeset scholarly editions in parallel texts

descriptions.text:
Reledpar is the replacement for the ledpar and the eledpar packages; it provides parallel-text typesetting (either in parallel columns, or on opposing pages), for the reledmac package.

The package is available as part of the reledmac distribution.

name: relenc
caption: A <q>relaxed</q> font encoding

descriptions.text: LaTeX package providing a relaxed font encoding to make available to a font designer more slots for insertion of ligatures and accented characters.

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

name: relsize
caption: Set the font size relative to the current font size

descriptions.text: The basic command of the package is \relsize, whose argument is a number of \magsteps to change size; from this are defined commands \larger, \smaller, \textlarger, etc.

name: removefr
caption: Remove from counter-reset lists

descriptions.text:
Defines an internal command \@removefromreset, which does the opposite of the (LaTeX internal) \@addtoreset.

The package is one of a collection of fragments designed for use by package writers and others.

name: remreset
caption: Remove counters from reset list

descriptions.text:
\@removefromreset is a companion to the standard \@addtoreset command which allows counters to be removed from the reset list of a controlling counter.

This package is now obsolete as its functionality has been incorporated into the LaTeX format, but it is still distributed as part of the carlisle bundle.

name: renditions
caption: Multiple versions from the same content

descriptions.text: The package sets up comment environments, called renditions; each rendition is thought of as a version of the basic content of the document that includes it.

name: reotex
caption: Draw Reo Channels and Circuits

descriptions.text: The package defines macros and other utilities to design Reo Circuits. The package requires PGF/TikZ support.

name: repeat
caption: Repeat execution of macros

descriptions.text:
Repeat is a really general loop macro, which can be nested to arbitrary depth without any grouping or such.

Documentation appears as comments at the start of the package file.

name: repeatindex
caption: Repeat items in an index after a page or column break

descriptions.text: This Package repeats item of an index if a page or column break occurs within a list of subitems. This helps to find out to which main item a subitem belongs.

name: repere
caption: MetaPost macros for secondary school mathematics teachers

descriptions.text:
This package provides MetaPost macros for drawing secondary school mathematics figures in a coordinate system:

  • axis, grids
  • points, vectors
  • functions (curves, tangents, integrals, sequences)
  • statistic diagrams
  • plane geometry (polygons, circles)
  • arrays and game boards

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: repltext
caption: Control how text gets copied from a PDF file

descriptions.text: The repltext package exposes to LaTeX a relatively obscure PDF feature: replacement text. When replacement text is specified for a piece of text, it is the replacement text, not the typeset text that is copied and pasted.

name: report
caption: Typeset a multi-chapter report

descriptions.text: The class provides typesetting rather similar to that of the book class, omitting some features relevant only when professional book-publishing is to be used.

name: reptheorem
caption: Repetition of theorem environments

descriptions.text:
When writing a large manuscript, it is sometimes beneficial to repeat a theorem (or lemma or …) at an earlier or later point for didactical purposes. However, thmtools’s built-in restatable only allows replicating theorems after they have been stated, and only in the same document.

This package solves the issue by making use of the .aux file, and also introduces its own file extension, .thm, to replicate theorems in other files.

name: required
caption: Packages <q>required</q> of a LaTeX distribution

descriptions.text:
These are packages that the LaTeX team have declared are required of any LaTeX distribution – in the sense that any package writer is entitled to assume the presence of these packages in support of her package.

The set comprises:

  • AmsLaTeX, mathematical support from the AMS;
  • The babel package for multilingual typesetting;
  • Standard LaTeX support for using Cyrillic alphabet fonts;
  • The standard LaTeX graphics and colour packages;
  • Basic support for using common Adobe Type 1 fonts with LaTeX – the psnfss ; and
  • Basic LaTeX latex-tools .

For distribution details, see the individual packages’ catalogue entries.

topics.details: root directory of a (sub-)tree of the archive

name: rerunfilecheck
caption: Checksum based rerun checks on auxiliary files

descriptions.text: The package provides additional rerun warnings if some auxiliary files have changed. It is based on MD5 checksum provided by pdfTeX, LuaTeX, XeTeX.

name: res
caption: A resumé class

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: An update, for current LaTeX, of a LaTeX 2.09 document style.

name: rescansync
caption: Re-scan tokens with synctex information

descriptions.text: Allow users to execute saved code to typeset text while preserving SyncTeX information.

name: resizegather
caption: Automatically resize overly large equations

descriptions.text:
Equations that are too large are resized to fit the available space. The environment gather of package amsmath is supported. Also the environments equation and displaymath are redefined using gather and its starred version.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: resmes
caption: Measure restriction symbol in LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides a simple macro \resmes that prints the measure restriction symbol.

name: ResolSysteme
caption: Work on linear systems using xint or pyluatex

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (in French) to perform calculations on small (2x2 or 3x3 or 4x4) linear systems, with xint or pyluatex:

  • \DetMatrice or \DetMatricePY to diplay the determinant of a matrix (with formatting options);
  • \MatriceInverse or \MatriceInversePY to display the invers of a matrix (with formatting options) ;
  • \SolutionSysteme or \SolutionSystemePY to display the solution of a linear system (with formatting options);
  • …

topics.details: package will use LuaTeX facilities if available

name: resphilosophica
caption: Typeset articles for the journal Res Philosophica

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a class for typesetting articles for the journal Res Philosophica.

This work was commissioned by the Saint Louis University.

name: responsive
caption: Responsive design methods for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
Responsive design aims to display text and other design elements well on variety of outputs, including electronic devices or various paper sizes. It originated on the Web, using Cascading Style Sheets to change design elements.

This package tries to achieve similar results with LaTeX. The main aim is to support the output of multiple editions of one document with readable font sizes regardless of the physical size of the produced PDF, from smartphones or e-ink readers to printed A4 pages.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: rest-api
caption: Describing a rest api

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides macros to describe rest apis for documentation purposes. The endpoints can hold the following information:

  • method
  • description
  • path parameter
  • request body and content type
  • response body, content type and status code

name: resumecls
caption: Typeset a resume both in English and Chinese

descriptions.text: A LaTeX document class to typeset a resume or CV both in English and Chinese with more ease and flexibility.

name: resumemac
caption: Plain TeX macros for resumés

descriptions.text: A set of macros is provided, together with an file that offers an example of use.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: RetosMatematicos
caption: LaTeX template for the Telegram group Retos Matemáticos

copyright.owner: Henry Díaz Bordón, José Manuel Sánchez Muñoz

descriptions.text:
This package provides the class RetoMatematico.cls, which is used to typeset the final solutions of the mathematical challenges published in the Telegram group Retos Matemáticos (by José Manuel Sánchez Muñoz).

Among its features, the class sets the document size to letter paper, switches the font to Palatino Linotype (via the mathpazo package), and places information such as the group’s ISSN and link in the page margins.

Further details and usage examples are available in the package documentation.

name: returntogrid
caption: Semi-automatic grid typesetting

descriptions.text: returntogrid offers a few commands to get something like an simple, semi-automatic grid typesetting. It does more or less what the existing gridset package does. The main differences to gridset are that returntogrid works also with LuaLaTeX and that it has also a command to do some horizontal movements to get to tab positions.

topics.details: typeset, snapping lines of text to a grid

name: revbadge
caption: Multi-color highlight builder featuring block and inline revision badges

descriptions.text:
The revbadge package provides an elegant, column-safe framework designed specifically for tracking major revisions and minor modifications in academic manuscripts. This package can also be used as a handy highlighting tool.

The revbadge block environment for handling long paragraphs, multi-line equations, lists, and sections; revbadgemultiline shares the same purpose but allows you to build multi-line badge labels; and the \revbadgeinline macro for executing tight, mid-sentence word corrections without disrupting standard line spacing. Both components feature a dynamic colored badge mechanism that labels modifications on the fly.

The package provides native, automated integration with hyperref and cleveref under a unified highlight reference counter. Additionally, revbadge comes pre-packaged with a vibrant, 24-theme colour palette accessible via highly memorable 4-letter macro colour identifiers (e.g., blue, gren, orng, purp, ylow, grey).

topics.details: document reviewing subjects relevant for TeX users

name: reverxii
caption: Playing Reversi in TeX

descriptions.text: Following the lead of xii.tex, this little (938 characters) program that plays Reversi. (The program incorporates some primitive AI.)

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements
TeX code as a source of humour

name: revnum
caption: Reverse enumerate

descriptions.text: Provides a reverse-enumerate environment (revnumerate) in which items are numbered in reverse order.

name: revquantum
caption: Hacks to make writing quantum papers for revtex4-1 less painful

descriptions.text: This package provides a number of useful hacks to solve common annoyances with the revtex4-1 package, and to define notation in common use within quantum information. In doing so, it imports and configures a number of commonly-available and used packages, and where reasonable, provides fallbacks. It also warns when users try to load packages which are known to be incompatible with revtex4-1.

name: revtex
caption: Styles for various Physics Journals

descriptions.text: Includes styles for American Physical Society, American Institute of Physics, and Optical Society of America. The distribution consists of the RevTeX class itself, and several support packages.

name: revtex4-0
caption: Styles for various Physics Journals (old version)

descriptions.text: This is an old version of revtex, and is kept as a courtesy to users having difficulty with the incompatibility of that latest version.

name: revtex4-1
caption: Styles for various Physics Journals

descriptions.text: This is an old version of revtex, and is kept as a courtesy to users having difficulty with the incompatibility of that latest version.

name: rfc2bib
caption: Generate BibTeX entries for IETF RFCs

descriptions.text:
The script translates an RFC index file from the IETF to a BibTeX file. It is probably GNU gawk-specific.

Please note that this package is now superseded by ietfbibs.

topics.details: derive BibTeX data from resources other than BibTeX libraries

name: rfil
caption: Ruby font installer library

descriptions.text: The Ruby font installer library (RFIL) is another attempt on font installation for TeX fonts. It consists of a set of example programs and several libraries for doing font related tasks, such as read/write tfm, afm, vf and enc files, creating font metrics, doing calculations and the like. The software is all written in Ruby.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: RGB
caption: Tables of RGB colour parameters

descriptions.text: The Linux rgb.txt (distributed as part of X11 distributions) is mechanically converted to a LaTeX file, which has been compiled to make the distribution. For details of the procedure, and sources, see the package’s home page.

name: rgltxdoc
caption: Common code for documentation of the author’s packages

descriptions.text: This package combines several other packages and defines additional macros and environments for documenting LaTeX code. The package mainly serves the purpose of combining the preferences used in the author’s own package documentations. However, others can use the package as well. Compatibility between versions cannot be guaranteed, however.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: ribbonproofs
caption: Drawing ribbon proofs

descriptions.text:
The package provides a way to draw ribbon proofs in LaTeX.

A ribbon proof is a diagrammatic representation of a mathematical proof that a computer program meets its specification. These diagrams are more human-readable, more scalable, and more easily modified than the corresponding textual proofs.

name: richtext
caption: Create rich text strings

descriptions.text:
The richtext package is used to create rich text strings that can, in turn,
     be inserted into the RV (and V) keys of text field. 
     Currently, only the eforms package supports the RV key.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

name: rigidnotation
caption: Typeset vectors and matrices following the RIGID notation

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX macros to easily and concisely typeset vectors and matrices in a flexible way such as to follow the RIGID notation convention. The package enables the user to define custom commands that can then be used in any math-mode environment to efficiently and rigorously typeset the notational elements commonly used in robotics research (and many other fields) for position vectors, rotation matrices, pose matrices, etc.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: rit-fonts
caption: Malayalam fonts by Rachana Institute of Typography (RIT)

copyright.owner: CV Radhakrishnan and Rachana Institute of Typography

descriptions.text:
The RIT font collection provides versions of 17 font families in Malayalam (the language spoken in the southern Indian state of Kerala) script in TrueType and WOFF2 formats. The fonts are:

  • RIT Ala
  • RIT Chingam
  • RIT Ezhuthu
  • RIT Indira
  • RIT Karuna
  • RIT Keralayeeam
  • RIT Keram
  • RIT Kutty
  • RIT Lasya
  • RIT Lekha
  • RIT MeeraNew
  • RIT Panmana
  • RIT Rachana
  • RIT Sundar
  • RIT TN Joy
  • RIT Thaara
  • RIT Uroob

A LaTeX package rit-fonts.sty that will help users to make use of these Unicode-compliant fonts in LaTeX documents with XeTeX or LuaTeX is also provided.

topics.details: fonts for languages of the Indian subcontinent
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: rjlparshap
caption: Support for use of \parshape in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides macros and environments that relieve the programmer of some of the difficulties of using \parshape in LaTeX macros. It does not actually calculate shapes in the way that the shapepar package does.

name: rlepsf
caption: Rewrite labels in EPS graphics

descriptions.text:
A macro package for use with epsf.tex which allows PostScript labels in an Encapsulated PostScript file to be replaced by TeX labels. The package provides commands \relabel (simply replace a PostScript string), \adjustrelabel (replace a PostScript string, with position adjustment), and \extralabel (add a label at given coordinates).

You can, if you so choose, use the facilities of the labelfig package in place of using \extralabel.

name: rmannot
caption: Create rich media annotations in a PDF file

descriptions.text:
The package is part of the AeB Pro family of packages. It creates rich media annotations, in which MOV, MP4, M4V, 3GP, 3G2, and MP3 files can be played.

Rich media annotation is a feature of Acrobat/Adobe Reader version 9. Acrobat Pro and Distiller version 9.0 or later are required to build a document, and Adobe Reader 9.0 or later is needed to activate the annotation and play the media.

topics.details: create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package
convert PostScript to PDF using Adobe Distiller

name: rmathbr
caption: Repeating of math operator at the broken line and the new line in inline equations

descriptions.text: Repeating of math operators at the broken line and the new line in inline equations is used in Cyrillic mathematical typography (Russian for example), but unfortunately LaTeX does not provide such an option. This package solves the problem by extending ideas described in M. I. Grinchuk TeX and Russian Traditions of Typesetting, TUGboat 17(4) (1996) 385 and supports most of LaTeX mathematical packages. See the documentation for details.

name: rmligs
caption: Remove incorrect ligatures in German documents

descriptions.text:
Ligatures, which are a pleasing feature of TeX's use of fonts, should not be placed in German words between the word stem and the rest of the word.

The rmligs package is a perl script that takes input in ISO 8859-1 or -15, UTF-8 or LaTeX-style umlaut encodings ("a, "u, etc.), and inserts a break where an inappropriate ligature would appear. So, for example, Auflage will be changed to Auf"|lage, which typesets in a typographically correct fashion.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: rmpage
caption: A package to help change page layout parameters in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package lets you change page layout parameters in small steps over a range of values using options. It can set \textwidth appropriately for the main fount, and ensure that the text fits inside the printable area of a printer. An rmpage-formatted document can be typeset identically without rmpage after a single cut and paste operation. Local configuration can set defaults: for all documents; and by class, by printer, and by paper size. The geometry package is better if you want to set page layout parameters to particular measurements.

name: rmthm
caption: Use a roman font for theorem statements

descriptions.text:
Modifies the theorem environment of LaTeX 2.09 to cause the statement of a theorem to appear in \rm.

LaTeX2e users should use a more general package (such as ntheorem) to support this requirement.

name: rnototex
caption: Convert from Runoff to LaTeX

descriptions.text: A (Pascal) program to translate (Digital Standard) Runoff into LaTeX. VAX executables for VMS v6.1 are provided.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: Robot Man
caption: A fun demo of AcroTeX eDucation Bundle facilities

descriptions.text: Robot man is distributed as part of the AeB Pro bundle (just for fun); the source is attached to the PDF file.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: robotarm
caption: TikZ powered LaTeX package to draw parameterized 2D robot arms

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package uses TikZ to draw parameterized 2D robot arms, for example to be used in educational material.

name: roboto
caption: Support for the Roboto family of fonts

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the Roboto Sans, Roboto Condensed, Roboto Mono, Roboto Slab and Roboto Serif families of fonts, designed by Christian Robertson and Greg Gazdowicz for Google.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font with adaptations to several languages
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: robust-externalize
caption: Cache anything (TikZ, python, ...) in a robust, efficient and pure way

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX library to cache anything (TikZ, python, ...), in a robust, efficient and pure way. We also provide a template system with placeholders to provide configurable templates.

For more information, see the documentation and the github repository.

name: robustcommand
caption: Declare robust command, with \newcommand checks

descriptions.text: The package merely provides a variation of \DeclareRobustCommand, which checks for the existence of a command before declaring it robust.

name: robustindex
caption: Create index with pagerefs

descriptions.text:
Third parties often change the page numbers without rerunning makeindex. One would like to make the page numbers in the index entries more robust.

This bundle provides robustindex.sty and robustglossary.sty, which use the \pageref mechanism to maintain correct page numbers.

name: rojud
caption: A font with the images of the counties of Romania

descriptions.text:
This package provides a Type 1 font with images of the 42 counties of Romania, constructed using a general method which is described in detail in the documentation.

The package name is an abbreviation of judeţele României (= counties of Romania).

topics.details: fonts designed more for fun than for actual use
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: romanbar
caption: Write roman number with <q>bars</q>

descriptions.text:
Bars, in the present context, are lines above and below text that abut with the text. Barred roman numerals are sometimes found in publications.

The package provides a function that prints barred roman numerals (converting arabic numerals if necessary).

The package also provides a predicate \ifnumeric.

name: romanbarpagenumber
caption: Typesetting roman page numbers

descriptions.text: The package romanbar allows to typeset roman numbers with bars. This package allows you to use those roman numbers as page number.

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

name: romandeadf
caption: Romande ADF fonts and LaTeX support

descriptions.text:
Romande ADF is a serif font family with oldstyle figures, designed as a substitute for Times, Tiffany or Caslon. The family currently includes upright, italic and small-caps shapes in each of regular and demi-bold weights and an italic script in regular. The support package renames the fonts according to the Karl Berry fontname scheme and defines four families. Two of these primarily provide access to the standard or default characters while the alternate families support alternate characters, additional ligatures and the long s. The included package files provide access to these features in LaTeX as explained in the documentation.

The LaTeX support requires the nfssext-cfr and the xkeyval packages.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: romaniantex
caption: LaTeX support for Romanian

descriptions.text: A LaTeX2e package for typesetting Romanian in a plain TeX environment. For LaTeX use, the package has been superseded by the Romanian option of babel.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: romanneg
caption: Roman page numbers negative

descriptions.text: Causes the page numbers in the DVI file (as defined by \count0) to be negative when roman pagenumbering is in effect.

topics.details: control sequence and typesettting of page numbers

name: romannum
caption: Generate roman numerals instead of arabic digits

descriptions.text: The romannum package changes LaTeX generated numbers to be printed with roman numerals instead of arabic digits. It requires the stdclsdv package. Users of the bookhands fonts may find this package useful.

name: rorlink
caption: Create ROR symbols which links to the given ROR-IDs

descriptions.text: This package provides an easy to use command. It takes an URL of the Research Organization Registry (ROR) as argument and creates a ROR symbol which links to the given URL – very similar to the orcidlink package from which it is derived. The symbol itself always fits with the chosen font size.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: rosario
caption: Using the free Rosario fonts with LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package provides the files required to use the Rosario fonts with LaTeX. Rosario is a set of four fonts provided by Héctor Gatti, Adobe Typekit & Omnibus-Type Team under the Open Font License (OFL), version 1.1. The fonts are copyright (c) 2012-2015, Omnibus-Type.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: rotate
caption: Rotate TeX boxes

descriptions.text:
Plain TeX macros to rotate boxes, using \special commands appropriate for dvips.

Users should note that the Plain TeX adaptation of the LaTeX graphics package provides this functionality, with more flexibility as to output capabilities.

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

name: rotate-textures
caption: Box rotation macros for Textures

descriptions.text:
Provides rotation macros specific to the (commercial) Textures distribution.

Modern users are perhaps better advised to use the (LaTeX) graphics package, or generic relatives, such as its Plain graphics adaptation.

name: rotating
caption: Rotation tools, including rotated full-page floats

descriptions.text:
A package built on the standard LaTeX graphics package to perform all the different sorts of rotation one might like, including complete figures and tables with their captions.
