If you want continuous text (i.e., more than one page) set in landscape mode, use the lscape package instead. The rotating packages only deals in rotated boxes (or floats, which are themselves boxes), and boxes always stay on one page.

If you need to use the facilities of the float in the same document, load rotating.sty via rotfloat, which smooths the path between the rotating and float packages.

The package is now part of the latex-graphics bundle, which is one of the collections in the LaTeX required set of packages.

topics.details: rotate typeset objects on their page

name: rotchiffre
caption: Perform simple rotation cyphers

descriptions.text:
The package defines a command \EdefRot that defines a macro (whose name is given as an argument) to the rotation of the given string. Available rotations are ROT13 (for letters), ROT5 (for digits), ROT18 (for digits and letters together) and ROT47 (for all ASCII characters).

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: rotfloat
caption: Rotate floats

descriptions.text: The float package provides commands to define new floats of various styles (plain, boxed, ruled, and userdefined ones); the rotating package provides new environments (sidewaysfigure and sidewaystable) which are rotated by 90 or 270 degrees. But what about new rotated floats, e.g. a rotated ruled one? This package makes this possible; it builds a bridge between the two packages and extends the commands from the float package to define rotated versions of the new floats, too.

name: rotpages
caption: Typeset sets of pages upside-down and backwards

descriptions.text: The rotpages package allows you to format documents where small sets of pages are rotated by 180 degrees and rearranged, so that they can be read by turning the printed copy upside-down. It was developed for collecting exercises and solutions: using the package, you can print the exercise text normally and the solutions rotated.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: rotunda
caption: Rotunda manuscript book-hand font

descriptions.text:
The rotunda and allrtnd packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Rotunda manuscript book-hand used between the 13th and 15th century AD. The font consists of lower- and uppercase letters, and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes
fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: RoueQuestions
caption: Draw a <q>question wheel</q> (roue de questions)

descriptions.text: This package helps to produce a game for students: It is a wheel displaying questions, with hidden answers inside.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: roundbox
caption: Round boxes in LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package implements a command \roundbox that can be used, in LaTeX, for producing boxes, framed with rounded corners.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: roundrect
caption: MetaPost macros for highly configurable rounded rectangles (optionally with text)

descriptions.text: The roundrect macros for MetaPost provide ways to produce rounded rectangles, which may or may not contain a title bar or text (the title bar may itself contain text). They are extremely configurable.

name: rpg-module
caption: Typesetting old-school Dungeons and Dragons modules

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX class for authors of Role-Playing Game adventure modules for Dungeons and Dragons and similar games. The typesetting is reminiscent of the old-school modules published in the early 1980s and attempts to recapture the look and feel of those classic adventures.

The package also includes the Basic Stats style, which contains stat blocks for every monster from the Moldvay/Cook/Marsh Basic/Expert version of the game.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: rpgicons
caption: Icons for tabletop role-playing games

descriptions.text:
This package provides a set of high-quality icons for use in notes for tabletop role-playing games. The icons are meant to be used in the body text, but they can also be used in other contexts such as graphics or diagrams.

The package comes in two variants, one based on the l3draw package, and the other on PGF/TikZ.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: rplain
caption: Redefines the plain pagestyle

descriptions.text: The package redefines the LaTeX pagestyle plain so the page numbers appear on the lower corners. The package was superseded by the fancyhdr package and is no longer supported.

name: rputover
caption: Place text over PSTricks objects without obscuring background colors

descriptions.text:
You create a PSTricks figure with regions filled with various colors. You add some lines over the colors. Now you want to add some labels. You’d like these labels to cover the lines but not the background colors. This style provides a way of doing that.

The package is now superseded by package pst-rputover by the same author and Thomas Söll

topics.details: package using PStricks for graphical output

name: RRGtrees
caption: Linguistic tree diagrams for Role and Reference Grammar (RRG) with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A set of LaTeX macros that makes it easy to produce linguistic tree diagrams suitable for Role and Reference Grammar (RRG). This package allows the construction of trees with crossing lines, as is required by this theory for many languages. There is no known limit on number of tree nodes or levels.

Requires the pst-node and pst-tree LaTeX packages.

name: rsc
caption: BibTeX style for use with RSC journals

descriptions.text: The rsc package provides a BibTeX style in accordance with the requirements of the Royal Society of Chemistry. It was originally based on the file pccp.bst, but also implements a number of styles from the achemso package. The package is now a stub for the chemstyle package, which the author developed to unify the writing of articles with a chemistry content.

name: rsfs
caption: Ralph Smith’s Formal Script font

descriptions.text:
The fonts provide uppercase formal script letters for use as symbols in scientific and mathematical typesetting (in contrast to the informal script fonts such as that used for the calligraphic symbols in the TeX maths symbol font). The fonts are provided as Metafont source, and as derived Adobe Type 1 format.

LaTeX support, for using these fonts in mathematics, is available via one of the packages calrsfs and mathrsfs.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: rsfso
caption: A mathematical calligraphic font based on rsfs

descriptions.text: The package provides virtual fonts and LaTeX support files for mathematical calligraphic fonts based on the rsfs Adobe Type 1 fonts (which must also be present for successful installation, with the slant substantially reduced. The output is quite similar to that from the Adobe Mathematical Pi script font.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: RST
caption: Drawing rhetorical structure analysis diagrams in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package is of interest for people working in linguistics and language technology.

Drawing rhetorical analyses is no fun when you need to change and update diagrams as you refine your work, or, more importantly, if a lot of analyses are to be drawn. Voila, there we go: This package enables us to typeset beautiful diagrams with no hassle. It is oriented towards the style of the diagrams shown in Mann&Thompson's Rhetorical Structure Theory and subsequent works. This package works perfectly with (LaTeX) and pdfLaTeX and does not require any special PostScript capabilities in the output side.

name: rterface
caption: Access to R analysis from within a document

descriptions.text: The package mediates interaction between LaTeX and R; it allows LaTeX to set R’s parameters, and provides code to read R output.

topics.details: typeset reports, diagrams, etc., of statistics
call external code and process the result

name: rtf2latex2e
caption: Convert Rich Text Format (RTF) files to LaTeX2e

descriptions.text: The package converts Rich Text Format (RTF) files to LaTeX2e, saving any image files it finds. Visual formatting, such as ruler positions, tabs, paragraph indentations, etc., is ignored. Users should expect the LaTeX output to need some manual editing; the result is not a reproduction of what you see on the WYSIWYG screen.

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

name: rtf2tex
caption: Convert RTF to TeX

descriptions.text: A translator that uses an existing RTF reader, to produce TeX source (not LaTeX).

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

name: rtkinenc
caption: Input encoding with fallback procedures

descriptions.text:
The rtkinenc package is functionally similar to the standard LaTeX package inputenc: both set up active characters so that an input character outside the range of 7-bit visible ASCII is converted into one or more corresponding LaTeX commands. The main difference lies in that rtkinenc allows the user to specify a fallback procedure to use when the text command corresponding to some input character isn't available.

Names of commands in rtkinenc have been selected so that it can read inputenc encoding definition files, and the aim is that rtkinenc should be backwards compatible with inputenc. rtkinenc is not a new version of inputenc though, nor is it part of standard LaTeX.

For an example of how rtkinenc is used, the user may look at the tclldoc class.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: rtklage
caption: Make suit details for German courts

descriptions.text: Provides support for lawsuits in German courts, based on Koma script classes.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: rtsched
caption: Draw Real-Time scheduling (GANTT) charts

descriptions.text:
The package offers facilities for drawing GANTT charts (chronograms). Such charts may be used as real-time timing diagrams, often needed for preparing articles, lectures and presentations in Real-Time Scheduling research.

The package relies on packages PSTricks and multido.

name: rub-kunstgeschichte
caption: A class for the art history institute at Ruhr University Bochum

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class implementing the guidelines on scientific writing of the art history institute (Kunstgeschichtliches Institut) at Ruhr University Bochum.

name: rubik
caption: Document Rubik cube configurations and rotation sequences

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides four packages:

  • rubikcube provides commands for typesetting Rubik cubes and their transformations,
  • rubiktwocube provides commands for typesetting Rubik twocubes and their transformations,
  • rubikrotation which can process a sequence of Rubik rotation moves, with the help of a Perl package executed via \write18 (shell escape) commands, and
  • rubikpatterns, a collection of well known patterns and their associated rotation sequences.

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: rubikcube
caption: Typeset Rubik cubes and move notation

descriptions.text:
The package provides LaTeX commands and macros for typesetting Rubik cube (3x3x3) notation, configurations, and rotation sequences, using the TikZ graphic language.

The package serves as part of the rubik bundle.

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: rubikrotation
caption: Processes a sequence of Rubik rotations

descriptions.text: The package is part of the rubik bundle, serving as an extension of the rubikcube package, providing the \RubikRotation command to process a sequence of Rubik rotation moves on-the-fly (using the external Perl script rubikrotation.pl), and to return the new Rubik cube state.

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: rubiktwocube
caption: Typeset Rubik TwoCubes and move notation

descriptions.text:
The package provides LaTeX commands and macros for typesetting Rubik TwoCube (2x2x2) notation, configurations, and rotation sequences, using the TikZ graphic language.

The package serves as part of the rubik bundle.

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: ruhyphen
caption: Russian hyphenation

descriptions.text: A collection of Russian hyphenation patterns supporting a number of Cyrillic font encodings, including T2, UCY (Omega Unicode Cyrillic), LCY, LWN (OT2), and koi8-r.

name: rule-d
caption: Provide LaTeX3 commands for typesetting rules

descriptions.text:
The package provides rule commands in a structure appropriate for use in LaTeX3 documents.

The package is distributed as part of the GS1 distribution.

name: ruled-tables
caption: Plain TeX table macros, with ruled capability

descriptions.text: These are still further developments of the fabled Plain TeX tables macros, but are substantially rewritten from the original.

name: ruler
caption: A typographic ruler for TeX

descriptions.text: The file processes to produce (real) rulers; the author suggests printing them on transparent plastic and trimming for use as a real ruler. The rule widths are 0.05mm, which can be challenging for (old) laser printers.

name: rulerbox
caption: Draw rulers around a box

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX package for drawing rulers around a box. This might be useful when showing the absolute size of something in electronic documents, or designating the relative scale in printed materials.

name: rulercompass
caption: A TikZ library for straight-edge and compass diagrams

descriptions.text: The package defines some commands and styles to support drawing straight-edge and compass diagrams with TikZ.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: runcode
caption: Execute foreign source code and embed the result in the pdf file

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package executes programming source codes (including all command line tools) from within LaTeX and embeds the output in the resulting .pdf file. Many programming languages can be easily used and any command-line executable can be invoked when preparing the .pdf file from a .tex file.

It is however recommended to use this package in server-mode together with the Python talk2stat package. Currently, this server-mode supports Julia, MatLab, Python, and R. More languages will be added. For more details and usage examples, refer to the package’s github repository.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: rune
caption: Two rune fonts

descriptions.text: This (seemingly very old) bundle contains two (apparently) working fonts, rune and srune (the latter has added Saxon runes); the fonts are distributed as Metafont source. There is no documentation available.

name: runic
caption: Fonts for Anglo-Saxon futharc script

descriptions.text: Fonts and macros for runic writing. The futharks script remained in use in England until just after printing was established. This is one of a series of archaic fonts.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

name: runtex
caption: Windows program to run TeX variant and various utils as needed

descriptions.text: A Win32 program(me) that tries to guess the number of times – if you neglected to tell it how often – [pdf][e][La]TeX should be executed and which other utilities-currently makeindex, xindy, MetaPost, Metafont, and BibTeX – if at all are run after the first TeX run. You can ask it to delete temporary files if nothing went wrong.

name: runtexfile
caption: Automate the process of compiling (La)TeX documents with index, bibliography, …

descriptions.text:
This package provides a small script like latexmk to run a TeX or LaTeX document controlled from within the document itself. The commands have to be defined at the beginning of the document, e.g.: 

      %! HV lualatex --shell-escape
      %! HV biber
      %! HV lualatex --shell-escape 
      %! HV xindex 
      %! HV xindex --config DIN2 -l DE -o test2.vwd 
      %! HV xindex --config DIN2 -l DE -o test2.dbd 
      %! HV lualatex --shell-escape 
      %! HV lualatex --shell-escape 
      
      \documentclass[...]{...} 
      …

The script itself does not parse the log file.

name: runtexshebang
caption: A Lua script running LaTeX document files with TeX-style shebang

descriptions.text:
In short, a TeX-style shebang (%#!) is a special kind of TeX comment that you include in your TeX/LaTeX document file to tell the operating system’s shell how to run the file for the rest of the file: 

      %#!lualatex foo.tex
      \documentclass{article}
      \begin{document}
        Hello, {\LaTeX} World!

        Happy {\TeX}ing.
      \end{document}

If you are using a TeX-style shebang, it must appear on the line that matched 20 lines or less in your LaTeX document, and it has to start with a TeX comment symbol (%) followed by a hash sign (#) and an exclamation mark (!), colloquially known as the bang, hence the name shebang for TeX/LaTeX.

name: ruscap
caption: A Metafont for rustic capitals

descriptions.text: This package contains the source for ruscap: a font for rustic capitals – an ancient Roman calligraphic script – created with Metafont.

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

name: russ
caption: LaTeX in Russian, without babel

descriptions.text:
The package aims to facilitate Russian typesetting (based on input using MicroSoft Code Page 1251). Russian hyphenation is selected, and various mathematical commands are set up in Russian style.

Furthermore all Cyrillic letters’ catcodes are set to letter, so that commands with Cyrillic letters in their names may be defined.

name: russian-help
caption: LaTeX help in Russian

name: rustic
caption: Roman Rustic manuscript book-hand font

descriptions.text:
The rustic and allrust packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Rustic manuscript book-hand used between the 1st and 6th century AD. The font consists of majuscules only, with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: rutitlepage
caption: Radboud University Titlepage Package

descriptions.text:
This is an unofficial LaTeX package to generate titlepages for the Radboud University, Nijmegen. It uses official vector logos from the university.

This package requires the following other LaTeX packages: geometry, graphicx, ifpdf, keyval, iflang, and, optionally, babel-dutch.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: rviewport
caption: Relative Viewport for Graphics Inclusion

descriptions.text:
Package graphicx provides a useful keyword viewport which allows to show just a part of an image. However, one needs to put there the actual coordinates of the viewport window. Sometimes it is useful to have relative coordinates as fractions of natural size. For example, one may want to print a large image on a spread, putting a half on a verso page, and another half on the next recto page. For this one would need a viewport occupying exactly one half of the file's bounding box, whatever the actual width of the image may be.

This package adds a new keyword rviewport to the graphicx package specifying Relative Viewport for graphics inclusion: a window defined by the given fractions of the natural width and height of the image.

name: rvwrite
caption: Increase the number of available output streams in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package addresses, for LaTeX documents, the severe limitation on the number of output streams that TeX provides.

The package uses a single TeX output stream, and writes marked-up output to this stream. The user may then post-process the marked-up output file, using LaTeX, and the document’s output appears as separate files, according to the calls made to the package.

The output to be post-processed uses macros from the widely-available ProTeX package.

name: rwth-ci
caption: LaTeX templates using CI of RWTH Aachen University

descriptions.text: The RWTH-CI-Bundle is the official LaTeX bundle of RWTH Aachen University to use their Corporate Identity within LaTeX.

name: ryersonSGSThesis
caption: Ryerson School of Graduate Studies thesis template

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class and template files for Ryerson School of Graduate Studies (SGS) theses.

name: ryethesis
caption: Class for Ryerson University Graduate School requirements

descriptions.text: The class offers support for formatting a thesis, dissertation or project according to Ryerson University’s School of Graduate Studies thesis formatting regulations.

name: s2latex
caption: A scribe to LaTeX converter

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
The program is written in C, and a Win32 port is provided.

The patchfile s2latex.patch provides a port to ANSI C and cleans up the Makefile.

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

name: sa-tikz
caption: TikZ library to draw switching architectures

descriptions.text: The package provides a library that offers an easy way to draw switching architectures and to customize their aspect.

name: sacsymb
caption: <q>Sacred Symbols</q> prepared with TikZ

descriptions.text: The author tells us: This is a package with symbols prepared with TikZ. These symbols are the variables used in the space of the collapse of the wave function of a quantum field associated with the micro-tubule while exploring an Orchestrated, objective reduction (Orch OR) theory of consciousness as applied to the three brains model of psychological experience.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: sae
caption: Typeset an SAE technical paper

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: This class provides correct formatting according to the requirements of an SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers) Technical Paper. It should be useful for authors whose papers have a high mathematical content.

name: saferef
caption: Safer references through strong typing of references

descriptions.text:
Provides a means of expressing typed references (as it were) within a document.

The package typedref offers an improvement of this package.

name: sageep
caption: Format papers for the annual meeting of EEGS

descriptions.text: The class provides formatting for papers for the annual meeting of the Environmental and Engineering Geophysical Society (EEGS) (Application of Geophysics to Engineering and Environmental Problems, known as SAGEEP).

name: SageTeX
caption: Embed Sage code and plots into LaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text: SageTeX allows you to embed code, the results of computations, plots, and graphics from the Sage mathematics software suite into LaTeX documents. It is similar in spirit to Literate Haskell and lhs2TeX.

topics.details: call external code and process the result

name: sam2p
caption: Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF

descriptions.text:
Sam2p is a UNIX command line utility written in ANSI C++ that converts many raster (bitmap) image formats into Adobe PostScript or PDF files and several other formats. The images are not vectorized. sam2p gives full control to the user to specify standards-compliance, compression, and bit depths. In some cases sam2p can compress an image 100 times smaller than the PostScript output of many other common image converters. Sam2p provides ZIP, RLE and LZW (de)compression filters even on output destined for PostScript Level 1 devices.

The author provides a script bundle, a2ping, that uses sam2p as part of a generic format conversion mechanism.

name: samples
caption: Samples of Plain TeX coding

descriptions.text: A collection of code samples that may prove useful.

topics.details: code that serves as examples of TeX programming

name: sanhyph
caption: Sanskrit hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text:
These patterns define hyphenation of Unicode input of Sanskrit and Prakrit in Devanagari, Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam and Telugu scripts.

The patterns are structured for use with XeTeX.

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: sanitize-umlaut
caption: Sanitize umlauts for MakeIndex and pdfLaTeX

copyright.owner: Prof. Dr. Dr. Thomas F. Sturm

descriptions.text:
This package sanitizes umlauts to be used directly in index entries for MakeIndex and friends with pdfLaTeX.

This means that inside \index an umlaut can be used as "U or as Ü. In both cases, the letter is written as "U into the raw index file for correct processing with MakeIndex and pdfLaTeX.

topics.details: adaptation of existing packages to UTF-8 input

name: sankey
caption: Draw Sankey diagrams with TikZ

descriptions.text: This package provides macros and an environment for creating Sankey diagrams, i.e. flow diagrams in which the width of the arrows is proportional to the flow rate.

name: sans
caption: Exchange Roman and Sans faces in a document

descriptions.text: Set the document with Computer Modern Sans as its Roman font, and Roman as its Sans font.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: sanskrit
caption: Sanskrit support

descriptions.text: A font and pre-processor suitable for the production of documents written in Sanskrit. Type 1 versions of the fonts are available.

documentation.details: Short introduction and Quick Start Guide

topics.details: support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: sanskrit-t1
caption: Type 1 version of <q>skt</q> fonts for Sanskrit

descriptions.text: The sanskrit-t1 font package provides Type 1 version of Charles Wikner’s skt font series for the Sanskrit language.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
support for languages of the Indian subcontinent

name: sansmath
caption: Maths in a sans font

descriptions.text: The package defines a new math version sans, and a command \sansmath that behaves somewhat like \boldmath.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: sansmathaccent
caption: Correct placement of accents in sans-serif maths

descriptions.text:
Sans serif maths (produced by the beamer class or the sfmath package) often has accents positioned incorrectly.

This package fixes the positioning of such accents when the default font (cmssi) is used for sans serif maths.

It will have no effect if used in a document that does not use the beamer class or the sfmath package.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: sansmathfonts
caption: Extended Computer Modern sans serif fonts

descriptions.text: Sans serif small caps and math fonts for use with Computer Modern.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: sapthesis
caption: Typeset theses for Sapienza-University, Rome

descriptions.text: The class will typeset Ph.D., Master, and Bachelor theses that adhere to the publishing guidelines of the Sapienza University of Rome.

name: sarabian
caption: Archaic South Arabian script font

descriptions.text:
The sarabian bundle provides PostScript Type 1 fonts for the South Arabian script which was in use for about 1000 years from roughly 600BC. The original glyphs were the work of Alan Stanier.

This is one of a series of fonts reproducing ancient scripts.

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: SASnRdisplay
caption: Typeset SAS or R code or output

descriptions.text:
The SASnRdisplay package serves as a front-end to listings, which permits statisticians and others to import source code and the results of their calculations or simulations into LaTeX projects.

The package is also capable of overloading the Sweave User Manual and SASweave packages.

topics.details: typeset reports, diagrams, etc., of statistics

name: sauerj
caption: A bundle of utilities by Jonathan Sauer

descriptions.text:
The bundle consists of:

  • a tool for collecting text for later re-use,
  • a tool for typesetting the "meta-information" within a text,
  • a tool for use in constructing macros with multiple optional parameters,
  • a package for multiple column parallel texts,
  • a tool for processing key-value structured lists, and
  • macros for typesetting a number as a German-language string.

name: sauter
caption: Wide range of design sizes for CM fonts

descriptions.text:
Extensions, originally to the CM fonts, providing a parameterization scheme to build Metafont fonts at true design sizes, for a large range of sizes.

The scheme has now been extended to a range of other fonts, including the AMS fonts, bbm, bbold, rsfs and wasy fonts.

name: sauterfonts
caption: Use Sauter’s fonts in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides font definition files (plus a replacement for the package exscale) to access many of the fonts in Sauter’s collection. These fonts are available in all point sizes and look nicer for such intermediate document sizes as 11pt.

Also included is the package sbbm, an alternative to access the bbm fonts.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: saveenv
caption: Save environment content verbatim

descriptions.text: This package provides tools to create your own verbatim environments, and works for all values of \endlinechar.

name: savefnmark
caption: Save name of the footnote mark for reuse

descriptions.text: Sometimes the same footnote applies to more than one location in a table. With this package the mark of a footnote can be saved into a name, and re-used subsequently without creating another footnote at the bottom.

name: savesym
caption: Redefine symbols where names conflict

descriptions.text: There are a number of symbols (e.g., \Square) that are defined by several packages. In order to typeset all the variants in a document, we have to give the glyph a unique name. To do that, we define \savesymbol{XXX}, which renames a symbol from \XXX to \origXXX, and \restoresymbols{yyy}{XXX}, which renames \origXXX back to \XXX and defines a new command, \yyyXXX, which corresponds to the most recently loaded version of \XXX.

name: savetrees
caption: Optimise the use of each page of a LaTeX document

descriptions.text:
The goal of the savetrees package is to pack as much text as possible onto each page of a LaTeX document. Admittedly, this makes the document far less attractive. Nevertheless, savetrees is a simple way to save paper when printing draft copies of a document. It can also be useful when trying to meet a tight page-length requirement for a conference or journal submission.

Most of the package options cover specific modifications to typesetting rules, but there are also options subtle, moderate and extreme options for the broad brush approach.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: sblarticle
caption: A LaTeX class for SBL style articles and papers

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class for producing articles and papers conforming to the style required by the Society of Biblical Literature. It depends on sblfonts for language support and biblatex-sbl for referencing.

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments
typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

name: sblbook
caption: A LaTeX class for SBL style print ready books

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class for producing print ready books conforming to the style required by the Society of Biblical Literature. It depends on sblfonts for language support, biblatex-sbl for referencing, sblidx for indexing and biblatex-sbl for Scripture references.

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

name: sblfonts
caption: Font and language set up for SBL style documents

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX package for setting up font and language support for documents conforming to the requirements of the Society of Biblical Literature. Greek and Hebrew languages are supported using the SBL fonts. If these fonts are not available then fonts included with TeX Live are used.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language
support is for a font not available on CTAN
typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: sblidx
caption: A LaTeX package for SBL style indices

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX package for creating indices in line with the requirements of the Society of Biblical Literature. Indices for ancient sources (via biblatex-sbl), modern authors (via biblatex-sbl) and subjects are supported. Number ranges are compressed and indexed items in notes are indicated using n. and nn.

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

name: sblreport
caption: A LaTeX class for SBL style theses

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class for producing theses conforming to the style required by the Society of Biblical Literature. It depends on sblfonts for language support and biblatex-sbl for referencing.

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

name: sbtex
caption: A compact TeX distribution for MS-DOS

descriptions.text: The distribution includes a small editor (te), but no auxiliary files.

name: sc21
caption: Title page for the old ISO TC97/SC21 committee

descriptions.text: A variant of the standard LaTeX 2.09 titlepage package, designed for N-numbered papers for the committee. (The committee covered, at various times, standardisation of OSI architecture, OSI upper layers, distributed processing, databases and graphics.)

name: sc21-wg1
caption: Title page for the old ISO TC97/SC21/WG1 working group

descriptions.text: A variant of the standard LaTeX 2.09 titlepage package, designed for N-numbered papers for the group. (The group covered, at various times, standardisation of OSI architecture, developments of the OSI model and distributed processing.)

name: scale
caption: Scale document by sqrt(2) or magstep(2)

descriptions.text: A package to scale a document by sqrt(2) (or by \magstep{2}). This is useful if you are preparing a document on, for example, A5 paper and want to print on A4 paper to achieve a better resolution.

name: scalebar
caption: Create scalebars for maps, diagrams or photos

descriptions.text: This is a small package to create scalebars for maps, diagrams or photos. It was designed for use with cave maps but can be used for anything from showing a scalebar in kilometres for topographic maps to a scalebar in micrometres for an electron microscope image.

name: scalefnt
caption: Rescale fonts to arbitrary sizes

descriptions.text:
\scalefont{2} selects the current font in twice the current size. \scalefont{.75} reduces the current font size by three quarters.

Note that the effectiveness of such operations depends on the LaTeX font selection for that font; it will typically work well for ordinary Type 1 fonts, but Metafont fonts are usually set up to work only at a discrete set of sizes.

The package is distributed as part of the carlisle bundle.

name: scalerel
caption: Constrained scaling and stretching of objects

descriptions.text:
The package provides four commands for vertically scaling and stretching objects. Its primary function is the ability to scale/stretch and shift one object to conform to the size of a specified second object. This feature can be useful in both equations and schematic diagrams.

Additionally, the scaling and stretching commands offer constraints on maximum width and/or minimum aspect ratio, which are often used to preserve legibility or for the sake of general appearance.

name: scaletextbullet
caption: Resize the \textbullet without changing its vertical center

descriptions.text: This package enables the user to resize the \textbullet without moving its vertical center. This process is not fully automated – the user must use \settextbulletfactor to set the \textbullet factor to the correct value to display the resized \textbullet at the correct height.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for miscellaneous fonts (not on CTAN)

name: scanpages
caption: Support importing and embellishing scanned documents

descriptions.text: The bundle provides support for the process of creating documents based on pre-TeX-era material that is available as scanned pages, only.

name: schedule
caption: Weekly schedules

descriptions.text: Automatically format weekly schedules using LaTeX’s picture environment. It requires the packages calc and color. Its main feature is the accuracy with which appointments are represented: boxes drawn to represent a particular appointment are accurate to the minute – i.e., a 31-minute appointment will have a box 1/30th longer than a 30-minute appointment. A number of features are included to allow the user to customize the output.

name: schedule209
caption: Typeset schedules

descriptions.text: The package implements a document style which enables the user to construct diagrams showing the planned progress of projects, etc. This package seems unrelated to the schedule package written for use with LaTeX 2e. The two packages provide very similar facilities, but the present package’s use of PostScript features (for shading schedule entry backgrounds) is entirely ad hoc.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: schemabloc
caption: Draw block diagrams, using TikZ

descriptions.text:
The package provides a set of macros for constructing block diagrams, using TikZ.

(The blox package is an English translation of this package.)

name: schemata
caption: Print topical diagrams

descriptions.text: The package facilitates the creation of topical schemata, i.e. outlines that use braces (or facsimiles thereof) to illustrate the breakdown of concepts and categories in Scholastic thought from late medieval and early modern periods.

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians
macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: schemeTeX
caption: Typesetting Scheme programs with LaTeX

descriptions.text: A sort of literate programming mechanism for Scheme. Prettily formats documentation and comments, leaving the Scheme code unchanged.

name: schemeweb
caption: Simple support for literate programming in Lisp

descriptions.text: SchemeWEB is a Unix filter that allows you to generate both Lisp and LaTeX code from one source file. The generated LaTeX code formats Lisp programs in typewriter font obeying the spacing in the source file. Comments may include arbitrary LaTeX commands. SchemeWEB was originally developed for the Scheme dialect of Lisp, but it can easily be used with most other dialects.

name: schola-otf
caption: Using the OpenType fonts TeX Gyre schola

descriptions.text:
This package can only be used with LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX. It does the font setting for the OpenType font TeX Gyre Schola for text and math.

The missing typefaces like bold math and slanted text are also defined

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: scholatex
caption: A tag-based language for print-ready teaching worksheets, built on LuaLaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: scholatex is a LuaLaTeX document class for teachers who need print-ready worksheets without writing LaTeX. The author writes a single .tex file in a compact, readable tag language; the class translates it to LaTeX at compile time and produces output of full LaTeX quality.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: ScholaX
caption: Extension of TeXGyreSchola (New Century Schoolbook) with math support

descriptions.text:
This package contains an extension of TeXGyreSchola with extensive superiors, inferior figures, upright punctuation glyphs added to the Italic face for a theorem font, plus slanted and bold slanted faces.

Math support is provided by one of two options to newtxmath, one of which uses an adaptation of the fourier math Greek letters.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: schooldocs
caption: Various layout styles for school documents

descriptions.text: The aim of this package is to offer diverse layout styles for school-related documents. It serves well in creating exercise sheets, exams, course materials. The package sets the page geometry (dimensions of text and margins) and the title formatting. Various styles are available defining settings for headers, footers or alternative title formatting, providing many customizable features.

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: schule
caption: Support for teachers at German schools

copyright.owner: Johannes Pieper, André Hilbig, Johannes Kuhaupt,                     Daniel Spittank, Ludger Humbert, Adrian Salamon

descriptions.text:
The schule bundle was built to provide packages and commands that could be useful for documents in German schools. At the moment its main focus lies on documents for informatics as a school subject. An extension for physics is currently in progress. Extensions for other subjects are welcome.

For the time being, the whole package splits up into individual packages for informatics (including syntax diagrams, Nassi–Shneiderman diagrams, sequence diagrams, object diagrams, and class diagrams) as well as classes for written exams (tests, quizzes, teaching observations, information sheets, worksheets, and answer keys).

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: schulmathematik
caption: Commands and document classes for German-speaking teachers of mathematics and physics

descriptions.text: The schulmathematik bundle provides two LaTeX packages and six document classes for German-speaking teachers of mathematics and physics.

topics.details: support for teachers and teaching administrators

name: schulschriften
caption: German <q>school scripts</q> from Suetterlin to the present day

descriptions.text: Das Paket enthält im wesentlichen die Metafont-Quelldatein für die folgenden Schulausgangsschriften: Suetterlinschrift, Deutsche Normalschrift, Lateinische Ausgangsschrift, Schulausgangsschrift, Vereinfachte Ausgangsschrift. Damit ist es möglich, beliebige deutsche Texte in diesen Schreibschriften zu schreiben.

name: schwalbe-chess
caption: Typeset the German chess magazine <q>Die Schwalbe</q>

descriptions.text: The package is based on chess-problem-diagrams, which in its turn has a dependency on the bartel-chess-fonts.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: schwell
caption: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting in Schwell style

descriptions.text: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting in a variation of the Sütterlin handwriting, invented by Ludwig Sütterlin, a German teacher and typographer.

name: scientific-thesis-cover
caption: Provides cover page and affirmation at the end of a thesis

descriptions.text: Institutions require a cover page and an affirmation at the end of a thesis. This package provides both.

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

name: scientificauthor
caption: Visual LaTeX editor

descriptions.text: Scientific Author is a visual LaTeX editor for mathematicians, scientists and engineers, supporting industry standards like LaTeX 2e. It is a visual document editor, which exports LaTeX for rendering by tools such as MiKTeX. Scientific Author also supports editing of mathematical notation through tool palettes and templates. LaTeX symbols are also supported, including American Mathematical Society symbols. It also enables easy editing of tables, footnotes, and margin notes.

topics.details: editor designed (or adapted) for use with (La)TeX

name: scientificpaper
caption: Format a scientific paper for journal publication

name: scientificviewer
caption: MacKichan software viewer

descriptions.text:
Scientific Viewer allows the user to read or print documents created with MacKichan Scientific Notebook, Scientific Word or Scientific Workplace; it may also be used to view many native LaTeX documents.

The viewer does not enable the user to manipulate the document in any way.

topics.details: application for viewing a typeset document on screen

name: SciKGTeX
caption: Mark research contributions in scientific documents and embed them in PDF metadata

descriptions.text: Scientific Knowledge Graph TeX (SciKgTeX) is a LuaLaTeX package which makes it possible to annotate specific research contributions in scientific documents. SciKGTeX will enrich the document by adding the marked contributions to PDF metadata in a structured XMP format which can be picked up by search engines and knowledge graphs.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: sciposter
caption: Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger

descriptions.text:
This collection of files contains LaTeX packages for posters of ISO A3 size and larger (ISO A0 is the default size). American paper sizes and custom paper are supported. In particular, sciposter.cls defines a document class which allows cutting and pasting most of an article to a poster without any editing (save reducing the size) – see the manual.

Sciposter does work for LaTeX, not just pdfLaTeX. However, xdvi produces strange results, though a recent version of dvips does create good ps-files from the dvi files.

Also note that logos must either be put in the current working directory or in the directories of your LaTeX distribution. For some reason graphicspath settings are ignored.

name: SciWordConv
caption: Use Scientific Word/WorkPlace files with another TeX

descriptions.text: These macros allows you to combine the power of the graphical front-end of Scientific Word/Scientific WorkPlace (SW/SWP) with one's own favourite TeX compiler (for example, MiKTeX). Currently includes support for Russian language; other languages can be handled easily.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: sclang-prettifier
caption: Prettyprinting SuperCollider source code

descriptions.text: Built on top of the listings package, the package allows effortless prettyprinting of SuperCollider source code in documents typeset with LaTeX & friends.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: scmac
caption: Typeset scripts with Plain TeX

name: scontents
caption: Stores LaTeX contents in memory or files

descriptions.text: This package stores valid LaTeX code in memory (sequences) using the l3seq module of expl3. The stored content (including verbatim) can be used as many times as desired in the document, additionally can be written to external files if desired.

name: scorecard
caption: Format a Baseball scorecard

descriptions.text: Formats a scorecard with which to score a baseball game, with additional space to record information with which to submit a details to newspapers, league offices, etc. Also provides boxes for other summary statistics.

topics.details: typeset cards for business, filing, etc.

name: Scrabble
caption: Commands for Scrabble boards

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands (in English and in French) to work with a Scrabble Board :

  • \ScrabbleBoard and \begin{EnvScrabble} and \ScrabblePutWord for the English version,
  • \PlateauScrabble and \begin{EnvScrabble} and \ScrabblePlaceMot for the French version.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: scraddr
caption: Provide data from scrlttr2’s address files

descriptions.text: The package is a part of the Koma-Script suite. The package uses adr-files to generate circular letters. The package provides commands to read the adr-files and to use the data of the address entries, not only with scrlttr2 class and not only for circular letters.

topics.details: lists of addresses, for a personal directory (or the like)

name: scrambledenvs
caption: Create and print scrambled environments

descriptions.text:
This package allows you to create and print scrambled environments for purposes such as randomized hint environments. You can mark a location with a series of hints, and then print the hints at the end in a pseudo-random order.

The general structure follows: there is an outer environment which creates the label, an inner environment that creates the references, and a print command that prints out all of the hints.

This generalizes beyond hints; one can create scrambled solutions as well, etc.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: scrartcl
caption: KOMA-Script article class

descriptions.text:
The class provides the article -like element of the koma-script collection.

The document layout of the class is less strident than that of article, and it offers much more flexibility than article via other elements of the koma-script collection.

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: scratch
caption: Draw programs like <q>scratch</q>

descriptions.text:
This package is now obsolete. From now on, scratch at scratch.mit.edu is now version3 with a new design. Please, use the scratch3 package to draw blocks with the new design.

This package permits to draw program charts in the style of the scatch project (scratch.mit.edu).

It depends on the other LaTeX packages TikZ and simplekv.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: scratch3
caption: Draw programs like <q>scratch</q>

descriptions.text:
This package permits to draw program charts in the style of the scatch project (scratch.mit.edu).

It depends on the other LaTeX packages TikZ and simplekv.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: ScratchX
caption: Include Scratch programs in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package can be used to include every kind of Scratch program in LaTeX documents. This may be particularly useful for Math Teachers and IT specialists.

The package depends on the following other LaTeX packages: calc, fp, ifsym, multido, tikz, xargs, and xstring.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: scrbase
caption: Provide basic features for KOMA-Script

descriptions.text:
The package is part of the KOMA-Script suite; it provides some basic functions used by KOMA-Script, that may also be useful to authors and users of other classes and packages.

Most notably, the package provides conditionals and an extended key=value handling mechanism that may be used for run-time options of classes and packages. Several packages of a family may share options and all the options of one family may be changed with a single command.

name: scrbook
caption: KOMA-Script book class

descriptions.text:
The class provides the book -like element of the koma-script collection.

The document layout of the class is more calm than that of book, and it offers much more flexibility than book via other elements of the koma-script collection.

name: scrdate
caption: Calendar date operations

descriptions.text: The package provides several operations with calender dates, such as to show the century or the decade of a year, calculate the day of the week of a given calender date, show the current calender date in ISO form. The package offers support for output in several languages.

name: screen
caption: Prepare a document for a simple previewer

descriptions.text: A small package designed to set geometry to prepare a (LaTeX 2.09) document for viewing with something like crudetype.

name: screenplay
caption: A class file to typeset screenplays

descriptions.text: The class implements the format recommended by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

name: screenplay-pkg
caption: Package version of the screenplay document class

descriptions.text:
This package implements the tools of the screenplay document class in the form of a package so that screenplay fragments can be included within another document class.

For full documentation of the available commands, please consult the screenplay class documentation in addition to the included package documentation.

name: screenwriter
caption: Write film and television screenplays

descriptions.text: This class provides a LaTeX document class for writing film and television screenplays. It is based on screenplay, but updated for current LaTeX distributions and extended with a modular language system and better integration with babel.

name: scrextend
caption: Use of components of KOMA-Script by other packages

descriptions.text: The package makes some features of the KOMA-Script classes available for other classes, e.g., for the standard classes.

topics.details: export features from a class for use elsewhere

name: scrhack
caption: Compatibility package to emulate the former KOMA-Script package scrhack

descriptions.text: Up to version 3.41, the scrhack package was part of KOMA-Script. It was originally intended to improve the compatibility of third-party packages with KOMA-Script. However, most of the so-called hacks also added additional functionality to the corresponding third-party package. On the other hand, it was sometimes urgent to react to a change in such a third-party package, which was difficult to do from within a large collection like KOMA-Script. Therefore, the scrhack part of KOMA-Script was split into several independent packages. And the scrhack spin-off was made to emulate the former KOMA-Script package of the same name.

topics.details: correct a problem, ahead of the “proper” fix

name: scrindex
caption: Make index package work with KOMA-Script classes

descriptions.text:
This package redefines environment `theindex' of package `index', if a class from KOMA-Script is loaded. Also option `idxtotoc' is supported. Index preambles can be given either by means of package `index' or via the interface provided by KOMA-Script.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: script
caption: Variant report and book styles

descriptions.text: A jiffy conversion to LaTeX2e of some old document styles.

name: script-font
caption: Handwriting font

descriptions.text: A font that resembles the author’s handwriting, distributed as Metafont source.

name: scriptfonts
caption: A summary of mathematical script fonts for LaTeX users

descriptions.text:
A development, with examples, of an answer in the UK TeX FAQ, showing the fonts generally available to the user of LaTeX.

The source isn't readily compilable, but contains notes on how it should be compiled.

name: ScriptTeX
caption: Macros for scripts and screenplays

descriptions.text: ScriptTeX provides Plain TeX macros to support both Screenplays and Stage Plays.

name: scripture
caption: A LaTeX style for typesetting Bible quotations

descriptions.text: The scripture package provides a set of macros for typesetting quotations from the Bible. It provides many features commonly seen in Bibles such as dropped text for chapter numbers, superscripts for verse numbers, indented lines for poetry sections, narrow sections and hanging paragraphs. A reference for the quotation can optionally be added.

topics.details: typeset devotional texts and other material of interest to theologians

name: scrjrnl
caption: Typeset diaries or journals

descriptions.text: A class, based on scrbook, designed for typesetting diaries, journals or devotionals.

name: scrjura
caption: KOMA-Script support for lawyers, etc

descriptions.text:
The package is part of the Koma-Script bundle. It provides environments for contracts, laws, acts or other legal purposes. It features support for automatic numbering of paragraphs, and semi-automatic numbering of sentences.

Support is offered for both German and English texts.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: scrlayer
caption: Manage text layers within KOMA-Script

descriptions.text: The package is part of the koma-script bundle, and provides control of background and foreground layers for a page style description.

name: scrlayer-fancyhdr
caption: Combining fancyhdr with KOMA-Script’s scrlayer

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package uses KOMA-Script’s scrlayer to redefine the page styles of package fancyhdr. This allows the combination of features of fancyhdr with features of scrlayer.

Before KOMA-Script v3.33 scrlayer-fancyhdr was part of KOMA-Script itself.

name: scrlayer-notecolumn
caption: Control note columns parallel to the main text

descriptions.text:
The package provides an end user interface to define and manage note columns, above scrlayer.

The note columns provide similar facilities to those of the LaTeX \marginpar command, extending them to more than a single column. The package provides page breaks inside note columns, and synchronisation between the main text and note columns.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: scrlayer-scrpage
caption: Define and manage page styles

descriptions.text: This package is the part of the Koma-Script bundle that provides an end user interface to scrlayer, allowing the user to define and manage page styles by controlling page headers and footers. The end user interface is compatible enough to that of the earlier scrpage2 package, so that users should easily be able to switch from the older package to the newer, more powerful, one.

name: scrletter
caption: Letter extension to KOMA-Script classes

descriptions.text:
Used in conjunction with one of the KOMA-Script (scrartcl, scrreprt, scrbook) or standard classes (article, report, book), this package provides the features of the letter class scrlttr2.

The package is part of the Koma-Script bundle.

name: scrlfile
caption: Installation control for KOMA-Script packages

descriptions.text:
The package provides hooks for the execution of commands before or after loading files, classes or packages. The package can also

  • execute commands after loading files, classes or packages,
  • prevent a package from being loaded, and
  • schedule the execution of commands before or after closing the .aux file at \end{document}

The package is part of the Koma-Script bundle.

topics.details: support for managing packages within documents

name: scrlttr2
caption: KOMA-Script letter class

descriptions.text:
The class was designed from scratch as a replacement for the standard LaTeX letter class.

Its interface is (basically) a key-value mechanism, with a wide range of parameters that define the basic layout of the letter.

name: scrlttr2copy
caption: A letter class option file for the automatic creation of copies

descriptions.text:
The file copy.lco provides the new class option copy for the KOMA-Script letter class scrlttr2.

If the option copy is given, all pages of a specific letter are duplicated with background text marking as copies.

name: scrpage2
caption: Control of page headers and footers in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package was designed to ease integration into documents using the Koma-Script suite. It incorporates a set of predefined, configurable page styles.

As of 2015, the author considers this package as obsolete and recommends using its successor scrlayer-scrpage instead.

name: scrreprt
caption: KOMA-Script report class

descriptions.text:
The class provides the report -like element of the Koma-Script collection.

The document layout of the class is more calm than that of report, and it offers much more flexibility than report via other elements of the Koma-Script collection.

name: scrtime
caption: Show the time of a LaTeX run

descriptions.text: The package provides time information for the current LaTeX run.

name: scrwfile
caption: Use LaTeX .aux file in place of \newrite files

descriptions.text: The package provides a means of sending all LaTeX \newrite, table of contents, and other miscellaneous output via the LaTeX .aux file. The mechanism subverts the mechanism of \newrite, and means there will never be a No room for new \write message.

name: scsnowman
caption: Snowman variants using TikZ

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides a command \scsnowman which can display many variants of snowman (yukidaruma in Japanese).

TikZ is required for drawing these snowmen.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: scyrillic
caption: A family of cyrillic fonts

descriptions.text: This family (distributed as Metafont source) provides a basic set of cyrillic glyphs, in an encoding that (apparently) only this family uses.

topics.details: fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts

name: sdaps
caption: LaTeX support files for SDAPS

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains LaTeX classes and packages to create machine readable questionnaires. Metadata is generated for the whole document and it is possible to process created forms fully automatically using the SDAPS main program.

Features include:

  • PDF Form generation
  • Advanced array-like layout
    • Can flow over multiple pages and repeats the header automatically
    • Optional document wide alignment of array environments
    • Has complex layout features like rotating the headers to safe space
    • Ability to exchange rows and columns on the fly
  • Different question types:
    • Freeform text
    • Single/multiple choice questions
    • Range questions
  • Layouting questions in rows or columns
  • Possibility to pre-fill questionnaires from LaTeX

topics.details: typeset tables that may be too big for a page
create pdf form fields, use form fields as an integral part of the package

name: sdrt
caption: Macros for Segmented Discourse Representation Theory

descriptions.text: The package provides macros to produce the Box notation of SDRT (and DRT), to draw trees representing discourse relations, and finally to have an easy access to various mathematical symbols used in that theory, mostly with automatic mathematics mode, so they work the same in formulae and in text.

name: sduthesis
caption: Thesis Template of Shandong University

descriptions.text: Thesis Template of Shandong University.

name: se2thesis
caption: A Thesis Class for the Chair of Software Engineering II at the University of Passau, Germany

descriptions.text: The se2thesis bundle provides a document class for writing a theses with the Chair of Software Engineering II at the University of Passau, Germany. The class is based on Markus Kohm’s KOMA-Script classes and provides several additions and customizations to these classes. While the class provides some basic settings, mostly regrading the type area, fonts, and the title page, it still provides large degrees of freedom to its users. However, the package’s documentation also provides recommendations regarding several aspects, for example, recommending BibLaTeX for bibliographies.

name: seatingchart
caption: Generation of seating charts

descriptions.text: This package enables the visualization of seating charts, whereby the seating layouts (i.e. the arrangement of seats in a room) and the seating scheme (i.e. the selection and labeling of occupied seats) can be controlled independently of each other.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: secdot
caption: Section numbers with trailing dots

descriptions.text: Makes the numbers of \section commands come out with a trailing dot. Includes a command whereby the same can be made to happen with other sectioning commands.

name: seceqn
caption: Number theorems by section

descriptions.text: The package formats equation numbers with a section number prefix, with the number itself reset for each section.

name: secnum
caption: A macro to format section numbering intuitively

descriptions.text:
This package provides a macro \setsecnum to format section numbering intuitively.

\setsecnum{1.1.1} will set the section numbering format to arabic.arabic.arabic and the depth to 3.

The package uses LaTeX3.

name: secret
caption: Put security classification marks in a document

descriptions.text:
The package puts a mark in the margin at the start of each paragraph, and at the top of a page when a paragraph runs over onto a new page.

The marks are programmed by commands \unclassified (mark (U)), \confidential (mark (C)), or \secret (mark (S)). The command \nosecret switches off marking.

name: secretx
caption: Put security classification marks in a document

descriptions.text: This package provides a set of macros for marking paragraphs in a document with a leading string and modifying the header and the footer of each page. It includes environmentS for marking large sections of text and environments for boxing figures and tables. This is the spiritual successor to secret.sty but adds the feature of marking the header and the footer correctly.

name: section
caption: Modifying section commands in LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package implements a pretty extensive scheme to make more manageable the business of configuring LaTeX output.

name: sectionbox
caption: Create fancy boxed ((sub)sub)sections

descriptions.text: Sectionbox is a LaTeX package for putting fancy colored boxes around sections, subsections, and subsubsections, especially for use in posters, etc. It was designed with the sciposter class in mind, and certainly works with that class and with derived classes.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: sectionbreak
caption: LaTeX support for section breaks

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX support for section breaks, used mainly in fiction books to signal changes in a story, like changes in time, location, etc. It supports the asterism symbol, text content, or custom macros as the section break mark symbol.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: sectsty
caption: Control sectional headers

descriptions.text: A LaTeX2e package to help change the style of any or all of LaTeX's sectional headers in the article, book, or report classes. Examples include the addition of rules above or below a section title.

name: seealso
caption: Improve the performance of \see macros with makeindex

descriptions.text: The package amends the \see and \seealso macros that are used in building indexes with makeindex, to deal with repetitions, and to ensure page numbers are present in the actual index entries.

name: sehyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for Swedish

name: selectp
caption: Select pages to be output

descriptions.text:
Defines a command \outputonly, whose argument is a list of pages to be output. With the command present (before \begin{document}), only those pages are output.

This package was inspired by code published by Knuth in TUGboat 8(2) (July 1987).

topics.details: select pages to be output, etc.

name: selectpage
caption: Select pages to be output from a document

descriptions.text:
Requires a file of page numbers, which specifies the numbers of pages to print (in generated order).

The code was published in TUGboat 8(2) (July 1987).

topics.details: select pages to be output, etc.

name: selinput
caption: Semi-automatic detection of input encoding

descriptions.text: This package selects the input encoding by specifying pairs of input characters and their glyph names.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: selnolig
caption: Selectively disable typographic ligatures

descriptions.text:
The package suppresses typographic ligatures selectively, i.e., based on predefined search patterns. The search patterns focus on ligatures deemed inappropriate because they span morpheme boundaries. For example, the word shelfful, which is mentioned in the TeXbook as a word for which the ff ligature might be inappropriate, is automatically typeset as shelf\/ful rather than as shel{ff}ul.

For English and German language documents, the package provides extensive rules for the selective suppression of so-called common ligatures. These comprise the ff, fi, fl, ffi, and ffl ligatures as well as the ft and fft ligatures. Other f-ligatures, such as fb, fh, fj and fk, are suppressed globally, while exceptions are made for names and words of non-English/German origin, such as Kafka and fjord.

For English language documents, the package further provides ligature suppression macros for a number of so-called discretionary or rare ligatures such as ct, st, and sp.

The package requires use of a recent LuaLaTeX format (for example those from TeX Live 2012 or 2013, or MiKTeX 2.9).

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
support for variations of typographic style

name: SemanTeX
caption: Semantic, keyval-based mathematics

descriptions.text:
The SemanTeX package for LaTeX delivers a more semantic, systematized way of writing mathematics, compared to the classical math syntax in LaTeX. The system uses keyval syntax, and the user can define their own keys and customize the system down to the last detail. At the same time, care has been taken to make the syntax as simple, natural, practical, and lightweight as possible.

Furthermore, the package has a companion package, called stripsemantex, which allows you to completely strip your documents of SemanTeX markup to prepare them e.g. for publication.

The package is still in beta, but is considered feature-complete and more or less stable, so using it at this point should be safe. Still, suggestions, ideas, and bug reports are more than welcome!

name: semantic
caption: Help for writing programming language semantics

descriptions.text: Eases the typesetting of notation of semantics and compilers. Includes T-diagrams, various derivation symbols and inference trees.

name: semantic-markup
caption: Meaningful semantic markup in the spirit of the Text Encoding Initiative

descriptions.text:
The package provides simple commands to allow authors (especially scholars in the humanities) to write with a focus on content rather than presentation. The commands are inspired by the XML elements of the Text Encoding Initiative. Commands like \term and \foreign are aliases for \emph. \quoted and \soCalled are aliases for quoting commands. These commands could be easily redefined for different formats.

The package also provides a footnote environment so that long footnotes can be more cleanly separated from the main text.

Because the author is a music scholar, the package also includes some macros for musical symbols and other basic notations for musical analysis.

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: semaphor
caption: Semaphore alphabet font

descriptions.text: These fonts represent semaphore in a highly schematic, but very clear, fashion. The fonts are provided as Metafont source, and in both OpenType and Adobe Type 1 formats.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts with specific small application areas

name: semesterplanner
caption: Create beautiful semester timetables and more

descriptions.text:
This package defines several useful environments for a beautiful printable semester plan. It includes a timetable (which is using the schedule-Package) as well as appointments, deadlines, and exams.

The package requires color, TikZ, schedule, and fontawesome. Furthermore, documents need to be compiled with LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: semesterplannerLua
caption: Draw timetables and other organizational matters useful for planning a semester

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package provides commands to print timetables, lists of appointments and exams. Also it is possible to draw calendars of specified ranges (and mark dates which were previously listed). Drawing the timetable is based on TikZ, which makes it very flexible.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: seminar
caption: Make overhead slides

descriptions.text:
A class that produces overhead slides (transparencies), with many facilities. The class requires availability of the fancybox package.

Seminar is also the basis of other classes, such as prosper. In fact, seminar is not nowadays reckoned a good basis for a presentation – users are advised to use more recent classes such as powerdot or beamer, both of which are tuned to 21st-century presentation styles.

Note that the seminar distribution relies on the xcomment package, which was once part of the bundle, but now has a separate existence.

name: semioneside
caption: Put only special contents on left-hand pages in two sided layout

descriptions.text: This package supports the preparation of semi one sided documents. That is, two sided documents, where all text is output on right-hand pages, as in one-sided documents – and only special contents are output on left-hand pages on user request, e.g., floating objects.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: semproc
caption: Seminar proceedings

descriptions.text:
The package provides functionality for typesetting seminar proceedings based on KOMA-Script's scrreprt class and etoc. It offers an alternative to \chapter that typesets the speaker and if necessary the typist of the notes for the talk in question.

Moreover, the class provides two types of table of contents. A global table of contents showing only the talks of the seminar and the respective speakers and a local table of contents for each talk showing the sections and subsections of the respective talk.

name: SemTeX
caption: Deals with stripped SemanTeX documents

descriptions.text:
This package is a small LaTeX package that adds a collection of simple macros for parentheses and bullets. It exists for one purpose only: To be loaded by documents which were originally typeset using the package SemanTeX, but which have been stripped of SemanTeX markup using the package stripsemantex which is part of SemanTeX. Therefore, unless your document is one of those, simply don't use this package.

And even if your document is one of those, there is a good chance you will not have to load it after all. In most cases, you will be able to replace the macros it provides by macros from other packages.

name: semtrans
caption: Transliteration of semitic languages

descriptions.text: A small set of commands to assist in transliterating languages such as Arabic, Hebrew and the Ethiopian languages.

name: sentences
caption: Numbered lists for sentences

descriptions.text:
The package defines sentences and subsentences list environments, whose entries may be referenced by number.

The package requires the maybeload and redefine packages.

name: sepfootnotes
caption: Support footnotes and endnotes from separate files

descriptions.text: The package supports footnotes and endnotes from separate files. This is achieved with commands \sepfootnotecontent and \sepfootnote; the former defines the content of a note, while the latter typesets that note.

name: sepnum
caption: Print numbers in a <q>friendly</q> format

descriptions.text: Provides a command to print a number with (potentially different) separators every three digits in the parts either side of the decimal point (the point itself is also configurable). The macro is fully expandable and not fragile (unless one of the separators is). There is also a command \sepnumform, that may be used when defining \the<counter> macros.

name: seqcalc
caption: A package for declarative sequent-calculus proofs

descriptions.text: This package provides a structured wrapper around the bussproofspackage. It provides a declarative interface for sequent calculus proofs, including rule declaration, rule application, formula normalization, shortcuts, and optional standard rule sets. The goal is to simplify the construction of proof trees while keeping the underlying bussproofs layout untouched.

name: seqsplit
caption: Split long sequences of characters in a neutral way

descriptions.text:
When one needs to type long sequences of letters (such as in base-sequences in genes) or of numbers (such as calculations of transcendental numbers), there's no obvious break points to be found. The package provides a command \seqsplit, which makes its argument splittable anywhere, and then leaves the TeX paragraph-maker to do the splitting.

While the package may obviously be used to typeset DNA sequences, the user may consider the dnaseq as a rather more powerful alternative.

name: serbian-apostrophe
caption: Commands for Serbian words with apostrophes

descriptions.text: The package provides a collection of commands (whose names are Serbian words) whose expansion is the Serbian word with appropriate apostrophes.

documentation.details: List of word commands and their expansion

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: serbian-book
caption: Support for use of memoir in Serbian

descriptions.text: The package provides a number of commands for adjusting memoir output to Serbian style.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: serbian-date-lat
caption: Updated date typesetting for Serbian

descriptions.text: Babel defines dates for Serbian texts, in Latin script. The style it uses does not match current practices. The present package defines a \date command that solves the problem.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: serbian-def-cyr
caption: Serbian cyrillic localization

descriptions.text: This package provides abstract, chapter, title, date etc, for serbian language in cyrillic scripts in T2A encoding and cp1251 code pages.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: serbian-lig
caption: Control ligatures in Serbian

descriptions.text: The package suppresses fi and fl (and other ligatures) in Serbian text written using Roman script.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: serbianpart
caption: Redefines \thepart to be used in Roman lettered Serbian

descriptions.text: The package redefines \thepart, to produce PART <alphabetical version of the number>, in Roman lettered Serbian.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Serbian

name: serial
caption: Generate serial letters

descriptions.text: The serial package provides a wrapper to the KOMA Script letter class scrlettr for the generation of serial letters. It contains different interfaces to data base generated adress files. Additionally, a configuration file allows easy customization of the letterheads etc. Requires scrlettr.cls from KOMA-Script and the following are recommended: inputenc, textmerg, delimtxt.

name: sesamanuel
caption: Class and package for sesamath books or paper

descriptions.text: The package contains a sesamanuel class which could be used to compose a student's classroom book with LaTeX, and also a sesamanuelTIKZ style to be used for TikZ pictures in the sesamath book.

name: sesstime
caption: Session and timing information in lecture notes
