font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font with adaptations to several languages

name: theapa
caption: APA (American Psychology Association) Reference Citation for LaTeX

descriptions.text: Certainly related to the same author’s newapa citation package, but the actual relationship isn’t entirely clear.

topics.details: support for typesetting texts relating to psychology
typesetting according to the rules of the American Psychological Association

name: theatre
caption: A sophisticated package for typesetting stage plays

descriptions.text: This package enables the user to typeset stage plays in a way that permits to create highly customized printouts for each actor.

name: thematicpuzzle
caption: Horizontal banners in a puzzle style

descriptions.text: With this package it is possible to create a horizontal banner in the form of a puzzle. There are some predefined themes.

name: theorem
caption: Manipulate theorem environments

descriptions.text:
Enhancements to LaTeX’s theorem environments, giving more choice in theorem layout. This package is no longer recommended by its author; he suggests users should use the AMS LaTeX amsthm package instead; another widely-used alternative is ntheorem.

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: theoremref
caption: References with automatic theorem names

descriptions.text:
The theoremref package provides variants of the \label and \ref commands for theorem-like environments, capable of automatically typesetting references including the theorem name (apart from the theorem number).

The scheme is particularly valuable if the author decides to change a lemma to a proposition or a theorem (or whatever).

name: thepdfnumber
caption: Print PDF numbers with minimal digits

descriptions.text:
The package provides a command (\thepdfnumber) that converts its argument to a canonical form. Conversion strips all leading and trailing zeros (but leaves a leading zero if 0<arg<1); it also strips + signs, and removes pairs of - signs.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: thermodynamics
caption: Macros for multicomponent thermodynamics documents

descriptions.text:
This package makes typesetting quantities found in thermodynamics texts relatively simple. The commands are flexible and intended to be relatively intuitive. It handles several sets of notation for total, specific, and molar quantities; allows changes between symbols (e.g., A vs. F for Helmholtz free energy); and greatly simplifies the typesetting of symbols and partial derivatives commonly encountered in mixture thermodynamics. Changes of one’s notes from one textbook to another can be achieved relatively easily by changing package options.

The package offers a collection of macros and environments which are intended to make typesetting thermodynamics documents faster, more convenient, and more reliable. Macros include symbols for extensive, molar, specific, and partial molar properties; excess and residual (departure) properties; partial derivatives; heat capacities, compressibilities, and expansivities; saturation, mixture, and pure-component properties; Henry’s Law parameters and activity coefficients; changes on mixing, fusion, reaction, sublimation, and vaporization; and sets of all moles/mole fractions/masses/etc. being held constant in derivatives. Conversion of notes between textbooks is trivial for textbooks supported by the package, and more general changes in notation are also possible through package options.

name: these
caption: Bibliography style for French theses

descriptions.text: The style is derived from the standard alpha.bst, with keywords translated and styles converted to French conventions.

name: thesis
caption: Typeset thesis

descriptions.text: Two classes (thesis and thema) developed from the report class for a more European and a more flexible look. The thesis class supports options like noindent, noitemization, headline, nocenter, crosshair, and chapterbib; thema adds facilities such as separately credited authors for each chapter.

name: thesis-ekf
caption: Thesis class for Eszterházy Károly Catholic University

descriptions.text: This bundle provides a LaTeX class for theses and dissertations at Eszterházy Károly Catholic University (Eger, Hungary). The documentation is written in Hungarian.

name: thesis-gwu
caption: Thesis class for George Washington University School of Engineering and Applied Science

descriptions.text:
This class is an attempt to create a standard format for GWU SEAS dissertations/theses.

It automatically handles many of the complicated formatting requirements and includes many useful packages.

An example thesis is provided serving as a user guide and a demonstration of the thesis.

name: thesis-qom
caption: Thesis style of the University of Qom, Iran

descriptions.text:
This package provides a class file for writing theses and dissertations according to the University of Qom Graduate Schools’s guidelines for the electronic submission of master theses and PhD dissertations. The class should meet all the current requirements and is updated whenever the university guidelines change.

The class needs XeLaTeX in conjunction with the following fonts: XB Niloofar, IranNastaliq, IRlotus, XB Zar, XB Titre, and Yas.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: thesis-titlepage-fhac
caption: Little style to create a standard titlepage for diploma thesis

descriptions.text: Yet another thesis titlepage style: support of Fachhochschule Aachen (Standort Juelich)

name: thinsp
caption: A stretchable \thinspace for LaTeX

descriptions.text: The package redefines \thinspace to have a stretch component.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: thirteen
caption: Print dates of Friday 13th days

descriptions.text: The (plain TeX) file prints the dates of Friday 13th days, from 1991–2003. (This was an exercise for beginner programmers in the 1960s…)

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: thmbox
caption: Decorate theorem statements

descriptions.text: The package defines an environment thmbox that presents theorems, definitions and similar objects in boxes decorated with frames and various aesthetic features. The standard macro \newtheorem may be redefined to use the environment.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: thmlist
caption: A LaTeX package for adding theorem environments quickly

descriptions.text:
This package provides a simple way for adding theorem environments quickly. Welcome to feedback bugs or ideas via email to xiamyphys@gmail.com.

The package has been superseded by whatsnote.

name: thmtools
caption: Extensions to theorem environments

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides several packages for commonly-needed support for typesetting theorems. The packages should work with kernel theorems (theorems out of the box with LaTeX), and the theorem and amsthm packages.

Features of the bundle include:

  • a key-value interface to \newtheorem;
  • a \listoftheorems command;
  • hyperref and autoref compatibility;
  • a mechanism for restating entire theorems in a single macro call.

name: thorshammer
caption: Assessment based on AcroTeX quizzes

descriptions.text:
This package implements an idea by Thorsten G. for assessment using PDF quizzes produced by the exerquiz package. Thorsten not only wanted to pose multiple choice, multiple selection, and fill-in type questions, but also wanted to ask extended response questions that would be manually evaluated. Once the quiz is graded, the instructor may optionally pass the quizzes through an Acrobat action sequence to extract the student’s name and grade from the quizzes. The extracted information is saved to a tab-delimited TXT file. The instructor can later merge this file into a larger spreadsheet.

WARNING: Adobe Acrobat DC or Adobe Acrobat XI is required for post PDF-creation. Any PDF-creator application is supported.

name: threadcol
caption: Organize document columns into PDF <q>article thread</q>

descriptions.text:
The package combines a document’s columns into a PDF article thread. PDF readers that support this mechanism (probably Adobe Acrobat/Reader only) can be instructed to scroll automatically from column to column, which facilitates on-screen reading of two-column documents.

Even for single-column documents, threadcol supports the creation of multiple article threads, which help organize discontiguous but logically related regions of text into a form that the user can scroll through as if its contents were contiguous.

name: threecol
caption: Three-column newsletter output

descriptions.text: The code, developed from an example in the TeXbook, provides a simple three-column output routine for Plain TeX.

topics.details: more than one column on the page

name: threecolumn
caption: LaTeX output in three columns

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text:
An extension to the LaTeX 2.09 output routine that allows three (equal width) column output.

Three-column output does not permit multi-column floats, and there are problems switching from three- to one- or two-column setting. (Users should be aware that the package may not work with a current LaTeX kernel.)

topics.details: more than one column on the page
package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: threeddice
caption: Create images of dice with one, two, or three faces showing, using MetaPost

descriptions.text: The package provides MetaPost code to create all possible symmetrical views (up to rotation) of a right-handed die. Configuration is possible by editing the source code, following the guidance in the documentation.

name: 3DLDF
caption: Three-dimensional drawing with MetaPost output

descriptions.text: GNU 3DLDF is a software package for three-dimensional drawing with MetaPost and Metafont output. The program 3dldf implements an interactive language similar to the Metafont and MetaPost languages.

name: threeparttable
caption: Tables with captions and notes all the same width

descriptions.text: Provides a scheme for tables that have a structured note section, after the caption. This scheme provides an answer to the old problem of putting footnotes in tables – by making footnotes entirely unnecessary. Note that a threeparttable is not a float of itself; but you can place it in a table or a table* environment, if necessary.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: threeparttablex
caption: Notes in longtables

descriptions.text: The package provides the functionality of the threeparttable package to tables created using the longtable package.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: thrmappendix
caption: Theorems, lemmas, etc., in appendix

descriptions.text: An implementation of theorems, lemmas, etc., that permits them to be repeated, with their proofs, in an appendix.

name: thsmc
caption: Metrics and LaTeX support for Sans Mono Condensed Font

descriptions.text: This package provides metric files and LaTeX support for The Sans Mono Condensed Family designed by Lucas de Groot, 1996. It has everything you need to typeset in this font – except the font itself, of course.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: thuaslogos
caption: Logos for The Hague University of Applied Sciences (THUAS)

copyright.owner: Jesse E. J. op den Brouw

descriptions.text: This package contains some logos of The Hague University of Applied Sciences (THUAS). These Logos are available in English and in Dutch. They are rendered via PGF.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: thubeamer
caption: A beamer theme for Tsinghua University

descriptions.text: This package provides a beamer theme designed for Tsinghua University.

name: thucoursework
caption: Coursework template for Tsinghua University

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX package for students of Tsinghua University to write coursework more efficiently. It can also be used by students from other universities.

Note that the package itself does not import the ctex package; to use it with Chinese writing, see example file ithw.tex for details.

name: thumb
caption: Thumb marks in documents

descriptions.text: Place thumb marks in books, manuals and reference maunals.

name: thumbpdf
caption: Thumbnails for pdfTeX and dvips/ps2pdf

descriptions.text: A Perl script that provides support for thumbnails in pdfTeX and dvips/ps2pdf. The script uses ghostscript to generate the thumbnails which get represented in a TeX readable file that is read by the package thumbpdf.sty to automatically include the thumbnails. This arrangement works with both plain TeX and LaTeX.

name: thumbs
caption: Create thumb indexes

descriptions.text: The package puts running, customizable thumb marks in the outer margin, moving downward as the chapter number (or whatever shall be marked by the thumb marks) increases. Additionally an overview page/table of thumb marks can be added automatically, which gives the names of the thumbed objects, the page where the object/thumb mark first appears, and the thumb mark itself at its correct position. The thumb marks are useful for large documents (such as reference guides, anthologies, etc.), where a quick and easy way to find (for example) a chapter is needed.

name: thumby
caption: Create thumb indexes for printed books

descriptions.text:
The package can generate thumb indexes for your document. It features printing thumb indexes on one- or two-sided pages, along with background- and foreground-color selection and full LaTeX styling of the chapter numbers in the thumb indexes. The height of each thumb index is automatically chosen based on the number of chapters in your document, while the width is chosen by the user.

The package is designed to work with the memoir class, and also requires PerlTeX and tikz/

name: thuthesis
caption: Thesis template for Tsinghua University

descriptions.text: This package establishes a simple and easy-to-use LaTeX template for Tsinghua dissertations, including general undergraduate research papers, masters theses, doctoral dissertations, and postdoctoral reports.

name: tib
caption: A bibliographic preprocessor

descriptions.text: Tib is a collection of four programs for making citations and reference lists in TeX documents. The main program, Tib, operates on a TeX file with incomplete or keyed citations, looks up the reference in a database, makes the complete citation and on command, makes a list of the references. The citations in the source document are enclosed in (non-TeX) escape characters which Tib recognizes. The output of Tib is another TeX file with complete citations and reference list formatted with a number of TeX control sequences and with definitions for these control sequences, ready to be processed by Plain TeX, LaTeX, or whatever.

name: tibetan
caption: An early LaTeX Tibetan package

descriptions.text: Provides a preprocessor (tfilt) and examples of using two Tibetan fonts. The fonts themselves are only provided as TFM and 300dpi PK files.

name: ticket
caption: Make labels, visiting-cards, pins with LaTeX

descriptions.text: Provides an easy to handle interface to produce visiting cards, labels for your files, stickers, pins and other stuff for your office, conferences etc. All you need is a definition of your ticket included in a ticket definition file and the two commands \ticketdefault and \ticket.

topics.details: typeset sets of labels (for cutting out, etc.)

name: ticollege
caption: Graphical representation of keys on a standard scientific calculator

descriptions.text: This package provides commands to draw scientific calculator keys with the help of TikZ. It also provides commands to draw the content of screens and of menu items.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: tictactoe
caption: Drawing tic-tac-toe or Noughts and Crosses games

descriptions.text: This package which provides commands for drawing grids for the game known variously as tic-tac-toe (and variants), Noughts and Crosses, Naughts and Crosses, Xs and Os, and so on.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: tidyres
caption: Create formal resumes easily

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package aims to provide users with a simple interface to create multi-column formal resumes.

name: tie
caption: Allow multiple web change files

descriptions.text: Tie was originally developed to allow web programmers to apply more than one change file to their source. The program may also be used to create a new version of a .web file that incorporates existing changes.

name: tiet-question-paper
caption: A LaTeX question paper class for the TIET

descriptions.text:
This package provides a LaTeX document class tiet-question-paper.cls in order to create question papers for the Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technologie (TIET).

Although created for the TIET, the module is easily adaptable to any organisation.

name: tif2eps
caption: A PostScript program for converting TIFF files to EPS

descriptions.text: TIF2EPS is a PostScript program for the conversion of TIFF files (ver. 6.0) to EPS ones. Compression (LZW, CCITT Fax, RLE, Flate, DCT) and ASCII85 encoding is available. The package can be used to generate colour-separated EPS files, EPS thumbnails, and small header EPS files that contain only a pointer to a source TIFF file. Employing Ghostscript guarantees portability and efficient processing.

name: tiff
caption: The tiff graphics package

name: tikz-3dplot
caption: Coordinate transformation styles for 3d plotting in TikZ

descriptions.text: The package provides straightforward ways to define three-dimensional coordinate frames through which to plot in TikZ. The user can specify the orientation of the main coordinate frame, and use standard TikZ commands and coordinates to render their tikzfigure. A secondary coordinate frame is provided to allow rotations and translations with respect to the main coordinate frame. In addition, the package can also handle plotting user-specified functions in spherical polar coordinates, where both the radius and fill color can be expressed as parametric functions of polar angles.

name: tikz-among-us
caption: Create some AmongUs characters in TikZ environments

descriptions.text: This package recreates some AmongUs characters in TikZ environments. Some interesting uses alongside other packages are also supported.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: TikZ-Bagua
caption: Draw Bagua symbols in Yijing

descriptions.text:
This package provides commands for drawing symbols in Yijing (I Ching) or Zhouyi using TikZ. There is no need for extra special fonts for showing these symbols.

The package relies on TikZ, bitset, xintexpr, xparse, and xstring.

name: tikz-bayesnet
caption: Draw Bayesian networks, graphical models and directed factor graphs

descriptions.text: The package provides a library supporting the display of Bayesian networks, graphical models and (directed) factor graphs in LaTeX.

topics.details: typeset reports, diagrams, etc., of statistics

name: tikz-bbox
caption: Precise determination of bounding boxes in TikZ

descriptions.text: The built-in determination of the bounding box in TikZ is not entirely accurate. This is because, for Bezier curves, it is the smallest box that contains all control points, which is in general larger than the box that just contains the curve. This library determines the exact bounding box of the curve.

name: tikz-bpmn
caption: A TikZ library for creating BPMN models

descriptions.text: This package provides primitives for drawing Business Process Modelling and Notation (BPMN) models. It includes tasks, subprocesses, events, task markers and gateways. The symbols aim to follow the BPMN standard as closely as possible. Please refer to the documentation for further information.

name: tikz-catan
caption: Draw Settlers of Catan board states with TikZ

descriptions.text: The package draws board states of The Settlers of Catan in LaTeX documents: full boards with resources, number tokens, ports, pieces, and the robber, plus silhouette, probability, and highlight views. Boards are declared as data and rendered through swappable callbacks. The only dependency is TikZ.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: tikz-cd
caption: Create commutative diagrams with TikZ

descriptions.text: The general-purpose drawing package TikZ can be used to typeset commutative diagrams and other kinds of mathematical pictures, generating high-quality results. The purpose of this package is to make the process of creation of such diagrams easier by providing a convenient set of macros and reasonable default settings. This package also includes an arrow tip library that match closely the arrows present in the Computer Modern typeface.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: tikz-chemlab
caption: A TikZ-based reimplementation for drawing chemical laboratory glassware

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros for drawing a variety of devices used mainly for chemical applications. Since most of these devices have a standardised design, tikz-chemlab spares you the trouble of having to create them manually. All basic objects are included in the file tikz-chemlabObj.tex and are loaded during the start of the package.

tikz-chemlab works with any LaTeX engine that supports TikZ. No PostScript dependency. No latex → dvips → ps2pdf pipeline needed.

This is a TikZ port of pst-labo (v2.07, 2025/07/15) by Denis Girou, Christophe Jorssen, Manuel Luque, and Herbert Voß. The port uses English command names with the tkz prefix instead of the original French pst names, and all option keys have been translated to English.

name: tikz-cookingsymbols
caption: Draw cooking symbols

descriptions.text: The package uses TikZ for drawing cooking symbols like top heat, airfryer and so on. The commands are provided in English and German. The size of the symbol is based on the font size and grabbed with \settoheight and \settodepth.

name: tikz-decofonts
caption: Simple decoration fonts, made with TikZ, for short texts

descriptions.text:
Some simple decoration fonts made with TikZ, for short texts:

  • paint brush;
  • ink brush;
  • pixelart brush;
  • bicolor texts;
  • surround or underline effect;
  • block of letters texts.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: tikz-dependency
caption: A library for drawing dependency graphs

descriptions.text:
The package provides a library that draws together existing TikZ facilities to make a comfortable environment for drawing dependency graphs.

Basic facilities of the package include a lot of styling facilities, to let you personalize the look and feel of the graphs.

name: tikz-dimline
caption: Technical dimension lines using PGF/TikZ

descriptions.text:
tikz-dimline helps drawing technical dimension lines in TikZ picture environments.

Its usage is similar to some contributions posted on stackexchange.

name: tikz-ext
caption: A collection of libraries for PGF/TikZ

descriptions.text:
This is a collection of PGF and TikZ libraries which were developed in response to questions on tex.stackexchange.com or texwelt.de.

These libraries can be loaded by either \usepgflibrary or \usetikzlibrary.

name: TikZ-FeynHand
caption: Feynman diagrams with TikZ

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This package lets you draw Feynman diagrams using TikZ.

It is a low-end modification of the TikZ-Feynman package, one of whose principal advantages is the automatic generation of diagrams, for which it needs LuaTeX. TikZ-FeynHand only provides the manual mode and hence runs in LaTeX without any reference to LuaTeX.

In addition it provides some new styles for vertices and propagators, alternative shorter keywords in addition to TikZ-Feynman’s longer ones, some shortcut commands for quickly customizing the diagrams’ look, and the new feature of putting one propagator “on top“ of another.

It also includes a quick user guide for getting started, with many examples and a 5-minute introduction to TikZ.

name: tikz-feynman
caption: Feynman diagrams with TikZ

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX package allowing Feynman diagrams to be easily generated within LaTeX with minimal user instructions and without the need of external programs. It builds upon the TikZ package and leverages the graph placement algorithms from TikZ in order to automate the placement of many vertices. tikz-feynman allows fine-tuned placement of vertices so that even complex diagrams can still be generated with ease.

topics.details: package will use LuaTeX facilities if available

name: tikz-imagelabels
caption: Put labels on images using TikZ

descriptions.text: This package allows to add label texts to an existing image with the aid of TikZ. This may be used to label certain features in an image.

name: tikz-inet
caption: Draw interaction nets with TikZ

descriptions.text: The package extends TikZ with macros to draw interaction nets.

name: tikz-kalender
caption: A LaTeX based calendar using TikZ

descriptions.text:
For usage see the example files tikz-kalender-example1.tex, tikz-kalender-example2.tex, tikz-kalender-example3.tex, and *.events. The Code is inspired by this document and is subject to the »Creative Commons attribution license (CC-BY-SA)«.

The class tikz-kalender requires the package TikZ and the TikZ libraries calc and calendar.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: tikz-karnaugh
caption: Typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ

descriptions.text:
The tikz-karnaugh package is a LaTeX package used to draw Karnaugh maps. It uses TikZ to produce high quality graph from 1 to 12 variables, but this upper limit depends on the TeX memory usage and can be different for you. It is very good for presentation since TikZ allows for a better control over the final appearance of the map. You can control colour, styles and distances.

It can be considered as an upgrade and extension of Andreas W. Wieland's karnaugh package towards TikZ supporting. Upgrade because uses TikZ for more option on typesetting and overall higher quality. Extension because it also supports American style and inputting the values as they would appear in the map or in the truth table. Complex maps with solution (implicants) pointed out can be generated with external java software (see documentation for details).

It supports both American and traditional (simplified labels) styles and from version 1.3 on American style is natively supported, therefore, no more addition work is required to typeset Gray coded labels, variable names etc. From version 1.4, two new macros allow typesetting a map much more similarly as it should appear. Original order, as the values appear in the truth table, still being supported.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: tikz-ladder
caption: Draw ladder diagrams using TikZ

descriptions.text: The tikz-ladder package contains a collection of symbols for typesetting ladder diagrams (PLC program) in agreement with the international standard IEC-61131-3/2013. It includes blocks (for representing functions and function blocks) besides contacts and coils. It extends the circuit library of TikZ and allows you to draw a ladder diagram in the same way as you would draw any other circuit.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: tikz-lake-fig
caption: Schematic diagrams of lakes

descriptions.text: This package contains a collection of schematic diagrams of lakes for use in LaTeX documents. Diagrams include representations of material budgets, fluxes, and connectivity arrangements.

name: tikz-layers
caption: TikZ provides graphical layers on TikZ: <q>behind</q>, <q>above</q> and <q>glass</q>

descriptions.text:
TikZ-layers is a tiny package that provides, along side background, typical graphical layers on TikZ: behind, above and glass.

The layers may be selected with one of the styles on behind layer, on above layer, on glass layer as an option to a {scope} environment.

name: tikz-mirror-lens
caption: Spherical mirrors and lenses in TikZ

descriptions.text: This package allows the automatic drawing of the image of objects in spherical mirrors and lenses from the data of the focus, from the position and height of the object. It calculates the position and height of the image, and also displays the notable rays.

name: tikz-nef
caption: Create diagrams for neural networks constructed with the methods of the Neural Engineering Framework (NEF)

descriptions.text:
The nef TikZ library provides predefined styles and shapes to create diagrams for neural networks constructed with the methods of the Neural Engineering Framework (NEF).

The following styles are supported:

  • ea: ensemble array
  • ens: ensemble
  • ext: external input or output
  • inhibt: inhibitory connection
  • net: network
  • pnode: pass-through node
  • rect: rectification ensemble
  • recurrent: recurrent connection

name: tikz-network
caption: Draw networks with TikZ

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This package allows the creation of images of complex networks that are seamlessly integrated into the underlying LaTeX files.

The package requires datatool, etex, graphicx, tikz, trimspaces, xifthen, and xkeyval.

name: tikz-nfold
caption: Triple, quadruple, and n-fold paths with TikZ

descriptions.text: This library adds higher-order paths to TikZ and also fixes some graphical issues with TikZ’ double paths, used e.g. in arrows with an Implies tip. It is also compatible with tikz-cd, adding support for triple and higher arrows. Macros to offset arbitrary paths are included as well.

name: tikz-opm
caption: Typeset OPM diagrams

descriptions.text: Typeset OPM (Object-Process Methodology) diagrams using LaTeX and PGF/TikZ.

name: tikz-optics
caption: A library for drawing optical setups with TikZ

descriptions.text: This package provides a new TikZ library designed to easily draw optical setups with TikZ. It provides shapes for lens, mirror, etc. The geometrically (in)correct computation of light rays through the setup is left to the user.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: tikz-osci
caption: Produce oscilloscope screen shots

descriptions.text: This package enables you to produce oscilloscope screen shots.

name: tikz-page
caption: Small macro to help building nice and complex layout materials

descriptions.text: The package provides a small macro to help building nice and complex layout materials.

name: tikz-palattice
caption: Draw particle accelerator lattices with TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package allows for drawing a map of a particle accelerator just by giving a list of elements – similar to lattice files for simulation software. The package includes 12 common element types like dipoles, quadrupoles, cavities, or screens, as well as automatic labels with element names, a legend, a rule, and an environment to fade out parts of the accelerator.

The coordinate of any element can be saved and used for custom TikZ drawings or annotations. Thereby, lattices can be connected to draw injection/extraction or even a complete accelerator facility.

name: TikZ-planets
caption: Illustrate celestial mechanics and the solar system

descriptions.text:
This TikZ-package makes it easy to illustrate celestial mechanics and the solar system. You can use it to draw sketches of the eclipses, the phases of the Moon, etc.

The package requires the standard packages TikZ, xcolor, xstring, and pgfkeys.

name: tikz-qtree
caption: Use existing qtree syntax for trees in TikZ

descriptions.text: The package provides a macro for drawing trees with TikZ using the easy syntax of Alexis Dimitriadis’ Qtree. It improves on TikZ’s standard tree-drawing facility by laying out tree nodes without collisions; it improves on Qtree by adding lots of features from TikZ (for example, edge labels, arrows between nodes); and it improves on pst-qtree in being usable with pdfTeX and XeTeX.

name: tikz-relay
caption: TikZ library for typesetting electrical diagrams

descriptions.text: This package contains a collection of symbols for typesetting electrical wiring diagrams for relay control systems. The symbols are meant to be in agreement with the international standard IEC-60617 which has been adopted worldwide, with perhaps the exception of the USA. It extends and modifies, when needed, the TikZ-library circuits.ee.IEC. A few non-standard symbols are also included mainly to be used in presentations, particularly with the beamer package.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: tikz-sections
caption: Draw structural cross-sections

descriptions.text: Preparing high-quality structural engineering figures for papers and reports is time-consuming. TikZ-Sections aims to make this easier for engineers and academics working with steel and reinforced-concrete sections.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: tikz-sfc
caption: Symbols collection for typesetting Sequential Function Chart (SFC) diagrams (PLC programs)

descriptions.text: This package contains a collection of symbols for typesetting Sequential Function Chart (SFC) diagrams in agreement with the international standard IEC-61131-3/2013. It includes steps (normal and initial), transitions, actions and actions qualifiers (with and without time duration). It extends the circuit library of TikZ and allows you to draw an SFC diagram in same way you would draw any other circuit.

topics.details: typesetting associated with engineering of whatever sort

name: tikz-shields
caption: Badges as in shields.io, but in LaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
A small package that allows to include in a LaTeX document shields badges, as in shields.io.

Various styles of badges and other features are available, including clickable links, logos, and color customization options.

name: tikz-swigs
caption: Horizontally and vertically split elliptical nodes

descriptions.text:
This package provides horizontally and vertically split elliptical (pairs of) nodes in TikZ.

The package name derives from the fact that split ellipses of this type are used to represent Single-World Intervention Graph (SWIG) models which are used in counterfactual causal inference.

name: tikz-timing
caption: Easy generation of timing diagrams as TikZ pictures

descriptions.text: This package provides macros and an environment to generate timing diagrams (digital waveforms) without much effort. The TikZ package is used to produce the graphics. The diagrams may be inserted into text (paragraphs, \hbox, etc.) and into tikzpictures. A tabular-like environment is provided to produce larger timing diagrams.

name: tikz-trackschematic
caption: A TikZ library for creating track diagrams in railways

descriptions.text:
This TikZ library is a toolbox of symbols geared primarily towards creating track schematic for either research or educational purposes. It provides a TikZ frontend to some of the symbols which may be needed to describe situations and layouts in railway operation.

The library is divided into sublibraries: topology, trafficcontrol, vehicles, constructions, electrics, symbology, and measures.

name: tikz-triminos
caption: Create triminos, made with TikZ

descriptions.text:
Create (1 or 9 or 12) TriMinos with some customizations:

  • size, font, logo, colors;
  • automatic texts adjustment;
  • full version, or joker usage.

Inspiration from Paul Matthies

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material
process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: tikz-truchet
caption: Draw Truchet tiles

descriptions.text: This is a package for LaTeX that draws Truchet tiles, as used in Colin Beveridge's article Too good to be Truchet in issue 08 of Chalkdust.

name: tikz2d-fr
caption: Work with some 2D TikZ commands (French)

descriptions.text:
This is a small package to work with some (French) 2D commands for TikZ:

  • freehand style mainlevee
  • define and mark points \DefinirPoints, \MarquerPoints
  • draw colored segments \TracerSegments

name: tikz3d-fr
caption: Work with some 3D figures

descriptions.text: This is a package for working with some 3D figures.

name: tikzbrickfigurines
caption: Draw brick figurines with TikZ

descriptions.text: A small LaTeX package to draw (2D) brick-figurines with TikZ. The user can modify colors and/or elements.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: TikZbricks
caption: Drawing bricks with TikZ

descriptions.text: A small LaTeX package to draw bricks with TikZ. The user can modify color, shape, and viewpoint.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: tikzcalendarnotes
caption: Highlighting, marking and annotating dates in a TikZ calendar

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This package offers a calendar arrangement (atop of the TikZ calendar library) and provides a set of commands to highlight, mark, and annotate dates in a calendar.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: tikzcodeblocks
caption: Helps to draw codeblocks like scratch, NEPO and PXT in TikZ

descriptions.text: tikzcodeblocks is a LaTeX package for typesetting blockwise graphic programming languages like scratch, nepo or pxt.

name: tikzdotncross
caption: Marking coordinates and crossing paths

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This package offers a few alternative ways for declaring and marking coordinates and drawing a line with jumps over an already existent path, which is quite a common issue when drawing, for instance, electronic circuits (like with CircuiTikZ).

name: TikZducks
caption: A little fun package for using rubber ducks in TikZ

descriptions.text: The package is a LaTeX package for ducks to be used in TikZ pictures. This project is a continuation of an answer at StackExchange How we can draw a duck?

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: tikzfill
caption: TikZ libraries for filling with images and patterns

copyright.owner: Prof. Dr. Dr. Thomas F. Sturm

descriptions.text: This is a collection of TikZ libraries which add further options to fill TikZ paths with images and patterns. The libraries comprise fillings with images from files and from TikZ pictures. Also, patterns of hexagons and of rhombi are provided.

name: tikzfxgraph
caption: Plotting functions in a simplified way

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This package is mostly a wrap around pgfplots and Gnuplot, hiding most of their inherent complexity.

name: tikzinclude
caption: Import TikZ images from colletions

descriptions.text: The package addresses the problem of importing only one TikZ-image from a file holding multiple images.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: TikZlings
caption: A collection of cute little animals and similar creatures

descriptions.text:
A collection of LaTeX packages for drawing cute little animals and similar creatures using TikZ.

Currently, the following TikZlings are included:

  • anteater
  • ape
  • bat
  • bear

  • bug

These little drawings can be customized in many ways.

name: tikzmark
caption: Use TikZ’s method of remembering a position on a page

descriptions.text: The tikzmark package defines a command to remember a position on a page for later (or earlier) use, primarily (but not exclusively) with TikZ.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: TikZmarmots
caption: Drawing little marmots in TikZ

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX package for marmots to be used in TikZ pictures.

These little figures are constructed in such a way that they may even borrow some accessories and other attributes from the TikZlings package.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: tikzorbital
caption: Atomic and molecular orbitals using TikZ

descriptions.text: Atomic s, p and d orbitals may be drawn, as well as molecular orbital diagrams.

name: tikzpackets
caption: Display network packets

descriptions.text: This package allows you to easily display network packets graphically.

name: tikzpagenodes
caption: A single TikZ node for the whole page

descriptions.text: The package provides special PGF/TikZ nodes for the text, marginpar, footer and header area of the current page. They are inspired by the current page node defined by PGF/TikZ itself.

name: tikzpeople
caption: Draw people-shaped nodes in TikZ

descriptions.text:
This package provides people-shaped nodes in the style of Microsoft Visio clip art, to be used with TikZ.

The available, highly customizable, node shapes are: alice, bob, bride, builder, businessman, charlie, chef, conductor, cowboy, criminal, dave, devil, duck, graduate, groom, guard, jester, judge, maininblack, mexican, nun, nurse, physician, pilot, police, priest, sailor, santa, surgeon.

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: tikzpfeile
caption: Draw arrows using PGF/TikZ

descriptions.text: In a document with a lot of diagrams created with PGF/TikZ, there is a possibility of the reader being distracted by different sorts of arrowheads in the diagrams and in the text (as, e.g., in \rightarrow). The package defines macros to create all arrows using PGF/TikZ, so as to avoid the problem.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: TikZpingus
caption: Penguins with TikZ

descriptions.text: tikzpingus is a package similar to TikZducks but with penguins and a vast set of gadgets and extras (capable of changing the wing-positions, body-types, and more).

topics.details: jokes, distractions, tongue-in-cheek packages, and other entertainment material

name: tikzposter
caption: Create scientific posters using TikZ

copyright.owner: Pascal Richter, Elena Botoeva,     Richard Barnard and Dirk Surmann

descriptions.text: A document class provides a simple way of using TikZ for generating posters. Several formatting options are available, and spacing and layout of the poster is to a large extent automated.

name: tikzquads
caption: A few shapes designed to be used with CircuiTikZ

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This package defines a few extra shapes, Quadripoles and single port, which can be used standalone, but are mainly meant to be used with CircuiTikZ.

name: tikzquests
caption: A parametric questions’ repositories framework

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This is a framework for building parametric questions’ repositories, which can be further used to construct parametric questions for exams. Unlike other packages of the kind this does not try to enforce any pre-defined presentation format, focusing only on how to set a repository of questions and use them.

name: tikzscale
caption: Resize pictures while respecting text size

descriptions.text: The package extends the \includegraphics command to support tikzpictures. It allows scaling of TikZ images and PGFPlots to a given width or height without changing the text size.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: tikzsymbols
caption: Some symbols created using TikZ

descriptions.text: The package provides various emoticons, cooking symbols and trees.

topics.details: create symbols, rather than select from a font

name: tikztosvg
caption: A utility for rendering TikZ diagrams to SVG

descriptions.text: This package provides a shell script that calls XeTeX and pdf2svg to convert TikZ environments to SVG files.

topics.details: convert TeX-ish sources to some other markup (than HTML)

name: tikzviolinplots
caption: Draws violin plots from data

descriptions.text:
This package enables the user to draw violin plots, calculating the kernel density estimation from the data and plotting the resulting curve inside a tikzpicture environment.

It supports different kernels, and allows the user to either set the bandwidth value for each plot or use a default value.

topics.details: typeset reports, diagrams, etc., of statistics

name: tile-graphic
caption: Create tiles of a graphical file

descriptions.text: This package breaks a given graphical file into n rows and m columns of subgraphics, which are called tiles. The tiles can be written separately to individual PDF files, or packaged into a single PDF file.

name: tilings
caption: A TikZ library for drawing tiles and tilings

descriptions.text:
This package provides a TikZ library for working with tiles, tilings, and tessellations. Using it, one can define tiles, place tiles, deform tiles, and – in some cases – apply replacement rules to generate tessellations. It has pre-defined tiles for most of the Penrose tile sets and the aperiodical polykite tiles.

This is a replacement for the penrose package, renamed as it now deals with more extensive tiles than just the Penrose tile sets.

name: timbreicmc
caption: Typeset documents with ICMC/USP watermarks

descriptions.text:
With this package you can typeset documents with ICMC/USP São Carlos watermarks.

ICMC is acronym for Instituto de Ciências Matemáticas e de Computação of the Universidade de São Paulo (USP), in the city of São Carlos-SP, Brazil.

topics.details: separate printing, under (or over) the page as a whole

name: time
caption: Defines a macro \now to print the current time

descriptions.text:
Defines a macro \now to print the current time, in a 12-hour clock format.

The package is part of the piff bundle.

name: time-gen
caption: Print the time (12-hour clock)

descriptions.text: A generic version of the functionality; uses registers without allocating them – a sin of which the LaTeX-based time.sty is not guilty.

name: timechart
caption: A package for drawing chronological charts

descriptions.text: This package provides for the easy creation of chronological charts which show visually the relative historical positions of people and events. Each event or period can be specified by a single line of LaTeX code comprising (possibly uncertain) start and finish dates and a label, and the package takes care of indicating the uncertainties and whether intervals extend beyond the specified bounds of the chart.

name: timeline
caption: Typeset time-lines, for planning, etc

descriptions.text: Defines a timeline environment, in which one places a bunch of \items. A small sample of use is provided.

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: timeop
caption: Calculates and displays arithmetic operations with durations

descriptions.text: This package can be used to add and subtract time information.

name: times
caption: Select Adobe Times Roman (or equivalent) as default font

descriptions.text:
The package is now obsolete, replaced by the mathptmx package, which supports Times Roman text and (mostly) matching mathematics.

The package remains available, for compatibility; both it and mathptmx are part of psnfss.

The font itself is part of Adobe's basic set, and is typically only available to users as part of their printer firmware.

topics.details: support is for a font not available on CTAN
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: timetab
caption: Typeset timetables

descriptions.text: Defines an environment timetab that prints a table, in the way one might when doing the job by hand. (The basic entry is \Lek, from German Lektur.)

name: timetable
caption: Generate timetables

descriptions.text: A highly-configurable package, with nice output and simple input. The macros use a radix sort mechanism so that the order of input is not critical.

name: timing
caption: Fonts and macro package for drawing timing diagrams

descriptions.text: The fonts are distributed as Metafont source.

name: timing-diagrams
caption: Draw timing diagrams

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands to draw and annotate various kinds of timing diagrams, using Tikz.

Documentation is sparse, but the source and the examples file should be of some use.

name: tinos
caption: Tinos fonts with LaTeX support

descriptions.text: Tinos, designed by Steve Matteson, is an innovative, refreshing serif design that is metrically compatible with Times New Roman.

topics.details: font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: tinyc2l
caption: Pretty print C/C++/Java source code using LaTeX

descriptions.text: Tiny_c2l is a small converter for pretty printing C/C++/Java source code using LaTeX. The converter has a large range of features, and is generated from the author’s converter generator code (the distribution also includes a covnerter that recognises no language features, and merely performs the text positioning part of the job that tiny_c2l does).

name: tipa
caption: Fonts and macros for IPA phonetics characters

descriptions.text: These fonts are considered the ultimate answer to IPA typesetting. The encoding of these 8-bit fonts has been registered as LaTeX standard encoding T3, and the set of addendum symbols as encoding TS3. Times-like Adobe Type 1 versions are provided for both the T3 and the TS3 fonts.

documentation.details: Discussion of the design of the fonts
