font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: tipa-de
caption: German translation of tipa documentation

descriptions.text: This is a translation of Fukui Rei's tipaman from the tipa bundle.

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language
documentation about choosing installing and using fonts

name: tipauni
caption: Producing Unicode characters with TIPA commands

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
Package TIPA uses the T3 encoding for producing IPA characters. The package is widely used in the field of linguistics, but because of the old encoding, the output documents are less productive than Unicode-based documents.

This package redefines most of the TIPA-commands for outputting Unicode characters. Users can now use their beloved TIPA shortcuts with the benefits of Unicode, i.e. searchability, copy-pasting, changing the font and many more.

As this package needs the fontspec package for loading an IPA font, it needs to be compiled with XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

This package can also be viewed as an ASCII-based input method for producing IPA characters in Unicode.

It needs the New Computer Modern font for printing IPA characters.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: tipfr
caption: Produces calculator’s keys with the help of TikZ

descriptions.text: The package provides commands to draw calculator keys with the help of TikZ. It also provides commands to draw the content of screens and of menu items.

name: tipos
caption: Description of fonts for TeX, in Spanish

descriptions.text: The document tipos.pdf describes (in Spanish) the large amount of types of files for fonts (tipo means font in Spanish). Tipos.pdf has been translated to German by Thomas Ruedas.

name: tiscreen
caption: Mimic the screen of older Texas Instruments calculators

descriptions.text:
This package mimics the screen of older Texas Instruments dot matrix display calculators, specifically the TI-82 STATS.

It relies on the lcd and xcolor packages.

topics.details: graphics produced by one of the *TeX engines

name: titlecaps
caption: Setting rich-text input into Titling Caps

descriptions.text: The package is intended for setting rich text into titling capitals (in which the first character of words are capitalized). It automatically accounts for diacritical marks (like umlauts), national symbols (like ae), punctuation, and font changing commands that alter the appearance or size of the text. It allows a list of predesignated words to be protected as lower-cased, and also allows for titling exceptions of various sorts.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: titlefoot
caption: Add special material to footer of title page

descriptions.text: Provides the capability of adding keywords (with a \keywords command), a running title (\runningtitle), AMS subject classifications (\amssubj), and an authors footnote’ as footnotes to the title or first page of a document. Works with any class for which the \thanks macro works (e.g., article).

name: titlepage-uni-dortmund
caption: Titlepage for University of Dortmund (Germany)

descriptions.text: This package introduces a titlepage layout to be used at the University of Dortmund (UDO). The implementation involves a usual LaTeX-document in addition to the general setup of the package. Please note that this is the first version of the UDO title, thus errors unknown to the developer may occur.

name: titlepages
caption: Sample titlepages, and how to code them

descriptions.text: The document provides examples of over two dozen title page designs based on a range of published books and theses, together with the LaTeX code used to create them.

topics.details: sample of use of macro collections, etc.

name: titlepic
caption: Add picture to title page of a document

descriptions.text:
The package allows you to place a picture on the title page (cover page) of a LaTeX document.

Example of usage:

  • \usepackage[cc]{titlepic}
  • \usepackage{graphicx}
  • \titlepic{\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{picture.png}}

The package currently only works with the document classes article, report and book.

name: titleps
caption: Page style control

descriptions.text:
The package provides page styles with a simple one-stage mechanism, including top marks; access to top-, first- and botmarks in a single header/footer; headers/footers for specific floats; multiple sets of marks (with e-TeX), and more.

The package is part of the titlesec distribution.

name: titleref
caption: A <q>\titleref</q> command to cross-reference section titles

descriptions.text: Defines a command \titleref that allows you to cross-reference section (and chapter, etc) titles and captions just like \ref and \pageref. The package does not interwork with hyperref; if you need hypertext capabilities, use nameref instead.

name: titles
caption: Titles of books, articles, etc. in LaTeX

descriptions.text: A LaTeX package defining macros that typeset the titles of books, journals, etc. and handle following spacing and punctuation intelligently, based on context. Useful for bibliographic databases and any document. Also includes other markup like \word, \defn, \phrase, etc.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: titlesec
caption: Select alternative section titles

descriptions.text: A package providing an interface to sectioning commands for selection from various title styles. E.g., marginal titles and to change the font of all headings with a single command, also providing simple one-step page styles. Also includes a package to change the page styles when there are floats in a page. You may assign headers/footers to individual floats, too.

name: titletoc
caption: Alternative headings for toc/lof/lot

descriptions.text: A companion for titlesec handling toc/lof/lot entries.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: titling
caption: Control over the typesetting of the \maketitle command

descriptions.text: The titling package provides control over the typesetting of the \maketitle command and \thanks commands, and makes the \title, \author and \date information permanently available. Multiple titles are allowed in a single document. New titling elements can be added and a titlepage title can be centered on a physical page.

name: tkbibtex
caption: A portable editor and browser for BibTeX files

descriptions.text:
Supports browsing, editing, searching, and annotations, in both GUI and command-line usage.

For command-line usage, the author’s more recent pybib package is preferable.

name: tkdvi
caption: DVI previewer built with the Tcl/Tk toolkit

descriptions.text: The previewer is built around a Tk extension dvi, and supports multiple windows displaying multiple pages from multiple DVI files simultaneously.

name: tkhyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for Turkish

descriptions.text:
These patterns were developed for the Ottoman Texts Project.

Note that hyphenation for modern Turkish texts is supported by the hyph-utf8 bundle.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkish

name: tktexcad
caption: Generate LaTeX picture environments

descriptions.text:
Tktexcad is at base a Python script, which uses the Tkinter extension. The script knows about the limitations of the picture environment, and only uses picture commands (apart from loading external graphics using graphicx).

There is provision for saving and reloading pictures and picture parts, but the only available export is LaTeX code.

name: tkz-base
caption: Tools for drawing with a cartesian coordinate system

descriptions.text: The bundle is a set of packages, designed to give mathematics teachers (and students) easy access to programming of drawings with TikZ.

name: tkz-berge
caption: Macros for drawing graphs of graph theory

descriptions.text:
The package provides a collection of useful macros for drawing classic graphs of graph theory, or to make other graphs.

This package has been taken temporarily out of circulation to give the author time to investigate some problems.

name: tkz-bernoulli
caption: Draw Bernoulli trees with TikZ

descriptions.text: This is a package for representing Bernoulli trees with PGF/TikZ.

name: tkz-doc
caption: Documentation macros for the TKZ series of packages

descriptions.text:
This bundle offers a documentation class (tkz-doc) and a package (tkzexample).

These files are used in the documentation of the author’s packages tkz-base, tkz-euclide, tkz-fct, tkz-linknodes, and tkz-tab.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation
print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result

name: tkz-elements
caption: A Lua library for drawing Euclidean geometry with TikZ or tkz-euclide

descriptions.text:
This package provides a library written in Lua, allowing to make all the necessary calculations to define the objects of a Euclidean geometry figure. You need to compile with LuaLaTeX. The definitions and calculations are only done with Lua.

The main possibility of programming proposed is oriented object programming with object classes like point, line, triangle, circle and now, conic. For the moment, once the calculations are done, it is tkz-euclide or TikZ which allows the drawings.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: tkz-euclide
caption: Tools for drawing Euclidean geometry

descriptions.text: The tkz-euclide package is a set of files designed to give math teachers and students easy access to the programming of Euclidean geometry with TikZ.

topics.details: package will use LuaTeX facilities if available

name: tkz-fct
caption: Tools for drawing graphs of functions

descriptions.text: The tkz-fct package is designed to give math teachers (and students) easy access to programming graphs of functions with TikZ and gnuplot.

name: tkz-graph
caption: Draw graph-theory graphs

descriptions.text: The package is designed to create graph diagrams as simply as possible, using TikZ.

name: tkz-grapheur
caption: A LaTeX package with tools for graph plotting (and TikZ)

descriptions.text:
This package provides some commands to help French mathematics teachers for 15-18 years olds, with graphs of functions:

  • define and draw functions and interpolations curves
  • work with integrals, tangents, intersections
  • get coordinates of points
  • ...

The syntax is rather explicit, like \DefinirCourbe, \RecupererCoordonnees,\TrouverIntersections, etc.

topics.details: plot a representation of a function

name: tkz-interval
caption: Interval brackets made with TikZ

descriptions.text: The idea is to provide a command for representing intervals with brackets created using TikZ, with automatic size management and customization of thickness and depth, for examples. It is also possible to specify surrounding spaces, and optional overlap for open brackets.

name: tkz-kiviat
caption: Draw Kiviat graphs

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to draw Kiviat Graphs directly, or with data from an external file. The drawing is done with the help of pgfplots.

This package has been taken temporarily out of circulation to give the author time to investigate some problems.

name: tkz-linknodes
caption: Link nodes in mathematical environments

descriptions.text:
The package arose from a requirement to link the elements of an amsmath align or aligned environment. The package makes use of PGF/TikZ.

The package documentation relies on the facilities of the tkz-doc bundle

This package has been taken temporarily out of circulation to give the author time to investigate some problems.

name: tkz-orm
caption: Create Object-Role Model (ORM) diagrams

descriptions.text: The package provides styles for drawing Object-Role Model (ORM) diagrams in TeX based on the PGF and TikZ picture environment.

name: tkz-tab
caption: Tables of signs and variations using PGF/TikZ

descriptions.text:
The package provides comprehensive facilities for preparing lists of signs and variations, using PGF.

The package documentation requires the tkz-doc bundle.

This package has been taken temporarily out of circulation to give the author time to investigate some problems.

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

name: tkzexample
caption: Package for the documentation of all tkz-* packages

descriptions.text: This package is needed to compile the documentation of all tkz-* packages (like tkz-euclide).

topics.details: print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result
macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: tlaunch
caption: A Windows GUI to run a networked TeX Live as if installed locally

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
TLaunch, or the TeX Live launcher, is a Windows GUI to run a shared or networked TeX Live. It takes care of all the configuration which would be done otherwise by a local installer.

The interface and file associations are configured via an ini file, which can be edited to give access to additional TeX-related software.

The author told us in March 2023: Please move tlaunch to obsolete. It is TeX Live-specific, and already part of the wintools package. Therefore a CTAN package is not terribly useful.

name: tlc-article
caption: LaTeX document class for consistently formatted formal documents

descriptions.text: The package provides a LaTeX document class based on the standard article class. It supplies a consistent layout for title pages, abstracts, tables of contents, headers, footers, and margins. Optional data files support custom layout definitions, headers and footers, logos, and document version metadata.

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: tlc2-errata
caption: Errata list for The LaTeX Companion, Second Edition

descriptions.text: Errata list for The LaTeX Companion, Second Edition (4. printing).

documentation.details: Errata list for The LaTeX Companion, Second Edition

topics.details: lists of errata in published books

name: tlc2-examples
caption: Examples from <q>The LaTeX Companion</q>, second edition

descriptions.text: The source of the examples printed in the book, together with necessary supporting files. The book was published by Addison-Wesley, 2004, ISBN 0-201-36299-6.

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

name: tlc3-examples
caption: All examples from <q>The LaTeX Companion</q>, third edition

descriptions.text: The PDFs (as used with spotcolor and trimming) and sources for all examples from the third edition (Parts I+II), together with necessary supporting files. The edition is published by Addison-Wesley, 2023, ISBN-13: 978-0-13-816648-9, ISBN-10: 0-13-816648-X (bundle of Part I & II).

topics.details: copies of examples from a published book

name: TLCockpit
caption: A GUI frontend to TeX Live Manager (tlmgr)

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: This package aims at being a GUI for tlmgr, the TeX Live Manager, with a modern look and feel. We take inspiration from the excellent TeX Live Utility for MacOS.

name: tlg2latex
caption: Prepare LaTeX from the Thesaurus Linguae Graecae

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format
support for studies in the humanities

name: tlmgr-intro-zh-cn
caption: A short tutorial on using tlmgr in Chinese

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This is a Chinese translation of the tlmgr documentation. It introduces some of the common usage of the TeX Live Manager.

The original can be found in the tlmgrbasics package.

name: tlmgrBasics
caption: A simplified documentation for tlmgr

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text: This package provides simplified documentation for tlmgr, the TeX Live Manager. It describes the most commonly-used actions and options in a convenient format.

name: tmmath
caption: Support for using the Micropress TM-Math fonts

descriptions.text: Support for typesetting math in a style that suits the Adobe Times text fonts. Commercial (Adobe type 1) versions of the HV-Math fonts are available from Micropress; free bitmap versions of the fonts from the Micropress fonts directories.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: tmmath-fonts
caption: Bitmap versions of the Micropress TM-Math fonts (Times Maths)

descriptions.text: This is the public part of the TM-Math font distribution: metrics, and a set of bitmap files (in .pk format). Actually to use the fonts, you are advised to use the macros by Walter Schmidt.

name: tmview
caption: A DVI previewer for SVGA displays

descriptions.text: An SVGA-lib based DVI-previewer offering xdvi-like anti-aliasing, text-string searching, arbitrary-zooming, bookmarks, some hypertex features, and rendering of eps-graphics by invoking Ghostscript. It supports The GNU/Linux framebuffer device and double-page viewing.

name: to-be-determined
caption: Highlight text passages that need further work

descriptions.text: This package provides a single command \tbd which highlights the pieces of text that need to be rewritten later. You can hide them all with a single package option hide, or just make them disappear entirely with the option off.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: toc
caption: Table of contents macros for Plain TeX

descriptions.text: A set of macros created for use in writing the table of contents for a document.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things
extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: toc-zar
caption: Plain TeX table of contents macros

descriptions.text: Stores table of contents information in a \vbox, and ships pages out of that as it fills up (producing pages with no page number).

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs
deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: tocbasic
caption: Management of tables/lists of contents (and the like)

descriptions.text:
The package provides means to create specialised table of contents-like lists of features of a document.

The package is distributed as part of the KOMA-Script bundle of packages and classes.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: tocbibind
caption: Add bibliography/index/contents to Table of Contents

descriptions.text: Automatically adds the bibliography and/or the index and/or the contents, etc., to the Table of Contents listing.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: tocdata
caption: Adds names to chapters, sections, figures in the TOC and LOF

descriptions.text:
The tocdata package may be used to add a small amount of data to an entry in the table of contents or list of figures, between the section or caption name and the page number. The typical use would be to add the name of an author or artist of a chapter or section, such as in an anthology or a collection of papers.

Additionally, user-level macros are provided which add the author’s name to a chapter or section, along with an optional prefix and/or suffix, and add to a figure the artist’s name, prefix, and suffix, plus optional additional text. Author and artist names are also added to the index. Additional user-level macros control formatting.

tocdata works with the TOC/LOF formatting of the default LaTeX classes, memoir, koma-script, and with titletoc, tocloft, tocbasic, and tocstyle.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: tocenter
caption: Centring (and other) Page Layout

descriptions.text:
Defines \ToCenter that calculates margins such that the text body (plus, optionally headers, footers and marginal texts) are centred on the page. Other commands with similar interfaces are also defined.

The package is part of the NCC tools bundle.

name: tocloft
caption: Control table of contents, figures, etc

descriptions.text: Provides control over the typography of the Table of Contents, List of Figures and List of Tables, and the ability to create new List of .... The ToC \parskip may be changed.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: tocstyle
caption: Define style of Table of contents (etc) files

descriptions.text:
The package permits the user to define the style of the Table of Contents table for a document, as well as the style of tables of floats, etc.

The package has been withdrawn from the koma-script bundle in Juli 2020 and is now considered obsolete. tocbasic and scrwfile should be used instead.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: tocvsec2
caption: Section numbering and table of contents control

descriptions.text: Provides control over section numbering (without recourse to starred sectional commands) and/or the entries in the Table of Contents on a section by section basis.

topics.details: deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: todo
caption: Make a to-do list for a document

descriptions.text: The package allows you to insert “to do“ marks in your document, to make lists of such items, and to cross-reference to them.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: todonotes
caption: Marking things to do in a LaTeX document

descriptions.text: The package lets the user mark things to do later, in a simple and visually appealing way. The package takes several options to enable customization/finetuning of the visual appearance.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: toil
caption: An installer of PostScript fonts for TeX

descriptions.text:
A flexible, AWK+Metafont-based Type One Install utiLity which facilitates installation of Adobe Type 1 fonts for (plain) TeX; an alternative for afm2tfm; starting from version 1.04, includes an option that enables neutralizing sidebars (via implicit kerning mechanism).

The package is only available for use under MS-DOS.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: tokcycle
caption: Build tools to process tokens from an input stream

descriptions.text:
The tokcycle package helps one to build tools to process tokens from an input stream. If a macro to process an arbitrary single token can be built, then tokcycle can provide a wrapper for cycling through an input stream (including macros, spaces, and groups) on a token-by-token basis, using the provided macro on each successive character.

tokcycle characterizes each successive token in the input stream as a Character, a Group, a Macro, or a Space. Each of these token categories are processed with a unique directive, to bring about the desired effect of the token cycle. If condition flags are provided to identify active, implicit, and catcode-6 tokens as they are digested. The package provides a number of options for handling groups.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: tokenizer
caption: A tokenizer

descriptions.text: A tokenizer for LaTeX. \GetTokens{Target1}{Target2}{Source} splits source into two tokens at the first encounter of a comma. The first token is saved in a newly created command with the name passed as <Target1> and the second token likewise. A package option trim causes leading and trailing space to be removed from each token; with this option, the \TrimSpaces command is defined, which removes leading and trailing spaces from its argument.

topics.details: read, process and convert CSV data

name: tokglobalstack
caption: Dedicated global stacks implementations

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: Global stack(s) of tokens implemented as variables or commands.

name: tokgroupmark
caption: Restoring tokens after closing multiple groups

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This package aims to solve the problem of how certain tokens can be preserved beyond a variable number of nested groups.

name: tokmap
caption: Iterate over a token list expandably, without dropping spaces or braced groups

descriptions.text:
Usage: \tokmap <command> { <tokens> } applies command over the token list tokens. Space tokens, left and right braces are replaced with the marker tokens \tokmap@space, \tokmap@bgroup, and \tokmap@egroup respectively (which are \ifx-equal to themselves exclusively). For convenience, command may contain multiple tokens. It is assumed that { and } are the only characters with category codes 1 (beginning of group) and 2 (end of group) respectively. Expandable.

This package may be used in LaTeX by \usepackage{tokmap}, or in plain TeX and other formats by \input{tokmap}.

See the visualtoks package for an example application.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: tokstools
caption: Tools for manipulating tokens

descriptions.text:
This package is still in the experimental stage. Therefore, its behavior is not guaranteed to match the description in the manual, and bugs of varying severity may occur.

Additionally, some features, as well as their syntax, may be subject to change.

It requires any modern engine that supports etex primitives and can therefore be used with either TeX or LaTeX.

The tokstools package provides tools for manipulating tokens and implements PEG-style grammars in TeX. Predefined elementary patterns can be combined to form grammars that search for matches within tokens.

Two categories of macros are provided:

  • those operating on individual tokens (\toksdo, \tokscount, and \printtoks);
  • those operating on tokens that have matched a grammar (\ifpegmatch, \pegcount, and \pegreplace)

name: tolkienfonts
caption: Use TTF <q>Tolkien</q> fonts from the WWW with pdfTeX

descriptions.text:
The virtual fonts in this package allow the user to easily write English, Quenya and Sindarin in several modes with J.R.R. Tolkien's tengwar, cirth, sarati and valmaric scripts, using freely available TrueType fonts found on the internet.

Support is at very nearly the highest possible level; the point of this package was to avoid bizarre spellings or lots of special commands.

Fonts supported are Tengwar Annatar, Cirth Erebor, Sarati and Valmaric Eldamar, and (with a little more work) Tengwar Parmaite, Eldamar, Noldor, Quenya and Sindarin.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font for an ‘invented’ language or script
support is for a font not available on CTAN

name: tonevalue
caption: Tool for linguists and phoneticians to visualize tone value patterns

descriptions.text: This package provides a TikZ-based solution to typeset visualisations of tone values. Currently, unt's model is implemented. Support for more models is planned.

name: toolbox
caption: Tool macros

descriptions.text: A package for (La)TeX which provides some macros which are convenient for writing indexes, glossaries, or other macros. It contains macros which support: implicit macros; fancy optional arguments; loops over tokenlists and itemlists; searching and splitting; controlled expansion; redefinition of macros; and concatenated macro names; macros for text replacement.

name: topcapt
caption: Place captions above figures or tables

descriptions.text: Defines a command \topcaption which does the same as \caption, except that it places itself correctly when put above the figure/table that it’s a caption of.

name: topfloat
caption: Move floats to the top of the page

name: topiclongtable
caption: Extend longtable with cells that merge hierarchically

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package extends longtable implementing cells that:

  • merge with the one above if it has the same content,
  • do not merge with the one above unless the ones on the left are merged,
  • are well behaved with respect to longtable chunking on page breaks,
  • and automatically draw the correct separation lines.

The typical use case is a table spanning multiple pages that contains a list of hierarchically organized topics (hence the package name).

The package depends on array, expl3, longtable, multirow, xparse, and zref-abspage.

topics.details: typeset tables that may be too big for a page

name: TOPletter
caption: Letter class for the Politecnico di Torino

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class for typesetting letters conforming to the official Corporate Image guidelines for the Politecnico di Torino. The class can be used for letters written in Italian and in English.

name: topsection
caption: An un-numbered top level section

descriptions.text:
The package implements a command \topsection, which creates an un-numbered section at the top level (chapter in book- or report-like classes, section in article-like classes). The section is used when the table of contents, index, etc., are prepared, so that documents can in some sense be class independent.

In collaboration with the nccsect package, the details of the \topsection may be written to the .aux file, and hence to the table of contents.

The package is part of the NCC tools bundle.

name: TOPtesi
caption: Bundle for typesetting multilanguage theses

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains everything needed for typesetting a bachelor, master, or PhD thesis in Italian (or in any other language supported by LaTeX: the bundle is constructed to support multilingual use). The infix strings may be selected and specified at will by means of a configuration file, so as to customize the layout of the front page to the requirements of a specific university. Thanks to its language management, the bundle is suited for multilanguage theses that are becoming more and more frequent thanks to the double degree programs of the European Community Socrates programs.

Toptesi is designed to save the PDF version of a thesis in PDF/A-1b compliant mode and with all the necessary metadata.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: totalcount
caption: Commands for typesetting total values of counters

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package offers commands for typesetting total values of counters.

name: totcount
caption: Find the last value of a counter

descriptions.text: The package records the value that was last set, for any counter of interest; since most such counters are simply incremented when they are changed, the recorded value will usually be the maximum value.

name: totpages
caption: Count pages in a document, and report last page number

descriptions.text: The package counts the actual pages in the document (as opposed to reporting the number of the last page, as does lastpage). The counter itself may be shipped out to the DVI file. The package uses the everyshi package for its task.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: tpcmfont
caption: Computer modern fonts in <q>true point sizes</q>

descriptions.text: Font Definition files for True Point Computer Modern (and actually, for Computer Concrete) in T1 encoding). For example, cmr11 is declared as cmr11, not as cmr10 at 10.95pt.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: tpic2pdftex
caption: Use tpic commands in pdfTeX

descriptions.text: This AWK script converts pic language, embedded inline (delimited by .PS and .PE markers), to \pdfliteral commands. It is now maintained as part of TeX Live.

name: tpslifonts
caption: A LaTeX package for configuring presentation fonts

descriptions.text:
This package aims to improve of font readability in presentations, especially with maths. The standard cm maths fonts at large design sizes are difficult to read from far away, especially at low resolutions and low contrast color choice. Using this package leads to much better overall readability of some font combinations. The package offers a couple of harmonising combinations of text and maths fonts from the (distant) relatives of computer modern fonts, with a couple of extras for optimising readability. Text fonts from computer modern roman, computer modern sans serif, SliTeX computer modern sans serif, computer modern bright, or concrete roman are available, in addition to maths fonts from computer modern maths, computer modern bright maths, or Euler fonts.

The package is part of the TeXPower bundle.

name: TpX
caption: A drawing tool for Windows

descriptions.text:
TpX is a lightweight, easy-to-use graphical editor for Windows platform for creating drawings and including them into TeX files in publication-ready form. It can also be used as a stand-alone editor for vector graphics.

The output is a file (with extension .TpX) containing the drawing as TeX code or as an \includegraphics link to an external file created by the program. The user can choose between several output formats. TpX saves its own data in TeX file comments so that the drawing can be loaded into TpX and edited again. This internal TpX format is based on XML and can easily be understood and edited.

TpX can import EMF/WMF pictures created by other Windows applications, including many applications producing scientific graphs. In most cases the result is nice, though sometimes the imported picture needs some manual editing. So TpX can be used as an EMF-to-any converter.

name: tqft
caption: Drawing TQFT diagrams with TikZ/PGF

descriptions.text: The package defines some node shapes useful for drawing TQFT diagrams with TikZ/PGF. That is, it defines highly customisable shapes that look like cobordisms between circles, such as those used in TQFT and other mathematical diagrams.

name: tr2latex
caption: Translate troff source to LaTeX

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: A development of Al-Yahya’s original troff-to-LaTeX. The translator recognises most -ms and -man macros, plus some eqn and tbl preprocessor commands; output is in LaTeX 2.09 format.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: trace
caption: Make sensible use of TeX tracing in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides the means to suppress excessive (and usually unnecessary) tracing inside some particularly verbose parts of LaTeX (such as the font selection routines, or the calc package's parsing of expressions).

The package therefore redefines a number of key commands to turn off tracing while they execute (those the author finds most annoying and noisy). Since it potentially modifies the content of other packages, the package should be loaded last in a document's preamble.

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: tracking
caption: Adjust tracking of strings

descriptions.text:
Automatically adjust spaces between symbols in words or phrases to fit them into a specified length. Any chain of symbols (including spaces) in the current font may be treated.

Commands \track{<length>}{<string>} (add space <length>, which may be <0, after each symbol of <string>), \fittrack{<length>}{<string>} (make <string> fit into width <length>, which may be smaller than the original width) and \ratiotrack{<ratio>}{<string>} (as \fittrack, with <length> replaced by <ratio> of the natural length of <string>).

name: tracklang
caption: Language and dialect tracker

descriptions.text:
The tracklang package is provided for package developers who want a simple interface to find out which languages the user has requested through packages such as babel or polyglossia.

This package does not provide any translations! Its purpose is simply to track which languages have been requested by the user.

Generic TeX code is in tracklang.tex for non-LaTeX users.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: trademarks
caption: A collection of trademarks and the like

descriptions.text: A collection of macros for common names of organisations and of products, typeset in such a way as to match their common representation.

name: traffic-light-protocol
caption: Show TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) tags

descriptions.text: This LaTeX package provides a command \tlp to display TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) labels. It currently relies on xcolor and LaTeX3.

name: trajan
caption: Fonts from the Trajan column in Rome

descriptions.text:
Provides fonts (both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format) based on the capitals carved on the Trajan column in Rome in 114 AD, together with macros to access the fonts.

Many typographers think these rank first among the Roman’s artistic legacy. The font is uppercase letters together with some punctuation and analphabetics; no lowercase or digits.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

name: tram
caption: Typeset tram boxes in LaTeX

descriptions.text: Tram boxes are highlighted with patterns of dots; the package defines an environment tram that typesets its content into a tram box. The pattern used may be selected in an optional argument to the environment.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: tramlines
caption:
A package for creating tramlines (lines above and below a title used
    by lawyers in the UK)

descriptions.text: This package automatically creates tramlines (lines above and below a title used by lawyers in the UK and the Commonwealth).

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: trans
caption: A simple TeX macro package for PostScript transformations

descriptions.text: Macros for easy transformations of PostScript objects, scaling, rotation, etc.

topics.details: support for other packages or for drivers

name: transfig
caption: Transform xfig pictures into many other formats

descriptions.text: Translates figures generated by xfig to a large variety of formats.

topics.details: convert one format of file to another

name: transition-metals
caption: Hybridization diagrams for transition metal complexes

descriptions.text: This package provides tools for drawing hybridization diagrams for transition-metal complexes. From a compact complex specification, it automatically derives the d-electron count, spin state, magnetic behaviour, effective atomic number, and the orbitals involved in hybridization.

caption: French translation of the documentation of Tabbing

descriptions.text: A translation to French (by the author) of the documentation of the Tabbing package.

topics.details: translation of material from the archive, to another language

name: translations
caption: Internationalisation of LaTeX2e packages

descriptions.text:
This package (once part of the exsheets package), provides a framework for providing multilingual features to a LaTeX package.

The package has its own basic dictionaries for English, Brazilian, Catalan, Dutch, French, German and Spanish; it aims to use translation material for English, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Catalan, Turkish, Croatian, Hungarian, Danish and Portuguese from babel or polyglossia if either is in use in the document. (Additional languages from the multilingual packages may be possible: ask the author.)

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: translator
caption: Easy translation of strings in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package provides a flexible mechanism for translating individual words into different languages. For example, it can be used to translate a word like figure into, say, the German word Abbildung. Such a translation mechanism is useful when the author of some package would like to localize the package such that texts are correctly translated into the language preferred by the user.

This package is not intended to be used to automatically translate more than a few words.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: transparent
caption: Using a color stack for transparency with pdfTeX

descriptions.text: pdfTeX and LuaTeX support several color stacks. This package shows how a separate color stack can be used for transparency, a property besides color that works across page breaks. If the PDF management is used it can also be used with other engines, but without support for page breaks.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: Transparent-IO
caption: Show for approval the filenames used in \input, \openin, or \openout

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros to make the file I/O in plain TeX more transparent. That is, every \input, \openin, and \openout operation by TeX is presented to the user who must check carefully if the file name of the source is acceptable. The user must sometimes enter additional text and has to specify the file name that the TeX operation should use.

The macros require a complex installation procedure; the package contains sed and bash scripts to do this on a UNIX-like operating system. Every installation is different from any other as password-protected macro names and private messages have to be chosen by the installer. Therefore, the files in the package cannot be used directly. The files carry the extension .org, and only after the user has performed an individual customization for a private installation the changed files are renamed and have the extension .tex. For details see the manual.

name: tree-dvips
caption: Trees and other linguists’ macros

descriptions.text:
The package defines a mechanism for specifying connected trees that uses a tabular environment to generate node positions. The package uses PostScript code, loaded by dvips, so output can only be generated by use of dvips.

The package lingmacros.sty defines a few macros for linguists: \enumsentence for enumerating sentence examples, simple tabular-based non-connected tree macros, and gloss macros.

name: treedef
caption: Macros to typeset trees in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: Macros that were (or seem to have been) the first higher-level means of representing tables in Plain TeX.

name: treesvr
caption: Tree macros

descriptions.text: The package lets you draw binary or ternary trees of any size.

name: treetex-ltx209
caption: Draw horizontally- or vertically-oriented trees

descriptions.text: Allows the automatic layout of n-ary trees with arbitrary node sizes in LaTeX, using an external C program to do much of the hard work.

name: treetex-plain
caption: Draw trees

descriptions.text: Macros to draw trees, within TeX (or LaTeX). The algorithm used is discussed in an accompanying paper (written using LaTeX 2.09).

name: trfsigns
caption: Typeset transform signs

descriptions.text: A package for typesetting various transformation signs for Laplace transforms, Fourier transforms and others.

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: trig
caption: Simple trigonometric functions

descriptions.text:
Provides the trigonometric functions sin, cos and tan, for use in the graphics and graphicx packages.

Before any trigonometric value is used, it must be pre-calculated, so a usage sequence might be \CalculateSin{22.5} ... \UseSin{22.5}; the argument may also be a LaTeX count, as in \UseTan{\value{mycounter}}, or a count register, as in \CalculateCos{\count@}.

The package is part of the latex-graphics bundle, which is one of the collections in the LaTeX required set of packages.

name: trigonometry
caption: Demonstration code for cos and sin in TeX macros

descriptions.text:
A document that both provides macros that are usable elsewhere, and demonstrates the macros.

The code uses the classical analytical expansion of sin and cos (the more recent trig uses a numerical analyst’s expansion).

name: trimspaces
caption: Trim spaces around an argument or within a macro

descriptions.text: A very short package that allows you to expandably remove spaces around a token list (commands are provided to remove spaces before, spaces after, or both); or to remove surrounding spaces within a macro definition, or to define space-stripped macros.

name: trivfloat
caption: Quick float definitions in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The trivfloat package provides a quick method for defining new float types in LaTeX. A single command sets up a new float in the same style as the LaTeX kernel figure and table float types.

The package works with memoir as well as the standard classes.

name: TrivialPursuit
caption: Insert Trivial Pursuit board game

descriptions.text: This is a package to display a Trivial Pursuit board game, with customization.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: trsym
caption: Symbols for transformations

descriptions.text: The bundle provides Metafont source for a small font used for (e.g.) Laplace transformations, together with a LaTeX .fd file and a package providing commands for the symbols’ use in mathematics.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: truchet
caption: Truchet tiling in MetaPost

descriptions.text: These macros were the author's response to a challenge at the 1995 GUTenberg congress; other solutions appeared in Les Cahiers Gutenberg.

topics.details: problems and puzzles, and their solutions

name: truecols
caption: Colour facilities for SliTeX

descriptions.text:
The package offers a means of creating SliTeX slides on a colour printer (SliTeX itself only offers an overlay mechanism for providing colour.)

The package is distributed as a LaTeX 2.09 .doc file (an early form of the .dtx mechanism). Such files are supposed to be runnable without benefit of the precursor docstrip mechanism.

name: truetypemetrics
caption: Metrics for some TrueType font families

descriptions.text:
This package contains metrics for three TrueType font families: Linotype Palatino, Linotype Frutiger and Monotype Berling.

Palatino comes with Microsoft Windows 2000 and XP, the others with Microsoft’s free e-book reader.

The complete (fontinst) sources for these metrics are included in the directory examples/ of the fontools package.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
support is for a font not available on CTAN

name: TrueTypeToType42
caption: Generate a Type 42 font from a TrueType font

descriptions.text: The package provides a PostScript program, to run under ghostscript, that will read a TrueType font and produce an Adobe Type 42 (PFA) font as output.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: truncate
caption: Truncate text to a specified width

descriptions.text: The package will by default break at word boundaries, but package options are offered to permit breaks within words.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: truthtable
caption: Automatically generate truth tables for given variables and statements

descriptions.text: This LuaLaTeX package permits to automatically generate truth tables given a table header. It supports a number of logical operations which can be combined as needed. It is built upon the luacode package.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: TrY
caption: Automation of TeX/LaTeX compilation

descriptions.text: The package offers a script that automates the compilation of TeX/LaTeX documents. TrY reads commands from the comment lines of the document and executes them automatically. TrY may be compared to arara, but is simpler. TrY has been written for Linux and works on Linux.

name: tsconfig
caption: Setup support for TeXshell

descriptions.text: The tsconfig program tries to make the configuration of the TeXshell by J. Schlegelmilch easier, especially if you have a lot of computers with different processors.

name: tsemlines
caption: Support for the ancient \emline macro

descriptions.text:
Occasional Documents appear, that use graphics generated by texcad from the emtex distribution.

These documents often use the \emline macro, which produced lines at an arbitrary orientation. The present package emulates the macro, using TikZ.

name: tsipa
caption: Macros and fonts to produce IPA typesetting

copyright.owner: Kobayashi Hajime, Fukui Rei and Shirakawa Shun

descriptions.text: The tsipa set has been superseded by tipa; see the documentation of that package for an outline of the shortcomings of tsipa, that tipa overcomes.

name: tsvtemplate
caption: Apply a template to a tsv file

descriptions.text:
This is a simple tsv (tab-separated values) reader for LuaLaTeX and plain LuaTeX.

It also supports (non-quoted) comma-separated values, or indeed values separated by any character.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: tt2001
caption: Type 1 EC fonts generated by TeXtrace

descriptions.text:
A TeX font package offering Computer Modern (EC fonts) in Adobe Type 1 format, using T1 and TS1 encoding. It contains Type 1 fonts converted from Metafont fonts and provides all of the EC and TC fonts. The glyph CharStrings are not optimized for size, and there are even some minor visual distortions from the original.

For an alternative, see the cm-super package, which covers the EC/TC family as well as other fonts.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: ttf-howto
caption: Using TrueType fonts with TeX systems

descriptions.text: The document describes how to use TrueType fonts by converting them to Adobe Type 1 format. The instructions seem to be couched in terms of use with MiKTeX, but they should act as a guide for use with other systems where the fonts can be made available. It also describes how to use automatically generated slanted and small capitals versions of the fonts.

topics.details: documentation about choosing installing and using fonts

name: ttf2mf
caption: Convert True Type fonts to Metafont

descriptions.text: A MS-Windows program which converts installed True Type fonts to Metafont format, using Windows API calls.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: ttf2pfb
caption: Make an Adobe Type 1 version of a TrueType font

descriptions.text: Ttf2pfb translates the format of a TrueType font into an Adobe Type 1 font, using the facilities of the freetype library. The package is distributed as a DOS/OS/2 executable.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: ttf2pt1
caption: Convert TrueType fonts to Adobe Type 1 format

copyright.owner: Andrew Weeks, Frank M. Siegert, Thomas Henlich and others

descriptions.text: Converts True Type fonts into PS Type 1 fonts: creates hinting information and AFM files (preserving kerning information); supports a wide range of font encodings; supports Asian fonts.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: ttf2tex
caption: Use TrueType fonts with teTeX

descriptions.text:
This script for the Bash shell was designed to create all files necessary to use TrueType fonts with teTeX from a set of TTF files. It sorted them, build the map files required by ttf2pk and pdfTeX, and optionally install them. The package was designed for UNIX/Linux systems running teTeX.

The package is no longer supported by anyone.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: ttftogf
caption: Convert True Type fonts to GF format

descriptions.text: This is a demo version of a 16-bit Windows application.

topics.details: process fonts for use with TeX (includes installation)

name: tth
caption: A TeX to HTML translator

descriptions.text: Both C source code and compiled executables for Windows and Linux are provided.

name: ttn
caption: TeX and TUG news archive

descriptions.text: TeX and TUG news was a printed bulletin of information about TUG and TeX doings in general. This digest provides sources for the copies that were published (volumes 1–3).

topics.details: sources and/or old copies of journals

name: ttt
caption: A Tibetan Transcript Transliterator for LaTeX

descriptions.text: The transcriptions work with Sirlin's fonts and macros, but the transcriber manages better support (particularly of ligatures) than other approaches to Tibetan.

name: tucv
caption: Support for typesetting a CV or résumeé

descriptions.text:
The package provides commands for typesetting a CV or résumé. It provides commands for general-purpose headings, entries, and item/description pairs, as well as more specific commands for formatting sections, with explicit inclusion of school, degree, employer, job, conference, and publications entries.

It tends to produce a somewhat long and quite detailed document but may also be suitable to support a shorter résumé.

The package relies on a sufficiently recent copy of the l3kernel and l3packages bundles.

name: tuda-ci
caption: LaTeX templates of Technische Universität Darmstadt

descriptions.text:
The TUDa-CI-Bundle provides a possibility to use the Corporate Design of TU Darmstadt in LaTeX.

It contains documentclasses as well as some helper packages and config files together with some templates for user documentation, which currently are only available in German.

name: tudscr
caption: Corporate Design of Technische Universität Dresden

descriptions.text:
The TUD-Script bundle provides both classes and packages in order to create LaTeX documents in the corporate design of the Technische Universität Dresden. It bases on the KOMA-Script bundle, which must necessarily be present.

For questions, problems and comments, please refer to either the LaTeX forum of the Dresden University of Technology or the GitHub tudscr repository.

The bundle offers:

  • the three document classes tudscrartcl, tudscrreprt, and tudscrbook which serve as wrapper classes for scrartcl, scrreprt, and scrbook,
  • the class tudscrposter for creating posters,
  • the package tudscrsupervisor providing environments and macros to create tasks, evaluations and notices for scientific theses,
  • the package tudscrfonts, which makes the corporate design fonts of the Technische Universität Dresden available for LaTeX standard classes and KOMA-Script classes,
  • the package fix-tudscrfonts, which provides the same fonts to additional corporate design classes not related to TUD-Script,
  • the package tudscrcomp, which simplifies the switch to TUD-Script from external corporate design classes,
  • the package mathswap for swapping math delimiters within numbers (similar to ionumbers),
  • the package twocolfix for fixing the positioning bug of headings in twocolumn layout, and
  • a comprehensive user documentation as well as several tutorials.

name: tufte-latex
caption: Document classes inspired by the work of Edward Tufte

copyright.owner: Bil Kleb, Bill Wood and Kevin Godby

descriptions.text: Provided are two classes inspired, respectively, by handouts and books created by Edward Tufte.

name: tugboat
caption: LaTeX macros for TUGboat articles

descriptions.text:
Provides ltugboat.cls for both regular and proceedings issues of the TUGboat journal.

Also provides a BibTeX style, tugboat.bst.

name: tugboat-plain
caption: Plain TeX macros for TUGboat

descriptions.text: The macros defined in this directory (in files tugboat.sty and tugboat.cmn) are used in papers written in Plain TeX for publication in TUGboat.

name: tugboat-toc
caption: An accumulation of TUGboat tables of contents

descriptions.text:
Includes driver files (tbcv*.tex) and the macros for formatting them. Requires plain TeX TUGboat macros.

The collection runs from volume 1 (1980) to volume 37 (2016).

name: tui
caption: Thesis style for the University of the Andes, Colombia

descriptions.text: Clase de Tesis doctorales para ingeniería, Universidad de los Andes, Bogotá.

Doctoral Dissertations from the Faculty of Engineering at the Universidad de los Andes, Bogota, Colombia.

The class is implemented as an extension of the memoir class.

name: tuple
caption: Expandable operations for tuples of numbers

descriptions.text:
Cette extension met à disposition des opérations développables pour les tuples de nombres :

  • len, sum, min, max, mean, med, quantile, écart type, get item, position d’un élément
  • tri, ajout ou modification(*) d’éléments, filtre, opérations, composition(*), coupure(*), formattage et affichage

Le tout avec une syntaxe concise et d'un usage facile et intuitif : 

                    object.methode1.methode2...

(*) : méthode non développable

This package provides expandable operations for tuples of numbers:

  • len, sum, min, max, mean, med, quantile, standard deviation, get item, position of item
  • sort, add or set(*) items, filter, operations, composition(*), split(*), formatting and display

All with a concise syntax that is easy and intuitive to use : 

            object.method1.method2...

(*): unexpandable method

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: turabian
caption: Create Turabian-formatted material using LaTeX

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a class file and a template for creating Turabian-formatted projects. The class file supports citation formatting conforming to the Turabian 8th Edition style guide.

topics.details: paper (simply) for communication, not necessarily for publication

name: turabian-formatting
caption: Formatting based on Turabian’s Manual

descriptions.text: The turabian-formatting package provides Chicago-style formatting based on Kate L. Turabian’s A Manual for Writers of Research Papers, Theses, and Dissertations: Chicago Style for Students and Researchers (9th edition).

name: turkce-sayi
caption: Automatic Turkish suffix handling for reference numbers

descriptions.text:
When a number in a Turkish document is generated by a cross-reference (\ref, \pageref, \cite), the correct form of any appended suffix depends on how that number is pronounced, an information that is not available at the time of editing. Specifying a suffix works for some numbers, but for others it silently results in incorrect output.

This package solves this problem at compile time via LuaTeX. It determines the phonological properties of the Turkish name of the number and applies the appropriate transformation rules.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkish

name: turkish
caption: LaTeX Support for Typesetting Turkish

descriptions.text: Fonts and macros for Ottoman Turkish and Modern Turkish in Roman letter transcription.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkish

name: turkishintro
caption: An introduction to LaTeX, in Turkish

descriptions.text: The present release comprises only volume 1.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkish

name: turkmen
caption: Babel support for Turkmen

descriptions.text: The package provides support for Turkmen in babel, but integration with babel is not available.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkmen
extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: turnstile
caption: Typeset the (logic) turnstile notation

descriptions.text: Among other uses, the turnstile sign is used by logicians for denoting a consequence relation, related to a given logic, between a collection of formulas and a derived formula.

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: turnthepage
caption: Provide <q>turn page</q> instructions

descriptions.text: The package prints a turn instruction at the bottom of odd-numbered pages (except the last). This is a common convention for examination papers and the like.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: tutodoc
caption: Typeset tutorial-like documentations

descriptions.text: This package provides some macros to write documentation of LaTeX packages in a tutorial style.

name: tuzuk
caption: Turkish bylaws and regulations document class

descriptions.text:
The tuzuk class provides a standardized format for writing bylaws and regulations in Turkish-governmental style. It includes features for creating numbered articles, subsections, and signature areas commonly found in legal documents.

Features:

  • Easy creation of numbered articles with the \madde command,
  • Section titles with \bolumadi,
  • Automatic lettered lists with the fikra environment,
  • Built-in signature area formatting with \imzalar,
  • Full Turkish language support.

Built originally for creating the regulation for Özgür Yazılım Derneği (The Free Software Association in Turkey), https://oyd.org.tr/.

Explanation of the package name: tüzük in Turkish means regulations, as a document. For example, GDPR, which stands for General Data Protection Regulation, translates as Genel Veri Koruma Tüzüğü. In Turkish law, the non-profit associations have a tüzük as their constitution-like governing document.

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Turkish
typesetting legal documents or study material

name: TVS
caption: TeX Versioning System

descriptions.text: A Perl script to collect all files which are needed to re-typeset TeX documents. It does it by parsing TeX logs. TVS is able to handle filenames intelligently.

topics.details: pack files up for distribution or archiving

name: tvthesis
caption: A LaTeX class for theses at the Tor Vergata University of Rome

descriptions.text: This package provides a complete LaTeX template for typesetting Master’s and PhD theses at the Università degli Studi di Roma Tor Vergata. It handles title-page layout, front matter, chapter formatting, and all the stylistic requirements of the university.

name: twcal
caption: Calligraphic font for typesetting handwriting

descriptions.text: A calligraphic font, designed in Metafont, which may be used for typesetting what Germans call the vereinfachte Ausgangsschrift. Macros (originally intended for use with LaTeX 2.09) are available.

name: tweb
caption: A web system for TeX macro sources

descriptions.text: Tweb uses noweb to provide a better means of printing TeX macro sources.

name: twemoji-colr
caption: Twemoji font in COLR/CPAL layered format

descriptions.text: This is a COLR/CPAL-based color OpenType font from the Twemoji collection of emoji images.

topics.details: fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: twemojis
caption: Use Twitter’s open source emojis through LaTeX commands

descriptions.text: This package provides a simple wrapper which allows to use Twitter’s open source emojis through LaTeX commands. This relies on images, so no fancy unicode-font stuff is needed and it should work on every installation.

name: twocolumns
caption: Knuth’s two-column output macros

descriptions.text: These are transcribed (by an unknown hand) from chapter 23 of the TeXbook.

topics.details: more than one column on the page
extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: 2in1
caption: Print two pages on a single page

descriptions.text: The package is for printing two pages on a single (landscape) A4 page. Page numbers appear on the included pages, and not on the landscape container page.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: twoopt
caption: Definitions with two optional arguments

descriptions.text:
Variants of \newcommand, \renewcommand and \providecommand are provided.

The package is part of the oberdiek bundle.

name: twoside
caption: Two-side typesetting in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: Defines macros that produce output destined for two-sided printing, with a gutter margin as specified by the user. A running head may also be specified.

topics.details: extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs

name: twoup-gen
caption: Macros to print two-up

descriptions.text: The 2up package offers considerable flexibility as to paper size and layout, and produces a standard dvi file without involving additional dvi or PostScript filters.

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: twoupltx
caption: Print two virtual pages on each physical page

descriptions.text: MiKTeX and many other TeX implementations include tools for massaging PostScript into booklet and two-up printing – that is, printing two logical pages side by side on one side of one sheet of paper. However, some LaTeX preliminaries are necessary to use those tools. The twoup package provides such preliminaries and gives advice on how to use the PostScript tools.

name: twoxtwogame
caption: Visualize 2×2 normal-form games

descriptions.text: This is a package for the visualization of 2×2 normal form games. The package is based on PGF/TikZ and produces beautiful vector graphics that are intended for use in scientific publications. The commands include the creation of graphical representations of 2×2 games, the visualization of equilibria in 2×2 games and game embeddings for 2×2 games.

topics.details: process game diagrams, gamebooks, and other amusements

name: txfonts
caption: Times-like fonts in support of mathematics

descriptions.text:
Txfonts supplies virtual text roman fonts using Adobe Times (or URW NimbusRomNo9L) with some modified and additional text symbols in the OT1, T1, and TS1 encodings; maths alphabets using Times/URW Nimbus; maths fonts providing all the symbols of the Computer Modern and AMS fonts, including all the Greek capital letters from CMR; and additional maths fonts of various other symbols.

The set is complemented by a sans-serif set of text fonts, based on Helvetica/NimbusSanL, and a monospace set.

All the fonts are in Type 1 format (AFM and PFB files), and are supported by TeX metrics (VF and TFM files) and macros for use with LaTeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: txfontsb
caption: Extensions to txfonts, using GNU Freefont

descriptions.text: A set of fonts that extend the txfonts bundle with small caps and old style numbers, together with Greek support. The extensions are made with modifications of the GNU Freefont.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: txgreeks
caption: Shape selection for TX fonts Greek letters

descriptions.text: The package allows LaTeX users who use the TX fonts to select the shapes (italic or upright) for the Greek lowercase and uppercase letters. Once the shapes for lowercase and uppercase have been selected via a package option, the \other prefix (e.g., \otheralpha) allows using the alternate glyph (as in the fourier package). The txgreeks package does not constrain the text font that may be used in the document.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: txp
caption: Draw text along a path

descriptions.text: The txp package provides a general-purpose MetaPost macro to draw abitrary text along a given path.

name: txt
caption: Output documents via terminals, line printers, etc

descriptions.text:
The package provides the means to prepare a DVI file for approximately laid-out monospace font text output. This output could then be converted to text using (for example) dvi2tty and then submitted to a line printer.

The package is incomplete (it relies on a font doc which it refers to as a pseudo-font but nowhere explains where it comes from). Furthermore, it was written for obsolete LaTeX 2.09 (though it runs, modulo the absence of the font) under current LaTeX.

name: txt2latex
caption: Convert text by fixing special chars and quote marks

descriptions.text: This is a small Perl script intended to facilitate batch conversion of largely unformatted ASCII text for use with LaTeX. In contrast to txt2tex, it does not assume the document has any underlying structure. Its sole purpose is to escape special LaTeX characters and to fix single and double quotation marks.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: txt2tex
caption: Add LaTeX markup to plain text

descriptions.text: Converts plain text into something with a little LaTeX formatting.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: TXUprCal
caption: Upright calligraphic font based on TX calligraphic

descriptions.text: This small package provides a means of loading as \mathcal upright versions of the calligraphic fonts from the TX font package. A scaled option to provided to allow arbitrary scaling.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: type1cm
caption: Arbitrary size font selection in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
LaTeX, by default, restricts the sizes at which you can use its default computer modern fonts, to a fixed set of discrete sizes (effectively, a set specified by Knuth). The type1cm package removes this restriction; this is particularly useful when using scalable versions of the cm fonts (Bakoma, or the versions from BSR/Y&Y, or True Type versions from Kinch, PCTeX, etc.). In fact, since modern distributions will automatically generate any bitmap font you might need, type1cm has wider application than just those using scaleable versions of the fonts.

Note that the LaTeX distribution now contains a package fix-cm, which performs the task of type1cm, as well as doing the same job for T1- and TS1-encoded ec fonts.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: type1ec
caption: Permit EC, TC and LH fonts at arbitrary sizes

descriptions.text:
Generates LaTeX font sizing instructions that allow any size to be scaled.

This package is part of the cm-super distribution.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: typearea
caption: Set page margins

descriptions.text: Typearea is a part of the koma-script bundle, and is well integrated with the requirements of classes in the bundle, but it is also convenient for use as a package in its own right.

name: typed-checklist
caption: Typesetting tasks, goals, milestones, artifacts, and more in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The main goal of this package is to provide means for typesetting checklists in a way that stipulates users to explicitly distinguish checklists for goals, for tasks, for artifacts, and for milestones – i.e., the type of checklist entries.

The intention behind this is that a user of the package is coerced to think about what kind of entries he/she adds to the checklist. This shall yield a clearer result and, in the long run, help with training to distinguish entries of different types.

name: typedref
caption: Eliminate errors by enforcing the types of labels

descriptions.text: The package is provided to help users avoid cross-reference errors; it replaces \ref with \figureref, \sectionref, \eqref, etc., so that you're forced to specify the kind of label you’re referencing. Each reference command also generates appropriate text automatically, so that instead of typing Figure~\ref{figure:key}, all you need is \figureref{figure:key}. The \label command is redefined to record the type with the label defined, so that each type of label has its own namespace.

name: typeface
caption: Select a balanced set of fonts

descriptions.text:
The package provides the means of establishing a consistent set of fonts for use in a LaTeX document. It allows mixing and matching the Type 1 font sets available on the archive (and it may be extended, via its configuration file, to support other fonts).

Font-set definition takes the form of a set of options that are read when the package is loaded: for each typographic category (main body font, sans-serif font, monospace font, mathematics fonts, text figures, and so on), a font or a transformation is given in those options.

The approach enables the user to remember their own configurations (as a single command) and to borrow configurations that other users have developed.

The present release is designated for review.

documentation.details: Properties of fonts that are available

name: typehtml
caption: Typeset HTML directly from LaTeX

descriptions.text: Can handle almost all of HTML2, and most of the math fragment of the draft HTML3.

topics.details: import files in a non-TeX (or different TeX) format

name: typeoutfileinfo
caption: Display class/package/file information

descriptions.text:
The package provides a minimalist shell script, for Unix systems, that displays the information content in a \ProvidesFile, \ProvidesPackage or \ProvidesClass command in a LaTeX source file.

The package requires that the readprov package is available.

name: typespec
caption: Create font samplers

descriptions.text: Creates a type specimen page with useful information about the typeface.

name: typewriter
caption: Typeset with a randomly variable monospace font

descriptions.text: The typewriter package uses the OpenType Computer Modern Unicode Typewriter font, together with a LuaTeX virtual font setup that introduces random variability in grey level and angle of each character. It was originally an answer to a question on stackexchange.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: typicons
caption: Font containing a set of web-related icons

descriptions.text:
This package grants access to 336 web-related icons provided by the included Typicons free font, designed by Stephen Hutchings and released under the SIL Open Font License. See http://www.typicons.com for more details about the font itself.

This package requires the fontspec package and either the Xe(La)TeX or Lua(La)TeX engine to load the included ttf font.

Once the package is loaded, icons can be accessed through the general \ticon command, which takes as argument the name of the desired icon, or through direct commands specific to each icon. The full list of icon designs, names and direct commands is showcased in the manual.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts
fonts that provide collections of symbols

name: typoaid
caption: Macros for font diagnostics

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros for measuring alphabet lengths (i.e. the length occupied by the characters abcd…xyz), em-widths and ex-heights, which may help in making typesetting decisions.

The package is compatible with pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX, and will accept font family switches defined via the fontspec package.

The plan is that future versions shall be able to provide even more diagnostic tools, and some LuaTeX-specific special commands, too.

The package relies on the following other LaTeX packages: expl3, array, booktabs, and siunitx.

topics.details: support for font development, testing and characterisation

name: typog
caption: Typographic fine-tuning and micro-typographic enhancements

descriptions.text:
This package provides macros for micro-typographic enhancements. It covers a variety of topics:

  • Precise hyphenation control
  • Disable/break ligatures
  • Manual italic correction
  • Extra kerning for slash and hyphen
  • Raising selected characters (e.g. hyphen, en-dash, and em-dash)
  • Aligning of the last line of a paragraph
  • Filling of the last line of a paragraph
  • Word spacing control
  • Microtype front-end
  • Slightly sloppy paragraphs
  • Vertically partially-tied paragraphs
  • Breakable displayed equations
  • Setspace front-end
  • Smooth ragged-right paragraphs

Moreover, typog provides an environment to flag interesting parts of the information deluge typically accumulating in a LaTeX log-file and an associated tool, typog-grep, that selectively retrieves these parts.

name: typografie
caption: A tutorial on typography

descriptions.text: The script of a tutorial held at the 1999 DANTE meeting by Axel Reichert on how to create a new documentclass in LaTeX with some examples (in German).

name: typogrid
caption: Print a typographic grid

descriptions.text: Draws a grid on every page of the document; the grid divides the page into columns, and may be used for fixing measurements of layout.

name: typstfun
caption: List of equivalent Typst function names of LaTeX commands

descriptions.text: This documentation lists equivalent Typst function names of LaTeX commands. Only math symbols provided by the LaTeX format or the amsmath bundle are included.

name: tzplot
caption: Plot graphs with TikZ abbreviations

descriptions.text:
This is a LaTeX package that provides TikZ-based macros to make it easy to draw graphs. The macros provided in this package are just abbreviations for TikZ codes, which can be complicated; but using the package will hopefully make drawing easier, especially when drawing repeatedly. The macros were chosen and developed with an emphasis on drawing graphs in economics.

The package depends on TikZ, xparse, and expl3.

topics.details: plot a representation of a function

name: u8tex
caption: Input Unicode characters in TeX notation, in emacs

descriptions.text: A file to provide an alternative, TeX-style, input method for UTF-8 characters in Otfried Cheong's extension of Mule-UCS.

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

name: uaclasses
caption: University of Arizona thesis and dissertation format

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX2e document class named ua-thesis for typesetting theses and dissertations in the official format required by the University of Arizona. Moreover, there is a fully compatible alternative document class my-thesis for private nice copies of the dissertation, and the respective title pages are available as separate packages to work with any document class.

name: uafthesis
caption: Document class for theses at University of Alaska Fairbanks

descriptions.text: This is an unofficial official class.

name: uAlberta
caption: A LaTeX template for the University of Alberta

descriptions.text: This package provides a comprehensive template designed to meet the formatting requirements of the University of Alberta ( https://www.ualberta.ca/en/graduate-studies/resources/graduate-students/thesis-preparation-requirements-deadlines/index.html) for MSc and PhD theses. It provides a structured and customizable framework that ensures compliance with university guidelines while allowing flexibility in document formatting.

name: uantwerpendocs
caption: Course texts, master theses, and exams in University of Antwerp style

descriptions.text: These class files implement the house style of the University of Antwerp. This package originated from the Faculty of Applied Engineering. Using these class files will make it easy for you to make and keep your documents compliant to this version and future versions of the house style of the University of Antwerp. This includes classes for course texts, master theses, phd theses, exams, reports and a beamer theme for slides.

name: uassign
caption: Environments and options for typesetting university assignments

descriptions.text: The purpose of this package is to provide simple question and solution style environments for typesetting university assignments.

name: ucalgmthesis
caption: LaTeX thesis class for University of Calgary Faculty of Graduate Studies

descriptions.text:
ucalgmthesis.cls is a LaTeX class file that produces documents according to the thesis guidelines of the University of Calgary Faculty of Graduate Studies.

It uses the memoir class, which provides very powerful and flexible mechanisms for book design and layout. All memoir commands for changing chapter and section headings, page layout, fancy foot- and endnotes, typesetting poems, etc., can be used. (Memoir is meant as a replacement for the standard LaTeX classes, so all standard LaTeX commands such as \chapter, \section, etc., still work.) Likewise, any of memoir’s class options can be passed as options to ucalgmthesis, in particular 12pt to select 12 point type (11 point is the default).

name: ucbthesis
caption: Thesis and dissertation class supporting UCB requirements

copyright.owner: Daniel Gildea, Ethan Munson, Paul Vojta

descriptions.text:
