The class provides the necessary framework for electronic submission of Masters theses and Ph.D. dissertations at the University of California, Berkeley.

It is based on the memoir class.

name: ucdavisthesis
caption: A thesis/dissertation class for University of California at Davis

descriptions.text: The ucdavisthesis class is a LaTeX class that allows you to create a dissertation or thesis conforming to UC Davis formatting requirements as of April 2016.

name: ucharcat
caption: Implementation of the (new in 2015) XeTeX \Ucharcat command in Lua, for LuaTeX

descriptions.text: The package implements the \Ucharcat command for LuaLaTeX. \Ucharcat is a new primitive in XeTeX, an extension of the existing \Uchar command, that allows the specification of the catcode as well as character code of the character token being constructed.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: ucharclasses
caption: Font actions in XeTeX according to what is being processed

descriptions.text: The package takes care of switching fonts when you switch from one Unicode block to another in the text of a document. This way, you can write a document with no explicit font selection, but a series of rules of the form when entering block …, switch font to use ….

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: ucph-revy
caption: Musical script formatting

descriptions.text: This package provides a class for typesetting scripts containing both lyrics and prose, in the style used by the student revues (revy) at the Faculties of Science at the University of Copenhagen (uchp).

name: ucs
caption: Extended UTF-8 input encoding support for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides the ucs package, and utf8x.def, together with a large number of support files.

The utf8x.def definition file for use with inputenc covers a wider range of Unicode characters than does utf8.def in the LaTeX distribution. The package provides facilities for efficient use of its large sets of Unicode characters.

Glyph production may be controlled by various options, which permits use of non-ASCII characters when coding mathematical formulae.

Note that the bundle previously had an alias unicode ; that alias has now been withdrawn, and no package of that name now exists.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: ucsmonograph
caption: Typesetting academic documents from the University of Caxias do Sul

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX class for typesetting academic documents according to the ABNT (Brazilian Technical Standards Association) standards and the UCS (University of Caxias do Sul) specifications.

name: ucthesis
caption: University of California thesis format

descriptions.text: A modified version of the standard LaTeX report style that is accepted for use with University of California PhD dissertations and Masters theses. A sample dissertation source and bibliography are provided.

name: ucthesis209
caption: LaTeX 2.09 document style for UC Theses

descriptions.text: An obsolescent LaTeX 2.09 predecessor of the current University of California thesis class; the latest version of the package seems to have been released as the current one was being developed.

name: udepcolor
caption: University of Piura (UDEP) institutional and corporate colors for digital and electronic media

descriptions.text:
This package defines University of Piura (UDEP) institutional and corporate colors for digital and electronic media according to brand and style guidelines published by UDEP DIRCOM.

The colors have been selected and implemented using the xcolor package and following the brand and visual identity guidelines of the University of Piura.

name: udes-genie-these
caption: A thesis class file for the Faculté de génie at the Université de Sherbrooke

descriptions.text:
The udes-genie-these class can be used for Ph.D. theses, master’s theses and project definitions at the Faculté de génie of the Université de Sherbrooke (Québec, Canada). The class file is coherent with the latest version of the Protocole de rédaction aux études supérieures which is available on the faculté’s intranet.

The class file documentation is in French, the language of the typical user at the Université de Sherbrooke. An example of use is also distributed with the documentation.

name: udesoftec
caption: Thesis class for the University of Duisburg-Essen

descriptions.text:
The class is designed for typesetting theses in the Research Group for Business Informatics and Software Engineering. (The class may also serve as a template for such theses.)

The class is designed for use with pdfLaTeX; input in UTF-8 encoding is assumed.

name: udiss
caption: A LaTeX bundle for typesetting dissertations

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: The udiss bundle is a LaTeX-class-file developed to assist students in typesetting their university dissertations. It is a collection of multiple support files. Universities often have strict requirements regarding the formatting of the dissertations/theses submitted to them. This bundle pre-supplies a generic style (university-agnostic) for creating dissertations. It also supports custom layouts required for different universities.

name: uebungsblatt
caption: A LaTeX class for writing exercise sheets

descriptions.text:
This package implements a LaTeX class for writing exercise sheets for a lecture.

Features:

  • quick typesetting of exercise sheets or their revisions,
  • simple user friendly commands,
  • elegant page formatting,
  • automatic numbering of exercises and sub-exercises,
  • the number of the exercise sheet is extracted automatically from the file name,
  • static information about the lectures and the authors needs to provided at one point only.

name: uestcthesis
caption: Thesis class for UESTC

descriptions.text: The class is for typesetting a thesis at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

name: ufrgscca
caption: A bundle for undergraduate students final work/report (tcc) at UFRGS/EE

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License, version 3

descriptions.text: This bundle is aimed at producing undergraduate students’ final work/report at UFRGS/EE (Engineering School at the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul), closely following ABNT rules (Brazilian Association for Technical Norms). It is composed of a main class, ufrgscca, and a set of auxiliary packages, some of which can be used independently.

name: ugarite
caption: Fonts for Ugaritic cuneiform script

descriptions.text:
Fonts (both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format) and macros for Ugaritic cuneiform writing. This script was in use about 1300 BCE.

This is one of a series of archaic fonts.

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: ugaritic
caption: A font for Ugaritic

descriptions.text: This is a Metafont source to generate Ugaritic script, which is a cuneiform alphabet.

topics.details: fonts reproducing archaic scripts or inscriptions

name: uhc
caption: Fonts for the Korean language

descriptions.text: Support for Korean documents written in Korean standard KSC codes for LaTeX2e.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: uhhassignment
caption: A document class for typesetting homework assignments

descriptions.text: This document class was created for typesetting solutions to homework assignments at the university of Hamburg (Universität Hamburg).

name: uhrzeit
caption: Time printing, in German

descriptions.text: The primary goal of this package is to facilitate formats and ranges of times as formerly used in Germany. A variety of printing formats are available.

name: uhthesis
caption: University of Houston thesis document style

descriptions.text: The LaTeX 2.09 style is said to be for University of Houston PhD and MS theses; it is derived from the standard report style.

name: uiucredborder
caption: Class for UIUC thesis red-bordered forms

descriptions.text: The class offers a means of filling out the red-bordered form that gets signed by the department head, your advisor, and – for doctoral dissertations – your thesis committee members.

name: uiucthesis
caption: UIUC thesis class

descriptions.text: The class produces a document that conforms to the format described in the University's Handbook for Graduate Students Preparing to Deposit.

name: ukbill
caption: A class for typesetting UK legislation

descriptions.text: This package provides formatting to easily typeset draft UK legislation. The libre font Palatine Parliamentary is required to use this package.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: ukdate
caption: Typeset date in a UK-ish form

descriptions.text:
Prints dates in a traditional English way: <day-of-week> <ordinal-day-of-month> <month> <year>, so for example Thursday 2nd February 2006. The ordinal letters (nd in the example) are underlined and raised.

Note that Babel British style also has an English date style, which has no day name, and which doesn't raise or underline the ordinal letters.

name: ukhyph
caption: Hyphenation patterns for British English

descriptions.text:
These patterns were derived from a word-division list generously provided by the Oxford University Press (for the purpose of generating these patterns, only). British English hyphenation differs from the default patterns provided with TeX, in that they are etymologically based; American patterns tend to be more pragmatically derived.

Version 2 has added a short list of hyphenation exceptions.

name: ukrhyph
caption: Hyphenation Patterns for Ukrainian

descriptions.text: A range of patterns, depending on the encoding of the output font (including the standard T2A, so one can use the patterns with free fonts).

topics.details: documentation in, and support for typesetting Ukrainian

name: UK-TeX
caption: The UK TeX digest

descriptions.text:
The UK TeX digest started (at a time when TeXhax was also available), at least partly justified by the oddities of internet access in the UK. The organisation of the digest was odd: a team of enthusiasts tried to provide answers to questions before the digest was published, so that readers would encounter a problem closely followed by a solution in the same issue.

Eventually, the UK TeX digest was merged with the TeXhax digest, and the merged list was run in the UK for a time, but without the distinctive experts group.

The archives are arranged by year, and run from 1987 to 1994.

name: uktug-bask
caption: Old copies and sources of Baskerville

descriptions.text: The source and PDF files of the UK TUG journal Baskerville, from volume 3 to volume 8.

topics.details: sources and/or old copies of journals

name: ulem
caption: Package for underlining

descriptions.text:
The package provides an \ul (underline) command which will break over line ends; this technique may be used to replace \em (both in that form and as the \emph command), so as to make output look as if it comes from a typewriter. The package also offers double and wavy underlining, and striking out (line through words) and crossing out (/// over words).

The package works with both Plain TeX and LaTeX.

name: ullrcorners
caption: Draw corners on the upper left and lower right sides of a word

descriptions.text: The package provides a command to surround a word or a sequence or words by small corners on the upper left and lower right sides. The typographical convention is inspired by Mastering Regular Expressions, by Jeffrey E. F. Friedl (O'Reilly Media, 2006), where it is used to delimit regular expressions.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: ulqda
caption: Support of Qualitative Data Analysis

descriptions.text:
The package is for use in Qualitative Data Analysis research. It supports the integration of Qualitative Data Analysis (QDA) research tasks, specifically for Grounded Theory, into the LaTeX work flow.

It assists in the analysis of textual data such as interview transcripts and field notes by providing the LaTeX user with macros which are used to markup textual information – for example, in-depth interviews.

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: ulsy
caption: Extra mathematical characters

descriptions.text:
Metafont source for the font, and LaTeX support. The font contains a contradiction symbol at various sizes, and an odplus symbol.

An autotraced outline version of the fonts is available in ulsy-ps.

name: ulsy-ps
caption: Extra mathematical characters in Adobe Type 1 format

descriptions.text: These are autotraced versions of the ulsy fonts.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: ulthese
caption: Thesis class and templates for Université Laval

descriptions.text: The package provides a class based on memoir to prepare theses and memoirs compliant with the presentation rules set forth by the Faculty of Graduate Studies of Université Laval, Québec, Canada. The class also comes with an extensive set of templates for the various types of theses and memoirs offered at Laval. Please note that the documentation for the class and the comments in the templates are all written in French, the language of the target audience.

name: Ultra-TeX
caption: An emacs TeX mode with <q>lightning completion</q>

descriptions.text: Ultra-TeX is an Emacs mode, a distant relation of AUC-Tex, with several enhancements (relative to the version it started from) and with a lightning completion mode that doesn't wait for a request for completion (the request is typically expressed by pressing the tab key).

topics.details: plug-ins for editors, for better (La)TeX and Meta* support

name: umbclegislation
caption:
A LaTeX class for building legislation files for UMBC Student
    Government Association Bills

descriptions.text:
LaTeX class for building legislation files for UMBC Student Government Association Bills.

Requires pdflatex and the mdframed enumitem, lineno, and xifthen packages.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: umich-thesis
caption: University of Michigan Thesis LaTeX class

descriptions.text: A LaTeX2e class to create a University of Michigan dissertation according to the Rackham dissertation handbook.

name: UML
caption: UML diagrams in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A PSTricks related package for writing UML (Unified Modelling Language) diagrams in LaTeX. Currently, it implements a subset of class diagrams, and some extra constructs as well.

The package cannot be used together with pst-uml.

topics.details: support for Universal Modelling Language diagrams
package using PStricks for graphical output

name: umlaute
caption: German input encodings in LaTeX

descriptions.text:
An early package for using alternate input encodings.

The author considers the package mostly obsolete, since most of its functions are taken by the inputenc package; however, inputenc doesn't support the roman8 and atari encodings, so umlaute remains the sole source of that support.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: umoline
caption: Underline text allowing line breaking

descriptions.text: Provides commands \Underline, \Midline and \Overline for underlining, striking out, and overlining their text arguments.

name: umrand
caption: Package for fancy box frames

descriptions.text:
The package includes both Metafont sources of the fonts and support macros.

An Adobe Type 1 version of the fonts is available in the niceframe fonts bundle.

topics.details: highlighting typeset material, fancy frames, watermarks, etc.

name: umthesis
caption: Dissertations at the University of Michigan

descriptions.text: The class loads book class, and makes minimal changes to it; its coding aims to be as robust as possible, and as a result it has few conflicts with potential add-on packages.

name: umtypewriter
caption: Fonts to typeset with the xgreek package

descriptions.text:
The UMTypewriter font family is a monospaced font family that was built from glyphs from the CB Greek fonts, the CyrTUG Cyrillic alphabet fonts (LH), and the standard Computer Modern font family.

It contains four OpenType fonts which are required for use of the xgreek package for XeLaTeX.

topics.details: fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts
font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: unam-thesis
caption: Create documents according to the UNAM guidelines

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: This is a class for creating dissertation documents according to the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) guidelines.

name: unamth-template
caption: UNAM Thesis LaTeX Template

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a template for UNAM’s College of Engineering Theses.

The work is based on Harish Bhanderi's PhD/MPhil template, then University of Cambridge.

name: unamthesis
caption: Style for Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico theses

descriptions.text: The package provides a customisable format to typeset Theses according to the Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico guidelines. Support for use in Scientific Workplace (SWP) 3.x is also provided. The bundle also includes an appropriate bibliographic style which enables the use of author-year schemes using the natbib package.

name: UnBTeX
caption: A class for theses at University of Brasilia (UnB)

descriptions.text:
This package provides a class based on abnTeX and compatible with pdflatex and BibTeXr to prepare bachelor, master, and doctoral theses for the University of Brasilia (UnB), Brazil. The class also comes with a template for the various types of theses for undergraduate and graduate programs at UnB.

The documentation for the class and the comments in the templates are all written in Portuguese, the language of the target audience.

name: uncial
caption: Uncial manuscript book-hand font

descriptions.text:
The uncial and alluncl packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Uncial manuscript book-hand used between the 3rd and 6th century AD. The font consists of minuscules and digits, with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided.

This is one of a set of manuscript fonts. Access to the docmfp package is desirable but not essential.

topics.details: fonts of scripts used for manuscript books

name: undar-digitacion
caption: Musical fingering diagrams of Pinkullo Huanuqueño, Flute (Recorder), Quena and Saxophone

copyright.owner: Aland Bravo Vecorena, Fredy Romulo Marcellini Morales,     Roberto Carlos Cardenas Viviano, Felix Hipolito Echevarria Ramirez

descriptions.text:
The package provides tools for generating:

  • Pinkullo Huanuqueño
  • Flute
  • Quena
  • Saxophone

The result will often be a PDF (or set of PDFs) that contain everything one will need for musical fingering diagrams of the Pinkullo Huanuqueño, Flute, Quena and Saxophone.

The package uses TikZ for most things and MusixTeX for music symbols.

name: undergradmath
caption: LaTeX Math for Undergraduates cheat sheet

descriptions.text: This is a cheat sheet for writing mathematics with LaTeX. It is aimed at US undergraduates.

topics.details: construction or application of mathematical symbols

name: underlin
caption: Underlined running heads

descriptions.text: Defines two pagestyles that provide underlined page heads in LaTeX.

name: underlin-generic
caption: Multi-word underlining

descriptions.text:
Provides a simple command \textul that will underline a multi-word argument, allowing line breaks between words.

The ulem package also provides this function (among others) in generic context; soul does the job, but is a LaTeX-only package.

name: underoverlap
caption: Position decorations over and under expressions

descriptions.text: The package overcomes TeX’s inherent limitations in commands that place decorations (such as braces) at arbitrary positions over and under expressions, overlapping as necessary.

name: underscore
caption: Control the behaviour of <q>_</q> in text

descriptions.text:
With the package, \_ in text mode (i.e., \textunderscore) prints an underscore so that hyphenation of words either side of it is not affected; a package option controls whether an actual hyphenation point appears after the underscore, or merely a break point.

The package also arranges that, while in text, _ itself behaves as \textunderscore (the behaviour of _ in maths mode is not affected).

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: undertilde
caption: Typeset a tilde under one (or many) maths symbols

descriptions.text: The implementation is probably less than totally robust, though undoubtedly better than that in the generic undertilde macros also available on CTAN.

name: undertilde-gen
caption: A simple macro for placing a tilde under a character

descriptions.text:
The code creates a \mathord at standard size (no attempt to adjust for different contexts in a mathematical expression).

Benjamin Bayart's undertilde (for all its faults) does the job better – the general user could easily remove the LaTeX mechanisms from the file.

name: undolabl
caption: Override existing labels

descriptions.text: The package allows the user to override existing labels (for example, those generated automatically).

name: undump
caption: Make a new executable with format loaded

descriptions.text:
Undump implements the pre-web2c mechanism for generating a new executable from an existing executable and a core dump. The output executable contains all the memory allocated by the run of the executable (up to its crash), and starts at main().

Different Unix styles (of the time) each had their own undump routine.

name: unfinished
caption: Mark unfinished parts of a document

descriptions.text: The package provides an unfinishedenvironment convenient for marking unfinished sections of a document. The environment complains if it thinks the document is not marked as a draft (in the sense of having \overfullrule non-zero.

name: unfonts-core
caption: TrueType version of Un-fonts

descriptions.text:
The Un-fonts come from the HLaTeX as type1 fonts in 1998 by Koaunghi Un, he made type1 fonts to use with Korean TeX (HLaTeX) in the late 1990's and released it under the GPL license.

They were converted to TrueType with the FontForge (PfaEdit) by Won-kyu Park in 2003.

Core families (9 fonts):

  • UnBatang, UnBatangBold: serif
  • UnDotum, UnDotumBold: sans-serif
  • UnGraphic, UnGraphicBold: sans-serif style
  • UnPilgi, UnPilgiBold: script
  • UnGungseo: cursive, brush-stroke

name: unfonts-extra
caption: TrueType version of Un-fonts

descriptions.text:
The Un-fonts come from the HLaTeX as type1 fonts in 1998 by Koaunghi Un, he made type1 fonts to use with Korean TeX (HLaTeX) in the late 1990's and released it under the GPL license.

They were converted to TrueType with the FontForge (PfaEdit) by Won-kyu Park in 2003.

Extra families (10 fonts):

  • UnPen, UnPenheulim: script
  • UnTaza: typewriter style
  • UnBom: decorative
  • UnShinmun
  • UnYetgul: old Korean printing style
  • UnJamoSora, UnJamoNovel, UnJamoDotum, UnJamoBatang

name: uni-titlepage
caption: Universal titlepages with configuration options and predefined styles

descriptions.text:
Creation of title pages is something most authors should not have to do. But reality is not perfect, so a lot of authors have to do it.

This package not only provides several pages for the title instead of only one – at least five are typical for a thesis! –, it also provides a bunch of predefined titlepage styles with several standard elements, and optionally additional elements.

name: uni-wtal-ger
caption: Citation style for literary studies at the University of Wuppertal

descriptions.text: The package defines a BibLaTeX citation style based on the author-title style of biblatex-dw. The citations are optimised for literary studies in faculty of humanities at the Bergische Universität Wuppertal.

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: uni-wtal-lin
caption: Citation style for linguistic studies at the University of Wuppertal

descriptions.text: The package defines a BibLaTeX citation style based on the standard author-year style. The citations are optimised for linguistic studies at the Institute of Linguistics at the Bergische Universität Wuppertal.

topics.details: support for studies in the humanities

name: unibidi-lua
caption: Unicode bidi algorithm implementation for various LuaTeX formats

descriptions.text: This Lua module is an implementation of the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm, based on the ConTeXt project's implementation, adapted for use in various LuaTeX formats. The core Lua module also works with texlua and plain Lua.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: unicode
caption: Extended UTF-8 input encoding for LaTeX

descriptions.text: This bundle has been renamed to ucs, to which users should switch (note that the package name has not changed, merely that of the enclosing bundle).

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: unicode-alphabets
caption: Macros for using characters from Unicode’s Private Use Area

descriptions.text:
While Unicode supports the vast majority of use cases, there are certain specialized niches which require characters and glyphs not (yet) represented in the standard. Thus the Private Use Area (PUA) at code points E000–F8FF, which enables third parties to define arbitrary character sets.

This package allows configuring a number of macros for using various PUA character sets in LaTeX (AGL, CYFI, MUFI, SIL, TITUS, UCSUR, UNZ), to enable transcription and display of medieval and other documents.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: unicode-bidi
caption: Experimental unicode bidi package for XeTeX

descriptions.text: The experimental unicode-bidi package allows to mix non-RTL script with RTL script without any markup.

name: unicode-data
caption: Unicode data and loaders for TeX

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides generic access to Unicode Consortium data for TeX use. It contains a set of text files provided by the Unicode Consortium which are currently all from Unicode 8.0.0, with the exception of MathClass.txt which is not currently part of the Unicode Character Database.

Accompanying these source data are generic TeX loader files allowing this data to be used as part of TeX runs, in particular in building format files. Currently there are two loader files: one for general character set up and one for initialising XeTeX character classes as has been carried out to date by unicode-letters.tex.

The source data are distributed in accordance with the license stipulated by the Unicode Consortium. The bundle as a whole is co-ordinated by the LaTeX3 Project as a general resource for TeX users.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX

name: unicode-math
caption: Unicode mathematics support for XeTeX and LuaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides a comprehensive implementation of unicode maths for XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. Unicode maths requires an OpenType mathematics font, of which there are now a number available via CTAN.

While backwards compatibility is strived for, there are some differences between the legacy mathematical definitions in LaTeX and amsmath, and the Unicode mathematics definitions. Care should be taken when transitioning from a legacy workflow to a Unicode-based one.

documentation.details: List of symbols defined by the package

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
LuaTeX and packages that require it
XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: unicode-math-input
caption: Allow entering Unicode symbols in math formulas

descriptions.text: This package allows entering Unicode symbols in math formulas. Unlike the unicode-math package, this does not change the math output encoding.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: unicodefonttable
caption: A Unicode font table generator

descriptions.text:
This package produces font tables for unicode fonts as well as for 8bit fonts. The table layout can be adjusted in various ways including restricting the range of output to show only a portion of a specific font.

To quickly produce a one-off table there is a stand-alone version unicodefont.tex that asks you a few questions and then generates the table – somewhat similar to nfssfont.tex for 8-bit fonts.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
lists of glyphs available from font(s)

name: UniFiTh
caption: Typeset theses for University of Florence (Italy)

descriptions.text: The package provides a class to typeset Ph.D., Master, and Bachelor theses that adhere to the publishing guidelines of the University of Florence (Italy).

name: unifront
caption: Give notes a unique front page for every chapter and section

descriptions.text:
This package can help you format your notes easily and give them a unique front page for every chapter and section.

It calculates your progress and then displays the progress bar under the title.

It also displays a partial table of contents under every progress bar and only shows the subdirectories of the current part.

To generate this, you can simply enter your current completed titles with a command that accepts Variable Arguments. Still, that also helps you review your notes.

You can also customise the colour of the bar.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)
deal with Tables of Contents, and of other such things

name: unigrazpub
caption: LaTeX templates for University of Graz Library Publishing Services

descriptions.text: This package provides a LaTeX class matching the preparation guidelines of the Library Publishing Services of University of Graz. The bundle also includes a comprehensive set of example files for books and collections.

name: unimath-plain-xetex
caption: OpenType math support in (plain) XeTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides OpenType math font support in plain TeX format. It only works with the XeTeX engine.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
extensions to Plain TeX for higher-level constructs
XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: uninormalize
caption: Unicode normalization support

descriptions.text: This package provides Unicode normalization (useful for composed characters) for LuaLaTeX.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: uniquecounter
caption: Provides unlimited unique counter

descriptions.text: This package provides a kind of counter that provides unique number values. Several counters can be created with different names. The numeric values are not limited.

name: unisc
caption: Unicode small caps with Lua/XeLaTeX

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: LaTeX produces small caps with \textsc{text} or {\scshape text}. Neither of these commands produce small caps in Unicode. If the output text is copied and pasted somewhere it shows the same characters as used in the input. This package aims to internally convert all the characters provided to the commands mentioned above. It assumes that the file using this package is compiled with Lua/XeLaTeX and a good Unicode font which has the small caps characters, e.g., Charis SIL.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: unisugar
caption: Define syntactic sugar for Unicode LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package allows the user to define shorthand aliases for single Unicode characters, and also provides support for such aliases in RTL-text.

The package requires an TeX-alike system that uses Unicode input in a native way: current examples are XeTeX and LuaTeX.

name: unitconv
caption: Convert a length into one with another unit

descriptions.text:
This package defines two macros to convert a value with unit into one with another unit. Supported are all TeX-related units, and also km and m. The output can be in scientific notation for large values.

The package only works with LuaLaTeX!

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: unitipa
caption: TIPA typefaces with Unicode characters as input

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text: A(n obsolete) package which used to provide a LuaLaTeX based code for converting Unicode IPA input to T3 encoded TIPA typefaces, but it is recommended to use CMU with Xe/LuaLaTeX instead for a better output.

topics.details: Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it
LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: unitn-bimrep
caption: A bimonthly report class for the PhD School of Materials, Mechatronics and System Engineering

descriptions.text: This package allows to rapidly write the bimonthly report for The Ph.D. School in Materials, Mechatronics and System Engineering. It allows to define the research activities, the participation to school and congress, and the publication performed by a student.

name: units
caption: Typeset units

descriptions.text:
The package is provided as a bundle with the nicefrac package for typing fractions.

Units uses nicefrac in typesetting physical units in a standard-looking sort of way.

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

name: unitsdef
caption: Typesetting units in LaTeX

descriptions.text: Many packages for typesetting units have been written for use in LaTeX2e. Some define macros to typeset a lot of units but do not suit to the actual font settings, some make the characters needed available but do not predefine any unit. This package tries to comply with both requirements. It predefines common units, defines an easy to use interface to define new units and changes the output concerning to the surrounding font settings.

topics.details: support for writers of scientific documents

name: universa
caption: Herbert Bayer’s <q>universal</q> font

descriptions.text: An implementation of the universal font by Herbert Bayer of the Bauhaus school. The Metafont sources of the fonts, and their LaTeX support, are all supplied in a LaTeX documented source (.dtx) file.

name: universalis
caption: Universalis font, with support

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer

descriptions.text: This package provides LaTeX, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX support for the UniversalisADFStd family of fonts, designed by Hirwin Harendal. The font is suitable as an alternative to fonts such as Adrian Frutiger's Univers and Frutiger.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support
font available in Adobe Type 1 format
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: univie-ling
caption: Papers, theses and research proposals in (Applied) Linguistics at Vienna University

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides LaTeX2e classes, BibLaTeX files, and templates suitable for student papers, PhD research proposals (Exposés), and theses in (Applied) Linguistics at the University of Vienna.

The classes implement some standards for these types of text, such as suitable title pages. They are particularly suited for the field of (Applied) Linguistics and pre-load some packages that are considered useful in this context.

The classes can also be used for General and Historical Linguistics as well as for other fields of study at Vienna University. In this case, however, some settings may have to be adjusted.

topics.details: LaTeX article classes and their developments

name: unixman
caption: Typeset to look like Unix man output

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 document style with commands suited to Unix man output.

name: unizgklasa
caption: A LaTeX class for theses at the Faculty of Graphic Arts in Zagreb

descriptions.text:
This class is intended for generating graduate and final theses according to the instructions of the Faculty of Graphic Arts, University of Zagreb. It does not necessarily correspond to the requirements of each component of the University, but is designed as an idea for linking and uniformizing the look of all graduate papers.

Anyone who likes it is welcome to use it.

name: unouter
caption: Suppress \outer flags in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: The package suppresses all the \outer flags on macros in Plain TeX; it also suppresses the \outer command.

name: unpacked
caption: Unpacked copy of the LaTeX sources

descriptions.text:
This package used to provide the source of LaTeX in its form immediately prior to compilation into a format. When LaTeX2e first appeared, this was a significant support to users (since unpacking used on some machines to take a very long time).

However, the world has moved on since then, most users obtain their LaTeX sources and formats via the distributions, and whoever is still interested in these files can easily obtain them by unpacking latex-base.tds.zip.

name: unravel
caption: Watching TeX digest tokens

descriptions.text:
The aim of this LaTeX package is to help debug complicated macros. This is done by letting the user step through the execution of some TeX code, going through the details of nested expansions, performing assignments, as well as some simple typesetting commands. To use this package, one should normally run TeX in a terminal.

The unravel package requires up-to-date versions of the l3kernel, l3packages and l3experimental bundles.

topics.details: support for package or document debugging

name: unswcover
caption: Typeset a dissertation cover page following UNSW guidelines

descriptions.text:
The package an UNSW cover sheet following the 2011 GRS guidelines.

It may also (optionally) provide other required sheets such as Originality, Copyright and Authenticity statements.

name: unswthesis
caption: UNSW theses

descriptions.text: The directory contains a bundle of things related to UNSW Theses; the author's own thesis was prepared using the class.

name: untex
caption: Strip (La)TeX commands from source file

descriptions.text:
The program will remove some LaTeX commands from a file (it will optionally try to strip out all mathematics, too). It also has an option to honour \input and \include commands in the file.

The program is distributed as C source in a .tar.gz file.

topics.details: derive plain text from a TeX document

name: uol-physics-report
caption: A LaTeX document class for writing lab reports

descriptions.text:
The package provides physics students at the University of Oldenburg with a prepared document class for writing laboratory reports for the laboratory courses conducted by the Institute of Physics.

The document class consists of predefined margins and heading formats. Furthermore, it presets the headers of the pages and excludes the titlepage and table of contents from the page numbering.

name: uothesis
caption: Class for dissertations and theses at the University of Oregon

descriptions.text: The class generates documents that are suitable for submission to the Graduate School and conform with the style requirements for dissertations and theses as laid out in the Fall 2010 UO graduate school student manual.

name: uowthesis
caption: Document class for dissertations at the University of Wollongong

descriptions.text: A document class for higher degree research theses in compliance with the specifications of University of Wollongong (UoW) theses in the Guidelines for Preparation and Submission of Higher Degree Research Theses (March 2006), by the Research Student Centre, Research & Innovation Division, UoW.

name: uowthesistitlepage
caption: Title page for dissertations at the University of Wollongong

descriptions.text:
The package redefines \maketitle to generate a title page for a University of Wollongong thesis, in accordance with the UoW branding guidelines. The package should be used with the book class to typeset a thesis.

The package also defines a \declaration command that typesets the declaration that this thesis is your own work, etc., which is required in the front of each PhD Thesis.

name: upca
caption: Print UPC-A barcodes

descriptions.text: The package defines a single macro \upca, to print UPC-A barcodes.

name: updatemarks
caption: Extract and update marks from boxes

descriptions.text: This package can help you update marks if you put your title in boxes. You can use \usepackage[minipage,multicol,tcolorbox]{updatemarks} in the preamble of your document so that marks in these environments can be found by LaTeX. You can use \ExtractMarks or \ExtractSplitMarks to save marks, and \UpdateMarks to reinsert them.

name: upgreek
caption: Upright Greek letters

descriptions.text:
A package to provide the upright Greek letters from the Euler or Adobe Symbol fonts as additional math symbols (\upalpha, \upbeta, etc.), with proper spacing and scaling in super- and subscripts.

This package is part of the was bundle.

name: uplatex
caption: pLaTeX2e and miscellaneous macros for upTeX

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides pLaTeX2e macros for upTeX by Takuji Tanaka.

This is a community edition syncing with platex.

The bundle depends on platex.

name: upmendex
caption: Multilingual index processor

descriptions.text:
The package is a multilingual index processor with the following features:

  • Mostly compatible with makeindex and upper compatible with mendex.
  • Supports UTF-8 and works with upLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.
  • Supports Latin (including non-English), Greek, Cyrillic, Korean Hangul and Chinese Han (Hanzi ideographs) scripts, as well as Japanese Kana.
  • Supports four kinds of sort orders (Pinyin, Radical-Stroke, Stroke and Zhuyin) for Chinese Han scripts (Hanzi ideographs).
  • Support Brahmic (Bengali, Devanagari, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Kannada, Lao, Malayalam, Oriya, Sinhala, Tamil, Telugu, Thai), Arabic and Hebrew scripts (experimental).
  • Applies International Components for Unicode (ICU) for sorting process.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: UPmethodology
caption: Writing specifications such as for UP-based methodologies

descriptions.text: The bundle allows the user to create Unified Process methodology (UP or RUP) based documents. The style provides document versioning, document history, document authors, document validators, specification description, task management, and several helping macros.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: uppunctlm
caption: Always keep upright shape for some punctuation marks and Arabic numerals

descriptions.text:
The package provides a mechanism to keep punctuation always in upright shape even if italic was specified. It is directed to Latin Modern fonts, and provides .tfm, .vf, .fd, and .sty files.

Here a list of punctuation characters always presented in upright shapes: comma, period, semicolon, colon, parentheses, square brackets, and Arabic numerals.

name: upquote
caption: Show <q>realistic</q> quotes in verbatim

descriptions.text:
Typewriter-style fonts are best for program listings, but Computer Modern Typewriter prints ` and ' as bent opening and closing single quotes. Other fonts, and most programming languages, print ` as a grave accent and ' upright; ' is used both to open and to close quoted strings.

The package switches the typewriter font to Computer Modern Typewriter in OT1 encoding, and modifies the behaviour of verbatim, verbatim*, \verb, and \verb* to print in the ` and ' way. It does this regardless of other fonts or encodings in use, so long as the package is loaded after the other fonts were.

The package does not affect \tt, \texttt, etc.

name: upref
caption: Ensure references are upright

descriptions.text:
The upref package redefines the LaTeX \ref command to ensure the numbers are upright, even in an italic or oblique environment.

The package is distributed as part of the AMS classes distribution.

name: uptex
caption: Unicode version of pTeX

descriptions.text:
upTeX is an extension of pTeX, using UTF-8 input and producing UTF-8 output. It was originally designed to improve support for Japanese, but is also useful for documents in Chinese and Korean.

It can process Chinese simplified, Chinese traditional, Japanese, and Korean simultaneously, and can also process original LaTeX with \inputenc{utf8} and Babel (Latin/Cyrillic/Greek etc.) by switching its \kcatcode tables.

topics.details: support for more than one (natural) language

name: uptex-base
caption: Plain TeX formats and documents for upTeX

descriptions.text: The bundle contains plain TeX format files and documents for upTeX and e-upTeX.

name: uptex-fonts
caption: Fonts for use with upTeX

descriptions.text:
The bundle contains fonts (TFM and VF) for use with upTeX.

This is a redistribution derived from the upTeX distribution by Takuji Tanaka.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: upzhkinsoku
caption: Supplementary Chinese kinsoku for Unicode *pTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides supplementary Chinese kinsoku (line breaking rules etc.) settings for Unicode (e-)upTeX (when using Unicode as its internal encoding), and ApTeX. Both LaTeX and plain TeX are supported.

name: urcls
caption: Beamer and scrlttr2 classes and styles for the University of Regensburg

descriptions.text:
The bundle provides a beamer-derived class and a theme style file for the corporate design of the University of Regensburg.

It also contains a scrlttr2-derived class for letters using the corporate design of the UR. Users may use the class itself (URbeamer) or use the theme in the usual way with \usetheme{UR}.

Examples of using both letters and presentations are provided as .tex and .pdf-files.

name: uri
caption: Hyperlinks for a wide range of URIs

descriptions.text: The package provides automatic hyperlinks for URIs of type arXiv, ASIN, DOI, HDL, NBN, OCLC, OID, PubMed, TINY, TINY with preview, and WebCite and provides commands \citeurl, \mailto, \ukoeln, and \uref.

name: url
caption: Verbatim with URL-sensitive line breaks

descriptions.text: The command \url is a form of verbatim command that allows linebreaks at certain characters or combinations of characters, accepts reconfiguration, and can usually be used in the argument to another command. (The \urldef command provides robust commands that serve in cases when \url doesn't work in an argument.) The command is intended for email addresses, hypertext links, directories/paths, etc., which normally have no spaces, so by default the package ignores spaces in its argument. However, a package option allows spaces, which is useful for operating systems where spaces are a common part of file names.

name: urlbst
caption: Web support for BibTeX

descriptions.text: Supports a new BibTeX webpage entry type and url, lastchecked, and eprint and DOI fields. The Perl script urlbst can be used to add this support to an arbitrary .bst file which has a reasonably conventional structure. The result is meant to be robust rather than pretty.

name: urw
caption: URW free font support

descriptions.text:
Fonts, font metrics, and macro support in LaTeX2e, for available URW fonts. Fonts provided are:

  • URW Antiqua;
  • URW Arial;
  • URW "base 35" collection;
  • URW Classico;
  • URW Garamond;
  • URW Grotesq; and
  • URW Letter Gothic.

name: urw-antiqua
caption: URW Antiqua condensed font, for use with TeX

descriptions.text: The package contains a copy of the Type 1 font URW Antiqua 2051 Regular Condensed released under the GPL by URW, with supporting files for use with (La)TeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: urw-arial
caption: URW Arial font pack for use with LaTeX

descriptions.text: The bundle provides Type 1 fonts providing the family URW A030 (Arial) released under the AFPL by URW, with supporting files for use with (La)TeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: URW-base35
caption: URW <q>Base 35</q> font pack for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
A set of fonts for use as drop-in replacements for Adobe’s basic set, comprising:

  • Century Schoolbook (substituting for Adobe’s New Century Schoolbook);
  • Dingbats (substituting for Adobe’s Zapf Dingbats);
  • Nimbus Mono L (substituting for Adobe’s Courier);
  • Nimbus Roman No9 L (substituting for Adobe’s Times);
  • Nimbus Sans L (substituting for Adobe’s Helvetica);
  • Standard Symbols L (substituting for Adobe’s Symbol);
  • URW Bookman;
  • URW Chancery L Medium Italic (substituting for Adobe’s Zapf Chancery);
  • URW Gothic L Book (substituting for Adobe’s Avant Garde); and
  • URW Palladio L (substituting for Adobe’s Palatino).

topics.details: listing a set of related fonts
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: urw-garamond
caption: URW Garamond No8 Adobe Type 1 fonts

descriptions.text:
This bundle provides a set of Adobe Type-1 fonts which URW has made available at no cost under the Aladdin Free Public License: GaramondNo8 Regular, Medium, Italic, and Medium Italic. Accompanying mathematics fonts are available from the MathDesign project.

The original distribution site of the font files is http://www.artifex.com/downloads/.

The fonts are accompanied by the TeX font metrics, virtual fonts, font definition and font mapping files to use them with the LaTeX typesetting system on Windows or Unix-like platforms.

documentation.details: Font sample and LaTeX usage details

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: URW-Grotesq
caption: URW Grotesq font pack for LaTeX

descriptions.text: The directory contains a copy of the Type 1 font ”URW Grotesq 2031 Bold‘ released under the GPL by URW, with supporting files for use with (La)TeX.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: urwchancal
caption: Use URW’s clone of Zapf Chancery as a maths alphabet

descriptions.text:
The package allows (the URW clone of) Zapf Chancery to function as a maths alphabet, the target of \mathcal or \mathscr, with accents appearing where they should, and other spacing parameters set to reasonable (not very tight) values.

The font itself may be found in the URW basic fonts collection.

This package supersedes the pzccal package.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for maths fonts

name: urwvf
caption: Support for use of free URW fonts

descriptions.text:
A collection of virtual fonts and other metrics and support files generated with fontinst 1.6, that offer access to the fonts which URW has made available under the GNU License: Antiqua, Grotesk, Nimbus and Nimbus Sans in OT1, T1, 8r and OT4 encodings, for use with LaTeX2e.

The Type 1 fonts themselves are separately available: urw.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: uscthesis
caption: USC thesis style for LaTeX 2.09

descriptions.text:
This is a document style for typesetting Theses or Dissertations in accordance with the University of Southern California Regulations for Format and Presentation of Theses and Dissertations. It provides some alternative bells and whistles such as support for multi-volume documents.

The style includes some hooks to enable it to be used in other institutions than USC.

name: usebib
caption: A simple bibliography processor

descriptions.text:
The package is described by its author as a poor person’s replacement for the more powerful methods provided by BibLaTeX to access data from a .bib file.

Its principle commands are \bibinput (which specifies a database to use) and \usebibdata (which typesets a single field from a specified entry in that database.

name: useclass
caption: Load classes as packages

descriptions.text: This package enables the usage of classes as packages. It was originally designed for the l3doc class, which is employed for documenting LaTeX code with numerous useful features. However, employing the l3doc class as a package is not convenient when using the developing class as the style for the document. Therefore, this package provides a simple interface for utilizing classes as packages.

topics.details: macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: usenix
caption: Style option to do Usenix conference proceedings

license.name: Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement

descriptions.text: This is an article.sty option, conforming to rules derived from Instructions for Usenix Authors and Speakers. Unfortunately the package author considered some of the details unclear, and was unable to clear up the problems for lack of communication with Usenix admin.

name: user-persona
caption: Typesetting User Persona sheets for UX and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction)

descriptions.text:
This package provides a structured environment and command set for typesetting professional user persona sheets in LaTeX. A user persona is a research-grounded representation of a target user group, synthesizing observed behaviours, goals, and frustrations into a humanized archetype (Cooper, 1999).

The package is intended for User Experience (UX) researchers, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) practitioners, and product designers who maintain documentation within a LaTeX workflow.

The central persona environment produces a two-column layout comprising a portrait image, an identity table, a pull-quote, and a set of colour-coded content cards. Cards may be placed in the left column, right column, or as a full-width span below both columns. Predefined semantic colours are supplied for common persona sections (Goals, Behaviours, Pain Points, Context). Inline pill labels and icon badges are supported via \personapill and \personabrand (using fontawesome5).

topics.details: layout of objects on the page

name: ushort
caption: Shorter (and longer) underlines and underbars

descriptions.text: Some engineers need underlined or twice underlined variables for which the usual \underline is too long. This package provides a generic command for creating underlines of various sizes and types.

name: ushyph
caption: US hyphenation patterns

descriptions.text:
Knuth's hyphenation patterns for English in American orthography (his hyphen.tex) appear here as ushyph1.tex; these patterns will be installed for the default language in any conventional TeX distribution.

In 1990, extended patterns for hyphenation of US English were published (TUGboat 11(1)). They appear here as ushyphen.tex (the basic set) and ushyphmax.tex (a set that is believed to find all admissable hyphenation points).

name: uspace
caption: Giving meaning to various Unicode space characters

descriptions.text: LaTeX package that gives meaning to various Unicode space characters.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines
Unicode, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: uspatent
caption: U.S. Patent Application Tools for LaTeX and LyX

descriptions.text: The package provides a class and other tools for developing a beautifully formatted, consistent U.S. Patent Application using LaTeX and/or LyX.

topics.details: typesetting legal documents or study material

name: usrguide
caption: Basic LaTeX for authors

descriptions.text:
The current version of this document covers new core commands using the expl3 (LaTeX3) syntax, which are now available to authors and package writers.

The historic version of this document documents user commands (other than font-handling commands) that differ in LaTeX2e from what was in the now-obsolete LaTeX 2.09.

Neither is a step-by-step tutorial for creating LaTeX documents; for that, see the tut-latex topic.

Part of a set of documentation that also covers font handling, class and package writing, typesetting Cyrillic, LaTeX font encodings, configuration options and modification of LaTeX.

name: ut-backref
caption: Modified backref

descriptions.text: A patched version of backref which adds a list of where the reference was cited, to each bibliography entry.

name: ut-thesis
caption: University of Toronto thesis style

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX document class implements the formatting requirements of the University of Toronto School of Graduate Studies (SGS), as of Fall 2020 ( https://www.sgs.utoronto.ca/academic-progress/program-completion/formatting).

For example usage, see the GitHub repository.

name: utbmciad-report
caption: A class and configuration file for writing high quality scientific or technical reports

descriptions.text:
LaTeX class and configuration file for typesetting a scientific or technical report following the template and guidelines from the Connaissance et Intelligence Articielle Distribuees (CIAD UR 7533) research laboratory of the Université de Technologie Belfort Montbéliard in France.

Built on top of the powerful UPmethodology suite, it provides a professional, ready-to-use structure with advanced formatting macros.

This class and configuration file could be easily extended and adapted to the style of your own institution.

utbmciad-report is part of the larger project TeX-templates.

Note on Licensing

The package contains two distinct types of material:

  1. LaTeX source code (all files that are under the src/ directory and any documentation source files).
  2. University and institutions logo images (all files under the logos/ directory).

The LaTeX source code is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version. A copy of the GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPLv3) is provided in the file `LICENSE.LGPLv3`.

The logo files are not licensed under the LGPLv3. They are the property of their respective university or institution and are included with permission for redistribution only as part of this complete package. They may NOT be modified, altered, or extracted and used separately without explicit written permission from the owning university or institution. The exact terms governing the logos are set forth in the file logos/LICENSE.logos. By redistributing this package, you agree to abide by those terms.

name: utexasthesis
caption: University of Texas at Austin graduate thesis style

descriptions.text: This class file complies with the Digital Submission Requirement for Masters and Ph.D. thesis submissions of the University of Texas at Austin.

name: utf2any
caption: Converting Unicoded text to LaTeX, HTML, etc

descriptions.text: Utf2any translates a file encoded in UTF-7 or UTF-8 (Unicode) into any 7- or 8-bit text format. Currently, mapping tables are supplied for LaTeX, HTML, ISO 8859-1, ISO 8859-15 and RFC 1345. These tables don't provide a complete mapping, but they can be easily extended to personal needs.

name: utf8add
caption: Additional support for UTF-8 encoded LaTeX input

license.name: GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer

descriptions.text:
This bundle contains the LaTeX packages utf8add.sty and utf8hax.sty.

The utf8add package provides additional support for the use of UTF-8 encoded input. This is intended for making LaTeX input more readable.

The utf8hax package is using UTF-8 characters for easier access to math in LaTeX, however making the LaTeX input less readable.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: utf8mex
caption: Tools to produce formats that read Polish language input

descriptions.text: The bundle provides files for building formats to read input in Polish encodings.

name: utfpatgen
caption: Generate hyphenation patterns from UTF-8 input

descriptions.text:
UTFPatgen takes a list of hyphenated words and outputs a set of patterns that can be used by the TeX hyphenation algorithm. The input encoding is UTF-8, and various hardwired limits in the original Patgen have been removed. Any number of hyphenation levels may be specified.

UTFPatgen is an extension and reimplementation, in CWEB, of the original Patgen, written by Frank M. Liang.

topics.details: support for generating or improving hyphenation tables

name: utfsym
caption: Provides various Unicode symbols

descriptions.text: This package provides various symbols from the Unicode in order to be able to use them originally in a school setting such as on worksheets.

name: util-half
caption: A half-tone font

descriptions.text: A simple font for drawing in half-tone; the font is distributed as Metafont source.

topics.details: fonts with specific small application areas

name: utopia
caption: Adobe Utopia fonts

descriptions.text:
The Adobe Standard Encoding set (upright and italic shapes, medium and bold weights) of the Utopia font family, which Adobe donated to the X Consortium.

Macro support, and maths fonts that match the Utopia family, are provided by the Fourier and the Mathdesign font packages.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: utorontothesis
caption: A thesis class definition for University of Toronto

descriptions.text: Probably superseded by ut-thesis.

name: utthesis
caption: Thesis package for the University of Texas at Austin

descriptions.text: LaTeX package for preparation of a thesis that meets the requirements of the Graduate School of the University of TeXas at Austin; to be used with report class at 11pt.

name: uvaletter
caption: Unofficial letterhead template for the University of Amsterdam

descriptions.text: This is an unofficial LaTeX package that provides a letterhead template for the University of Amsterdam. The design mimics the official Word template of the University and complies with the University’s house style.

name: uvlhighlight
caption: Syntax highlighting for Universal Variability Language

descriptions.text:
This package provides syntax highlighting for the Universal Variability Language (UVL) in LaTeX. It is based on the listings package and supports all UVL keywords.

The package includes multiple visual themes (default, Flamapy, UVLS dark mode, and black & white) and provides inline commands for semantic highlighting. It also supports user-defined features’ attributes and the inclusion of external .uvl files.

topics.details: highlight syntax of computer code, etc.

name: uwa-colours
caption: The colour palette of The University of Western Australia

descriptions.text: This package uses the xcolor package to define macros for the colour palette of The University of Western Australia.

name: uwa-letterhead
caption: The letterhead of the University of Western Australia

descriptions.text:
This package generates the letterhead of the University of Western Australia.

It requires the UWA logo in PDF format, which is available in SVG format at https://static-listing.weboffice.uwa.edu.au/visualid/core-rebrand/img/uwacrest/, and uses the Arial and UWA Slab fonts by default.

The package works with XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.

name: uwa-pcf
caption: A Participant Consent Form (PCF) for a human research protocol at the University of Western Australia

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX class generates a Participant Consent Form (PCF) for a human research protocol at the University of Western Australia.

It requires the UWA logo in PDF format, which is available in SVG format at https://static-listing.weboffice.uwa.edu.au/visualid/core-rebrand/img/uwacrest/, and uses the Arial and UWA Slab fonts by default.

The class works with XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. It depends on the uwa-letterhead package.

name: uwa-pif
caption: A Participant Information Form (PIF) for a human research protocol at the University of Western Australia

descriptions.text:
This package generates a Participant Information Form (PIF) for a human research protocol at the University of Western Australia.

It requires the UWA logo in PDF format, which is available in SVG format at https://static-listing.weboffice.uwa.edu.au/visualid/core-rebrand/img/uwacrest/, and uses the Calibri fonts by default.

The class works with XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. It depends on the uwa-letterhead package.

name: uwmslide
caption: Slides with a simple Power Point like appearance

descriptions.text: A slide format which produces slides with a simple Power Point like appearance. Several useful features include: use of standard titlepage to produce title slide; several slide environments including plain (page with a title), double slide (two column page with slide title), item slide (item list with title), left item slide, and right item slide. Logos are placed in the upper left corner of each slide if the logo file logo.eps is present. Preconfigured in landscape mode by default and uses Times Roman by default (originally, it was claimed, for simple conversion to PDF format).

name: uwthesis
caption: University of Washington thesis class

name: uwthesis209
caption: LaTeX 2.09 style for University of Washington theses

descriptions.text: The bundle provides a LaTeX 2.09 document style for theses presented at the University of Washington.

name: va
caption: Handwriting fonts

descriptions.text: Two fonts, va14 and vacal14, provided as Metafont source. The distribution includes a LaTeX .fd file, and full macro support for use with LaTeX is available in the fundus bundle.

name: vak
caption: BibTeX style for Russian Theses, books, etc

descriptions.text:
The file can be used to format the bibliographies of PhD theses, books etc., according to the latest Russian standards: GOST 7.82 – 2001 and GOST 7.1 – 2003. It introduces the minimum number of new entries and styles to cover all frequently used situations. The style file provides an easy way to perform a semiautomatic, or a completely manual sort of the list of the references.

Processing bibliographies produced by the style requires a 8-bit BibTeX system.

name: Vancouver
caption: Bibliographic style file for Biomedical Journals

descriptions.text: This BibTeX style file is generated with the docstrip utility and modified manually to meet the Uniform Requirements for Manuscripts Submitted to Biomedical Journals as published in N Engl J Med 1997;336:309-315 (also known as the Vancouver style). The complete set of requirements may be viewed on the ICMJE web site.

topics.details: support for documents in biomedical research

name: variablelm
caption: Font definitions for the variable Latin Modern fonts

descriptions.text: This package provides a mechanism for scaling a typeface. It is directed at the Latin Modern fonts and provides the font definitions and the corresponding style file. This mechanism is useful in mixed text compositions, for example Japanese–Latin.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: variations
caption: Typeset tables of variations of functions

descriptions.text: The package provides macros for typesetting tables showing variations of functions according to French usage. These macros may be used by both LaTeX and plain TeX users.

topics.details: mathematical tables of signs and variations

name: varindent
caption: Make paragraph indentation match the length of the line above

descriptions.text: The package will cause paragraphs to indent to the same position as the end of the last line of the previous paragraph, unless the resulting position would take you to within 2\parindent of the end of the line.

name: varindex
caption: Luxury frontend to the \index command

descriptions.text: Provides a convenient front-end for the \index command. For example, with it you can generate multiple index entries in almost any form by a single command. The package is highly customizable, and works with all versions of LaTeX and probably most other TeX formats.

name: varioref
caption: Intelligent page references

descriptions.text:
The package introduces commands \vref and \vpageref. The \vref command refers to labels in the same way as does \ref, but if the thing referred to is on a different page, the result will be decorated with on the facing page or on page <n>, and so on, as appropriate. The \vpageref command similarly decorates a page number; there are also commands \vrefrange and \vpagerefrange for ranges of labels.

The package is language-sensitive, and has definitions for its decorative words in several languages.

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

topics.details: support for variations of typographic style

name: varisize
caption: Change font size in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: A series of files, each of which defines a size-change macro. Note that 10point.tex is by convention called by one of the other files, so that there's always a way back.

name: varsects
caption: A simple package for controlling headings

descriptions.text: Redefines chapter, section, etc., headings using redefinable macros.

name: VarsFromJobname
caption: Extract variables from the name of the LaTeX file

descriptions.text: The package allows the user to extract information from the job name, provided that the name has been structured appropriately: the package expects the file name to consist of a set of words separated by hyphens.

topics.details: support for keeping track of document development

name: varwidth
caption: A variable-width minipage

descriptions.text: The varwidth environment is superficially similar to minipage, but the specified width is just a maximum value – the box may get a narrower natural width.

topics.details: set up things to fit in a given space

name: VauCanSon-G
caption: PSTricks macros for drawing automata

descriptions.text: VauCanSon-G is a package that enables the user to draw automata within texts written using LaTeX. The package macros make use of commands of PStricks.

topics.details: finite-state machines, automata, labelled graphs, etc.
package using PStricks for graphical output

name: vc
caption: The vc (version control) bundle

descriptions.text:
This is a script based approach to version control for TeX documents. It works more reliably than do keyword-substitution-based approaches, since it tracks more than just .tex files; it can work on all files in a working copy.

The vc bundle macros work with LaTeX and plain TeX. Currently, Bazaar-, Git- and Subversion-based repositories are supported; scripts are provided for use with both Unix and Windows.

name: vcell
caption: Vertical alignment of content inside table cells

descriptions.text: This package offers low-level macros to build rows with vertically-aligned cells (top, middle or bottom) and calculate the height of a row. These cells can have variable or fixed height and can be paragraph-cells or inline-cells. Different vertical alignments can be used in the same row.

name: vdm
caption: Typesetting VDM schemas

descriptions.text: The package conforms to the BSI concrete syntax for VDM, and enables the user to concentrate on VDM specifications rather than typesetting format. Note that it does not cover the whole of BSI VDM.

name: vdmlisting
caption: Typesetting VDM in ASCII syntax

descriptions.text: The package is an extension for the listings package that provides a source code printer for LaTeX. This package defines new language definitions and listing environments for the three language dialects of the Vienna Development Method: VDM-SL, VDM-PP and VDM-RT. If one wants to typeset VDM with a mathematical syntax instead of the ASCII syntax used here one should use the vdm pacakge instead

name: vector
caption: LaTeX macros for vectors

descriptions.text: Macros for convenient representation of vectors in LaTeX, both symbolically and as implicit or explicit rows/columns of elements.

name: vectorlogos
caption: Vectorial logos (GeoGebra, Emacs, Scratch, ...) with <q>inline</q> support

descriptions.text: With this package you can insert vectorial logos of some classic software. The format of the logos is pdf. The package provides macros to insert them inline, with automatic height and alignment.

topics.details: symbols or drawings to specify an object, including icons

name: venn
caption: Creating Venn diagrams with MetaPost

descriptions.text: MetaPost macros for venn diagrams.

name: venndiagram
caption: Creating Venn diagrams with TikZ

descriptions.text: The package assists generation of simple two- and three-set Venn diagrams for lectures or assignment sheets. The package requires the TikZ package.

name: venturisADF
caption: Venturis ADF fonts collection

descriptions.text: Serif and sans serif complete text font families, in both Adobe Type 1 and OpenType formats for publication. The family is based on Utopia family, and has been modified and developed by the Arkandis Digital foundry. Support for using the fonts, in LaTeX, is also provided (and makes use of the nfssext-cfr package).

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: verbasef
caption: VERBatim automatic splitting of external files

descriptions.text:
The package allows you to input (subsections of a) file, print them in verbatim mode, while automatically breaking up the input lines into pieces of a given length, which are output as figures. These figures are posted using the [H] specification, which forces LaTeX to place the figure at the spot of invocation, rather than floating the figures to the top of the next page.

The package requires the verbatim, here and vrbexin packages.

name: verbatim
caption: Reimplementation of and extensions to LaTeX verbatim

descriptions.text:
The verbatim package reimplements the LaTeX verbatim and verbatim* environments. The package also provides a comment environment (that skips everything between \begin{comment} and \end{comment}), and a command \verbatiminput for typesetting the contents of a file, verbatim.

The package is part of the latex-tools bundle in the LaTeX required distribution.

name: verbatim-gen
caption: Generic macros for setting text verbatim

descriptions.text: Defines a verbatim environment – one types \verbatim<text>\mitabrev. Short-form versions used as |<text>| or Ý<text>Ý are provided for small chunks of text.

name: verbatim-pln
caption: Define new verbatim <q>environments</q> in Plain TeX

descriptions.text:
Defines a command \newverbatimenvironment that allows the user to create their own verbatim commands.

The macros use the maybeload and redefine macro bundles.

name: verbatim-tub
caption: Plain TeX macros for verbatim

descriptions.text: This an extract from the Plain TeX macros for TUGboat production.

name: verbatimbox
caption: Deposit verbatim text in a box

descriptions.text:
The package provides a verbbox environment (which uses techniques similar to those of the boxedverbatim environment of the moreverb package) to place its contents into a globally available box, or into a box specified by the user.

The global box may then be used in a variety of situations (for example, providing a replica of the boxedverbatim environment itself). A valuable use is in places where the standard verbatim environment (which is based on a trivlist) may not appear.

The package makes use of the verbatim package (which is a required part of any LaTeX distribution).

name: verbatimcopy
caption: Make copies of text documents from within LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package provides \VerbatimCopy{in}{out} that will enable LaTeX to take a verbatim copy of one text file, and save it under another name.

The package provides a means to specify the output directory to be used, but does no checking and may therefore overwrite an important file if used injudiciously.

name: verbdef
caption: Define commands which expand to verbatim text

descriptions.text: The package defines a single command \verbdef (which has a *-form, like \verb). \verbdef will define a robust command whose body expands to verbatim text. By using commands defined by \verbdef, one can put verbatim text into the arguments of commands; since the defined command is robust, it doesn't matter if the argument is moving. (Full details of syntax and caveats about use are in comments in the file itself.)

name: verbinp
caption: <q>8-bit</q> verbatim

descriptions.text: In the days before the advent of LaTeX2e, and of the inputenc package, this package enabled the use of ISO 8859-1 coded verbatim input through a \verbinput command.

name: verbments
caption: Syntax highlighting of source code in LaTeX documents

descriptions.text: The package provides an environment for syntax highlighting source code in LaTeX documents. The highlighted source code output is formatted via powerful Pygments library of the Python language.

name: verbtext
caption: Verbatim, interpreting non-ascii text

descriptions.text: The package provides common verbatim facilities (inline text and text input from a file), and is set up to interpret other than plain ASCII text (specifically ISO 8859-1 and Microsoft code pages 437 and 850); nothing more than the cmtt font family is needed.

topics.details: input encoding support for TeX engines

name: verbtim2
caption: Verbatim listings in Plain TeX

descriptions.text: Verbatim macros, including verbatim file input and verbatim with numbered lines.

name: verdana
caption: Macros and metrics for using Verdana with LaTeX

descriptions.text:
The package provides a T1-encoded wrapper for using the Verdana (sans-serif) font with pdfLaTeX. The TrueType files are not part of the package; if they are not provided with your operating system, you may download them (address in the documentation).

Not all distributions of the fonts offer the f-ligatures (fi, ff and fl) common in TeX-related fonts; the package has an option to avoid usage of such ligatures.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
support is for a font not available on CTAN

name: verifica
caption: Typeset (Italian high school) exercises

descriptions.text: This class provides various environments and commands to produce the typical exercises contained in a test. It is mainly intended for Italian high school teachers, as the style is probably more in line with Italian high school tests.

name: verifiche
caption: A LaTeX package to typeset (Italian) high school tests

descriptions.text:
The purpose of this package is to manage the exercises for a test, their points, levels of difficulty, and solutions. Some typical formats of exercises are already implemented:

  • Plain exercise
  • Complete the Text
  • True or false
  • Closed questions
  • Open questions
  • Find the error

name: verifycommand
caption: Verifies definitions are unchanged, such as before patching

descriptions.text:
This package is intended for package authors who patch code from other packages.

To improve reliability, the verifycommand package provides a way to verify that macros or environments have not changed. This allows a package author to check before patching a definition. If a definition is not as expected, a warning is issued. At the end of the compile, a list of all changed definitions is displayed.

name: verse
caption: Aids for typesetting simple verse

descriptions.text: The package documentation discusses approaches to the problem; the package is strong on layout, from simple alternate-line indentation to the Mouse's tale from Alice in Wonderland.

name: version
caption: Conditionally include text

descriptions.text:
Defines macros \includeversion{NAME} and \excludeversion{NAME}, each of which defines an environment NAME whose text is to be included or excluded from compilation.
