caption: Allow URL breaks at any alphanumerical character

descriptions.text:
This package loads url by default and defines possible URL breaks for all alphanumerical characters, as well as = / . : * - ~ ' "

All arguments which are valid for url can be used and will be passed on to this package. For more information read the documentation of url itself.

name: xwatermark
caption: Graphics and text watermarks on selected pages

descriptions.text:
The package extends the author’s draftmark and the watermark packages.

It is currently unmaintained and does not work with modern LaTeX releases.

topics.details: decorate/confuse text by adding a background

name: xwpick
caption: Pick an image from an X display

descriptions.text: Xwpick lets you pick an image from an arbitrary window or rectangular area of an X11-server and write it to a file in a variety of formats. The area to grab is selected using a blinking rectangle. Formats supported are PostScript, GIF, PCX, PICT and PPM.

topics.details: graphics generator whose output is good for use with TeX

name: xyling
caption: Draw syntactic trees, etc., for linguistics literature, using xy-pic

descriptions.text: The macros in this package model the construction of linguistic tree structures as a genuinely graphical problem: they contain two types of objects, BRANCHES and NODE LABELS, and these are positioned relative to a GRID. It is essential that each of these three elements is constructed independent of the other two, and hence they can be modified without unwanted side effects. The macros are based on the xy-pic package.

name: xymatrix
caption: Commutative diagrams using XY-pic

descriptions.text:
The macros are said, in Milne’s guide to be among the most commonly used, despite their sub-optimal syntax.

The macros are distributed as part of the xy-pic bundle.

name: xymtex
caption: Typesetting chemical structures

descriptions.text:
XyMTeX is a set of packages for drawing a wide variety of chemical structural formulas in a way that reflects their structure. The package provides three output modes: LaTeX, PostScript and PDF.

XyMTeX’s commands have a systematic set of arguments for specifying substituents and their positions, endocyclic double bonds, and bond patterns. In some cases there are additional arguments for specifying hetero-atoms on the vertices of heterocycles. It is believed that this systematic design allows XyMTeX to operate as a practical (device-independent) tool for use with LaTeX.

name: xypic
caption: Flexible diagramming macros

copyright.owner: Kristoffer H. Rose and Ross Moore and others

descriptions.text:
A package for typesetting a variety of graphs and diagrams with TeX. Xy-pic works with most formats (including LaTeX, AMS-LaTeX, AMS-TeX, and plain TeX).

The distribution includes Michael Barr’s diag package, which was previously distributed stand-alone.

name: xypic-tut-pt
caption: A tutorial for XY-pic, in Portuguese

name: xytree
caption: Tree macros using XY-Pic

descriptions.text:
The package provides means to draw linguistic syntactic trees with ease and to support hopefully sufficient functionalities, that the linguist may need.

The package (of course) depends on the XY-Pic package.

name: yacco2
caption: Multi-threaded LR(1) compiler/compiler that emits literate grammar documents

descriptions.text:
The package provides a multi-threaded LR(1) compiler/compiler that emits literate grammar documents. The distribution contains the programs: compiler/compiler o2 and its linker o2linker, along with its runtime library yacco2.

There are build scripts for platforms: Apple, GNU, Solaris. Various documents, grammars, reference manual, quality assurance suites, and generated c++ source code are included. These items are elaborated upon in the READMEv1.0.pdf document.

name: yafoot
caption: A bundle of miscellaneous footnote packages

descriptions.text:
Contains three packages:

  • pfnote to number footnotes per page;
  • fnpos to control the position of footnotes; and
  • dblfnote to make footnotes double-columned.

name: yagusylo
caption: A symbol loader

descriptions.text:
The name is by way of being an acronym for Yet Another Grand Unified Symbols Loader…

The package allows the user to access a symbol without loading the package that usually provides it; this has the advantage of avoiding the name clashes that so commonly trouble those who load symbol-packages.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other support for symbol fonts

name: yaletter
caption: Extremely flexible macros for letters, envelopes, and label sheets

descriptions.text: The yaletter class provides extremely configurable macros for typesetting letters in any conceivable style. It provides facilities for maintaining easily-accessible databases of letterheads and addresses for repeat use. It further provides easy macros for envelopes and for label sheets. Finally, it provides some nice defaults for a few of the more common styles and sizes.

name: YAMLvars
caption: A YAML parser and tool for easy LaTeX definition creation

descriptions.text: This LuaLaTeX package provides a YAML parser and some functions to declare and define LaTeX definitions using YAML files.

topics.details: LuaTeX and packages that require it

name: yandy
caption: TUG release of Y and Y’s TeX distribution

descriptions.text:
Y&Y were a small TeX distributor, whose Windows TeX system was highly thought of. The business ceased trading 2003, and TUG was granted the right to distribute it; this version has been adjusted in a small way, and can run under Windows 7 & 8 (which were a fair time in the future when TUG was granted its rights).

The program can only produce DVI files; users should acquire a DVI reader elsewhere.

name: yannisgr
caption: Greek fonts by Yannis Haralambous

descriptions.text:
A family of 7-bit fonts with a code table designed for setting modern polytonic Greek.

The fonts are provided as Metafont source; macros to produce a Greek variant of Plain TeX (including a hyphenation table adapted to the fonts’ code table) are provided.

topics.details: font for Greek (archaic, classical and modern)

name: yathesis
caption: A LaTeX class for writing a thesis following French rules

descriptions.text:
The purpose of yathesis is to facilitate the typesetting of theses prepared in France, whatever the disciplines and institutes. It implements most notably recommendations from the Ministry of Higher Education and Research, and this transparently to the user. It has also been designed to (optionally) take advantage of powerful tools available in LaTeX, including packages:

  • BibLaTeX for the bibliography;
  • glossaries for the glossary, list of acronyms and symbols list.

The yathesis class, based on the book class, aims to be both simple to use and, to some extent, (easily) customizable.

yathesis comes with templates and samples in the doc/latex/yathesis/french/exemples/ directory in the distribution. They can also be tested on Overleaf (template and specimen).

Note: The ya in the package name stands for yet another.

name: yax
caption: Yet Another Key System

descriptions.text:
YaX is advertised as a key system, but it rather organizes attributes in parameters, which parameters can be executed, so that YaX is halfway between key management and macro definition (and actually hopes to provide a user’s interface).

Values assigned to attributes can be retrieved and tested in various ways, with full expandability ensured as much as possible.

Finally, YaX’s syntax is a quite peculiar (as few braces as possible), but may be customized.

YaX is based on texapi and thus requires e-TeX.

name: yazd-thesis
caption: A template for the Yazd University

descriptions.text: This package offers a document class for typesetting theses and dissertations at the Yazd University. The class requires use of XeLaTeX.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: yb-book
caption: Template for YB Branded Books

descriptions.text: This template helps the author design books published on Amazon under the Y.B. brand. You are welcome to use it too for your own books.

name: ycbook
caption: A versatile book class

descriptions.text: This class is intended to be an interpretation of the mwbk class which is a part of the mwcls package. The mwcls classes are simple, yet powerful and customizable classes that allow the end-user to customize the layout of headers, headings etc. They also have the benefit of being more economic in space than the most common LaTeX classes, while keeping a clear appearance and a smooth flow.

name: ydoc
caption: Macros for documentation of LaTeX classes and packages

descriptions.text:
The package provides macros and environments to document LaTeX packages and classes. It is an (as yet unfinished) alternative to the ltxdoc class and the doc or xdoc packages. The aim is to provide a different layout and more modern styles (using the xcolor, hyperref packages, etc.)

This is an alpha release, and should probably not (yet) be used with other packages, since the implementation might change. Nevertheless, the author uses it to document his own packages.

topics.details: print (La)TeX code verbatim alongside the rendered result
macros and tools for preparing documentation

name: Yet-Another-Guide-LaTeX2e
caption: A short guide to using LaTeX2e to typeset high quality documents

descriptions.text: This document is a short guide to using LaTeX2e to typeset high quality documents. It focuses on users of Windows and guides the reader through installation, some of LaTeX’s conventions, and creating the front matter, body and end matter. The appendices contain a list of useful facilities not otherwise covered in this document and a list of helpful resources.

name: yfonts
caption: Support for old German fonts

descriptions.text: A LaTeX interface to the old-german fonts designed by Yannis Haralambous: Gothic, Schwabacher, Fraktur and the baroque initials.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: yfonts-otf
caption: OpenType version of the Old German fonts designed by Yannis Haralambous

descriptions.text:
This is an OpenType version of the Old German fonts yfrak, ygoth, yswab designed by Yannis Haralambous in Metafont. The OpenType features make it easier to deal with the long/round s and with older forms of umlauts (small e over the letter).

A style file yfonts-otf.sty is provided as a replacement, for LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX, of yfonts.sty or oldgerm.sty.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes
metrics, macro incantations and other font support

name: yfonts-t1
caption: Old German-style fonts, in Adobe type 1 format

descriptions.text: This package comprises type 1 versions of the Gothic, Schwabacher and Fraktur fonts of Yannis Haralambous’ set of old German fonts.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes
font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: yfrak
caption: Old German Fraktur font

descriptions.text:
This original is provided as Metafont source; an Adobe Type 1 version is available as part of yfonts-t1.

The fonts are encoded somewhat like OT1, but a virtual font, that presents the font as if T1-encoded, is available.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: ygoth
caption: Old German Gothic font

descriptions.text:
This original is provided as Metafont source; an Adobe Type 1 version is available as part of yfonts-t1.

The fonts are encoded somewhat like OT1, but a virtual font, that presents the font as if T1-encoded, is available.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: yhmath
caption: Extended maths fonts for LaTeX

descriptions.text: The yhmath bundle contains fonts (in Metafont and type 1 format) and a LaTeX package for using them.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format

name: yi4latex
caption: Yi (Southern Chinese) support

descriptions.text: Package to provide support in LaTeX for writing all standardized Yi characters. Yi (also known as Lolo) is spoken in Southern China; the script is syllabic, based on an older, ideographic system.

name: yinit
caption: Old German decorative initials

descriptions.text: A font of initial letters, supplied as Metafont source in OT1 encoding only.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: yinit-as
caption: Additions to Yannis Haralambous’ Old German decorative initials

descriptions.text: This package contains a modified driver file, yinitas.mf, as well as a LaTeX file initials.sty.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: yinit-otf
caption: OTF conversion of Yannis Haralambous’ Old German decorative initials

descriptions.text:
This package is a conversion of the yinit font into OTF.

Original Metafont files for yinit are in the yinit package.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: york-thesis
caption: A thesis class file for York University, Toronto

descriptions.text: York Graduate Studies has again changed the requirements for theses and dissertations. The established york-thesis class file now implements the changes made in Spring 2005.

name: young
caption: Young tableaux

descriptions.text: Defines an environment Young that provides basic support for Young tableaux.

name: youngtab
caption: Typeset Young-Tableaux

descriptions.text: A package for typesetting Young-Tableaux, mathematical symbols for the representations of groups, providing two macros, \yng(1) and \young(1) to generate the whole Young-Tableau.

topics.details: macros that are independent of the (TeX) format in use

name: yplan
caption: Daily planner type calendar

descriptions.text:
Prints two six-monthly vertical-type daily planner (i.e., months along the top, days downwards), with each 6-month period fitting onto a single A4 (or US letter) sheet. The package offers support for English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese.

The previous scheme of annual updates has now been abandoned, in favour of a Perl script yplan that generates a year’s planner automatically. (The last manually-generated LaTeX file remains on the archive.)

topics.details: typeset calendars, diaries, planning charts, etc.

name: yquant
caption: Typesetting quantum circuits in a human-readable language

descriptions.text:
This LaTeX package allows to quickly draw quantum circuits.

It bridges the gap between the two groups of packages that already exist: those that use a logic-oriented custom language, which is then translated into TeX by means of an external program; and the pure TeX versions that mainly provide some macros to allow for an easier input.

yquant is a pure-LaTeX solution – i.e., it requires no external program – that introduces a logic oriented language and thus brings the best of both worlds together. It builds on and interacts with TikZ, which brings an enourmous flexibility for customization of individual circuits.

name: Ysabeau
caption: Ysabeau fonts with LaTeX support for traditional TeX engines

descriptions.text:
Ysabeau is a free type family. It combines the time-honored and supremely readable letterforms of the Garamond legacy with the clean crispness of a low-contrast sans serif, rendering it well suited for body copy as well as display.

This package provides LaTeX font support for traditional TeX engines (pdfTeX, dvips, and so on). For XeTeX or LuaTeX users, OpenType and TrueType fonts are provided only to use with the fontspec package.

topics.details: font available in Adobe Type 1 format
fonts for Cyrillic and related scripts
font designed for use as body font for Latin-based script documents
metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: yswab
caption: Old German Schwabacher font

descriptions.text:
This font is offer as Metafont source; an Adobe Type 1 version is available as part of yfonts-t1.

The fonts are encoded somewhat like OT1, but a virtual font, that presents the font as if T1-encoded, is available.

topics.details: font for gothic or blackletter shapes

name: yt4pdf
caption: Play YouTube videos in a PDF

descriptions.text:
The package uses the rmannot package to embed a special SWF file to play the YouTube videos. There is a complete set of buttons that come with the package to control the video: play, pause, stop loading, rewind, load a video by its YouTube video ID, and a button to view a video on the YouTube web site.

This package is now obsolete, since the author told us in July 2020: I am withdrawing my package yt4pdf from CTAN. It is based on the Flash play, which is no longer supported in PDF. You may wish to use its successor ltx4yt instead.

name: ytableau
caption: Many-featured Young tableaux and Young diagrams

descriptions.text: The package provides several functions for drawing Young tableaux and Young diagrams, extending the young and youngtab packages but providing lots more features. Skew and coloured tableaux are easy, and pgfkeys-enabled options are provided both at package load and configurably.

name: ytex
caption: Macro package developed at MIT

descriptions.text:
Ytex aims to support the novice user, while providing a comfortable home for the TeX programmer, who will find a library-like collection of support macros.

The package uses the author’s plain-cm package.

name: zaccone
caption: Different configuration for different captions

descriptions.text: A LaTeX 2.09 package to provide different caption formats according to the float they are in. The package defines formats for figure and table captions (with the table captions arranged to sit above the table); however the author’s intention was (apparently) that the user should edit the package to set up their own formatting.

name: zahl2string
caption: Format numbers as German words

descriptions.text:
Produces number strings (eins, zwei, …) or ordinal number strings (erste, zweite, …) for numbers in the range 0 to 999,999,999.

This package is part of the sauerj bundle.

name: zblbuild
caption: Help with the choice of a BibLaTeX style and options

descriptions.text:
zblbuild stands for Zenity BibLaTeX Build.

This package provides a shell + GUI script designed to make the choice of a BibLaTeX style and its options easier. The script requires:

  • a standard bash shell
  • a recent version of zenity (version 3.x)

The script has been tested only on a Linux platform, but should work on any platform running bash + zenity.

name: zbmath-review-template
caption: Template for a zbMATH Open review

descriptions.text:
This package contains a template for zbMATH Open reviews. It will show what your review will look like on zbMATH Open and you can test whether your LaTeX-Code will compile on our system.

The template has to be compiled using XeLaTeX and relies on scrartcl, scrlayer-scrpage, amsfonts, amssymb, amsmath, babel, enumitem, etoolbox, fontspec, gensymb, geometry, graphicx, mathrsfs, mathtools, stmaryrd, textcomp, tikz-cd, xcolor, and xparse.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: zebra
caption: Writing revision toolkits

descriptions.text:
This package provides inline note-taking macros (\todo, \comment, \fixed, \note, \placeholder) for collaborative paper writing. Notes are colour-coded, numbered, and marked in the margin for quick scanning. A summary table and clickable note list are appended at the end of the document. Custom note types and margin symbols are supported.

Note: This package was previously distributed as zebra-goodies. The old name still works, but prints a deprecation warning – zebra is the name of the package author’s lab.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: zeckendorf
caption: Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman representations of big integers

descriptions.text:
This package extends the \xinteval syntax to do algebra in Q(phi) (where phi is the golden ratio), and compute Fibonacci numbers, Zeckendorf representations of positive integers and Bergman phi-representations of the positive elements of Z[phi]. The $ character is used to compute the Knuth Fibonacci multiplication.

The package can be used either in a LaTeX document, or with Plain eTeX, or on the command line in an interactive session using eTeX.

Being based upon xintexpr, it allows to compute with arbitrarily big integers, the reasonable use being with integers of at most a few hundreds of digits.

name: zed
caption: Typeset Z specifications

descriptions.text:
A LaTeX 2.09 package for the task; it has been re-implemented for current LaTeX in zed2e and ObjectZ.

Note that this package, as it stands, uses the MSX and MSY fonts, which are no longer available (though virtual fonts are available that map them to the more recent MSA and MSB fonts.

topics.details: package only known to work with LaTeX 2.09

name: zed-csp
caption: Typesetting Z and CSP format specifications

descriptions.text: The package supports real-time CSP and incorporates the functionality of Spivey's original Z package, written for LaTeX 2.09.

name: zefonts
caption: Virtual fonts to provide T1 encoding from existing fonts

descriptions.text:
The package provides virtual T1 encoded (mostly) Computer Modern fonts based on (OT1) Computer Modern together with Times and Helvetica fonts, intended to simulate ec fonts.

The 'ae' fonts do a similar task, but miss some glyphs that aren’t available in OT1.

topics.details: font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: zennote
caption: Streamline your note-taking process!

descriptions.text:
This package aims to provide you with an easy interface to speed up the process when organizing and producing elegant notes.

All the tables, figures, equations, and listings are labelled according to the notenumber with the \titlebox command.

The noteframe environment helps you generate fancy colored boxes to emphasize the important information (e.g. Theorems, Equations, Proofs, etc.) in your document. You can customize the style and color to denote different categories, too.

topics.details: general notes (not including endnotes or footnotes)

name: zero
caption: Start list (etc.) numbering at zero

descriptions.text: The package initializes all existing counters such that numbering, where appropriate, starts at zero (instead of one). Numbering still starts at one for footnotes on the title page, parts, footnotes in minipages, and enumerated lists nested two levels or deeper, since these use a non-arabic numbering format.

name: zhlineskip
caption: Line spacing for CJK documents

descriptions.text: This package supports typesetting CJK documents. It allows users to specify the two ratios between the leading and the font size of the body text and the footnote text. For CJK typesetting, these ratios usually range from 1.5 to 1.67. This package is also capable of restoring the math leading to that of the Latin text (usually 1.2 times the font size). Finally, it is possible to achieve the Microsoft Word multiple line spacing style using zhlineskip.

name: zhlipsum
caption: Chinese dummy text

descriptions.text: This package provides an interface to dummy text in Chinese language, which will be useful for testing Chinese documents. UTF-8, GBK and Big5 encodings are supported.

topics.details: work done for the project to upgrade LaTeX
dummy text generator for tests and examples

name: zhmakeindex
caption: Makeindex replacement for Chinese users

descriptions.text:
The program provides full Unicode and Chinese sorting support.

The program is distributed with binaries for a variety of platforms.

name: zhmCJK
caption: Simplify configuration of CJK installations for Chinese

descriptions.text:
The package is designed to ease the complex business of setting up CJK fonts. The package relies on the fact at all CJK fonts share the same metrics; it provides macros that create the NFSS font definition and actual font mappings dynamically.

As a result, zmhCJK provides similar facilities and interfaces to those of xeCJK; TrueType CJK fonts may be used to generate PDF output with pdfTeX or with the DVIPDFMx driver.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: zhmetrics
caption: TFM subfont files for using Chinese fonts in 8-bit TeX

descriptions.text:
These are metrics to use existing Chinese TrueType fonts in workflows that use LaTeX & dvipdfmx, or pdfLaTeX. The fonts themselves are not included in the package.

Six font families are supported: kai, song, lishu, fangsong, youyuan and hei. Two encodings (GBK and UTF-8) are supported.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)

name: zhmetrics-uptex
caption: Chinese font metrics for upTeX

descriptions.text: The package contains some Chinese font metrics (JFM, VF, etc) for upTeX engine, together with a simple DVIPDFMx font mapping of Fandol fonts for DVIPDFMx.

topics.details: fonts for far eastern languages (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)
metrics, macro incantations and other support for miscellaneous fonts (not on CTAN)

name: zhnumber
caption: Typeset Chinese representations of numbers

descriptions.text: The package provides commands to typeset Chinese representations of numbers. The main difference between this package and CJKnumb is that the commands provided are expandable in the proper way.

name: zhspacing
caption: Spacing for mixed CJK-English documents in XeTeX

descriptions.text:
The package manages spacing in a CJK document; between consecutive Chinese letters, spaces are ignored, but a consistent space is inserted between Chinese text and English (or mathematics).

The package may be used by any document format under XeTeX.

topics.details: extra language ‘drivers’ for existing multilingual packages

name: ziffer
caption: Conversion of punctuation in maths mode

descriptions.text:
The package modifies the behaviour of characters in maths mode so that:

  • . is used as a one-thousand separator (as is common in Germany)
  • , is used as a decimal separator (as is common in Germany)
  • -- is represented with spacing as appropriate to such constructs as 1.000,--.

These conversions may be switched on and off.

name: zigaretten
caption: Propaganda and mind-numbing for cigarette addicts

descriptions.text:
The package produces wrappers for cigarette packages. These have a dual purpose:

  • they enable the addict (for some small time) to forget about the damage he/she is doing, and
  • they may be used to transmit alternative propaganda.

name: zip
caption: Barcodes for USA ZIP code

descriptions.text: Special-purpose barcoding, done entirely using TeX rules (no special font or calculations outside TeX).

name: zitie
caption: Create CJK character calligraphy practicing sheets

descriptions.text: This is a LaTeX package for creating CJK character calligraphy practicing sheets (copybooks). Currently, only XeTeX is supported.

topics.details: XeTeX, material supporting it, and packages requiring it

name: zlmtt
caption: Use Latin Modern Typewriter fonts

descriptions.text: The package allows selection of Latin Modern Typewriter fonts with scaling and access to all its features.

topics.details: metrics, macro incantations and other font support
font providing LaTeX T1 encoding support

name: zootaxa-bst
caption: A BibTeX style for the journal Zootaxa

descriptions.text:
This package provides a .bst reference style file for the journal Zootaxa that publishes contributions in zoology and classification.

This is a fork of apa.bst as provided by TeX Live since this style file resembled the most Zootaxa’s own style. Further modifications were made to the code in order to generate in-text citations and bibliography sections appropriately.

name: zref
caption: A new reference scheme for LaTeX

descriptions.text:
This package offers a means to remove the limitation, of only two properties, that is inherent in the way LaTeX’s reference system works. The package implements an extensible referencing system, where properties may be defined and used in the course of a document. It provides an interface for macro programmers to access the new reference scheme and some modules that use it.

Modules available are:

  • zref-user, use zref for traditional labels and references;
  • zref-abspage, retrieve absolute page numbers (physical pages, as opposed to the logical page number that is normally typeset when a page number is requested;
  • zref-lastpage, provide a zref-label for the last page of the document;
  • zref-nextpage, provide the page number of the next page of the document;
  • zref-totpages, provide the total number of pages in the document;
  • zref-pagelayout, provide the page layout parameters of a each page (which may then be printed at the end of the document);
  • zref-perpage, make a counter reset for each new page;
  • zref-titleref, make section title or caption text available through the reference system; zref-savepos, make positions on a page available;
  • zref-dotfill, controlled dot-filling;
  • zref-env, record the latest environment’s name and the line it started on; and
  • zref-xr, provide the facilities of the xr and xr-hyper packages.

name: zref-check
caption: Flexible cross-references with contextual checks based on zref

descriptions.text:
This package provides an user interface for making LaTeX cross-references flexibly, while allowing to have them checked for consistency with the document structure as typeset.

Statements such as above, on the next page, previously, as will be discussed, on the previous chapter and so on can be given to \zcheck in free-form, and a set of checks can be specified to be run against a given label, which will result in a warning at compilation time if any of these checks fail.

\zctarget and the zcregion environment are also defined as a means to easily set label targets to arbitrary places in the text which can be referred to by \zcheck.

name: zref-clever
caption: Clever LaTeX cross-references based on zref

descriptions.text: This package provides a user interface for making LaTeX cross-references which automates some of their typical features, thus easing their input in the document and improving the consistency of typeset results. A reference made with \zcref includes a name according to its type, and lists of multiple labels can be automatically sorted and compressed into ranges when due. The reference format is highly and easily customizable, both globally and locally. The package is based on zref’s extensible referencing system.

name: zref-vario
caption: Extended LaTeX page cross-references with varioref and zref-clever

descriptions.text: This package offers a compatibility layer for varioref to be used alongside zref-clever. It provides \z... counterparts to varioref's main reference commands, each of which essentially does some (scoped) setup for varioref, then calls the original one.

name: ZUGFeRD
caption: ZUGFeRD and Faktur-X invoicing using LaTeX

descriptions.text: This package provides interfaces to allow creating ZUGFeRD or Faktur-X invoices with LaTeX including the XML file. It can be used to modify personal invoicing templates to fulfil the requirements for digital invoicing without further modification of the invoicing processes.

name: zwgetfdate
caption: Get package or file date

descriptions.text: The package can fetch the date declaration of packages and files used by a document, and then provide the information in macros. The facilities provide a means of obtaining the date of a package being documented; this is mainly of use when doc/docstrip.

name: zwpagelayout
caption: Page layout and crop-marks

descriptions.text:
This package was developed as a typographers’ toolbox offering important basic features for everyday work. It allows setting the paper size and the page layout; it can print crop marks; and it can reflect pages both horizontally and vertically.

The package facilities work with TeX (output via dvips or (x)dvipdfm(x)), and with pdfTeX.

name: zx-calculus
caption: A library to typeset ZX Calculus diagrams

descriptions.text: This library (based on the great TikZ and TikZ-cd packages) allows you to typeset ZX-calculus directly in LaTeX. It comes with many pre-built wire shapes, a highly customizable node style (with multiple flavours for putting labels inside or outside nodes), and a debugging mode to avoid getting lost in big diagrams.

name: ZzTeX
caption: A full-featured TeX macro package for producing books, journals, and manuals

descriptions.text:
The ZzTeX macro package is a full-featured TeX macro package specially designed for producing books, journals, and manuals. Development of the package began in 1989. Since then, about 500 textbooks and journals have been produced with it for a variety of publishers. Numerous authors have used the package to produce subsequent editions of their books.

ZzTeX runs under Plain TeX.

The only documentation available for the package is contained in the zz*.dat files that accompany the TeX files.
